content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 234

I need to tell you something that genuinely surprised the shit out of me.

A few days ago, I started a Skool community fully expecting it to be fine. Helpful. Quiet.

Instead, within days, it lit me up in a way I didn’t see coming.

I’ve had deeper conversations with people on my email list in a matter of days than I’ve had in years. And it’s clarified something really important about connection, growth, and the kind of business I actually want to build.

So today, I want to share my honest thoughts about this Skool experiment. Not as a platform review. Not as a strategy pitch.

But as a real-time reflection on depth, accessibility, and why small rooms matter more than we think.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
I need to tell you something that genuinely surprised the shit out of me. A few days ago, I started a school community, fully expecting it to be fine, helpful, quiet, and instead it has lit me up in a matter of days. I’ve had deeper conversations with people on my email list than I’ve had in years and it’s made something really clear to me. Today I want to tell you about my school experiment. Why I’ve decided to jump on in what I am seeing and and the lessons that I’m already learning so that you can take all of these learnings and apply it to your own business in your own way. Let’s talk about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:39]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years. And the same is possible for you too. Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:11]:
Hey. Hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. Now today’s episode is very much a thinking out loud one and if you’ve been here a while, you know that these episodes are actually my favorite. So today I want to talk about my school experiment. And before you tune out thinking this is about a platform, it really isn’t. This is more about connection, depth, fun and remembering why we started business in the first place. Now let me be very clear.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:40]:
I was very skeptical. I did not jump into school excited. I resisted it for a long time because honestly, I’m not a huge Hermozy fan. I didn’t understand the tape on the nose. I thought that this space being school from the outside, I thought it would be very much bro marketer kind of hustle culture. Like I just didn’t think it would be very aligned. I have since googled her Moses tape situation and found out that it actually helped him breathe. So now I feel a bit shitty judging him on that.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:11]:
But regardless, he also made that part of his personal brand which I do think is weird. That aside, if you are listening to this thinking, hang on, you started a school community. Same. I am surprised too. This wasn’t a grand strategy. There was no funnel, there was no monetization plan. I created this school group purely out of curiosity. That was it.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:32]:
I honestly thought people would lurk, engagement would be really slow it would take weeks for anyone to open up and it might feel a bit flat. You know that feeling when something is fine but it’s not alive? A lot of Facebook groups have that feeling, right? That’s kind of what I expected. But instead, within days, I have over 130 people that have joined from my email list. People are posting, they’re being thoughtful, open, honest. We’re having really deep conversations. And this has caught me so much off guard. I’ve already had one on one conversations with people inside that group who until now were just a name and an email address on my list. Some of them have been on my list for years.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:14]:
Years. And yet we’d never actually spoken. There was no tone, no nuance, no back and forth, just email receive, repeat, right? But suddenly in a smaller room, they’re telling me what’s really going on. Not the polished version, not the this sounds smart version, the actual real version. And it reminded me of something I think we’ve all forgotten a little bit. Going deep beats going wide. Every single time. Small rooms change how people speak.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:44]:
They soften, they stop performing, they stop trying to impress. They just talk. And trust forms fast when people feel safe. We know this now. This actually connects to something I shared back in episode 222, which was called the number one email strategy that no one’s talking about. In that episode, I talked about the Empire Mixer. So back in October last year, I started hosting networking events for my email list. Invite only superintentional connection led.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:14]:
And on paper they were great. We’d have maybe 50, sometimes 55 women register and then around 30 to 35 would actually attend. And then I noticed something interesting. Each time I hosted one, which was monthly, the attendance dropped slightly. Not because people didn’t care, not because the conversations weren’t valuable, everyone loved them. But because of life time zones, kids, energy, capacity, it started to feel like, oh, another zoom meeting, right? And what this school experiment has shown me is that accessibility wins every time. A space people can drop into when it suits them, when they have the energy, when it feels fun for them. Like that creates far more connection than a calendar dependent event ever can.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:59]:
Because inside this community, no one is missing out if they can’t make a call. The conversation is already happening, the connection is already there. And then, yes, we can host networking calls inside the group, right? Amazing. But they’re layered on top of connection already, not replacing it. So if you can’t make the call, you’re still a part of the room, you’re still a part of the group, you’re still being seen, you still feel connected. This feels so much more human and so much more sustainable. Now I want to be really clear and make sure I say that this isn’t about email failing. I want to be super clear with this.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:33]:
This is not an email doesn’t work conversation. Email is still my home. It is still powerful. It’s still where long term relationships get built. But community adds a different dimension because email is me talking to you, community is us talking with each other. And that changes everything. I’ve had more meaningful conversations in a few days than I sometimes do in months of sending emails. Not because the emails are bad, but because intimacy is built in these smaller spaces.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:02]:
The other thing that I am loving about this school experiment is, is that I am getting a voice of customer without feeling gross about it, right? So from like a voice of customer perspective, holy shit, it’s gold. People are telling me in their own words what they’re stuck on, what they’re tired of, what they don’t want anymore, what they’re craving instead. And then here’s the part that matters most to me. There’s nothing for sale in this group. It’s free. There’s no pitch. So people aren’t guarded, they’re not wondering, is this leading somewhere? They’re just being themselves. And that kind of insight, you can’t fake it, you can’t survey it, you can’t reverse engineer it.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:38]:
You just have to listen and it’s there. Which I think is so incredible. Now I want to share something personal as well. I have a post it note on my desk that says what feels fun right now? I’ve had this post it note on my desk now for probably a good 18 months. And the reason that I wrote it was because 18 months ago, when I created it, I was not feeling like I was having any fun in my business. And I was starting to really resent some of the work I was doing. So I say that because somewhere last year, I stopped asking myself that question. It wasn’t intentional, it wasn’t dramatic.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:10]:
I just got busy. I was focused. I was being responsible. The school community has reminded me that fun is information. Like this has felt light, playful, alive. I want to check in, I want to reply, I want to be there. And that feeling matters because when business stops being fun, it starts to feel heavy. And heavy businesses do not last.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:34]:
Fun isn’t a reward. It’s actually a signal of what we’re building. A signal of the strength of what we’re building. Now, this experiment is teaching me a few things. Really. Clearly, people want quieter rooms. I already knew that from my Empire expansion events. But they want quieter rooms.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:51]:
They want to feel seen. They want pressure free spaces that build trust fast. That depth creates momentum, right? And that growth doesn’t need to be loud to be powerful. And honestly, this experiment in just a couple days has reminded me that it gets to be simple, right? We get to keep things human and grounded and real. And the connection that we get to have because of that, oh my goodness. That is what I want more of in my business. Which brings me to this. Next month I’ve decided to run a Breakup with Instagram Challenge inside this school group because this feels like the right room for that conversation.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:28]:
So there’s no yelling into the void. There’s no performing for strangers. We’re going to be sitting in a space with people who are already questioning the noise. So I ask you if social media feels heavy, if it feels draining, if you want to grow without burning yourself out and pointing and dancing and all the things, this is your invitation. So right now, the community is completely free. There’s nothing for sale that might change one day or it might not. I’m letting it unfold. But if you are craving depth over noise, a real conversation, a space that feels calm and thoughtful, I would love to welcome you in.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:03]:
You’ll find the link in the show notes, so go and request to join. You’ll be inside then when we do the Breaking up with Instagram challenge next month, I would love to have a conversation and see you in there. Now, I do want to say, whether you join or not, I want to leave you with this question. What feels fun right now? And where might you be craving depth instead of just more? I would love you to sit with that. Follow those answers. They will never lead you astray. All right, my loves, that is it from me this week. I hope that you found that interesting.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:36]:
Please come and join the school community if you want to stay up to date with what I’m doing over there. If you want to see it in real time until next week, I will talk to you soon. I hope you’re doing really well. Have a beautiful rest of your week. I will see you next Friday. Bye for now.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:49]:
Have a great day.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:50]:
Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:51]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:17]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:19]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why small rooms create deeper trust than big audiences
– How accessibility beats attendance when it comes to connection
– Why email still matters – and how community expands it
– The role fun plays in sustainable business growth
– How to build depth without burning yourself out

A room you can step into

If you’re craving a quieter room and deeper connection, I’ve opened a free Skool community where these conversations are already happening.

You can request to join the Skool community here:
skool.com/online-biz-growth

Why I was SO skeptical going in…

Let me be very clear.

I did not jump into Skool excited.

I resisted it for a long time. Partly because I’m not a huge Hormozi fan, and partly because from the outside, Skool felt very bro-marketer, hustle-culture coded.

I genuinely didn’t think it would be aligned.

This wasn’t some grand strategy. There was no funnel. No monetisation plan. I created the community purely out of curiosity.

That was it.

I assumed people would lurk.
That engagement would be slow.
That it would take weeks for anyone to open up.

You know that feeling when something is fine, but it’s not alive?

That’s what I expected.

What actually happened instead

Within days, over 130 people joined from my email list.

People started posting.
They were thoughtful.
Open.
Honest.

We were having real conversations.

I’ve already had one-on-one chats inside that space with people who, until now, were just names on my list. Some of them have been there for years.

Years.

And yet we’d never actually spoken.

Email is powerful, but it’s still mostly one-directional. I talk, you read. There’s no tone, no nuance, no back and forth.

In this smaller room, people started sharing what’s really going on. Not the polished version. The real version.

And it reminded me of something we all know deep down.

Going deep beats going wide. Every single time.

Small rooms change how people show up

In small rooms, people soften.

They stop performing.
They stop trying to impress.
They just talk.

Trust forms fast when people feel safe.

This connects directly to something I shared back in Episode 222, where I talked about the Empire Mixers. Those invite-only networking events for my email list.

On paper, they were great.
But attendance slowly dropped over time.

Not because people didn’t care.
Because life happens.

Time zones.
Kids.
Energy.
Capacity.

What this Skool experiment has shown me is that accessibility wins every time.

A space people can drop into when it suits them creates far more connection than calendar-dependent events ever can.

No one misses out.
The conversation keeps moving.
The room stays alive.

That feels deeply human.

Why this is not an “Email Is Dead” conversation

I want to be really clear about this.

This is not an email-is-failing conversation.

Email is still my home.
It’s still powerful.
It’s still where long-term relationships are built.

But community adds a different dimension.

Email is me talking to you.
Community is us talking with each other.

And that changes everything.

I’ve had more meaningful conversations in a few days than I sometimes do in months of emails. Not because the emails aren’t good, but because intimacy lives in smaller spaces.

The unexpected gift of Voice of Customer

From a business perspective, this has been gold.

People are telling me, in their own words:

  • What they’re stuck on
  • What they’re tired of
  • What they don’t want anymore
  • What they’re craving instead

And here’s the key part.

There is nothing for sale in this group.

So people aren’t guarded.
They’re not wondering where it’s leading.
They’re just being themselves.

You can’t fake that kind of insight.
You can’t survey it.
You can’t reverse engineer it.

You just have to listen.

Fun is information 💃🏼

I want to share something personal.

I’ve had a post-it note on my desk for about 18 months that says, What feels fun right now?

I wrote it at a time when business felt heavy and joyless.

Somewhere along the way, I stopped asking that question. Not intentionally. I just got busy. Responsible. Focused.

This Skool community reminded me that fun is information.

This feels light.
Playful.
Alive.

I want to show up. And that matters.

Because when business stops being fun, it starts to feel heavy. And heavy businesses don’t last.

Fun isn’t a reward. It’s a signal.

What this experiment is teaching me

Very clearly, this experiment is reinforcing a few things I already suspected.

People want quieter rooms.
They want to feel seen.
They want pressure-free spaces that build trust fast.
They want depth, not noise.

Growth does not need to be loud to be powerful.

And connection does not need to be complicated.

Where this is heading next

Because this space feels like the right room, next month I’m running a Break Up With Instagram Challenge inside the Skool community.

No yelling into the void.
No performing for strangers.
Just a room of people already questioning the noise.

Right now, the community is completely free.

That might change.
Or it might not.

I’m letting it unfold.

One question to leave you with

Whether you join the community or not, I want you to sit with this.

What feels fun right now?
And where might you be craving depth instead of more?

Because that question is exactly what led me to create the Skool space in the first place.

If you’re craving a quieter room, real conversation, and a place to explore growth without noise or performance, I’ve opened a free Skool community for my email list.

It’s a space to drop in when it suits you, connect without pressure, and be part of conversations that feel thoughtful, grounded, and human.

https://www.skool.com/online-biz-growth

They will not lead you astray.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 233

Let me ask you something.

When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence?

Not skimmed.
Not tolerated.
Actually enjoyed.

That question is the reason I stopped sending them.

And what I do instead has completely changed how people engage with my emails.

You can grab the Start Here email template I talk about in this episode for free here: CLICK HERE

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why the delivery email is usually the most-opened email you’ll ever send
– What’s actually happening with inbox behaviour as we move into 2026
– How one “Start Here” email can replace an entire welcome sequence
– What to include in that email so it builds trust and invites action
– Why treating subscribers like adults leads to better long-term results

A different way to welcome people in…

Email works best when it feels human, not engineered.

If you want your inbox to feel calmer, clearer, and more intentional, here’s how I can help:

Get a clear, 3-step plan to simplify your welcome experience and email ecosystem.

Why welcome sequences started to feel off

Before anyone panics, this is not a “welcome sequences are dead” rant.

They still work.
They still convert.
They still have a place.

They just don’t fit how I want to show up anymore.
Or how my audience wants to be treated heading into 2026.

Funnels and sequences honestly annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

They know when they’ve entered a funnel.
They know the pacing.
They know what’s coming next.

And when people realise they’re in a sequence, something subtle shifts.

They skim more.
They click less.
They wait it out.

Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to feel back in control.

That matters to me.

I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery.

I want them to feel like a room you’ve just walked into.

The assumption most welcome sequences are built on

Most welcome sequences are based on an old belief.

That attention equals readiness.

That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be nurtured, educated, and gently guided toward an offer over the next five to seven emails.

But inbox behaviour has changed.

Across platforms, we’re seeing that the delivery email gets the highest open rates. Often 20 to 40 percent higher than follow-up emails in the same sequence.

Click rates peak there too.

Not email three.
Not email five.
The very first one.

So instead of dragging people through a sequence and hoping they stay engaged, I decided to respect that moment.

If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then it should do the work.

What I use instead…

I send one email.

I call it a Start Here email.

It still delivers the thing they signed up for. That part matters.

But instead of drip-feeding orientation over a week, I give people everything upfront.

Clearly.
Honestly.
Without manipulation.

This one email answers the questions every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not.

Who are you really?
What kind of emails do you send?
How often will I hear from you?
What do you actually help with?
Where do I go if I want more?

I don’t hide that information across multiple emails.

I let them decide what happens next.

Why this works better for my audience

Yes, my Start Here email has more than one link.

I know. That breaks the old rules.

But those rules were written for a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being carefully guided from point A to point B.

That time is over.

My list is full of intelligent women. They don’t need to be funnelled down a narrow path or protected from “too many options.”

Giving people choice builds trust.

And trust converts when they’re ready. Not because you timed email number four perfectly.

What people actually need right now

People aren’t short on information.

They’re drowning in it.

What they’re short on is orientation.

They want to know:
Am I in the right place?
Is this person for me?
Does this feel safe, calm, and relevant?

A Start Here email can answer all of that without pressure.

And because it lives in one place, it becomes an anchor.

People can save it.
Come back to it.
Click when they’re ready.

That lines up with how people actually behave in inboxes now.

Longer decision cycles.
Fewer impulsive clicks.
Stronger trust when they do move.

What I include in my Start Here email

Conceptually, it does four things.

I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio.

I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what I send, and what I don’t send. Predictability builds safety.

I give a few clear places to explore. A loved free resource, the podcast, and one way to work with me.

And I invite conversation.

I ask them to reply. I remind them it’s actually me. I ask how they found me.

Even if most people never reply, that invitation alone changes how the inbox feels.

The difference in tone matters

A welcome sequence says, “Sit down, I’ll take you through this.”

A Start Here email says, “Welcome. You’ve arrived. Take what you need.”

That difference matters.

It tells your subscriber they’re not a number.
Not a lead.
Not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose.

They have agency from the very first email.

And in my experience, that creates better long-term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

If welcome sequences feel heavy, performative, or outdated for your business, this is a simple experiment worth running.

You don’t need to burn everything down.

Turn off your sequence.
Grab my template here: Start Here Email Template
Write the email.
Track it for 30 days.

Watch the data.
Notice how it feels.
Pay attention to replies and engagement.

I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

content:

I don’t think most women in business need another strategy.
I think they need to loosen their grip.

On timelines.
On expectations.
On proving that the last investment wasn’t a mistake.

This episode is for every woman who’s been burned by a mastermind, a mentor, or a “safe room” that turned out not to be so safe – and kept going anyway.

And yeah… I’m sharing a personal story here that I’ve never brought to the podcast before.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

[00:00:00] I don’t think most women in business need another strategy. I think they need to loosen their grip on timelines, on expectations, on proving that the last investment that they made wasn’t a mistake. Today I’m gonna be talking to every woman that has been burnt by a mastermind and kept going. Anyway, I’m also gonna share a really personal story of my own mastermind drama that I’ve never brought to the podcast.

[00:00:22] So buckle in. Let’s get started.

[00:00:25] Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the email growth show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. [00:00:49] Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

[00:00:56] Hey. Hey, welcome back to the email growth show. I am so [00:01:00] excited that you’re here. So this episode is for the woman who’s invested before she’s shown up before, she has trusted a room, a mentor, a promise, and walked away tighter and not lighter. It’s also for the woman who isn’t burnt out, but is definitely overworking.

[00:01:16] Let’s talk about both here is what I’m noticing. A lot of smart, capable business owners are working really hard. Really hard, not falling apart. They’re not chaotic. They’re just constantly gripping. Gripping the plan, gripping the data, gripping the strategy, gripping the outcome, and when things don’t move fast enough.

[00:01:40] The instinct is to grip tighter, right? To invest again, to push harder, to stay longer, to prove something, especially if you’ve been burnt before. That’s why this idea of a clenched fist hit me so deeply because a clenched fist can work, but it can’t receive. And I realized [00:02:00] honestly, that I do this too. I hold tightly to my timelines, my expectations, my definition of success, the numbers, the metrics, the proof when sometimes what the business actually needs is just for me to breathe, to slow down, to open that clenched fist and actually receive, not to stop caring, but to stop forcing. A lot of us have been disappointed. A lot of us have been burnt by masterminds or group coaching or coaches or investments before. If you’ve learned the hard way that not every shiny room is safe, your nervous system learns to protect you.

[00:02:37] So gripping harder feels responsible. It feels smart, it feels like you’re in control, but over time, it also makes growth heavier than it needs to be. Now I wanna share a little context here because this didn’t come from nowhere for me. My very first mastermind experience was back in 2021. It was with someone who was very Instagram famous in the online space at the [00:03:00] time.

[00:03:00] I listened to her podcast and I joined full of trust, full of belief, full of excitement. I stayed for over a year, and I even renewed after that and became alumni, and over that time. Oh, fuck. I got burnt bad, not in a like dramatic public way, but in a really quiet, painful way. Ideas that I’d shared were taken and passed off as her own.

[00:03:24] The boundary between friend and client became blurred, and when my personal life went through a genuinely hard financial season, there was no softness. There was no compassion, no empathy. There was just the contract, and look, I signed it. I wasn’t asking for special treatment, but what broke something in me was that realization that I wasn’t actually valued as a person in her space.

[00:03:45] I was a number, I was a transaction, I was a seat. And for somebody that feels things deeply, which I am, I’m a total empath, that really hurt me, especially because I’d been led to believe that we were friends. So the deeper lesson here is [00:04:00] that that experience changed how I show up in business.

[00:04:03] It taught me that proximity doesn’t equal care. It taught me that access doesn’t equal safety. And also that success doesn’t mean somebody has integrity. When you have been burned like that, when you’ve been hurt deeply by somebody like that, you do grip harder.

[00:04:18] Next time you watch more closely, you protect yourself. You stay longer than you should. You tell yourself, I just need to make this work. And that’s not weakness, like that’s self protection.

[00:04:29] And that’s what our nervous system is wired to do. That is a good thing. so this week I just wrapped up my third empire expansion event. It was amazing. The women inside that room were incredible. We had some great connection, some great conversation, and it honestly filled me up.

[00:04:46] At the end of day two, I said to my husband like, oh my gosh, this is what I was made to do. Like I loved it so much, but it was interesting ’cause there was a theme that came out of day one especially, and. Not that anybody that came to the event was burnt [00:05:00] out. They were definitely functioning. They’re capable, they’re ambitious, but they were overworking so incredibly much.

[00:05:08] and a lot of it in invisible ways. There was a lot of overthinking. There was over efforting, there was overhold, and that clenched fist energy slowly teaches our body that growth needs strain, right? That growth requires that overworking when actually. It doesn’t, and when we are used to that, when we’re wired for that,

[00:05:28] , when our past experience, whether that’s the past six months, two years, or whatever, when our past experience has told us that that is what we need to do when opportunities show up, when support is available, receiving feels unsafe. So I wanted to speak to any of the women listening that have been burnt by a mentor, a mastermind, a coach, anyone in the online space specifically before, I just want you to hear this.

[00:05:54] Just because you were burnt doesn’t mean you were bad at choosing, right? It just means that you were more discerning now, which is a [00:06:00] fantastic thing. At a certain level of business, you don’t need louder height, more content, or bigger rooms. You need safety. You need clarity. You need collaboration and relationships, and you need leadership that doesn’t disappear when things get human or when life starts to life because it is bound to happen, right?

[00:06:20] That is not being difficult, that is just being experienced. So I wanna wrap this conversation up with this thought, and this is a thought that I keep coming back to. Growth, actually doesn’t respond to pressure. It responds to clarity. And clarity often comes when you loosen your grip.

[00:06:40] When you open your hand, right, when you stop forcing timelines, when you stop proving, when you stop staying out of obligation. An open hand doesn’t mean giving up. It means that you’re trusting that you don’t have to strangle your business to make it grow. So this is also why I’ve built my work the way I have.

[00:06:59] I have [00:07:00] smaller rooms now. I have clearer expectations. I have real conversations. Human support, not keep up or fall behind, not performance, not pretending we’re friends when the money is the only thing holding us together. And that’s an episode all for its own, I think. But I never want someone in my world to feel like a number.

[00:07:20] I actually had one of our celebration calls, which is like the wrap up calls I do with every attendee after the empire expansion events. I actually had one of them yesterday. It was the first one out of the group that I’d had and. The attendee said something so beautiful to me. Towards the end of the call, she said, you were the first coach.

Like I could have started crying on the call because that is exactly the type of feeling. That I want people to know they can have with me. I want the women that I’m working with to feel safe with me, to know that they’re safe with me, to be able [00:08:00] to breathe and relax and loosen their grip and open their hand, and then we work together and they get to receive.

[00:08:06] Like that is the experience that I’m going for. And to hear that mirrored back from somebody that was at the event Was everything that little testimonial or mention in that conversation meant more to me than. the flashy income claims, right? Like I’ve got those two. Like, yes, my clients have three times their revenue, have hit milestone months have grown their email list by 300%. Like whatever. Like, I’ve got all of those, but to me it’s more about how do they feel?

[00:08:33] And if somebody can feel safe, then fuck yeah, we can go after all of those business goals and we can get them, But how they feel is everything. I never want somebody in my world to feel like a number. So in closing, if you’ve ever been burnt before, if you’re listening to this, please don’t harden.

[00:08:47] Please don’t close. Please don’t grip so tightly that nothing you can reach you. And if you are working really hard right now, if you know that you are exhausted in your bones and you are pushing whatever you can uphill, you’re not falling apart, but you’re [00:09:00] holding everything And your knuckles are turning white.

[00:09:03] This is your permission to soften the grip this year. This is your permission to open your palm to breathe, to let support land instead of forcing it progress. Trust me my love. [00:09:20] Thank you so much for trusting me with this conversation and thank you for being the kind of woman who’s willing to lead with both wisdom and heart. I love you so much. I’m so grateful that you are here, and I will see you next week. Alright, bye for now.

[00:09:34] Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others.

[00:09:51] Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you, who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their [00:10:00] business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening, and I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why overworking often comes before burnout
– How being “loyal” to the wrong container can quietly stall your growth
– The difference between effort and expansion and why pressure isn’t the answer
– What a clenched fist vs an open hand looks like in business leadership
– How to rebuild trust with yourself after a disappointing investment

Ready for a room that actually feels safe & strategic?

The Empire Expansion Event is for experienced women who are done forcing, done proving, and ready to grow with clarity, support, and leadership that stays human.

Apply for the Empire Expansion Event now.

P.S. You don’t need another strategy.
You need the right room – and the permission to open your hand.

The clenched-fist season no one talks about

Here’s what I’m noticing everywhere right now.

Smart. Capable. Experienced women working really hard.

Not falling apart.
Not chaotic.
Just constantly gripping.

Gripping the plan.
Gripping the data.
Gripping the strategy.
Gripping the outcome.

And when things don’t move fast enough?
The instinct is to grip tighter.

Invest again.
Push harder.
Stay longer.
Prove something.

Especially if you’ve been burned before.
That’s why this image of a clenched fist hit me so deeply.

Because a clenched fist can work…
But it can’t receive.

And I realised – honestly – I do this too.

I hold tightly to timelines, metrics, numbers, proof.
When sometimes what my business actually needs is for me to breathe…
To slow down…
To open my hand.

Not to stop caring – but to stop forcing.

What getting burned actually does to your nervous system

A lot of us have been disappointed.
Burned by masterminds.
Burned by group programs.
Burned by coaches who promised safety, sisterhood, and support – and delivered pressure, silence, or ego instead.

When that happens, your nervous system adapts.
It learns to protect you.

So gripping harder feels responsible.
It feels smart.
It feels like control.

And for a while?
It works.

But over time, it also makes growth heavier than it needs to be.

The mastermind experience that changed everything for me

My very first mastermind experience was back in 2021.

The mentor was very Instagram-famous at the time.
I listened to her podcast.
I trusted her voice.
I joined full of belief and excitement.

I stayed over a year.
I renewed.
I became alumni.

And quietly – painfully – I got burned.

Ideas I shared were taken and passed off as her own.
Boundaries between friend and client blurred.
And when my personal life hit a genuinely hard financial season?

There was no softness.
No empathy.
Just the contract.

I wasn’t asking for special treatment – I’d signed the agreement. But what broke something in me was realising I wasn’t valued as a person.

I was a seat.
A number.
A transaction.

And when you’re an empath – when you feel deeply – that kind of realisation cuts.

The invisible lesson that lingers

That experience shaped how I show up in business more than I realised at the time.

It taught me:

  • Proximity doesn’t equal care
  • Access doesn’t equal safety
  • Success doesn’t equal integrity

And when you’ve been burned like that?
You protect yourself next time.

You watch more closely.
You stay longer than you should.
You tell yourself, I just need to make this work.

That’s not weakness.
That’s self-protection.

And your nervous system is doing exactly what it’s designed to do.

What I saw inside the Empire Expansion Event

I’ve just wrapped up my third Empire Expansion Event, and it filled me up in the best way.

But something really clear came up – especially on day one.

None of the women were “burnt out.”
They were functioning.
Capable.
Ambitious.

But they were overworking in invisible ways.

Overthinking.
Over-efforting.
Over-holding.

That clenched-fist energy teaches your body that growth requires strain.
That success has to feel heavy.

So when support does appear?
Receiving feels unsafe.

If you’ve been burned, hear this…

Just because you were burned doesn’t mean you were bad at choosing.

It means you’re more discerning now.
And that’s a strength at this level of business.

You don’t need louder hype or bigger rooms.

You need:

  • Safety
  • Clarity
  • Real collaboration
  • Leadership that doesn’t disappear when life gets human

That’s not being difficult.
That’s being experienced.

Growth doesn’t respond to pressure

This is the thought I keep coming back to:

Growth doesn’t respond to pressure.
It responds to clarity.

And clarity often comes when you loosen your grip.

When you stop forcing timelines.
When you stop proving.
When you stop staying out of obligation.

An open hand doesn’t mean giving up.
It means trusting that you don’t have to strangle your business to make it grow.

Why I built my work differently…

This is why my work looks the way it does now.

Smaller rooms.
Clear expectations.
Real conversations.
Human support.

No “keep up or fall behind.”
No performative friendship.
No pretending money is the only thing holding us together.

I never want someone in my world to feel like a number.

One of the women from the Empire Expansion Event said something to me on her celebration call that I’ll never forget:

“You’re the first coach my nervous system has actually felt safe with.”

That mattered more to me than any flashy income claim ever could.

Because yes – my clients grow revenue.
Yes – they hit milestone months.
Yes – they grow their lists.

But how they feel always comes first.

Finally…

If you’ve ever been burned – please don’t harden.
Please don’t close.
Please don’t grip so tightly that nothing new can reach you.

And if you’re holding everything right now – white knuckles and all – this is your permission to soften.

To open your palm.
To breathe.
To let support land instead of forcing progress.

You don’t need to push harder.
You might just need to receive differently.

You need the right room – and the permission to open your hand.

If your email list feels quieter than usual right now – fewer replies, fewer clicks, less visible engagement – I want you to pause before you rewrite your funnel, change platforms, or decide something is wrong with your business.

Feat. Cheryl Rerick

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 228

If you’re growing your email list…
Sending weekly newsletters…
Launching when you can muster the energy…

but sales still feel inconsistent AF – this episode is for you.

Because here’s the uncomfortable truth most people don’t want to hear:

Your email list isn’t cold. It’s under-nurtured.

And no – another launch won’t fix that.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I sat down with one of my favourite email nerds and dear friends, Cheryl Rerick, to talk about what actually happens after someone joins your list… and why that awkward “now what?” phase is where the real money lives.

Let’s get into it.

Listen to this episode here:

** Read time: 5 – 6 mins | Listen time: 26 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why most email lists aren’t cold – they’re under-nurtured
– What evergreen email sequences actually are [and what they’re not]
– Why customer research matters more than copy tricks
– How to choose the right offer to sell on automation
– How to repeat your core message without boring yourself to death

The biggest missed opportunity on your email list

Most business owners do two things really well:

✔ They build a list
✔ They sell hard during launches

And then…

They stop.

The welcome sequence ends.
The launch wraps.
And suddenly it’s just “send a newsletter and hope for the best.”

Cheryl calls this the largest untapped opportunity in your business – the people who didn’t buy right away… but didn’t unsubscribe either.

They’re still curious.
Still watching.
Still warming up.

They just need a better journey.

Evergreen email sequences ≠ lazy marketing

Let’s clear this up right now.

Evergreen email sequences are not:

  • Copy-pasted newsletters dumped into automation
  • “Set and forget” spammy funnels
  • A replacement for relationship-building

They are:

  • A strategic sales journey stretched over time
  • A way to keep selling without screaming “BUY NOW”
  • A pressure-relief valve for your nervous system

As Cheryl explains, an evergreen sequence is basically a sales page… but delivered via email, slowly, and with way more nuance.

And honestly? It’s how modern buyers want to be sold to.

Why your messaging matters more than your tech

Before you touch automation, Cheryl is very clear on one thing:

You need to talk to real humans.

Not ChatGPT.
Not vibes.
Not “what you think your audience feels.”

Actual people.

Because the difference between “this sounds good” and “holy shit, that’s me” often comes down to one sentence – lifted directly from someone’s mouth.

[Side note: one of Cheryl’s best-converting sales page lines literally came from a client saying selling via email felt like “standing on the corner naked with a sign that says buy my shit.” ICONIC.]

This is why evergreen sequences work when they’re done right – they reflect how your audience already thinks and feels, not how you wish they did.

Step one: Audit your offers [before you automate anything]

Not everything should be evergreen.

Some offers are:

  • Too time-intensive
  • Cohort-based
  • Better live

So before you build sequences, you need to ask:

  • What can be sold on automation?
  • What makes sense as a next step for my audience?
  • Where are people getting stuck right now?

This is where strategy beats hustle every single time.

Because when the offer matches the moment your subscriber is in?
Sales feel easy. Natural. Expected.

The real magic: repetition without boredom

Here’s the part I loved most in this conversation.

We know people need to hear our message 40+ times before they buy.
But saying the same shit over and over in real time gets boring fast.

Evergreen sequences solve that.

They let your audience hear your core message repeatedly – while you get to move on, create, rest, or show up live when it actually matters.

Same message.
Different stories.
Different angles.

No burnout required.

If this episode made you realise your nurture is messy…

Good. That’s awareness – not failure.

And if you’re thinking:

“I know I should be doing this… but I have no idea where to start.”
That’s exactly where I come in.

👉 Book a Business Breakthrough Audit

I’ll personally review:

  • Your email list + visibility
  • Your offers + nurture gaps
  • What to automate [and what to stop overcomplicating]

And I’ll send you a clear 3-step action plan you can actually implement, without burning your whole system down.

Cheryl Rerick is an email strategist, automation engineer, and deliverability expert who helps online business owners turn their email list into a long-term sales engine. She specialises in evergreen email sequences that nurture, connect, and convert, without hustle or hype.

title: 3 Visibility Moves to Scale Your Business in 2026 Without Burnout

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 228

A lot of smart, capable business owners are doing everything they were told would work.

They’re showing up.
They’re creating content.
They’re being visible.

And yet… things feel oddly stalled.

Not failing.
Not collapsing.
Just not really moving.

If that’s you, I want you to hear this first.

Nothing has gone wrong.

You’re not behind.
And you’re not missing some secret tactic.

What’s happening is quieter than that.

And that’s exactly what I want to talk about today.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why being “everywhere” is slowing your growth
– The difference between audiences and rooms – and why trust matters more than reach
– How to create visibility that leads to momentum instead of burnout
– What it really takes to build a calm, scalable business in 2026

Your Next Step Starts With Direction

If these visibility shifts have you realising you want growth that feels calmer, clearer, and more intentional in 2026, that’s exactly what we work through inside the Empire Expansion Event.

This is where we zoom out, simplify your visibility, and map a growth ecosystem that actually fits you – without hustle, pressure, or performative marketing.

If you’re ready to rethink how visibility feels, come inside the Empire Expansion Event.

Why Visibility Feels Heavier Than It Used To

As we move toward the end of the year, I’ve been having the same conversation with so many women.

They sound confident on the outside.
But underneath, they’re tired.

They’re creating.
They’re showing up.
They’re doing “visibility.”

But it feels effort-heavy. Disconnected. Harder than it should be.

And here’s what I’m noticing.

Visibility has become noisy.

More platforms.
More output.
More pressure to be consistent and polished and everywhere at once.

Most business owners aren’t struggling because they’re invisible.

They’re struggling because their visibility isn’t landing.

It’s not turning into clarity.
It’s not building trust.
And it’s definitely not feeling easeful.

Growth doesn’t respond to pressure.

It responds to clarity.

And visibility only works when it feels safe to be seen as yourself, not as a brand persona you’re trying to maintain.

Visibility Move One: Depth Over Distribution

One of the biggest patterns I see is business owners spreading themselves across platforms in the name of growth, but losing connection in the process.

Depth builds familiarity.
Familiarity builds trust.
Trust creates sustainable sales.

In 2026, the businesses that scale will not be the ones everywhere.

They’ll be the ones who choose one primary visibility lane and commit to it deeply.

Not because other platforms are bad.
But because your message needs somewhere to breathe.

It needs a home base.

For me, that has always been email and podcasting. Those platforms allow me to go deep, tell stories, lead conversations, and build real relationships.

Choosing one platform and going deep does not limit your growth.

It anchors it.
It also gives you breathing room when life is lifing.

On hard weeks, you only need to show up well in one place. Not five.

That single decision alone creates consistency without burnout.

Visibility Move Two: Rooms Over Audiences

Here’s another shift I’m seeing.

People are moving away from passive consumption and toward participation.

Audiences listen.
Rooms engage.
Workshops.
Events.
Live conversations.
Small, intentional spaces.

These are not about big numbers.

They’re about building trust faster.

And your business will only ever grow at the speed of trust.
When people experience you, not just your content, something shifts.

Questions get answered.
Confidence builds.
Momentum starts to feel real.

Every major growth leap in my business has come from rooms like this.

Not flashy ones.
Not massive ones.

Human ones.

Some of the most powerful rooms I’ve held had fewer than 30 women in them.

And the depth of trust built in those spaces has shaped my business far more than any viral moment ever could.

Visibility Move Three: Visibility With Direction

This is where things quietly break down for a lot of people.

Visibility without direction creates exhaustion.
Visibility with direction creates momentum and revenue.

Here’s the question I always come back to.

If someone loves what I just shared, what happens next?

Not in a salesy way.
In a respectful way.

Is the next step clear?
Is it easy?
Do they know where to go?

Clarity is kindness. For you and for your audience.

When your visibility leads somewhere intentional, your ecosystem starts to compound instead of resetting every month.

Think about this.

What is your signature offer?
Where do you actually want to lead people?

Once you know that, you can reverse engineer the visibility that supports it.

This is how calm, profitable businesses are built.

Not by chasing attention.
But by creating ecosystems that make sense.

What This Means for Your 2026 Growth

There is no single right visibility model.

Every strategy works when it’s aligned.

What I am noticing, though, is this.

The businesses that feel calm, profitable, and sustainable are not chasing more.

They know:

  • Where they show up
  • Who they are speaking to
  • What comes next

That clarity changes everything.

You don’t need to overhaul your business overnight.
You don’t need to follow someone else’s blueprint.

You get to decide what 2026 looks like for you.

But if something inside you is whispering, I want growth that feels steadier than this – listen.

Your Next Step Starts With Clarity

If these visibility shifts have you realising you want growth that feels calmer, clearer, and more intentional in 2026, that’s exactly what we work through inside the Empire Expansion Event.

This is where we zoom out, simplify your visibility, and map a growth ecosystem that actually fits you — without hustle, pressure, or performative marketing.

Come build your 2026 visibility plan inside the Empire Expansion Event.

P.S. You don’t need to be everywhere to scale. You need clarity, trust, and a strategy that compounds instead of resets.

title: Workshops Are the Most Underrated Conversion Event in Online Business

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 227

People love to say you need funnels, ads, and a massive audience to sell online.
But the biggest growth spurts I see rarely come from any of that.

They come from workshops.

And most business owners are massively underestimating just how powerful workshops really are.

After the Empire Expansion Event last month, this became impossible to ignore. Conversation after conversation revealed the same thing: women are already sitting on one of the strongest conversion tools available to them, but they are only using it halfway.

This episode needed to happen.

Because workshops are not just “nice free content”. They are not just a visibility play. And they are definitely not something you have to wait to earn the right to use.

Workshops are one of the simplest and cleanest conversion strategies you can build into your business.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why workshops outperform almost every other conversion event (even if you’re early in business)
– The psychology behind why they build trust faster than funnels
– The difference between running a class and running a conversion event
– How workshops help you grow your list, validate your offers, and strengthen your messaging – all at once
– What to say after your workshop to turn interest into actual sales
– Why workshops will be one of the smartest strategies heading into 2026

Ready to Turn Workshops Into Real Conversion Events?

If you want help turning workshops into real conversion events, the Empire Expansion Event is where we build this properly.

Join the Empire Expansion Event

P.S. If workshops are not part of your strategy yet, you are leaving trust, clarity, and sales on the table. Come to the Empire Expansion Event and let’s fix that.

The moment it clicked

At the Empire Expansion Event, one business owner shared a story that stuck with me.

She had just run a workshop. Not a tiny one. Not a “five people showed up and maybe one bought later” kind of workshop.

This one added over 100 people to her email list in 24 hours. The Zoom room was full. The energy was high. And when it was over, she said something that made me laugh out loud.

She joked that she had no idea workshops could be conversion events.

She knew workshops could build visibility.
She knew they could grow a list.
She knew they could warm people up.

What she had not connected was that this was already one of the most effective ways to convert.

That comment made something very clear to me. A lot of business owners are running workshops without treating them like the conversion moments they are.

Why workshops convert when other things don’t

Workshops work because they collapse the gap between stranger and client faster than almost anything else.

First, they create instant relevance.

When someone signs up for a workshop, they are raising their hand. They are saying, “This problem matters to me.” That clarity alone creates connection. Specificity converts.

Second, workshops position you as the guide, not the guru.

People do not want to be lectured. They want to experience your thinking, your coaching style, and your way of solving problems. A workshop lets them do that in real time.

Third, they build trust quickly.

You answer questions. You respond to what is actually coming up. You adjust as you go. Trust built in one hour can outperform months of passive nurturing.

And finally, workshops attract aligned people.

A workshop is not designed to go viral. It is designed to go deep. You do not need hundreds of signups. You need the right people in the room. Depth beats volume every time.

Why workshops belong in your 2026 strategy

Workshops are one of the highest return on investment moves you can make.

You do not need a huge audience.
You do not need a complicated funnel.
You do not need a long launch runway.

One well-positioned workshop can give you:

  • New, genuinely interested leads
  • Real feedback on your messaging
  • Content you can repurpose across your business
  • Clarity on what your audience actually wants
  • Proof of concept for bigger offers
  • Confidence in your ideas
  • Revenue

Very few conversion events offer all of that at once.

The biggest mistake people make with workshops

They treat them like content.

A workshop is not content.
It is a conversion moment.

If you treat your workshop like a webinar, it will underperform.
If you treat it like a coaching experience and a community moment, everything changes.

How to sell after a workshop without feeling pushy

Hosting the workshop is only step one. What happens next is where most people go wrong.

Here is a simple, effective structure that works.

First, send the replay email with a clear next step.
Tell people what you covered, why it matters, and what to do next. Book a call, join a waitlist, or reply with a takeaway. Momentum matters more than pressure.

Second, send a behind-the-scenes follow-up.
This email shares what you noticed during the workshop and what that tells you about what they might need next. It feels personal and invites conversation. Conversations lead to clients.

Third, send a value-driven bridge email.
This is where you connect the dots between the problem, the workshop, and your offer. You teach while you sell.

Fourth, invite them into your offer clearly.
This is not a hype email. It is an invitation. You explain what working together looks like, who it is for, and what changes.

Finally, close with safety.
Let them know the door is open. No pressure. No urgency. People buy when they feel safe.

If you are planning your next workshop

Be specific about the promise.
Focus on one transformation.
Coach more than you teach.
Make the call to action the natural next step.
Follow up with connection.

Your workshop is not the end of the process. It is the beginning.

The real takeaway

Workshops are not about selling harder.
They are about serving deeply enough that selling becomes obvious.

You do not need a bigger audience or a perfect funnel to run one.
You need a clear topic, a willingness to show up, and an hour.

You are more ready than you think.

Ready to Turn Workshops Into Real Conversion Events?

If you want help turning workshops into real conversion events, the Empire Expansion Event is where we build this properly.

Join the Empire Expansion Event

P.S. If workshops are not part of your strategy yet, you are leaving trust, clarity, and sales on the table. Come to the Empire Expansion Event and let’s fix that.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 226

Before we even get into strategy, funnels, or visibility, I want to talk about something far more uncomfortable.

Loyalty.

Not the kind we praise publicly. The quiet kind. The kind that keeps women in rooms they’ve already outgrown, convincing themselves they should stay because leaving would feel wrong.

If you have ever thought, “I know this isn’t working anymore, but I already committed,” this conversation is for you.

Because here is the truth most of this industry avoids saying out loud:

Your loyalty belongs to your future self, not to your coach.

And staying in a container that stopped serving you months ago is not integrity. It is fear dressed up as responsibility.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The difference between loyalty and self-abandonment
– Why women stay in containers long after the growth stops
– How the sunken cost fallacy keeps you stuck
– Signs you’ve outgrown a coach, room, or program
– How to choose support aligned with your next-level self

Step Into the Room That Matches Your Future Self

If this episode has landed hard, take that seriously.

If you can feel that you have outgrown your current support, or you know your next level requires clearer strategy and stronger positioning, the Empire Expansion Event is where this conversation becomes practical.

This is not about blowing up your business or making emotional decisions.
It is about clarity, direction, and choosing the environment that actually supports where you are going next.

If you want your next move to be intentional, not reactive, this is the room.

Join the Empire Expansion Event

P.S. Loyalty to your future self requires honesty. Sometimes the bravest move is choosing a new room.

The loyalty trap no one warns you about

Over the past few months, I have heard the same sentence repeated in different ways.

“I want to work with you, but I’m already in another program.”
“My contract doesn’t end until March.”
“I feel bad leaving. I love my coach.”
“I should see it through.”

Every time someone says this, I feel it in my body. Because I have been that woman.

I have stayed in rooms longer than I should have. Not because the coach was bad. Not because the container was wrong. But because I did not want to be that client. The one who leaves early. The one who changes her mind. The one who looks flaky or disloyal.

So I stayed. Month after month. Call after call.

And my body knew long before my mind caught up.

I felt flat after sessions.
Confused instead of clarified.
Like I was shrinking my needs to fit the room instead of expanding into my next level.

That was the moment it clicked.

I was being more loyal to the container than to the woman I was becoming.

When loyalty turns into self-abandonment

Women are taught to keep commitments at all costs.

Finish what you start.
Do not question the expert.
Do not disappoint anyone.
Be grateful. Be easy. Be loyal.

All of that sounds virtuous, until it becomes self-abandonment.

Staying in support that no longer supports you is not loyalty. It is sacrifice.

And empire-building women do not grow by sacrificing themselves to old decisions.

The sunken cost fallacy, explained honestly

This is the part most people avoid naming.

“I’ve already invested so much.”
“Leaving now would make it a waste.”
“I should get every last drop out of this.”

Here is the hard truth.

The moment you realise a container no longer serves you, staying becomes the waste.

The money is already spent.
The decision now is about direction, not justification.

Staying does not honour your future. It protects your pride.

And I see women stay out of guilt far more often than they stay out of growth.

Coaching is a business relationship, not a marriage. You are not cheating on anyone by choosing a room that supports your next level.

You are allowed to outgrow people. Even good people.

Outgrowing a container does not make you disloyal

Sometimes the coach is lovely.
Sometimes the community is kind.
Sometimes the container was exactly what you needed.

For a season.

But seasons shift.

You can outgrow a methodology.
You can outgrow a pace.
You can outgrow a philosophy.
You can outgrow a room.

That is not betrayal. That is graduation.

And graduation is not disrespectful. It is evolution.

How to know when it’s time to move on

Your nervous system usually knows before your mind is ready to admit it.

Ask yourself honestly:

How do you feel when you get off calls?
Flat or expanded?
Activated or confused?

Are you hearing the same advice on repeat?
Does it feel generic or disconnected from your actual business?

Do you feel safe asking for support?
Are you making visible progress?

Are you shrinking to fit the room instead of rising to lead it?
Are you more excited by other conversations, other mentors, other directions?

If you are waiting it out instead of being activated, you are not growing. You are maintaining.

And maintenance is not why you invested.

Loyalty to your future self looks different

Picture the version of you stepping into 2026.

She has a self-sustaining email list.
Spacious visibility.
Recurring revenue.
Clear messaging.
Simple, strategic growth.

That woman does not stay in rooms out of obligation.

She chooses environments that expand her.
She is not loyal to past decisions. She is loyal to her direction.

When something stops supporting her trajectory, she pivots. Not out of disrespect, but out of self-respect

This is your permission slip

If this episode is hitting you in the gut, take it as a check-in.

Ask yourself:

Am I staying because this is aligned, or because leaving feels uncomfortable?
Am I honouring my expansion, or my guilt?

Your next level does not come from loyalty to the past.
It comes from courage in the present.

A note on choosing the right room

When I created Empress, I built it intentionally differently.

Not a passive mastermind.
Not a place where you disappear quietly.
Not a space where you hope your question gets picked.

It is co-creative, strategic, personalised, and intimate. Real progress. Real support. Real momentum.

Women do not join because they need another coach. They join because they need a partner. A strategist. Someone who can name the gaps clearly and walk with them.

Because the wrong room keeps you stagnant.
The right room can change everything.

Next Step: Get Clarity Before You Commit

If you are unsure whether your current support still fits, clarity comes first.

The Empire Expansion Event is designed to help you step back, look at the full picture, and get honest about what is actually going to move your business forward next.

It is not about leaving rooms impulsively.
It is not about chasing the next shiny thing.

It is about choosing your next move intentionally, with strategy, support, and space to think clearly.

Join the Empire Expansion Event

You are not meant to stay small to keep the peace. You are meant to grow with the right room behind you.

Feat. Madelyn Furlong

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 225

If there’s one thing I know to be true about running an online business, it’s this:
Your happiest customers are your strongest growth strategy.

Not the algorithm.
Not the trends.
Not throwing cash at ads.

It’s the people who’ve experienced you – your energy, your support, your magic – and can’t help but tell everyone they know.

In EP 225 of The Email Growth Show, I sat down with marketing strategist & website designer Madeline Furlong, and holy shit… this conversation is a masterclass in building a business where your people don’t just buy – they advocate.
They cheer.
They become your megaphone.

And here’s the best part?
You don’t need a giant team, a perfect memory, or endless hours to make it happen.

You just need three simple pillars.

Let’s break them down.

Listen to this episode here:

** Read time: 6 – 7 mins | Listen time: 31 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The 3-part framework that turns clients into loyal, vocal superfans
– How to create human-first connections even at scale
– Why storytelling is your most underrated customer connection tool
– Simple ways to go the extra mile without burning out
– How to weave genuine delight into your client experience
– The biggest mistakes biz owners make that block referrals

Let’s start with the truth…

People don’t remember the deliverables.
They remember how you made them feel.

Madeline shared a story from her early business days: she kept hiring the service providers who made her feel valued, remembered, and genuinely cared for, not the ones with the fanciest portfolios.

And your clients?
They’re the same.

They want to feel seen.
They want to feel important.
They want to feel like more than a transaction.

Which is exactly why Madeline built her framework around three pillars – ones you can apply immediately, no matter your niche or business stage.

Pillar 1: Organization
(AKA: Respecting your clients’ time + energy)

Madeline and I both admitted we’re obsessed with systems and for good reason.
Most people think “organization” is about color-coded folders or a perfect ClickUp setup.

Nope.

It’s about respect.

Being organized tells your clients:

  • “I’ve got you.”
  • “You’re safe here.”
  • “You don’t have to chase me for answers.”
  • “I’m paying attention.”

Even tiny systems create huge emotional impact.

Easy ways to build this in immediately:

  • Create a simple onboarding SOP
  • Use reminders (ClickUp, phone alarms, or even email snoozing like we talked about in the episode)
  • Let clients know when you’re away and when to expect replies
  • Build a predictable communication rhythm

Your organization becomes part of your brand promise – and people talk about it.

Pillar 2: Personalization
(AKA: The stuff AI can’t replicate)

This is the secret sauce.

Madeline told the story of her favourite businesses – the ones that remembered her kid’s name, checked in “just because,” or followed up weeks later about something small she’d mentioned in passing.

These gestures don’t require superhuman memory – they require a simple system + a human heart.

Easy personalization touchpoints:

  • A quick Loom video to wrap a project
  • Personal check-ins weeks after a service ends
  • Referencing something specific they told you
  • Sending a birthday card via an automated service (yes, she gave us that gem!)
  • Using someone’s name correctly (I double-checked her name before recording — and she felt that)

Online business often feels a little cold.
Personalization puts the warmth back.

Pillar 3: Going the Extra Mile

NOT:
Burning yourself out to over-deliver.

YES:
Adding intentional moments that feel special.

Madeline talked about the importance of being thoughtful, not excessive.

Sometimes it’s:

  • Noticing something on your client’s Instagram and offering a helpful tip
  • Checking in when you know they’re traveling
  • Adding a bonus resource because you saw they truly needed it
  • Or simply giving them a heads up when you’ll be replying slower (this was my fave example – it costs nothing, saves EVERYTHING).

Going the extra mile isn’t about doing more work…
It’s about creating more connection.

The Power of Storytelling (and why it turns customers into superfans)

THIS part of the conversation was gold.

Madeline shared a wild story about a tornado, her dad rappelling into a ravine to rescue a piece of their greenhouse, and how she tied it back to website strategy.

And guess what?
People ate it up.

Stories stick.
They humanize you.
They make people feel connected in ways no “value-packed tip carousel” ever could.

Your competitors can duplicate your offers.
They can duplicate your emails.
They can even use your damn fonts.

But they can’t duplicate your stories.

The Biggest Mistake Business Owners Make

Madeline named the elephant in the room:
Most businesses treat customers like checkboxes.

Deliverables? Done.
Contract? Done.
Offboarding? Done.

But no relationship.
No connection.
No loyalty.

Which means no referrals.

And she also pointed out the other big mistake:
Making yourself the hero of your marketing.
Your client is the hero. You are the guide.

(If everyone listening just fixed THAT… your conversions would skyrocket.)

Okay Kylie… But where do I start?

Madeline gave us three practical, zero-fluff steps:

1. Send an “I care about you” email to your list

Ask:
“What are you stuck on right now? What questions do you wish more people were answering?”

It starts conversations AND shows you’re human.

2. Choose ONE area of the framework to improve

Organization
Personalization
Or going the extra mile

Set a timer.
Make one % improvement.
Repeat weekly.

3. Build a referral system

Because when you do all the above?
People want to talk about you.

Reward that.

Let’s wrap this up in a bow…

Your customers become cheerleaders when you:

  • Respect them
  • See them
  • Delight them
  • Tell stories
  • And build small but meaningful touchpoints

This isn’t the sexy stuff – but holy shit, it works.

And if you’re ready to build an audience + customer base who rave about you without relying on social media?

You need to be at the Empire Expansion Event.

This is your roadmap to visibility that compounds, without content hamster-wheeling.
