content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 224

Have you ever looked ahead to a new year and thought, I know I want it to feel different… but how do I actually plan for that?

That’s exactly where I am right now.

So today, I’m taking you behind the scenes of how I’m planning 2026 in a way that honours my life, my energy, my family, and the empire I’m building.

This isn’t about creating a colour-coded planner that you abandon by February.

And it’s definitely not about pretending you’re going to wake up on January 1st with unlimited energy and a brand new personality.

This is about creating a year that actually holds you.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Life First, Business Second: Learn to map out personal priorities first, ensuring your business supports your lifestyle rather than the other way around.
– Leveraging Data & Reflections for Better Decisions: Understand how to use data from 2025 to inform your strategies and set goals.
– Crafting Revenue Goals with Flexibility: Set income targets without feeling locked in, leaving room for new opportunities and inspiration.
– Sync Your Life & Business Calendar: Find out how aligning your calendar with personal events and business goals prevents burnout and keeps motivation high.

Planning 2026 Without Burning Yourself Out

If this episode has you realising you want to grow in a way that actually fits your life, here’s how I can support you next:

👉 Book a Business Breakthrough Audit
If you want clarity on how to grow your business in 2026 without relying on big launches, constant output, or pushing past your capacity, this is your starting point. I’ll personally review your visibility, offer flow, and email ecosystem, then send you a simple 3-step action plan you can implement immediately – grounded in what you can realistically hold.

Why 2026 Needs to Be Planned Differently

The last year has changed me.

You’ve probably felt it in my content.
In my grounding.
In my clarity and confidence.

And because of that, 2026 cannot be planned the way I used to plan.

I don’t want a year that looks impressive on paper but feels exhausting to live inside.

I want a year that supports how I show up as a mother, a partner, a business owner, and a woman building something deeply intentional.

So here are the four steps I’m using to map the year ahead.

Step One Start With Your Life Not Your Business

This is the biggest shift I’ve made in how I plan.

I used to start with launches, revenue goals, and visibility plans, then try to squeeze my life into whatever space was left.

That’s how burnout happens.
That’s how resentment builds.
That’s how you end up feeling like an employee in your own business.

Now, the very first thing I do is open my calendar and block out what matters most.

School holidays.
Family commitments.
Travel.
Downtime.

I plan around seasons of high energy and seasons where I need more rest.

I don’t stack launches in school holiday chaos.
I don’t overload January after a big December.
And I build recovery time around my Empire Expansion Events because guiding dozens of women through deep work deserves space afterwards.

Life is not an afterthought.
It’s the foundation.

Step Two Review the Past Year With Honesty Not Judgment

Before I plan forward, I always look back.

Not through the lens of what I did wrong, but through compassion and curiosity.

I scroll my camera roll.
I review my email list growth month by month.
I reflect on when I felt alive and when I felt stretched too thin.

I look at:

  • What worked easily
  • Where I pushed too hard
  • Where things felt aligned
  • Where they quietly didn’t

This kind of reflection gives you data you can’t get anywhere else.

It shows you patterns.

And once you can see the patterns, you can plan with far more clarity.

Step Three Build Revenue Around Your Actual Capacity

This one matters more than most people realise.

I am no longer willing to build a business that demands more than I can realistically give.

Before I map revenue goals or projections, I ask one simple question.

What do I actually have capacity for?

Not the fantasy version of me.
Not the hyper-optimistic January version of me.
The real version of me.

The mum.
The partner.
The woman running a household and supporting clients deeply.

Once I’m honest about capacity, I can build revenue plans that feel grounded instead of stressful.

This is how sustainable scaling happens.

Not by forcing more.

By creating smarter.

Step Four Map the Year With Flexibility

Once I have my life in the calendar, I’ve reflected on the past year, and I understand my capacity, I start sketching the structure of the year ahead.

Not rigid plans.

Architecture.

Launch seasons.
Event seasons.
Evergreen focus.
Quiet creation time.
Rest and recovery windows.

Every plan must include room for being human.

White space matters.
Flexibility matters.
Permission to change matters.

This isn’t about getting it perfect.
It’s about creating a structure that supports you instead of squeezing you.

And when your year supports you, everything else changes.

Your content lands deeper.
Your offers feel easier.
Your confidence expands.
Your business grows.

You Get to Plan Your Year On Purpose

As you start thinking about 2026, I want you to know this.

You don’t need to rush.
You don’t need a perfect planner.
You don’t need unrealistic expectations.

You get to build a year that honours your energy, your life, and the woman you’re becoming.

And that is powerful.

Your Next Step

If, as you’re mapping out 2026, you realise you want clarity, perspective, or support holding the big picture of your business, this is exactly what my Business Breakthrough Audit is designed for.

We’ll look at your visibility, list growth, and offers through the lens of the empire you’re building.

Book a Business Breakthrough Audit and create a 2026 plan that actually fits your life.

P.S. You don’t need a more disciplined plan. You need one that supports you on your hardest days as well as your best ones.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 223

I didn’t see this one coming.

A few months ago, I launched a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit. It was meant to be simple. Low pressure. A quick, personalised video to help women get unstuck.

Nothing fancy.
No funnel wizardry.
No grand expectations.

And then my inbox started blowing up.

One woman told me she got more clarity from this $44 audit than she did from a $5,000 mastermind.

At first, I honestly didn’t believe her. I thought she was just being kind.

Then I heard it again.
And again.
From different women, in completely different businesses.

And that’s when I realised this conversation wasn’t actually about the audit.

It was about clarity.
Connection.
And what really creates transformation.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why clarity often beats complexity (and what “big programs” tend to miss)
– How intimacy and attention create real transformation, not just more information
– What these $44 audits have taught me about leadership, generosity, and depth
– Why sometimes the simplest offer you create ends up being your most powerful one

Sometimes It’s Not More Strategy

Sometimes the shift you need doesn’t come from more content or a bigger room.
It comes from being seen.

If you want personalised clarity on what’s actually holding your business back, you can start with a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit.

How Something Small Became So Powerful

These audits started as a side offer.

Something I could do between bigger projects.
Something personal.
Something genuinely helpful.

Inside each audit, I look at three things:

  • Visibility
  • Email list growth
  • Offers

Women answer a few questions, then I go behind the scenes and record a private Loom video pulling their business apart with fresh eyes.

No templates.
No checklists.
No generic advice.

Just me, talking directly to her.

The videos usually run 20 to 30 minutes, and they’re deeply personal. I’m not speaking to an “ideal client avatar.” I’m speaking to one woman, exactly where she is.

And that intimacy changes everything.

Why Clarity Hits Harder Than Content

One woman told me she watched her audit twice and planned to watch it again.

Another said it was worth ten times the price.

Another, who had been in multiple masterminds, told me that one video gave her more clarity than six months of group coaching.

That stopped me in my tracks.

Because if that’s true, then maybe we’ve misunderstood where transformation actually comes from.

It doesn’t always come from access.
Or proximity.
Or volume.

Sometimes it comes from precision.

From being met exactly where you are by someone who is actually paying attention.

What We Lose As Things Get Bigger

As businesses scale, we automate.
We systemise.
We template.

And listen, I love a good system.

But no system can replace being seen.

When I record these audits, I’m not thinking about selling anything else. I’m thinking about helping someone see their business clearly.

Where they’re blocked.
Where they’re brilliant.
Where they’re playing smaller than they realise.

That moment of clarity is what creates the shift.

Not a perfect strategy.
Not another framework.

Clarity hands people their power back.

The Truth About Masterminds and Big Rooms

I’ve been on the other side too.

I’ve paid for masterminds that were beautifully run, full of smart women, with great content.

And still felt unseen.

Not because the coach wasn’t good.
But because the support wasn’t specific.

It was for the room.
Not for me.

And that’s not wrong. That’s just how group spaces work.

But growth doesn’t always happen in big rooms.

Sometimes it happens in quiet corners.
In one conversation.
In one reflection that cracks something open.

Why These Audits Work So Well

These $44 audits were never designed to make money.

They were designed to build trust.

Ironically, they ended up doing both.

Because when you genuinely help someone with no agenda, they remember. They come back. They tell their friends.

Not because you nurtured them through a funnel.
But because you actually gave a shit.

Many of these women have gone on to work with me in deeper ways. Not because I pushed them there, but because they felt seen.

That’s what builds real loyalty.

The Bigger Lesson Here

These audits have changed me.

They’ve reminded me why I started doing this work in the first place.

Not to be the biggest.
Not to be the flashiest.

But to be the most human.

Sometimes the thing holding someone back isn’t strategy.

It’s noise.
Distraction.
Too many voices.

And all they need is one clear mirror.

A Question For You

Where might you be overcomplicating things?

Where are you chasing bigger when your audience actually wants deeper?

Your next big win might not come from another launch, course, or funnel.

It might come from one small, potent offer.
The thing that feels obvious to you.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 222

You don’t need a bigger list.
You need a deeper one.

And that truth hit me in the most human, grounding, holy-shit-this-is-why-I-do-this way when I hosted a networking mixer last month = just for my email list.

No ads.
No big launch energy.
No growth objective.

Just… connection.

There were women who’d joined my world days earlier. Others who’d been opening my emails for two years. Different countries. Different businesses. Different stages.

But the energy in that Zoom room?

Instant connection.
Real conversation.
Momentum – without thousands of people.

And it reminded me of something we don’t hear enough in online business…

Reach without relationships means nothing.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why list size doesn’t equal momentum
– The real difference between a “big” list and a “deep” one
– How trust and connection impact sales more than reach
– The three foundations of a deeper email list
– Simple ways to turn subscribers into a real community

Ready to grow without the hustle?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – If you want a simple, sustainable plan for growing your business without relying on big sales weekends, book a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit. I’ll personally review your visibility, offer flow, and list strategy – and send you a 3-step action plan you can implement right away.

The lie we’ve all been sold: bigger is better

For years, I chased numbers.

I genuinely believed that once I hit a certain list size – 5k, 10k, that magic number – everything would click. More sales. More ease. More authority.

But I’ve seen behind the curtain.

I’ve watched business owners with massive lists struggle to convert a damn thing.
And I’ve watched women with 300 subscribers sell out offers effortlessly.
The difference isn’t volume.

It’s vibe.
It’s trust.
It’s connection.

Because if your list doesn’t know you…
If they don’t feel seen…
Adding more people just multiplies the disconnection.

What a “deeper list” actually looks like

That mixer? It wasn’t flashy.
About 50 people registered.
35 showed up live.

But something shifted within the first 90 seconds.

I asked everyone to drop two words in the chat describing how they felt.
Excited.
Grateful.
Tired but happy to be here.
Curious.
Inspired.

Women were showing up between school drop-offs, client calls, dinner prep – and they were present.

Then the walls came down.

The chat turned into:
– “Let’s collaborate.”
– “Email me.”
– “I need you on my podcast.”

I didn’t orchestrate it.
I didn’t force it.
I just held the space.

And by the end, the DMs rolled in:

“The energy was so genuine.”
“The conversations felt real.”
“You’ve built something really special here.”

That’s a deeper list.

Not giant.
Not loud.
But connected.

Why i’d rather build braver rooms than bigger ones

That experience reminded me why I don’t want massive, anonymous audiences.
I want braver rooms.

It’s why everything I host – from Empire Mixers to my Empire Expansion Events – is intentionally intimate, curated, and personal. Because when the right people are in the room, something f*cking powerful happens.

Women stop performing.
They stop posturing.
They start connecting.

And your email list can feel like that too.
It doesn’t have to be transactional.
It can be relational.

A place where people don’t just consume – they contribute.

How to build a deeper email list [without more hustle]

A deeper list is built on three things:

1. Personalisation

Write like you’re talking to one person.
Not an audience.
Not “hey everyone”.

One human – like a voice note to your biz bestie.
That’s where connection starts.

2. Consistency [Not Perfection]

Depth grows from rhythm – not rigid schedules.
You don’t need polished essays.
You don’t need perfect timing.

You just need presence.

A question.
A quick update.
Two honest lines.

Relationships don’t grow in silence.

3. Reciprocity

Invite replies.
Ask questions.
Celebrate your people.

A deeper list isn’t passive – it talks back.

And that’s when everything shifts.

What changes when you choose depth over width

You stop hustling for strangers.
You start nurturing people who already raised their hand.

Launches feel easier.
Sales feel cleaner.
Your inbox fills with real conversations, not just automation notifications.

And honestly?
Your business starts to feel good again.

No more performing.
No more chasing virality.
Just serving the humans who chose you.

Your next step

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 220

Black Friday isn’t the business lifeline so many make it out to be. It won’t magically fix low sales, messy positioning, or a cold email list. What it will do is amplify whatever foundation you already have – good or bad.

In this episode, I break down why chasing quick cash through discounts rarely works long-term, and what to focus on instead if you want to see real, sustainable growth.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why discounting isn’t the shortcut you think it is
– The three real reasons your Black Friday sale isn’t converting
– How to know if you have a volume or messaging problem
– The 3 ways to approach Black Friday: Lead, Nurture, or Sell

Ready to grow without the hustle?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – If you want a simple, sustainable plan for growing your business without relying on big sales weekends, book a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit. I’ll personally review your visibility, offer flow, and list strategy – and send you a 3-step action plan you can implement right away.

The illusion of the “Big Weekend”?

Every year, we’re bombarded with the same noise – endless countdowns, flashing banners, “biggest deal ever” emails. And it’s tempting, right? It feels like if you don’t join in, you’ll miss the moment, lose momentum, or look like you’re “not doing enough.”

But here’s the truth: Black Friday is not a strategy. It’s a magnifying glass. It doesn’t create success; it exposes it.

If your messaging isn’t clear, if your audience isn’t nurtured, if your offer doesn’t resonate – no amount of discounting will change that. You might get a few sales, sure, but they’ll be driven by urgency, not loyalty. And urgency fades fast.

Why the hype doesn’t translate to conversions

When you build your offers or your marketing around trends instead of strategy, you attract the wrong kind of buyer – the kind who only shows up for a discount.

If your list has gone cold or your audience barely knows what you offer, throwing out a flash sale doesn’t warm them up; it just confuses them. They might click, but they won’t convert.

That’s because Black Friday isn’t about “more eyeballs.” It’s about readiness – your readiness and their readiness. When either side is missing, the sale falls flat.

The Shift: From panic to purpose

Instead of asking, “What should I discount?”, the better question is, “What’s my goal right now?”

Maybe you don’t need a sale at all. Maybe you need more people discovering your world – that’s a lead season. Maybe you’ve got an audience who knows you but isn’t quite ready to buy – that’s a nurture season. Or maybe your people are already primed, warmed, and ready – that’s when a sales season actually works.

Trying to sell in a nurture season feels like shouting into the void.
Trying to grow your list in a sell season wastes momentum.

The magic happens when you align your goals with where your people actually are.

What to do instead

Here’s the honest truth: strategy will always beat spontaneity.

If you’re going to take part in Black Friday at all, do it with intention. Use it as a time to clarify your message, showcase your best offer, and strengthen your audience relationships.

That might look like offering a “value boost” instead of a discount – adding a bonus, giving early access, or rewarding loyalty. It might look like using the season to nurture your list – sending helpful, story-led emails instead of sales pitches. Or it might look like skipping it altogether and focusing on what’s next – your 2026 plan, your evergreen funnel, your long game.

When your positioning is clear and your offer aligned, you don’t need to scream for attention.
People already trust you.

The deeper lesson…

Black Friday reveals how well your business is built. If your foundation is shaky, it’ll crumble under pressure. If it’s solid – if your audience trusts you, if your systems are strong, if your message is clear – then every promotion (holiday or not) becomes easier.

You don’t need to chase every marketing moment to grow. You just need to know who you are, what you stand for, and how to communicate that consistently, not just when everyone else is shouting.

Because the truth is, sustainable businesses aren’t built in one weekend.

They’re built over months and years of clarity, consistency, and connection.

If you’re tired of throwing discounts into the void and hoping something sticks, maybe it’s time to step back and look at your bigger picture.

Your next sale doesn’t need to be louder – it needs to be clearer.

And when you approach seasons like Black Friday with calm, strategy, and alignment instead of panic and pressure, that’s when your business really starts to grow.

Your next step

Your next level of growth isn’t hiding in another discount weekend – it’s in clarity.
My Business Breakthrough audit is your personalised roadmap to more sales, visibility, and momentum – without the hustle or burnout.

Let’s turn your next move into your best move.

Feat. Laura Kendrick from Cheeky Copy

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 221

Your website shouldn’t just exist to prove you’re in business – it should actively grow your business.

If you’ve ever wondered why your site looks good but doesn’t convert, this episode of The Email Growth Show will change the way you think about website strategy forever.

I sat down with Laura Kendrick, a UX copywriter and strategist who helps high-performing founders turn their websites into conversion machines. We talked about the small tweaks that make a big difference – from simplifying your calls-to-action to designing your homepage for cold traffic – and how clarity in your copy always beats cleverness.

Listen to this episode here:

** Read time: 6 – 7 mins | Listen time: 40 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why your homepage needs to speak to cold traffic
– How to remove friction from your sales pages
– The difference between clear and clever copy
– And how to create a seamless journey that moves people from curious to converted…

The website problem no one talks about

Here’s what most entrepreneurs do:

They spend hours perfecting their color palette, tweaking their fonts, and writing clever headlines that sound good… but don’t actually sell.

Then they wonder why their site looks amazing but still feels like a digital business card – a static space that says “I exist” instead of “Here’s how I can help you.”

Laura calls this the “hang your shingle” mentality – that old-school idea of putting up a sign to prove you’re open for business.

And while it might make your business feel legitimate, it doesn’t bring in clients.

Your website should be more than a badge of credibility. It should be your hardest-working salesperson – guiding visitors from curiosity to clarity to conversion.

How to make your website work for you

According to Laura, the first step is understanding that not everyone who lands on your site knows who you are. Even if your warmest leads come from your podcast, email list, or bundles – your website still needs to speak to cold traffic.

That means when a total stranger finds you on Google, your homepage should immediately answer three things:

  • Who you help
  • What you do
  • Why it matters

That first section of your homepage – known as “above the fold” – is your first impression. It’s where people decide if they’re in the right place.

Once they scroll, you can speak to the warmer leads – the ones who are already curious or ready to buy. Give them a clear next step, a reason to keep going, and an obvious path forward.

Your website isn’t a one-way announcement – it’s a conversation.

Clear over clever: The copy rule that changes everything

One of Laura’s mantras?
“Clear over clever, every time.”

It’s easy to fall in love with creative taglines or branded phrases (we all do it), but if your audience has to stop and think about what you mean – you’ve lost them.

People don’t have the context you do. They don’t know your backstory, your offer names, or your inside jokes.

So instead of relying on witty wordplay, make it clear what each offer actually is.

If you have multiple offers – like a mastermind, a membership, and a self-paced course – make sure those are labeled clearly. Use drop-downs, tabs, or buttons that say exactly what people can expect.

It’s not about stripping away your personality. It’s about making sure your brilliance is accessible.

Because clever might catch attention – but clarity converts.

Remove the friction…

Let’s talk about what really stops people from buying: friction.

Every extra click, every confusing button, every unnecessary step adds resistance between your audience and a sale.

If someone has to click five times before they reach your checkout, you’ve probably lost them by click three.

Laura’s rule? One clear call-to-action. One button. One goal.

If they’re on a sales page, the only job of that page is to sell that offer.
No distractions. No shiny links to blog posts or free resources.

Remove your navigation bar, skip the footer links, and get rid of your social icons. The more you keep them focused, the easier it is for them to say yes.

And if you’re using a platform like ThriveCart, keep your checkout simple.
It should look and feel like an extension of your sales page, not a completely new space. The fonts, colors, and copy should all match.

Every extra click costs conversions – and your goal is to make buying feel effortless.

Why this matters

When your website is strategic and clear, it doesn’t just “look legit.”

It:

  • Converts visitors into clients 24/7
  • Builds trust through consistency
  • Reflects your growth and authority
  • Frees up your time to focus on the work that lights you up

You don’t need to post more, shout louder, or add another platform.
You just need to make sure the home base of your business – your website – is working for you.

Because when your copy is clear and your strategy is strong, sales start to feel effortless.

Ready to grow without guessing?

I’ll personally review your visibility, offers, and email strategy, then send you a private video with a 3-step action plan to help you grow without burnout.

It’s not always possible, and that’s fine. But in an ideal world, it’s right there. So they’re just like, go. And that one button push is the one that’s confirming their credit card information or confirming that they want to put in the application with you.

Kylie Kelly [00:18:01]:
Mm. And so I’m just thinking about this with my own website now. So with my sales pages on Showit and I have my ThriveCart checkouts I could easily embed. I’ve never thought to do that. It’s almost like the ThriveCart is like a mini sales page that they’re reading the same information again. Right. Fiction. I can see that now is friction.

Kylie Kelly [00:18:17]:
So, like, way better to embed the checkout in the actual sales page. Oh, interesting.

Laura Kendrick [00:18:22]:
But if you can’t do that, which you can’t always do, that not all platforms will let you do that. And that’s okay if you can’t do that. One of the like key things is to make sure they look the same so that they know like the verbiage is the same, the colors are the same, the fonts are the same, the basics there are the same so that they know they actually went like it. It feels seamless. It feels like oh, I’m in the right place. It’s that kind of that well known like pat on the shoulder of like yes, you did this correctly. And we want to keep them moving so making that as easy. So having like if you go from a full on sales page to like Yeah, I have ThriveCart too and you can create a whole sales page in there too.

Laura Kendrick [00:19:05]:
Don’t do that. If you have a full sales page on your website, don’t click them over to another full sales page where they have to scroll again because that is friction. So yes, ideally it is in the website if possible. But if not, if you have to have a button and you have the sales page on your website, you want them to go to the a simple version of the checkout and it doesn’t ha like it can have some copy on it, it can have the bullets of like just a reminder refresher of this is what you’re getting, this is what you’re signing into. Here’s another little testimonial but have it like you know, be off to the side or you know what I mean, like just a little bit versus having to scroll through a massive thing to get to the bottom again because that’s going to, that’s going to turn people off.

Kylie Kelly [00:19:50]:
And this is good news because really when we think about it, we’re doing twice as much work building out that second thing in thriveguard when we actually don’t need to. That’s really exciting. Talk to me about call to action buttons because when you were saying that I was like, oh my gosh, I’m so guilty of this because I’ll have like by now 300 times on a page and it’s like anchored down to like different places instead of it being to the checkout to buy now. So like what should somebody do best practice with call to action buttons.

Laura Kendrick [00:20:17]:
I mean if you’re getting into a sales page, there should only ever be one call to action on sales page ever. And that is Buy Now. Like there should not be a like in the middle of the sales page. We’ll sign up for this lead magnet. Your sales page is at the Very end of your sales funnel. These people know who you are. They are warmed up. If they’ve clicked in, they are interested.

Laura Kendrick [00:20:35]:
They are just deciding whether or not now is the time or not, whether or not this is the offer or not. They don’t need anything else other than to land into this one single offer. Do not take them anywhere else. Remove the header, the footer. Get rid of your social links. You don’t want them going to your social media when they are, like, on that final step. Like, oh, my God, no, there should. And also there should not be like a highlighted space for like, SEO purposes where you’re sending them to a blog post to.

Laura Kendrick [00:21:04]:
For them to understand what this word means. They’re in your world. They’re at the end of the funnel. They should know what that word means. And if they don’t, they will Google it on their own. Don’t do that. One call to action only on a sales page. And it should be to the checkout or apply or whatever that endpoint is.

Laura Kendrick [00:21:20]:
Yes, you can have. Some websites will enable you to have, you know, 50 buttons and only one price. That stack, which, if you’re unfamiliar, the price stack is the space where you’re saying, this is how much it is. Let’s go. You can have every single button go to that anchor point and I’m sure you’ve seen it. If you don’t have it on your own, where you click the button at the very top and it just zips down to the bottom to that price tag and says, here’s how much it is. That’s great. If you can do that, do that.

Laura Kendrick [00:21:50]:
If you can’t do that, have every button go to the checkout. And if you can anchor to that one spot, then every button on the page that feels relevant goes to that anchor point. And then that one button goes to the checkout or the checkout is embedded right there. And the copy on those buttons can and really should vary, but they should all be clear. They should all say what is like, in some way, what they can expect to happen next. And like, yes, they don’t all have to be so clear that it’s like, purchase here, buy now. Like, those can be used. But it.

Laura Kendrick [00:22:27]:
They can say things of, I don’t know. For me, it could be off the top of my head. It could be something like, I want better copy or I want my sales page to convert or I want my website to convert. Those could be. That’s copy. That’s clear. Honestly, I would take away the. Some of the that verbiage to make it shorter.

Laura Kendrick [00:22:43]:
But that is also clear they know what’s going to happen next. And it, it’s not something that’s like, like trying to think of really bad call to action copy and it’s not coming to my mind of like, I don’t know, something of like. And my daughter just popped into my head of like sales pages are like princesses, you know, like what? Nobody’s going to know what that means and nobody’s going to click that button. Or if they do, it’s out of morbid curiosity of like, what happens when I do this. Making sure that they’re all clear, making sure it does exactly what it says it’s going to do. And you can even create what we call in the UX world microcopy and put it underneath the.

Kylie Kelly [00:23:17]:
The button.

Laura Kendrick [00:23:18]:
Small little sentence that is very clear on what’s going to happen in the next step and that immensely clarifies for people and makes it. That removes actually a ton of friction because one of the reasons people won’t do the things is because they’re not sure what’s going to happen when they do.

Kylie Kelly [00:23:34]:
Oh my God, so much, so much good stuff there. I love that. Thank you. Okay, so let’s think about the call to action buttons on let’s say the homepage. Right? Let’s go back to websites away from sales pages. I could talk to you about sales pages until I’m blowing the face back to the website. How do we figure out that journey? So, like thinking about the homepage, putting ourselves into the customer’s state of mind when they’re landing on our homepage, how do we figure this out? How do we know where they should go? When should they go to the about page? When should they go to the services page? Like what, what’s that look like?

Laura Kendrick [00:24:04]:
Honestly, it’s in having clarity on those things, which is, you know, clarity compass. Yay. Thought about that.

Kylie Kelly [00:24:10]:
Well, got something for you.

Laura Kendrick [00:24:13]:
Yeah, right. Ding, ding, ding. No, but it is about having. No, having a really clear understanding of who your audience is, what you want them to do, what their pain points are like once you have your messaging dialed in, your brand voice dialed in, your voice of customer dialed in. These things make it so this journey is really easy because you understand who it is that you’re calling in, you understand what they need to hear and you also, if your messaging is really dialed in, you also know where they are on their awareness journey, when they’re clicking in the page. And yes, we put elements in for that Cold audience who happens to just stumble upon it because, I don’t know, they mistyped something. But in doing that, like, we want to be crystal clear on what we do and who we do it for. And in a way that is not about you, it’s not stroking your ego.

Laura Kendrick [00:25:04]:
It’s not making an offer with the things of like, well, when you get into this offer, you get 1, 2 and 3. Like, you get this many calls, you get this, this and this. And people do want to know that, usually right at the bitter end of their buying decision. But first they want to know that they’re in the right place. They want to know that this person gets them. They want to know their pain is seen and understood and that their goals and desires are like, that’s what this person is aimed at. Because there are a hundred percent people out in the world who are looking for somebody who can just write a piece of button copy without any thought. That just makes it clever and funny.

Laura Kendrick [00:25:51]:
And like is on brand. Great. I’m not their copywriter. The person who is like, I want this to hum. Like, I want to not have to think about this. I want this to be a strategy. I want these conversions to happen. And not like, I don’t want it piecemealed anymore.

Laura Kendrick [00:26:07]:
I don’t want it stitched together, duct taped together. Like, I want a whole picture that makes sense for me. My business, that’s me. They’re in the right place and my website will tell them that.

Kylie Kelly [00:26:19]:
I love that advice. And I think again, the clearer we can get about who we’re trying to serve, and we’ve talked about this before, but like that evolves too. So I’m guessing as that evolves, it’s updating the copy. Right. It’s not this one and done type thing. It’s going to be a living, breathing part of your business, right?

Laura Kendrick [00:26:34]:
Yeah. And it doesn’t, it doesn’t have to be totally rewritten without, you know, it doesn’t have to be this big whitewashed thing of like, oh, I need a totally new website. Sure, every once in a while that’s fun. Or your offers change so much or you’re like, I just need a different vibe in those moments. Yeah, it might need a total rewrite, but sometimes it’s just a tweak. It might even be as simple as like a little bit of a headline shift or just a little bit of like the pain point that we’re really dialed into here is no longer the right one. For instance, I actually, this is something that I Totally. Just repackaged.

Laura Kendrick [00:27:11]:
One of the first VIP days I ever came out with was a messaging VIP day. And the way I was talking about it, I realized was calling in very new business owners, which was super fun and I really enjoyed working with them. But also the funnel to from that to done for you copy was going to be years, which was not ideal for me in my business, and also who I wanted to work with. I was stepping into this holistic space, which is a totally different group of people than new people are just trying to get their footing. When you’re starting to think in strategy, you’re starting to talk further down the line. And so I had abandoned this VIP day almost entirely and just had whipped it out for clients who I was already working with, who I felt it would really help. And it was super fun. But now I’ve shifted it into this package with something else with other things involved.

Laura Kendrick [00:28:07]:
And it’s in essence, the same thing, but it’s been packaged with all these other things. And I’m talking about it in a very different way. It’s the same offer, but it’s being spoken of in a way that actually resonates with my ideal client now and not necessarily somebody who just bought that domain or hasn’t even bought that domain and has just started an Instagram account and is just trying to figure out what do I really want to do. This is not necessarily the right offer for them.

Kylie Kelly [00:28:37]:
Yeah. And that just goes to the power of the messaging and knowing your ideal client. Right. And the tweaks you might need to make along that journey. I love that. Do you know something funny? So I have Hot Jar set up for my website. I love. I’m a nerd.

Kylie Kelly [00:28:49]:
I love data. I love heat tracking. I want to see where those people are clicking. I want to see what’s happening. Like, I’ll sit there with a cup of coffee and watch those replays for, like, way too long. That I should admit. But do you know what’s funny? Is that often I’m like, what the.

Laura Kendrick [00:29:01]:
What the.

Kylie Kelly [00:29:02]:
Do I do with this information now? I’ve been watching this. I see where they’re clicking, I see where they’re dropping off, but I don’t know what to do with that information. Is that when we should come to someone like you, like, what do we do with that then? Like, how do we figure this out?

Laura Kendrick [00:29:16]:
That is such good information to have. And even the clients I have that don’t have those things in place, we put them into place. We. We create dashboards. We put Hotjar into place because we want to see it afterwards. Because there is always, no matter where you are in your business, there is always an element of, in the common vernacular, throwing spaghetti at the wall. In the copy UX and strategy world, we like to refine or call it AB testing, but it is, there’s always an element of play because that’s what it is. And you are experimenting and seeing what lands.

Laura Kendrick [00:29:52]:
And that’s how you can tell. Oh, first of all, you can tell is the thing landing in general. You can also tell how, like, what kind of buyer type you have. You can also tell where are they on their awareness journey. Because if you have, if everybody who comes to your website is clicking that like, you know, headlined button and actually converting, it’s like, oh, damn, they don’t need a whole lot. Like, what I’m doing elsewhere is closing this gap and they don’t need much. Or I have a lot of people who are like really quick decision makers. So maybe the copy on your website can be diminished or your sales page can be very much simplified because you don’t have the people who need all the information.

Laura Kendrick [00:30:33]:
I don’t know, like, we would have to look at all that information, but it can also be an element of like, well, that really didn’t land with them. So like, that’s a, that’s a dead zone over there. So maybe we need to either shift it, play with the messaging or maybe retire the offer. I don’t know the answer there either, but we would have to look at it and kind of assess it against who your audience is. But yes, that is when you are at the point where you are interested in data or at least have the like, red flags of like, I should be interested in data or looking at my data. That’s a point where it’s like, okay, now it’s time to bring in somebody who really understands the strategy here to help me game plan this and figure out how can we tip the scales. Because before that you’re probably still in a fairly significant like feeling it out phase and we all have to move through that. To be fair, we never fully move out of it, but we have to move through the like, hardcore.

Laura Kendrick [00:31:37]:
I mean, we’re just taking the colander of spaghetti and like chucking it all at the wall and going, what’s working? And then getting into the like, okay, I saw those two pieces stuck. So now we’re dealing with the details of like, how can I make them stick longer? And you know, and you’re starting to pull play in that nuance and the kind of minutiae of it all. And once you’re getting into that, like, you have this offer that is. And I kind of hate the. The terminology, but you have a proven offer and you’re feeling good about your audience and you’re. You’re really understanding them, that’s the time to really start to dial this in. Because that’s when your website should really and truly no longer be the thing that’s like, look, I have pretty pictures of myself. And yes, I’m for real.

Laura Kendrick [00:32:22]:
And sure, Google knows who I am, but the only way people really convert is when I’m in a launch cycle or I actively tell them, you must buy now. Like, your website can very easily be working literally while you’re sleeping behind the scenes. Like, in your case, Kylie, being in Australia, like, a huge chunk of your audience is in North America, and it’s like, your website should actively be selling while you’re sleeping.

Kylie Kelly [00:32:48]:
It’s so funny. Like, I always used to think that was bullshit. When people talk about, like, oh, I was in the Bahama is having a pina colada and I just made this much money and I was like, oh, whatever. Like, what a work. But part of that, when you do have things like your website, like your email list, when you’ve built up that audience, when you have evergreen offers, like, there is this part in business that actually gets to be easy. And I love the fact that you said about throwing spaghetti at the wall and then you caught a play, and I was like, yes, because it’s not a bad thing. It is a stage that everyone goes through. And a lot of people, I hear like, oh, I don’t want to just throw spaghetti at the wall.

Kylie Kelly [00:33:20]:
I’m like, why not have a. Have a fucking food fight? Like, it’s fun. Like, throw it out. What happens? And that’s how we figure it out, right?

Laura Kendrick [00:33:26]:
Like, it really doesn’t go away because, like, here’s the thing. I decided first that I wanted to work with a different clientele. Like, I wanted it to shift because I wanted to work more deeply with my clients. So I didn’t want to have to, you know, for financial reasons and energy reasons. I didn’t want to have to work with 50 clients in a month because that means no client can have my full attention. I can’t do a deep dive. I’m stressed about client acquisition, money, all the things, and it’s like, I don’t want to be there. I love deep diving.

Laura Kendrick [00:33:59]:
I love looking at the strategy, at the numbers at the words, at the messaging. That’s where I live and thrive and I love deep long term relationships. Like I am that person who I don’t want to go to dinner with 50 people and have a whole lot of small talk. I want to go to dinner with one person and like, understand your backstory, the intimate details of your relationship with your partner and like how you parent and you know, what’s your blood type? Like that’s where I live and love. And so in order to do that I have to shift my packaging. And so I understood that first. I understand because I’m not fully there in, in this particular moment. I understand the long term goal and where I want to live and also understand that that may shift because I may get feedback that’s like, maybe I don’t like that client in the long run, but I understand where I’m headed.

Laura Kendrick [00:34:53]:
And with that, now I’m playing like I repackaged the VIP day and the offers into a different framework and into not a framework into a different package and a different offer with different messaging aimed at different people’s issues, problems, pain points, goals, where they are. And that’s resonating with people and that is aiming at this space. So like I started in one space, but to be quite honest with you, that offer pack like set up may last, it may not, I don’t know. And so I’m still playing with this. Like I have my North Star and I’m aiming there, but within this, like, I know who I’m talking to, I know what I want, I know how I want to work with people. Now I’m playing within that space rather than I want to write copy for people. And I have no idea what that looks like or who that is or what I’m going to specialize in. And like, like, let’s just see what I like to do.

Laura Kendrick [00:35:48]:
That phase I moved out of and moved into the, like, these are the things that call my name. This is where I want to live. Now let’s play in the how do we get the right thing, to work with the right people in the right way. That feels good for me and my people.

Kylie Kelly [00:36:01]:
Yeah, I love that. And I think then when we are open to play in those different parts of our business, as that journey kind of continues, when we know that that’s part of how we get to do business, that is the way that we get there is by playing, is by testing, trying new things. It just takes the pressure off that one fucking thing working right, like, because then we can throw something out there and be like, oh, well, that didn’t land. Okay, let’s do something else. Like, I think so often, especially when people are new to business or perhaps perfectionists, perhaps, whatever the thing is, like, there’s so much pressure for that one thing to work and then it doesn’t work and then it’s a complete mind, right? So I think knowing that, like, okay, we get to play, some things won’t work, some things will. We might not even like it when we get there, who knows? But let’s play and have fun and try and figure this out. And I think that’s why I like business so much, is because I love the puzzle. I love the puzzle pieces.

Kylie Kelly [00:36:51]:
I love not seeing the COVID but trying to figure out where the fuck they go. Like, I love that. So, yeah, I love that you shared this because I think it just gives all of our listeners some permission to play, which is so important.

Laura Kendrick [00:37:02]:
Permission to abandon a piece of the play if it doesn’t work for you. Like, I think that sometimes there’s too much pressure put on. Is the income coming in, is the, like, is this landing with the clients? And like, yes, that stuff is important. We can’t, you know, eat hopes and dreams. But even if you find something that really works for a while and if it stops feeding your soul permission to play and shift in a different direction and be like, not my thing anymore and let it go. Because I think that’s an important facet of all of this too, that we’re sometimes so focused on the client, which we should be. But there also has to be an element of like, what about your energy? What about your output? What about where your heart sings and living in that space too, because that’s where this becomes amazing, is where that Venn diagram crosses of where you are in your full joy and your clients are sitting here going, yes, I need more of this in my life, so stay in that space.

Kylie Kelly [00:38:02]:
Yes, yes. I mean, I think I’m a pretty good example of that. Like, I pivot. I pivot a lot. And you know, I to it like with the membership, I built it up to be this incredible, you know, I had 240 members at some point and then I started to resent it because I was on Zoom all the time and I didn’t have capacity and I couldn’t go deep and I was giving support, but it was a pretty light surface of support for that many people and I didn’t want to build a team. So it’s like also having that bravery, I guess, to be able to be like, ah, this isn’t working anymore. I’m choosing to do something different and then going after that. Right?

Laura Kendrick [00:38:38]:
Yeah. Permission to burn the fucker down when you’re done.

Kylie Kelly [00:38:41]:
I love that. Oh my gosh, Lauren, this has been so good. Thank you so much for sharing so much with us. I have loved this conversation. I know our listeners would too. Can you please share with us again that URL for the Clarity Compass?

Laura Kendrick [00:38:53]:
Yes, it is cheeky copy. Co Clarity dash compass.

Kylie Kelly [00:38:59]:
Amazing. I will put the link in the show notes of course. But yeah, thank you again for being here.

Laura Kendrick [00:39:05]:
Yeah, it was super fun. Thank you.

Kylie Kelly [00:39:07]:
Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 219

A client of mine is hosting a summit right now, and she told me something that stopped me in my tracks.

One of her speakers has a huge email list. Thousands of subscribers.

And yet…
No clicks.
No purchases.
No engagement.

Then she said, “It’s funny though — your list actually does convert.”

And that right there is the conversation we need to have.

Because this has nothing to do with list size.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The real reason engagement drops even when your list is “growing”
– How unclear positioning confuses your audience and kills conversions
– Why the way you grow your list determines how well it performs later
– Simple questions to audit your positioning and message clarity

If Your Email List Isn’t Converting, It’s Probably Not Your Emails. It’s your positioning

If you want a clear outside perspective on where your message is muddy and what to fix first, that’s exactly what my Business Breakthrough Audit is for.

One personalised review.
Three clarity shifts.
A plan you can actually implement.

Big Lists Don’t Convert. Clear Positioning Does

You can have:

  • Thousands of subscribers
  • Consistent emails
  • A beautiful funnel

And still make no sales.

Why?

Because if people don’t understand who you are, what you do, and why it matters to them, they won’t take action.

Volume does not drive conversion. Clarity does.

My audience knows me.
They know what I stand for.
They know what to expect when my name shows up in their inbox.

There is a clear through-line from how people find me, to how I nurture them, to how I sell.

That doesn’t happen accidentally.

That is positioning.

What Positioning Actually Is [And Why It Matters So Much]

Positioning is the perception people have of you in their minds.

It’s not just your niche.
It’s not your tagline.
It’s not your bio.

It’s the identity you build through:

  • Your tone
  • Your messaging
  • Your offers
  • Your content
  • Your collaborations
  • Your freebies

All of it.

And here’s the uncomfortable truth:

If your positioning is unclear, your audience is confused.
And a confused audience does not click.
A confused audience does not buy.

They scroll.
They lurk.
They ghost.

Not because they don’t like you, but because they don’t get you.

Why Clear Positioning Makes Email So Much Easier

When your positioning is clear, your emails don’t have to work as hard.

Before someone even opens your email, there’s already recognition.

This is for me.
I trust her.
I like how she thinks.

That happens before the subject line does its job.

But when positioning is muddy?

You can write the most beautifully crafted, high-converting sequence in the world and it will still fall flat — because people don’t see themselves in it.

No amount of copy can compensate for unclear positioning.

Where Most Email Lists Go Wrong

This usually starts at the list growth stage.

If people join your list because of a random freebie, bundle, or collaboration that has nothing to do with your actual work, they didn’t opt in for you.

They opted in for the thing.

That doesn’t make them bad subscribers.
But it does mean conversion will be harder.

That’s why I’m incredibly intentional about how I grow my list.

Yes, I use bundles.
Yes, I use summits.
Yes, I collaborate.

But everything connects back to my positioning.

People don’t just know me as “email marketing.”

They know me as:

  • Build your business without social media
  • Relationships over algorithms
  • Connection over hustle

That clarity creates trust before I ever sell anything.

If Your Email List Isn’t Converting, Ask Yourself This

Before you rewrite another sequence, ask:

  • Can someone explain what I do in one sentence?
  • Do people know what makes me different?
  • Have I been consistent in my messaging?
  • Does my freebie reflect what I actually sell?

If your answer is “I’m not sure” to any of those…

You don’t need new emails.
You need clarity.

Because positioning determines whether people trust you enough to take the next step.

How to Fix Unclear Positioning

If your list feels quiet or unresponsive, start here:

1. Revisit your core message
What do you actually want to be known for?

2. Audit your freebies
Are they attracting the right people — or just more people?

3. Clarify your offers
Is there a clear path from opt-in to paid support?

4. Simplify your visibility
Consistency of message matters more than platform volume.

5. Speak like a leader
Your audience follows clarity, not cleverness.

Authority creates safety. Safety creates conversions.

Clarity Is What Turns Subscribers Into Buyers

If you’ve been wondering why your email list feels quiet, it might not be your emails at all.

It might be your positioning.

And if you want an outside perspective on where your clarity is breaking down, this is exactly what I do inside my Business Breakthrough Audit.

I review your visibility, offers, and email strategy and show you the three clarity shifts I’d make if I were in your shoes.

No “post more on Instagram” advice.
Ever.

Just a grounded, personalised plan to turn quiet subscribers into engaged buyers.

More subscribers will not fix unclear positioning

But when your message is clear?

Your email list won’t just grow.

It will convert.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 218

Somewhere in the shiny online business world, we decided that in order to be credible, we had to be broken first.

That our power only counts if it’s earned through pain.
That our story only matters if it includes rock bottom.

And the more we hear the same I lost it all before I found myself stories, the more it quietly reinforces a belief that I think is deeply toxic for women.

That our strength has to be proven through suffering.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why vulnerability ≠ credibility
– How we’ve confused drama with depth
– And what authentic storytelling looks like now

A Simple Next Step

If this stirred something for you, clarity is usually the next move.

My Business Breakthrough Audit gives you an outside perspective on your message, positioning, and next steps – without noise, drama, or overcomplication.

You don’t need to fall apart to rise.
You just need clarity, alignment, and the courage to lead differently.

The Event That Sparked This Conversation

I went to a beautiful women-in-business event this week.

Stunning venue.
Thoughtful curation.
Incredible women on stage.

And yet, by the third keynote, I felt exhausted.

Not because the stories weren’t powerful – they were.

But because they were the same story.

Rock bottom.
Tears.
Redemption.
Success.

Over and over again.

And I found myself thinking, haven’t we evolved past this yet?

When Vulnerability Becomes a Formula

I love storytelling.
I believe in vulnerability.
I value honesty.

But what I witnessed didn’t feel like truth.

It felt like a script.

Cue the pain. Cue the tears. Cue the rise.

Instead of leaving inspired, I left drained.

And that’s when the real question landed for me.

Have we mistaken vulnerability for credibility?

The Quiet Damage This Does to Women

Somewhere along the way, many women internalised this idea:

  • I can’t lead unless I’ve survived something tragic
  • I can’t speak with authority unless I’ve rebuilt myself from the ashes
  • I can’t be inspiring unless my story makes people cry

I remember sitting in rooms like this years ago and thinking, maybe I just haven’t earned it yet.

Like I needed a bigger failure.
A darker chapter.
A more dramatic rebirth.

That belief keeps women small.

Because while they wait for their “worthy” story, they silence themselves.

You Don’t Need Pain to Be Powerful

Here’s what I believe now.

You don’t need pain to be powerful.

You can be powerful because you chose alignment.
Because you built something sustainable instead of sensational.
Because you led yourself without losing yourself first.

That is leadership.

And yet, the women quietly growing businesses with integrity and consistency are often overlooked – because their story isn’t dramatic enough.

When Popularity Lowers the Bar

Another thing that struck me hard that day?

It almost didn’t matter what was said on stage.

The audience was already clapping.
Already swooning.
Already posting.

Once someone reaches a certain level of visibility, the bar seems to drop.

They can recycle the same story from ten years ago and it’s still called “life-changing”.

But shouldn’t leadership evolve as we do?

What I Wish Women on Stage Would Do Instead

I don’t want less honesty.

I want different honesty.

What if speakers started with curiosity instead of tragedy?

What if instead of I hit rock bottom, we heard:

  • This is what I’m questioning right now
  • This is what I’m experimenting with
  • This is what I’m learning without burning everything down

Because resilience isn’t only built in the dark.

It’s built in the everyday.

In boundaries.
In quiet pivots.
In choosing rest.
In choosing sustainability over reinvention.

We Don’t Need Trauma Porn. We Need Truth.

One panel at the event stood out.

They spoke about nervous systems.
About capacity.
About filling yourself up first.

It was refreshing.

And it made me want more depth and less drama.

More substance.
More nuance.
More leadership.

The business world doesn’t need more celebrity coaches.

It needs truth tellers.

A Message for the Next Era of Women in Business

We don’t need more rock bottoms.

We need more honesty about what growth actually looks like.

We’ve evolved.

And our stories should too.

A Simple Next Step

If this conversation resonated and you’re craving clarity, leadership, and depth in your own business, sometimes the most powerful move is getting an outside perspective.

That’s exactly what my Business Breakthrough Audit is designed for.

One personalised review.
Three clarity shifts.
A grounded plan to move forward without drama or noise.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 217

So many brilliant women downplay their expertise because they don’t want to come across as braggy, arrogant, or “too much.”

But let’s be honest: hiding your brilliance helps no one.

Not you.
Not your clients.
Not the people who are literally searching for the solution you already have.

In this post (and the matching podcast episode 🎧), I’m diving into why women hide their expertise, how to reframe visibility so it doesn’t feel gross, and practical ways to finally start being seen – without feeling like you’re tooting your own horn.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why hiding your expertise is keeping you stuck (and broke)
– The difference between bragging and actually owning your brilliance
– My journey from “I’m just an introvert” to stepping into Big Deal Energy
– Six simple ways to share your expertise without feeling like you’re showing off

Ready to be seen?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll personally review your visibility, your offers, and your email list strategy, then send you a private video with the exact clarity shifts I’d make if I were in your shoes. No cookie-cutter advice. Just a personalised 3-step action plan to help you step out of hiding and start being seen with confidence.

Why do we hide our expertise?

If you’ve ever found yourself softening your wins, playing down your achievements, or waiting for someone else to recognise you – you’re not alone.

Here’s what I see all the time:

  • Watered-down introductions. You’ve done incredible work, but when someone asks what you do? You give the smallest, safest version.
  • Downplaying wins. Instead of celebrating a client transformation or a big milestone, you brush it off with, “Oh, it was nothing.”
  • Waiting for recognition. You hope if you just keep your head down, someone will notice and crown you as “the go-to.”

Here’s the kicker: if you’re waiting for someone else to put the spotlight on you, you’ll be waiting forever.

And in the online space? Quiet brilliance doesn’t get rewarded.
Clarity and confidence do.

A story that changed how I see this

When I joined a mastermind led by a multiple 7–8 figure business owner, I was stunned by something he admitted.

Despite running a wildly successful company, he hadn’t really put himself out there.
No ads.
No big visibility campaigns. He leaned on partnerships and smart behind-the-scenes strategies.

And here’s the wild part: I’d never heard of him until he pitched me to speak at his event.

That blew my mind.

Because if he could stay hidden in plain sight – with all that success – how many of us are also quietly hiding instead of fully owning our brilliance?

Bragging vs. Owning your brilliance

Let’s be real: nobody wants to be “that person” online. The one posting humblebrags and endless screenshots of Stripe notifications.

But here’s the difference:

  • Bragging is ego. It’s inflating yourself without depth or proof.
  • Owning your brilliance is service. It’s showing what’s possible, so your audience can see the path forward.

Sharing your expertise isn’t about saying, “Look at me.”
It’s about saying, “Look at what’s possible for you.”

My journey from hiding to Big Deal Energy

For years, I thought I was just an introvert.

And to a degree, I am – I still get sweaty palms before meeting new people, and after an event, I need alone time to recharge.

But looking back, I realised it wasn’t just introversion.
It was fear.

Fear of being seen.
Fear of being judged.
Fear of people thinking I was “up myself.”

So “I’m an introvert” became my shield.

It wasn’t until my biz bestie Leanne Sia introduced me to the idea of Big Deal Energy that things started to shift.

She helped me see that I wasn’t really an introvert – I was hiding. And when I stopped hiding, when I started owning my brilliance unapologetically, everything changed.

That’s when I started saying out loud: I built my business without social media.
That’s when people started to notice.

6 ways to be seen without feeling braggy

If you’re ready to step forward, here are six practical ways to start showing your expertise without the ick:

1. TELL STORIES, NOT STATS

Share client journeys instead of just your numbers.

2. EDUCATE, DON’T ANNOUNCE

Give lessons learned instead of just dropping achievements.

3. ANCHOR IN SERVICE

Connect your message back to the people you help.

4. KEEP A BRAG BOOK

Collect your testimonials and wins so you get comfortable saying them out loud.

5. PICK YOUR STAGE WISELY

You don’t need to be everywhere – just intentional about where you show up.

6. CELEBRATE PUBLICLY, CONNECT PRIVATELY.

Share your wins, but also personally thank the people who helped you.

The bigger movement

This isn’t just about you.

Every time a woman chooses to stop hiding, it gives permission for another woman to do the same.

The more of us who step forward, unapologetically owning our brilliance?

The more powerful we rise together.

So, let’s audit where you’re hiding…

If you’re thinking, “Okay Kylie, I know I’m hiding. I know I’m downplaying. But where do I even start?” – that’s exactly why I created my Business Breakthrough Audit.

It’s a $44 deep dive into your visibility, your email list, and your sales flow. I’ll show you exactly where you’re holding back and give you a 3-step plan to start being seen without feeling braggy.

👉 Grab your audit here.

Because the brilliance you carry today? You earned it.
And it’s time the world saw it.

content:
Feat. Tracy Hoth from Simply Squared Away

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 216

Struggling to find that one PDF… again?
In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I chat with professional organiser & life coach Tracy Hoth about a deceptively simple framework that can tidy up your digital life, your workspace and even your mind.

Her promise? “Sort, purge, assign homes, set limits, and maintain.” Do those five steps and you can organise literally everything: your computer, Canva, bookmarks, calendar, and that never-ending to-do list.

Listen to this episode here:

** Read time: 4 – 5 mins | Listen time: 23 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The 5 steps to organize anything – sort, purge, assign homes, set limits, maintain.
– How to use just five file folders (operations, marketing, content, education, clients) to anchor your digital system.
– Why naming files and being consistent is more powerful than colour-coding perfection.
– How Tracy manages her schedule and to-do list to reduce overwhelm.

What does it really mean to be organised?

When you hear “professional organizer,” you might picture rainbow-ordered bookshelves or Pinterest-perfect pantries. Tracy is quick to bust that myth.

“Being organized just means you know what you have and you can find it when you need it.” – Tracy Hoth

That’s it. No perfection required.
Organisation is about function, not aesthetics.

And here’s the best part: once you put simple structures in place, your brain has more space for creativity, strategy, and actual CEO-level decisions.

The 5 steps to organise anything

Tracy uses the same five steps across every part of her business and life:

  1. Sort – Group like with like. Don’t decide, just gather.
  2. Purge – Once everything’s sorted, delete or archive what doesn’t belong.
  3. Assign Homes – Decide where things live so you can find them again.
  4. Set Limits – Create constraints so your systems don’t bloat.
  5. Maintain – Schedule regular tidy-up sessions.

Whether it’s your desktop, your calendar, or your closet – these five steps always apply.

Why this matters for Business Owners

This isn’t about having tidy folders just for the sake of it – organisation creates capacity.

When your backend is clean, you save hours every week hunting for files, free up brainpower for strategy and creativity, and launch faster because your assets and processes are actually reusable. Most importantly, you start to feel like the CEO of your business instead of the assistant chasing paperwork.

And let’s be real: when you feel like a CEO, you show up like one – and that confidence ripples into how you serve clients, pitch collaborations, and grow your visibility.

Organise your digital files with the “Five Files”

Digital clutter is one of the biggest time wasters for business owners. How much time do you spend searching for that one PDF or duplicating things you already have?

Tracy’s solution: pick one hub (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, or your computer) and create just five master folders for your business:

  • Operations – Inward-facing admin like finances, SOPs, legal.
  • Marketing – Outward-facing assets like emails, graphics, PR, launches.
  • My Content – Courses, podcasts, articles, templates you create.
  • Education – Programs, downloads, trainings you’ve purchased.
  • Clients – Client folders, contracts, call notes, deliverables.

Everything goes into one of those five. No more endless subfolders. No more “random” on your desktop.

Canva, Email, and… the Bookmarks Bar

Here’s where it gets fun: the same Five Files structure works everywhere.

  • In Canva: Create folders for each of the five categories and name designs first before creating them. Monthly maintenance keeps it sane.
  • In Gmail: Mirror the Five Files as labels. Use the Snooze feature for deadlines and follow-ups instead of drowning in tasks.
  • In Your Bookmarks Bar: Build folders by program or project (portal, Zoom link, notes doc, resources) so everything you need is one click away.

Tracy calls bookmarks one of the biggest ROI moves you can make. Once you stop juggling 27 tabs, your brain feels lighter instantly.

Using the 5 steps to organize your time

Overwhelm usually starts with your calendar, and Tracy recommends applying the same five steps of her organizing system to time management.

Begin by sorting with a brain dump of every task, email, and errand onto paper.
Then purge by delaying, delegating, or deleting what doesn’t belong right now.
Next, assign homes by putting real tasks into calendar blocks instead of keeping them swirling in your head.
From there, set limits by capping your day realistically or even theming your weeks (like dedicating CEO weeks to big-picture work). Finally, maintain your system with weekly and monthly planning rituals.

The result? You stop reacting to your calendar and start owning it.

Ready to organise more than just files?

If your backend is messy, your visibility usually is too. That’s why I created the Business Breakthrough Audit – a $44 personalised video review where I walk through your visibility, email list, and offers, and show you the exact 3 clarity shifts I’d make if I were in your shoes.

And I can help you uncover it.

Tracy Hoth (rhymes with “both”) is the heart behind Simply Squared Away. Since launching her organizing business in 2008, she’s guided hundreds of clients – from homes to offices – and mentors coaches and entrepreneurs on creating order in their work and life.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 215

Let’s cut through the noise for a second.

Being visible does not equal being profitable.

You can post consistently.
You can guest everywhere.
You can run bundles, summits, and collaborations.

And still feel stuck when it comes to sales.

Because if the right people aren’t seeing you – the ones who are ready and able to buy – all that visibility is just attention.

And attention on its own isn’t enough.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The #1 visibility mistake keeping women stuck in busy-but-broke mode
– Why murky messaging and vague freebies kill your conversions
– How to audit your visibility with 3 simple but powerful questions
– The exact pathway to turn visibility into paying clients (without burning out)
– Why positioning is the silent killer of conversions and how to fix it

A Clear Way Forward

If your visibility isn’t turning into clients, clarity is the missing piece.

If you want a personalised outside perspective on what to refine first, book a Business Breakthrough Audit and I’ll show you exactly where your positioning and visibility need tightening.

And if you’re ready to zoom out and build a visibility strategy that attracts the right people long-term, join the Empire Expansion Event and map what actually moves the needle next.

Visibility isn’t the goal. Clients are.

And when your visibility is aligned with the right people, the right message, and the right next step?

Everything starts to click.

Visibility Without Direction Is Just Noise

This became painfully clear during my Empire Expansion Event.

Again and again, the issue wasn’t visibility itself.

It was visibility without direction.

Or worse, visibility in front of the wrong audience.

You can have:

  • 10,000 Instagram followers
  • A recognisable name in your niche
  • Reels, bundles, and podcast features

And still feel invisible when it comes to your bank account.

Why?

Because noise does not build trust.
And trust is what converts.

The Biggest Visibility Mistake I See

Trying to be everywhere for everyone.

Not every audience is your audience.
Not every stage is your stage.
Not every opportunity is actually an opportunity.

When you chase everything:

  • You end up in rooms full of peers instead of buyers
  • You burn out on platforms your people don’t care about
  • You look busy but feel frustrated

Busy visibility is not the same as profitable visibility.

The Visibility to Clients Pathway

If you want your visibility to turn into clients, these three things matter more than anything else.

1. Get in the Right Rooms

Before you say yes, ask:

  • Is my ideal client here?
  • Is she actually paying attention?
  • Does she trust the person hosting this space?

If the answer is yes, it’s strategic.

If it’s no, it’s a distraction – even if it looks shiny.

The prettiest distractions are often the most expensive ones.

2. Nail Your Message

Visibility without clear positioning is like shouting in a crowded bar.

Everyone hears you.
No one remembers you.

Your message should make the right person think,
“Oh my god – she’s talking to me.”

That means:

  • No vague “I help women” messaging
  • No freebies that apply to anyone with a pulse
  • Yes to sharp, specific language

Clarity attracts buyers and repels everyone else.

3. Always Give a Next Step

Visibility is not just being seen.

It’s about building a bridge.

Every time you show up, ask yourself:

  • Where am I leading people next?

A podcast episode.
A free resource.
An audit.

If you’re visible with no direction, you’re leaving connection and money on the table.

Three Questions to Audit Your Visibility

If things aren’t converting, start here.

Who are you trying to attract?
Do you actually know her pains, desires, and buying power?

Where is she already paying attention?
Stop dragging her into spaces she doesn’t care about.

Do your offers and messaging match?
If your freebie doesn’t connect to your paid work…

That gap kills conversions.

Positioning Is the Real Issue

If your visibility isn’t converting, it’s usually not because you’re not working hard enough.

It’s because your positioning is unclear.

If your lead magnet could be for anyone, it will attract no one.
If your message is helpful but not compelling, people disappear.
If your offer sounds like everyone else’s, it blends into the noise.

You don’t need more eyes. You need the right ones.

A Clear Way Forward

If you’re doing all the things and still can’t see why it’s not working, this is exactly why I created my Business Breakthrough Audit.

I review your visibility, list growth, offers, and messaging and show you:

  • What’s working
  • What’s not
  • What to fix first

No fluff.
No overwhelm.
Just clarity.
