title: How to Grow Your Business Without Posting On Social Media Every Day
excerpt: THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 214 Let’s name the lie we’ve all been sold. More posting equals more visibility equals more sales. You and I both know that’s not true. You can spend hours creating content, get a stack of likes, and still not make a single sale. Social media might amplify your message, but […]
content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 214

Let’s name the lie we’ve all been sold.

More posting equals more visibility equals more sales.

You and I both know that’s not true.

You can spend hours creating content, get a stack of likes, and still not make a single sale. Social media might amplify your message, but it cannot be the foundation of your business.

An empire built on Instagram is an empire built on rented land.

And landlords change the rules whenever they want.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The lie that “more posting = more sales” (and why the algorithm is stacked against you)
– Why organic reach has collapsed and why it’s not your fault if your reels aren’t converting
– The 3 things that really grow your business: Clarity, Connection, and Credibility
– Smart swaps to replace daily posting with strategies that compound over time
– A client story that proves you can sell more while posting less

A Simple Way to Get Clear

If you’re ready to step off the content treadmill but don’t know where to start, this is exactly why I created my Business Breakthrough Audit.

I’ll review your visibility, email list, and offers and show you:

  • What’s working
  • What’s draining you
  • What to focus on next

No “just post more” advice.
Just a clear path forward.

Why Social Media Feels So Heavy Right Now

If you feel like your business lives or dies by your last post, you’re not dramatic.

You’re responding exactly how these platforms were designed to make you feel.

Endless trends.
Algorithm anxiety.
The pressure to be relatable, visible, and consistent at all times.

That’s not a motivation problem. That’s a design problem.

Organic reach has collapsed.
Audiences are numb.
Trust is harder to earn than ever.

And here’s the part most people won’t say out loud.

Social media isn’t designed to help you sell. It’s designed to keep people scrolling.

Attention Is Not the Same as Trust

This is the shift most business owners haven’t made yet.

You can have:

  • Thousands of followers
  • Strong engagement
  • Consistent posting

And still struggle to convert.

Why?

Because attention doesn’t automatically equal trust.

And without trust, visibility is just noise.

Your audience has been sold to, burned, and over-promised to. Their trust threshold is higher than it used to be.

Which means shallow visibility no longer cuts it.

What Actually Works Instead

Social media can be a tool.

But it should never be the backbone.

The businesses growing steadily in 2025 and beyond are focused on visibility that compounds, not visibility that disappears in 24 hours.

This is where my three C’s come in.

Clarity Comes First

If your offer isn’t clear, no amount of content will save it.

People should understand:

  • What you do
  • Who it’s for
  • Why it matters

In one sentence.

Clarity creates recognition.
Recognition creates trust.
Trust creates sales.

Connection Beats Content

You don’t build real connection through a post that vanishes tomorrow.

Connection is built through:

  • Email
  • Podcasting
  • Long-form content
  • Trusted collaborations

Spaces where people can linger.

In a trust recession, connection is the currency.

Credibility Builds Faster Than Consistency

You don’t need to post every day to be seen as legitimate.

Borrowed authority works.

Guesting.
Collaborations.
Bundles.
Speaking in trusted rooms.

Credibility turns you into the obvious choice.

And none of it requires dancing for the algorithm.

What to Swap If You Want Out of the Social Media Cycle

Try this instead:

  • Swap daily reels for weekly emails
  • Swap story marathons for collaborations
  • Swap grid posts for searchable content
  • Swap algorithm chasing for authority building

These strategies work while you sleep.

That’s compounding visibility.

You’re Not Trapped

Your business is not married to social media.

You don’t need to post every day to make sales.
You need clarity.
You need connection.
You need credibility.

And those last longer than any algorithm ever will.

You’re Not Trapped

If you’re tired of chasing the algorithm, there is another way.

My Business Breakthrough Audit gives you a clear plan to grow your business without relying on daily posting or social media pressure.

Social media can amplify your business.
But it should never run it.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 213

Let’s be real:

“Charge what you’re worth” might be the most overused (and toxic) piece of advice in online business.

It sounds empowering.
It looks great on a motivational graphic.

But in 2025? It’s useless.

Because here’s the truth:
Buyers don’t care what you’re “worth” if they don’t trust you’ll deliver.

They’re not impulse-buying $2,000 programs off a pretty Instagram story anymore. They’re not swayed by fake urgency countdowns or recycled launch tactics. We’re in a trust recession and your audience is watching longer, researching harder, and making decisions differently.

So what does get people to buy in 2025?

Clarity. Connection. Confidence.

If you’ve been raising your prices but still hearing crickets, this one’s going to hit home.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why “charge what you’re worth” falls flat in today’s market
– The 3 things buyers actually want before they say yes
– And how to shift your offers and visibility so you can sell with ease, without lowering your prices or hustling harder

Ready to sell smarter in 2025?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll personally review your visibility, offers, and email list strategy, then send you a private video with the exact clarity shifts I’d make if I were in your shoes. No “post more” advice. Just a personalised 3-step action plan to help you start converting with confidence.

The market shift (& your 2025 reality check)

Here’s what’s different now compared to even two or three years ago.

The market has grown up. Buyers have seen everything.

 – The fake ‘only 3 spots left’ countdowns.
– The recycled plug-and-play launch templates.
– The ‘I made $100K overnight’ IG stories.

They’re not impressed anymore.

We’re smack-bang in what I’ve been calling a trust recession.
People are slower to buy.
They’re not impulse-clicking a $2,000 program off the back of a pretty Instagram reel anymore.

If you missed it, I actually did a whole episode about this – it’s Ep 187, The #1 Strategy That’s Still Working in 2025: Trust. Go & dig into that if you want a deeper dive into building trust.

But here’s the quick version: trust is everything.
And if your audience doesn’t trust you’ll deliver? The sale won’t happen. Period.

Now, they’re watching longer.
They’re fact-checking.
They’re stalking your emails and your website to see if your story matches up.

And the noise? Next level.
The industry is crowded. Which means if your offer isn’t crystal clear, right up front, it’s invisible.

So if you’re out here chanting affirmations, hiking your prices, posting daily, but you haven’t done the foundational clarity work? You’re not going to hear crickets because you’re ‘not worthy.’ You’re going to hear crickets because the market has changed and you haven’t.”

Why “Charge What You’re Worth” falls flat

Let’s dismantle this nonsense.

‘Charge what you’re worth’ sounds good on Instagram.
It gives you a five-second dopamine hit. But in real life? It falls apart.

1. First, it centers you, not your client. Your client isn’t lying awake thinking, ‘Hmm, I wonder what Kylie is worth as a human today?’ They’re thinking: ‘Can she solve my problem? Can I trust her to deliver?’

2. Second, it skips the strategy. Confidence is great, but confidence without clarity is like screaming into a void. If you can’t explain who your offer is for, what it solves, and why it matters, jacking up the price won’t fix that.

3. Third, it assumes money follows mindset alone. And this one stings, but it’s true: I’ve seen women raise their prices because their coach told them to… but they didn’t change their positioning, their messaging, or their proof. 

And then they were crushed when no one bought.

It wasn’t that they were ‘too expensive.’

It was that buyers didn’t understand the damn offer. They couldn’t see the value. They didn’t trust it yet. That’s the real issue.
Not your worth.
Not your confidence.
Not that you need another pep talk.

Clarity, connection, confidence. That’s the currency now.

How buyers are actually deciding in 2025

So if they’re not buying your worth, what are they buying?

Here’s what I’ve seen again and again in my audits, in my mastermind, and in my own launches:

1. CLARITY

– Do I understand in one line what this is and who it’s for?
– Is the transformation obvious to me – not you, but me, the buyer?
– Or am I working way too hard to figure it out?

If I have to scroll your sales page and still can’t tell what the hell you’re offering… I’m out.

Buyers don’t want homework.

They want clarity. Instantly.

2. CONNECTION

– Do I feel like I actually know you?
– Have you shown up consistently enough that I trust your voice?
– Or do you only pop up when you’re in launch mode, waving around a cart-close date?

Connection is everything right now.

In a trust recession, people are buying from the business owners who feel closest to them, not the ones shouting the loudest.

3. CONFIDENCE IN YOU

– Do I feel confident in you as the obvious choice?
– Have you shown your credibility, your authority, your proof?
– Do I feel safe investing in you?

And let me be crystal clear: this is not about whether you feel confident.

This is about whether your audience feels confident in you.

That’s it. That’s the formula.

Clarity. Connection. Confidence.

When those three are in place? Selling feels like breathing.

When they’re not? You can scream ‘charge what you’re worth’ all day long… and nothing changes.

Here’s an example for you…

Let me bring this home with a client story.

I had an Business Breakthrough audit client come in with this gorgeous offer. She’d priced it higher than she ever had before. She was doing all the things: showing up on social, sending emails, getting visible.

But… crickets.

She thought the problem was her price. She thought maybe she wasn’t ‘brave enough.’ She’d been told to just ‘own her worth.’

But when I looked at it? The price wasn’t the problem. Her offer made sense to her, but not to her audience. We reworked the messaging so her ideal client could see themselves in it.

Suddenly the penny dropped for her people. And guess what? Sales started to flow. No price cut. No 24/7 Instagram hustle. No extra freebie. Just clarity.

That’s how it works in 2025. It’s not about raising your price, it’s about making your value undeniable.

Your next step

Stop obsessing over charging ‘what you’re worth.’

You are priceless.

Your worth as a human has nothing to do with your offer price.

What matters is whether your audience sees your clarity, feels your connection, and has confidence in you as the obvious choice.

That’s how buyers are really making decisions in 2025.

That’s how you stop chasing sales and start building an empire.

Here’s what I want you to do today: Take five minutes and look at your main offer through the eyes of a stranger.

Could they answer these three questions in under 30 seconds?

  1. Do I know what this is?
  2. Do I know who it’s for?
  3. Do I understand why it matters?

If the answer isn’t a crystal-clear YES to all three? That’s your homework. Tighten it up.

Want my eyes on your offer asap?

That’s literally what I do in my Business Breakthrough Audits.

For just $66, I’ll record you a private video walking through your visibility, your email list, and your offers. I’ll show you exactly what I see, what I’d shift, and the three things I’d focus on right now if I were you.

No surface level BS.
No ‘just post more’ advice.
Just a clear path forward.

title: Featured on Website Planet: From Weddings to Visibility Coaching
excerpt: I’m so excited to share that I was recently featured on Website Planet! 🎉 In this interview, I opened up about my journey from wedding photographer to visibility strategist, why I believe building an email list is more powerful than relying on social media, and the exact framework I use to help women grow their […]
content:
I’m so excited to share that I was recently featured on Website Planet! 🎉

In this interview, I opened up about my journey from wedding photographer to visibility strategist, why I believe building an email list is more powerful than relying on social media, and the exact framework I use to help women grow their businesses with more ease, confidence, and consistency.

→ You can read the full interview here.

My journey from weddings to visibility coaching

When the pandemic hit in 2020, every single one of my weddings was canceled. After more than a decade as a wedding photographer, I was suddenly faced with a choice:

wait it out, or step into something new.

What I realised was that I wasn’t just passionate about capturing love stories – I was passionate about helping women write their own business stories. I’d been experimenting with collaborations and email marketing for years, and I knew I could help other entrepreneurs grow their visibility in a way that felt natural and sustainable.

That’s where my role as a visibility coach was born.

The RISE Framework

At the heart of my work is my RISE Framework – the simple, repeatable system I use with clients who want to grow without burning out:

  • Reach: Attract new people using collaborations, podcast guesting, and other high-trust visibility strategies (without the endless scroll).
  • Influence: Build real relationships with your audience through nurture sequences, storytelling, and consistent connection.
  • Scale: Put systems in place that let you grow your business and your impact without maxing out your capacity.
  • Empower: Step into CEO energy – building a business that feels good, honors your values, and gives you the freedom you started all this for.

These four pillars together create not just a business, but a sustainable empire.

Why email beats the algorithm every time

In the feature, I also talked about why email marketing is the most powerful tool we have as entrepreneurs. Social media is great for visibility, but at the end of the day, you don’t own your audience there. Algorithms change. Trends come and go.

But your email list? That’s yours. It’s where real conversations happen. It’s where trust is built. It’s where sales are made.

That’s why so much of what I teach comes back to growing, nurturing, and selling through email – because it works.

What 200+ podcast episodes have taught me

Another big part of our conversation was my podcast, The Email Growth Show. After more than 200 episodes, I’ve learned that consistency doesn’t have to mean burnout. It’s about finding rhythms that work for you, repurposing what you already have, and showing up in ways that feel aligned.

The lesson?

You don’t need to be everywhere.
You just need to be somewhere consistently.

What “Being Bold” means to me in 2025

One of my favorite parts of the feature was sharing what “being bold” looks like for me this year.

For me, bold isn’t about being the loudest in the room. It’s about making intentional choices, owning my voice, and helping other women step into their own version of bold – unapologetically, without waiting for permission.

That’s the energy I’m carrying into every mastermind call, every collaboration, every email I send.

Thank you Website Planet!

A huge thank you to Website Planet for the feature. I’m so grateful for the chance to share my story and, more importantly, to remind women that you can build a business that feels aligned, sustainable, and truly yours.

content:
Feat. Kris Jones from Red Door Designs

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 212

If your content feels chaotic, your funnel’s disjointed, or you’re constantly second-guessing what to say, this episode is a breath of fresh, story-driven air.

Kris Jones is a messaging strategist who helps entrepreneurs craft the one story that anchors everything – your sales page, your email welcome sequence, your podcast intro, your Instagram bio. All of it.

We talk about how to simplify your message using her signature “One Story” method and why it’s the key to selling more by saying less.

Listen to this episode here:

** Read time: 5 – 6 mins | Listen time: 22 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why storytelling is your most underrated (and underused) conversion tool
– The “One Story” framework that simplifies every piece of your marketing
– How to write a brand story that sells, without sounding salesy
– The mindset shift that makes your client the hero (and you the guide)
– Why one story is better than 17 different taglines (and how to find yours)

The power of one story…

Here’s what most online business owners do:

  • Write one story for their website
  • Another for their launch emails
  • Something completely different for guest interviews
  • And end up confusing themselves and their audience

Kris’s approach is different.

She teaches how to create a clear, emotionally resonant story that shows your ideal client what’s possible – by walking them through a relatable transformation.

Your story becomes the foundation.

Everything else flows from there.

What makes a good story?

According to Kris, a powerful brand story isn’t about making yourself look impressive – it’s about helping your ideal client see themselves in the transformation.

Your story should position them as the hero (with you as the guide), highlight both the emotional and tangible shifts they can expect, and paint a clear before-and-after journey.

The more specific the details, the more relatable and effective it becomes. And when done right? That one story can anchor your entire marketing strategy, no need to rewrite it 50 different ways for every platform.

Where to use your story (hint: everywhere!)

You don’t need to overthink this.

Once you’ve nailed your One Story, it becomes the through line for your entire brand – the foundation you can keep coming back to instead of reinventing the wheel every time you write or speak.

You can weave it into your website copy (especially your About page, homepage, and services page), bake it into your welcome sequence and nurture emails, and use it to create stronger hooks for podcast episodes, intros, and guest pitches.

It becomes the heartbeat of your interviews, the backbone of your sales pages, and the emotional anchor for your launch content. When your story is solid, you stop second-guessing what to say and start creating real resonance, the kind that builds connection, trust, and conversions.

A quick story audit you can do right now

If you’re listening and thinking, “I don’t even know what my story is anymore…”

Here’s what you can ask:

  • What transformation do I help people create?
  • What version of themselves are they becoming through my work?
  • What did I have to overcome to now guide others through this?
  • What details and emotions would make this story more relatable?

When you answer those questions, the clarity comes rushing in.

Your next step:

If reading this has you realising your brand story is murky, missing, or misaligned – don’t panic. You don’t need to burn everything down or start from scratch. You just need one clear, powerful story that positions your client as the hero and shows them what’s possible.

And I can help you uncover it.

Book a $44 Business Breakthrough Session – I’ll review your messaging, offers, and email flow, then give you a personalised action plan to clarify your story and amplify your impact.

Remember: you don’t need more content.
You need clearer connection.

After 20 years of crafting stories for giants like Nike and Adidas, she discovered something shocking: a single, well-told story can replace all your marketing and double your revenue.

Today, she helps coaches and consultants scale from 30K to 300K months using her Signature Story-Selling SystemTM – proving that you don’t need endless content or complicated funnels to attract premium clients. Just one story, told
well.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 211

If you wait until October to plan Q4, you’re already behind.
And if you try to scale by doing more without a strategy? Hello, burnout.

In this episode, I’m walking you through the 5 core shifts I’m making to grow my business (and my clients’ businesses) without relying on social media – and how you can use Q4 as your launchpad for 2026, not your burnout crash zone.

If you’ve ever rolled into November throwing together a last-minute offer (👋 been there), or if you’re ready for your next quarter to feel profitable and sustainable – this episode is for you.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why Q4 is not the time to wing it – and what to do instead
– How to make visibility moves now that keep bringing leads next year
– The biggest money-making mistake I see in Q4 (and what to do instead)
– Why you don’t need a brand-new offer to hit your revenue goals
– How to reframe existing offers with seasonal positioning that converts
– The “Start with Your Life” planning method that saved my sanity (and my sales)

Want help making Q4 your most profitable quarter yet?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll review your visibility, offers, and list growth strategy, then give you a personalised action plan to scale smarter in Q4 (without burning out).

Or just listen to the full episode here:
5 Shifts I’m Making to Scale Without Social Media in Q4 [Ep 211]

Why Q4 matters more than you think

Let’s be real – it’s still Q3. Thinking about Q4 might feel a little extra.
But here’s the truth:

The people who win in Q4 aren’t the ones scrambling in December.
They’re the ones laying the foundations now.

Q4 isn’t just the final sprint – it’s the slingshot for your entire next year.
Your audience is buying, businesses are budgeting, and your future momentum depends on what you do now.

The biggest mistake? Wing-it energy

I’ve been that person who rolls into Black Friday with a vague idea and zero lead time.

Yes, I made sales…
But come January? I was back at square one.

Everything changed when I stopped treating Q4 like a scramble and started treating it like the strategic season it is – one that can compound your visibility, sales, and sanity for the next 12 months.

5 Shifts I’m Making to Scale Without Social Media in Q4

Here’s exactly how I’m approaching this season differently and how you can too:

1. PRIORITISING VISIBILITY THAT STACKS

If your list resets to zero every Monday, you’re on the hustle hamster wheel.

Instead of posting constantly, I’m focusing on compound visibility:

  • Guest podcasting
  • Collaborative bundles
  • Co-hosted workshops
  • Freebie swaps with aligned creators

This kind of visibility brings leads now and later. One of my private clients booked 3 podcast interviews in October. Two brought in leads immediately, and the third? It aired in January and brought in $12K in sales. Without her lifting a finger.

💬 Ask yourself: Where can I show up in Q4 that brings me leads in Q1?

2. MONETISING WHAT’S ALREADY WORKING

Q4 isn’t the time to build something new from scratch, it’s the time to squeeze the juice out of what’s already working.

Instead of launching a new offer, I’m tweaking existing ones:

  • Adjusting pricing
  • Adding high-value bonuses
  • Repositioning offers for seasonal alignment

Last year, I helped a client reframe her group program as a “2025 Growth Jumpstart.”
Same content, no new delivery…

Result? $18K in sales in 10 days before Christmas.
Yes please.

3. STARTING WITH MY LIST, NOT MY LAUNCH CALENDAR

Let’s be honest: Q4 is full.
Family. Holidays. School breaks. Events.

So my planning starts with life.
I block out rest, recovery, and capacity first – then build business around that.

This keeps me grounded, resourced, and out of the “Yes” trap I fell into years ago (you know… saying yes to everything out of fear I’d miss the opportunity).

4. PLANNING MY OFFERS WITH RUNWAY, NOT PANIC

Your audience needs lead time.

If you launch a Black Friday deal with zero pre-launch or warm-up content, don’t be surprised if results are… meh.

So I’m building runway into everything:

  • Teasing offers early
  • Sending reminder emails
  • Creating a short but strategic pre-launch

Whether it’s a live promo or evergreen funnel – prepping your audience is what drives conversions.

5. LETTING Q4 SET THE STAGE FOR 2026

This isn’t about chasing Q4 revenue.
This is about rolling into January in momentum mode, not dragging yourself across the finish line.

Your Q4 plan should feel like a decision, not a reaction.

Ready to Build Your Q4 Plan Now?

That’s exactly what we’ll do together inside my free 2-day workshop:
The Empire Expansion Event ✨

You’ll:

  • Map out your 12-month growth plan, starting with Q4
  • Pinpoint your highest ROI visibility moves
  • Refine your messaging so your offers basically sell themselves

It’s live. It’s actionable. It’s not fluff.
And it will save you from the chaos spiral I used to live in every single year.

3 Ways to Monetise Your Email List That Aren’t Selling Your Own Offers

Why this matters (& why you’re probably missing out)

Here’s the deal – your email list is a business asset.

But most business owners treat it like a dusty treadmill they only hop on when they feel guilty.

They send a flurry of emails during a launch… and then ghost their subscribers until the next one.

The problem?

  • Your audience stops expecting to hear from you regularly
  • Your income becomes feast or famine
  • You miss out on easy, low-effort revenue in between launches

Your list should be always on, always working in the background, and not just something you ‘turn on’ when you’re going to sell something.

Sponsorships: How to get paid to email your audience

This is the strategy I’m using right now and it works.

Someone pays to get their offer featured in your email. You’re basically saying: “Hey, I’ve got an engaged audience who trusts me. Want me to introduce you?”

WHY IT WORKS:

  • The sponsor gets a warm, aligned audience
  • You get paid
  • Your subscribers discover something genuinely useful (because you only feature aligned offers)

HOW TO PRICE IT:

  • Smaller list? $97–$147 per spot is a great starting point
  • Highly engaged or niche audience? $197–$297+ is more than fair
  • Add upsells like “I’ll write the copy for you” (I offer this for $77 extra)

Pro tip: Keep it exclusive. If you promote everyone, your audience tunes out. Think of it like matchmaking!

Affiliate offers that sell through your email list

Affiliate marketing = getting paid to share what you already love.

If you’re already raving about a tool, course, or service to your biz friends, check if they have an affiliate program. You could earn a commission every time someone buys through your link.

The key: Storytelling over selling.

Share:

  • How you use it
  • The transformation it’s given you
  • Why it’s worth the investment

Example: My Try Interact quiz funnel. I share my results, show my backend data, and then drop my affiliate link (you can see more detail about that here!)

No hard pitch – just “Here’s what I use and love – go check it out.”

Collaborative paid bundles & features

This one’s a little more work upfront, but the payoff is big.

You gather a group of aligned business owners, everyone contributes something valuable, and you either:

  • Sell the bundle and split the profits
  • Or charge contributors a flat fee for access to your audience

It’s part monetisation, part visibility swap, part list-building powerhouse. And you’re not selling your thing – you’re curating something that makes your audience’s life easier.

How to do this without losing trust…

If every email turns into a billboard, your open rates will tank.

Here’s my 80/20 monetization rule:

  • Only feature what you’d spend your own money on
  • Give before you take – 80% nurture, 20% promotion
  • Always disclose if it’s sponsored or an affiliate link
  • Curate with intention – your audience should know you only share things worth their time

Your next step…

Pick one of these strategies and try it in the next 14 days:

  • Want the fastest cash? Sponsored spots
  • Want evergreen income? Affiliate promotions
  • Want list growth + income? Collaborative bundles

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 209

If you’ve heard the whispers that quizzes are “so 2019” or “no one fills those out anymore” – I’m here to call bullshit. Because in July 2025 alone, my new quiz brought in 135 leads with a jaw-dropping 86% conversion rate.
No ads.
No launch.
No dancing reels.

Just one high-converting quiz, built on the platform I swear by – Try Interact (yep, that’s my affiliate link 💁🏼‍♀️)

Let’s talk about why quizzes still work in 2025 and how to create one that doesn’t just collect names, but actually grows your business.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– How my quiz brought in 135 leads in 30 days with an 86% conversion rate (no ads, no launch, no going viral)
– Why quizzes still work in 2025 and the mistakes that make most of them flop
– The 3 things every high-converting quiz must do to generate leads & sales
– How I use quiz data to segment my audience and sell smarter
– Which quiz type is right for your business based on what you sell

Want help crafting your quiz funnel?

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll review your visibility, list growth, and offers and give you a personalised plan to move forward with clarity (and peace).

→ Join The Email Growth Club – If you want coaching, templates, feedback and step-by-step support to grow your list and sell smarter – this is the space for you.

Or just listen to the full episode here:
Why Quizzes Still Work in 2025 (And How to Know Which One to Create)

The numbers don’t lie (here’s my quiz data)

My quiz – What Visibility Strategy Matches Your Business Personality? – launched on June 30, 2025. In the first 30 days, here’s what happened:

  • 239 views
  • 157 quiz starts
  • 135 completions
  • 135 new leads
  • 86% conversion rate from starts to leads

Let me say that again: 86% of people who started the quiz joined my list. 🤯

That’s not a fluke.
That’s intentional strategy.

Why quizzes still work (when done right)

Here’s why quiz funnels are still a powerful tool in 2025, especially if you’re a coach, service provider, or building a personal brand:

✅ 1. THEY’RE PERSONAL & INTERACTIVE

Quizzes put your lead at the center.

It’s not just “Download my free guide” – it’s “Tell me who you are and I’ll give you exactly what you need.” That micro-personaliSation goes a long way in a noisy online world.

✅ 2. THEY SEGMENT YOUR AUDIENCE INSTANTLY

My quiz has four outcomes:

  • Influence Builder
  • Scale Seeker
  • Empowered CEO
  • Reach Queen

Each one triggers a tailored nurture sequence that speaks directly to that archetype. It’s high-touch strategy at scale.

✅ 3. THEY’RE FAST & FUN

With short attention spans and inbox overload, quick and engaging content wins. A good quiz feels more like Buzzfeed, less like homework – and that boosts opt-ins like crazy.

✅ 4. THEY GIVE YOU REAL BUYER DATA

Try Interact’s backend shows me:

  • What percentage of users choose each result (over 50% are Influence Builders!).
  • Which questions are converting best.
  • How each result is performing in terms of CTA clicks.

This isn’t just a freebie – it’s a mini market research tool.

The quiz strategy that converts

Here’s how I made my quiz actually work — no fluff, no Disney princess energy:

It’s Curiosity-Driven

People want to know what kind of visibility strategy fits them. It feels like personality-meets-strategy — and that blend is compelling.

It’s Tied to My Paid Offers

Each outcome leads into either The Email Growth Club or Headliner Mastermind — naturally and clearly. It’s not just content for content’s sake.

It Has Segmented Follow-Up

Each result unlocks a custom 4-email sequence. I’m not blasting one generic pitch to everyone. I’m meeting them where they are.

It Informs My Business Decisions

Knowing that half my audience identifies as Influence Builders? That’s pure gold. It helps me write better emails, craft stronger offers, and show up more strategically.

So… what quiz should YOU create?

Here’s how I guide my clients when building a quiz:

→ If You Sell a Signature Offer (like coaching or a mastermind)

Create a diagnostic quiz.
Example: “What’s Blocking You From Scaling to $10k Months?”

It reveals the gap and your offer becomes the solution.

→ If You Sell Courses or Digital Products

Create a personality-style quiz.
Example: “What Type of CEO Are You?”

Then match each result with the right product path.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 208

After four days of complete silence at a retreat in Northern NSW, I came back more grounded, clear, and connected than I’ve felt in years.

Today, we’re not talking about funnels or freebies or email strategy.
We’re talking about what happens when you stop doing altogether.

When you close the laptop.
Turn off the notifications.
And finally sit still long enough to hear your own voice again.

This isn’t a breakdown of business tactics.
It’s a reflection on what I learned during four days of complete silence – no phone, no talking, no reading or planning – and how it cracked me open in the best possible way.

So if you’ve been feeling disconnected, depleted, or like you’re holding it all together with duct tape and to-do lists… come in close.
Let’s talk about stillness.
Spaciousness.

And what it really means to lead from within.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– 5 powerful lessons silence taught me about business, burnout, and alignment
– Why clarity doesn’t always come from doing more
– How your body holds the truth even when your brain resists it
– What I’m changing in how I run my business and how you can create your own version of spaciousness

If you’re craving space, alignment & strategy that feels like you…

Here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll review your visibility, list growth, and offers and give you a personalised plan to move forward with clarity (and peace).

→ Join The Headliner Mastermind – where we blend visibility strategy, embodiment, and real leadership growth, without adding to your burnout.

The real reason I went on a silent retreat…

I booked the retreat thinking I just needed a break – a few days without kids, voxer dings, or back-to-back calls.

But what I got? Was so much more than rest.

There was no phone. No talking. No reading. Just me, my nervous system, and the voice inside me I usually drown out with productivity, podcasts, and planning.

The first few hours were wildly uncomfortable…
But once the noise softened, clarity came through.

5 things silence cracked open for me

✅ 1. SILENCE IS CONFRONTING – BUT IT’S WHERE I FOUND CLARITY

Don’t create a new one, reposition your best-performing freebie.
I’ve always told clients that clarity comes from action. But now I also believe this:

Clarity comes from space. From not trying to fix or force anything.

Sitting barefoot in the grass, staring at Mount Warning in total stillness, I realized something profound:

I’d been thinking so much… I’d stopped feeling.

Your soul doesn’t need more strategy, it needs space to speak.

✅ 2. CREATING SPACE INSIDE MATTERS MORE THAN OUTSIDE

I thought I just needed a weekend off to catch up on work.

My laptop was packed.
My brain was planning funnel tweaks.

But the real breakthrough?

You can clear your calendar – and still be cluttered as f*ck on the inside.

What I needed wasn’t time to get more done.
It was internal spaciousness, a release of unprocessed grief, invisible pressure, and lingering stories that weren’t even mine.

✅ 3. YOUR BODY KNOWS BEFORE YOUR BRAIN EVEN CATCHES UP

This retreat wasn’t just silent, it was somatic.

There was breathwork, grounding, cold plunges, Reiki, barefoot walks… and even a 35-minute cry over a succulent (yes, really).

And here’s the thing: if your body is screaming no, even the most beautifully mapped-out strategy will fall flat. That’s why embodiment work is becoming part of how I support clients, especially inside my mastermind.

✅ 4. DOING LESS CAN MOVE YOU FORWARD FASTER

I didn’t map a funnel.
I didn’t hustle.
I didn’t “get ahead.”

I walked. I cried. I napped.
And somehow, I came home with more clarity than any planning session has ever given me.

The best ideas don’t come when you’re pushing.
They come when you’re present.

✅ 5. STILLNESS ISN’T SOMETHING YOU EARN, IT’S SOMETHING YOU DESERVE

This retreat reminded me that I don’t have to prove anything.

I don’t need to earn rest.
I don’t need to deserve silence.
I just need to listen.

And you do too.

If you’re holding it all together with duct tape and to-do lists…
If your brain has 72 tabs open and your body feels heavy…
You don’t need a four-day retreat.
You just need space.
And permission.

Ready to build from stillness, not stress?

You don’t have to burn out to course-correct.
You don’t have to wait for rock bottom to choose rest.

Your energy matters.
Your peace matters.

And your next level will require it.

content:
Let’s be real: if you’ve ever felt like you’re yelling into the void online, you’re not alone.
There’s content everywhere, but actual connection?

That’s the missing piece.

That’s where events come in.

Not just webinars or free trainings, I’m talking high-converting, high-connection moments that let your people experience your magic in real time.

They’re powerful.
They’re personal.
And when done right? They’re a visibility rocket ship.
Let’s dive in.

In this post, you’ll learn:

  • How to use live events to grow your audience with intention
  • What makes events like panels, workshops, and collaborations great for credibility
  • How I’ve used Inside the Inbox as a repeatable visibility strategy
  • 7 event strategies you can start using now, even if your audience is small

#1: Host live workshops that solve one juicy problem

Want dreamy, aligned humans signing up fast?
Forget the 57-step funnel, run a live workshop.

Make it simple.
Make it specific.
Solve one thing they’re googling at 2am.

Give them a mini transformation they can feel.
It builds trust, boosts conversions, and positions you as the go-to expert, not just another online voice with vibes.

→ Main takeaway: Live workshops = high-impact, low-drama growth.

#2: Speak at other people’s events, regardless of their size!

You don’t need your own massive platform to show up and shine.

Borrow someone else’s audience and borrow their credibility while you’re at it.

I got paid $500 to speak at the Smart Business Mastermind Event recently – and I got access to a totally new (and totally aligned) audience in the process.

Always check the vibe:
→ Do the values match?
→ Is the topic aligned?
→ Are the people inside your dream client bubble?

When it’s a yes – go all in.
Show up.
Serve.
And watch your visibility skyrocket.

#3: Collaborate on panels or roundtables = instant credibility

When you share a screen with other experts, your authority goes through the roof.
Panels and roundtables are a brilliant way to fast track your credibility.

They’re also super shareable.
Everyone promotes, everyone wins, and your name shows up next to people your audience already trusts.

→ Pro Tip: Make sure the topic lights you up. Then show up, speak up, and let the ripple effect do its thing.

#4: Create a signature virtual event that becomes your thing

Want to be unforgettable?

Don’t just post more content – create an experience.

For me, that’s Inside the Inbox, my signature annual virtual event that puts me on the map every damn time. You can read more about that here: Inside The Inbox: A Fresh Take on List Growth, Email Strategy & Visibility

It brings in new leads, builds brand equity, and gives people something to look forward to.

Not just a freebie – a freaking moment.

That’s how you create buzz without burnout.

#5: Go behind the scenes: Raw beats perfect, always

Not every event needs slides, scripts, or slick branding.

A live Q&A.
A behind-the-scenes tour.
A co-working hour where you get real.

These off-the-cuff moments are where trust is built.

Pull back the curtain.
Let your people see how you actually work – that’s what makes you magnetic, btw.

#6: Use every event as a goldmine of market research

Real talk:

Your audience is telling you what they need, if you’re listening.

That random question someone asked in your workshop?
💡 That’s your next blog post.
💡 Your next freebie.
💡 Maybe even your next offer.

Stop talking at your people.
Start with them.

Your next big business shift could come straight from that Q&A chat.

#7: Repurpose the sh*t out of every event

The event is just the beginning.

Now? Milk that magic.

  • Turn the replay into a lead magnet
  • Turn the Q&A into a blog
  • Send snippets to your email list
  • Clip the good bits for Instagram

Hosting or speaking in one killer event = a month of content.

Don’t let it die in the Zoom graveyard.

Final word… this approach works.

You don’t need a massive audience or fancy tech.

You need one intentional event that shows people who you really are and what you really help with.

That’s what moves the needle.
That’s what builds a brand.

💬 So tell me: which one of these 7 ideas is calling your name?

Slide into the comments, spill your tea, or reply to this post if you’re nodding along and ready to use events to grow your credibility & audience.

Not sure how to show up in a way that actually works for you?

Take my Visibility Personality Quiz and get your custom strategy in 2 minutes.
You’ll walk away knowing exactly how to grow your audience without burning out!

Click here to take the quiz today!

content:
Feat. Nadine Nethery from Can Do Content

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 207

Think you really know your audience?

If you’ve been writing sales pages, planning offers, or launching programs based on assumptions (hello, outdated “ideal client avatars”), this episode is going to rock your world.

Because Nadine Nethery, audience-driven copywriter turned customer experience strategist, is here to call BS on guessing.

Instead, she shares how to actually ask your people the right questions, organize what they tell you, and turn that into copy, offers, and customer experiences that make people go:

💡 “Oh my God, it’s like she’s reading my mind.”

This isn’t just about sending one random survey.
It’s about creating a simple, repeatable system to gather the gold your audience is already handing you…

and then actually using it to sell more and serve better.

Listen to this episode here:

** Episode Duration: 27:03 mins **

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why skipping audience research is costing you sales
– The exact 10-question survey Nadine recommends sending today
– The only type of survey questions you should ask (and the ones to avoid)
– How to organise all that “voice of customer” data so you can use it for copy, sales pages, and content
– Ways to do audience research even if you don’t have a big list (or any list yet!)

Why most customer research fails (& what to do instead)

If your “ideal client avatar” looks like:
“She’s 34, shops at Target, has 2.5 kids, and likes oat milk lattes” – Nadine says that’s useless.

You don’t need to know her coffee order.
You need to know what’s actually keeping her stuck, what she’s tried before, and how she describes the problem in her own words.

That’s what makes your copy feel like magic and makes people trust you enough to buy.

The problem?

Most business owners are guessing.

The #1 mistake you’re making with surveys

Multiple choice. Drop-downs. Tick boxes.

NOPE.

Those are based on your assumptions.
And they’re keeping you blind to what people are really struggling with.

Nadine says:
→ Ask open-ended questions only.
→ Let your audience tell you what you don’t know to ask.

And bonus:
You can literally copy & paste their words onto your sales page.

10 customer survey questions to write copy that converts

You don’t need to overthink this.
Nadine recommends sending a simple, 10-question survey that walks your customer back through their experience with you.

Some of her go-to questions:

  1. What was happening before you worked with me / bought this?
  2. What finally made you decide to go for it?
  3. What immediate wins or changes did you notice?
  4. What has changed for you since?
  5. If you had to sum up what this has meant for you in 4 sentences or less, what would you say?


That last question?

Gold.
It often pulls out fresh testimonials you’ve never captured before.

What if you don’t have a big email list?

No excuses.

Nadine says you can:

– Listen in on Facebook groups or Reddit threads where your audience hangs out.
– Pay attention to how they describe their problems to other people.
– Check competitor testimonials to see what problems they solved.
– Post your survey in communities (with permission).

And please – don’t just ask your mum or your biz bestie.

You need real buyers or potential buyers.

How to organize all this data (without going cross-eyed)

The easiest way? Buckets.

Nadine organizes all her survey responses into a few simple categories so she (and her clients) can reuse the insights over and over again:

✅ Objections
✅ Beliefs (true + false)
✅ Desires
✅ Pain points

Next time you’re writing an email, planning content, or updating your sales page, you can just dip into those buckets and pull out a juicy, real customer statement.

How to use survey data to improve your copy & sales

Collecting data is one thing.

Actually using it?

That’s where most people stop.

Nadine suggests setting a recurring “CEO Date” with yourself every 3 months. Go through your survey responses, DMs, email replies, and jot down:

✔ What’s working
✔ What objections are still popping up
✔ What you can tweak to make buying an easier yes

You don’t have to change everything overnight.

But this simple habit will make your copy sharper, your offers stronger, and your customers feel seen.

Your next step:

Want to try this yourself?

Here’s where to start:

  1. Write your first 10-question survey.
    Keep it open-ended. Focus on what life looked like before, during, and after working with you.
  2. Send it with an incentive.
    A $50 gift card, a free workshop, even a donation to charity – incentivised surveys get way more responses.
  3. Organise answers into buckets.
    Objections, beliefs, desires, pain points. Copy and paste exact phrases.
  4. Update your copy.
    Use those real words everywhere – on sales pages, in emails, even in Instagram captions.
  5. Make it a habit.
    Every 3 months, revisit what you’re hearing and tweak accordingly.


The fastest way to grow your list and sell more? Know exactly what your audience wants – and give it to them.

Inside The Email Growth Club, I’ll show you how to turn real audience insights into emails, offers, and lead magnets that convert (without dancing on Reels or throwing cash at ads).

Nadine Nethery is an audience-driven copywriter turned customer experience strategist for savvy online business owners who want to intentionally attract, retain and wow their dream customers.

Over the past 8+ years, Nadine has given hundreds of industry-disrupting online business owners the words to shine and the strategies to build a sustainable audience-centred business. And she’s on a mission to make mediocre brand experiences a thing of the past!

title: How to Use Blogging to Attract Aligned Clients and Grow Your Email List
excerpt: With Special Guest, Eden from Maven Made Copy If you’ve ever thought, “Blogging sounds great, but who has the time?” – this one’s for you. Eden from Maven Made Copy has blogged every single week for over a year and not just for the sake of consistency. Her blog posts are strategic visibility tools that […]
content:
With Special Guest, Eden from Maven Made Copy

If you’ve ever thought, “Blogging sounds great, but who has the time?” – this one’s for you.

Eden from Maven Made Copy has blogged every single week for over a year and not just for the sake of consistency. Her blog posts are strategic visibility tools that bring in the right clients, grow her email list, and keep working for her long after she hits publish.

I sat down with Eden to talk about how she does it, how blogging and email work together, and why blogging is still 100% worth it in 2025.

In this post, you’ll learn:

  • How to stay consistent with blogging (even when life gets busy)
  • What actually makes a blog post bring in aligned clients, not just random traffic
  • How to use blogging and email together to grow your list
  • Easy SEO tips that matter (and what to skip when you’re starting out)
  • Why blogging is still 100% worth it in 2025 (yes, even with AI search results!)

How Eden blogs consistently (even when life gets busy)

The biggest reason Eden blogs so consistently? She treats her business like a client. She explained that she adds all her own business tasks to Asana the same way she would for client work. “I wouldn’t miss a deadline for a client, and I won’t miss one for myself,” she says.

Planning ahead is another key piece. Eden doesn’t sit down each week wondering what to write about – she already knows. “I spend time planning my content ahead of time, so I’m not scrambling to write a blog. I have the topic and keyword picked out, so what to write about isn’t a question. I usually have at least a month (ideally a quarter) of topics planned.”

Her best tool for staying consistent is a strategic content calendar.

It keeps her from writing just for the sake of posting and helps her stay focused on topics that actually matter to her audience. (You can grab her free Blog Content Calendar here.)

Inside The Email Growth Club, we create content plans like this every month to help you grow your list without burning out.

Why blogging attracts aligned clients (not just random traffic)

Blogging can sometimes bring in random website visitors, but Eden says you can influence who finds you by being intentional with your keywords and topics. “You can’t control who lands on your website, but you can tell search engines who you want to come to your website through keywords,” she explains.

Every blog post you publish is another chance to help search engines understand who you help and what you do. “The more it understands your business, the better traffic it gives you,” she says.

And the simplest way to get the right people reading?
Write posts that are actually useful for your ideal clients. “If you directly answer their questions in your blog posts, they’ll find your website organically.”

Using your blog to grow your email list

Eden never publishes a blog without a call-to-action, because she knows most people won’t just “come back later” to her website. “I have a CTA to join my email list in every single blog I publish,” she says. “I never know how someone is going to find my website. Maybe it’s through a blog I published a year ago, or the one I published last week… I can’t assume that they know who I am just because I’ve been in business for a while.”

She recommends always giving readers a clear next step – whether that’s joining your list, downloading a freebie, or signing up for a webinar.

Just make sure the call-to-action fits naturally with the blog topic.

p.s Want to know which visibility strategy will help you grow your email list faster?
Take my free quiz: What Visibility Strategy Matches Your Business Personality? here!

How to come up with endless blog post ideas

If you’re stuck on what to blog about, Eden has a simple strategy that works for beginners and seasoned bloggers alike. She goes back through old posts to find topics she can expand on.

She gave the example of working with a client who offered SEO and branding services. They talked about domain authority a lot but had never written a full post on it. So she suggested a post breaking it down, what it is, why it’s important, and how to increase it.

This approach works because you already know your audience is interested in those topics, you can add internal links between posts to help with SEO, and you’re anticipating the questions your audience is asking.

If you’re starting fresh with no previous blogs to build on, Eden says to think about the questions your clients always ask – or even the questions you had yourself when you were starting out.

Simple SEO tips that matter

You don’t need to be an SEO expert to get results from blogging.

Eden recommends starting with the basics:

  • Break up your content with headers and shorter paragraphs (for skimmability)
  • Link to other pages or posts on your website
  • Add alt text to images with relevant keywords
  • Fix or remove broken links
  • Always end with a clear call-to-action

These small steps add up over time and help search engines understand your content.

Why Blogging is still worth it in 2025 (even with AI search results)

With AI answering search queries directly in search results, some business owners wonder if blogging is still worth it.

Eden’s answer? Absolutely.

“Would you rather spend 10 minutes on a social media post that will have about an hour of visibility, or two hours on a blog that will be shown in search results for years?” she says. “Some of my (and my client’s) best blog posts are ones we wrote years ago. Those are the blogs bringing in hundreds of clicks per month.”

And AI doesn’t replace blogging – it relies on it. “AI uses information it finds on the internet to provide answers – AKA, your blog posts. AI needs us to continue creating content, and we won’t be penalised for doing so.”

The only catch?

Be patient. “You can’t expect to see results overnight. Or honestly, in the first few months. But the effort you put in now will pay off down the line (and in big ways!). The sooner you start, the sooner you’ll reap the benefits.”

And finally… what about repurposing blog posts into emails?

You don’t have to write brand new content for your email list every time. Eden recommends using sections of your blogs to create email content.

“Most blog posts will have multiple sections and key takeaways. Use one of those main points as your email content. Expand upon the topic a little more and provide additional value to your subscribers.”

She might, for example, take one tip from her blog post about common content writing mistakes and turn it into an email with a link to the full post for readers who want more.

Remember, blogging only works if you’re writing with purpose. “A blog post should answer a real question or solve a specific problem for your target audience. No fluff – just useful, relevant content. You can have a super strong SEO strategy, but if the topic isn’t relevant to your audience, they aren’t going to read it. You’ll get random people on your website who don’t care about your offers.”

The bottom line?

Make sure every post is written for your audience, not just for search engines.

If you love this no-fluff approach, you’ll also love my post on Email Marketing Myths: The Truth About What Actually Works in 2025 – because the same rule applies to email: the most important thing to focus on is building trust and serving your ideal client! Always.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 206

If you’re tired of shouting into the void and wondering why your list growth has stalled, this episode is for you.

Today we’re talking about that infuriating moment in business:

When you’re doing all the things…
Posting. Collaborating. Podcasting. Swapping freebies.
And still?
Crickets.
Your list isn’t growing. Your audience feels stale. And you’re wondering, is it me?

Let’s break this down and I’ll walk you through exactly what to look at, shift, or stop doing if you’re stuck in an audience growth plateau and thought “WTF do I focus on next?”

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why your audience hasn’t disappeared – but how you reach them has to evolve
– 3 reasons your old strategies (reels, bundles, FB groups) aren’t converting anymore
– 5 strategic shifts to refresh your visibility & attract the right people
– Why sometimes the smartest move is nurture, not more noise

Need help getting unstuck?

If this hit home and you’re ready to actually grow with intention (not more noise), here’s how I can help:

→ Book a Business Breakthrough – I’ll audit your visibility, list growth, and offer flow and give you a 3-step action plan to get unstuck fast.

→ Join The Email Growth Club – where we build simple, strategic list growth and nurture plans that actually work (and feel good doing it).

Why your list growth stalled (& why it’s not about you)

Before you scrap your offers or spiral into “maybe I’m just not cut out for this” territory – pause.
Your worth isn’t the problem. And it’s probably not your offer either.
The real culprits?

1. YOUR LEAD MAGNET ISN’T PULLING IT’S WEIGHT

If your freebie is too broad, too fluffy, or completely disconnected from what you sell, people will scroll right past it.

2. YOU’RE BLENDING IN

If your messaging sounds like every other “10 tips to grow your biz” post, you’re getting filtered out before you’re even noticed.

Your point of view matters more than ever.

3. YOU’RE BUSY, NOT STRATEGIC

Showing up everywhere ≠ growing your audience.
Are you actually visible in the right rooms with the right people?
Or just posting because Instagram told you to be consistent?

Why old strategies don’t work anymore

The online business world has changed – fast. What worked in 2022?
Pretty much dead in the water now.

  • Instagram reach is buried unless you’re dancing, trending, or paying.
  • Facebook groups are ghost towns unless hyper-niched.
  • SEO is slow as hell without fresh content and strong backlinks.

And the biggest shift?

WE’RE IN A TRUST RECESSION

People are skeptical, burnt out, and can smell a copy-paste tactic from a mile away.

They don’t want polished. They want personal.

Algorithms aren’t here to help you grow anymore, they’re here to make you pay.
If you’re still relying on old methods, no wonder you feel stuck.
Your audience hasn’t disappeared, but how you reach them has to change.

5 moves to get unstuck (& grow with intention)

Here’s exactly what I tell my clients inside The Email Growth Club and Headliner Mastermind when they’re stuck in an audience growth plateau:

✅ 1. REFRESH YOUR LEAD MAGNET POSITIONING

Don’t create a new one, reposition your best-performing freebie.
Ask yourself:

  • Does it solve a problem your ideal client knows she has?
  • Does it naturally lead to your paid offer?
  • Would you download it yourself if you saw it?

Reverse-engineer it from your paid offer if needed.

✅ 2. DO ONE HIGH QUALITY COLLABORATION

Not five bundles. Not a random summit.
One curated, strategic collab that borrows someone else’s trust – think:

  • A bundle with aligned experts
  • A co-hosted workshop
  • A podcast swap

✅ 3. TAP INTO SMALLER, MORE ALIGNED AUDIENCES

Forget going viral.

Focus on the right rooms:

  • Pitch 3 niche podcasts your ideal client actually listens to
  • Swap freebies or inbox features with biz friends
  • Personally share your freebie with warm DMs (no sleaze)

✅ 4. AUDIT THE HELL OUT OF YOUR CALL TO ACTION

Go look at your podcast outro, email signature, blog sidebar, IG bio.
Do you have ONE clear CTA, or are you throwing 7 links at people hoping something sticks?
Clarity converts.
Confused people don’t click.

✅ 5. DO REAL MARKET RESEARCH

Stop guessing.
Ask your people.

  • Run a quick survey
  • DM past clients
  • Ask what problem tipped them into saying yes

The gold you get from their words will tighten your messaging instantly.

The bottom line…

Audience growth isn’t about doing more.

It’s about doing the right things for the right people in the right way.

And sometimes?
The strategy isn’t to add more leads – it’s to nurture the ones already circling.

If you’re in a season of rest or recalibration, own that.

Deepen relationships with the people already in your world.

When you’re ready to push visibility again, it’ll land stronger.

Let’s make it happen.

Is she obsessively checking her inbox during nap time? Is she hanging out in a specific Facebook group or opening certain newsletters religiously? Stop building a soapbox and expecting her to fucking find it. Start walking into her world and meeting her where she already is. If you want to grow your audience, get in front of somebody else’s guest, teach, swap freebies.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:35]:
Get into her inbox through someone she already trusts. That is the fastest way to grow with intention. And then question number three. Do your lead magnets and messaging actually match? Let’s get spicy. If your freebie is another generic 10 tips to do X, Y and z checklist. Babe, she’s not fucking downloading it. She’s drowning in PDFs that she’s never even read. I want you to ask yourself, does your freebie solve a real problem she knows she has? That part is important.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:01]:
Is it so juicy that she would share it with her biz bestie? Does it naturally lead to the thing that you actually sell? Because if you’re just giving away something that has nothing to do with your offer, congratulations, you’ve just built a list of people who’ll never fucking buy anything from you and your copy. It needs more confidence. No more apologetic. If you want to speak like you know what the hell you’re fucking doing, because I can guarantee that you do. Oh, spicy. I told you. Now let’s talk strategy. So after you’ve asked yourself those questions, I want to go through some strategies that I recommend instead.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:33]:
So if your audience isn’t growing, this is what I suggest. Number one, refresh your lead magnet positioning. Don’t create a new one yet. Instead I want to take your current best performing free resource and ask, is it solving a problem my ideal client knows she has? Does it naturally lead into your signature offer like super clearly? And would you download this if you saw it in the wild? If not, it’s time to reposition it. Tweak the headline, shift the format, make it more specific and if you’re stuck, reverse engineer it. Start with the offer. Ask yourself what does somebody need to believe, understand or experience before they’re ready to buy this. Then turn that into your freebie.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:13]:
That is how you build a list of buyers, not just browsers. And then number two, do one high quality collaboration. Not five fucking bundles, not a summit and a giveaway in a random guest expert spot. One strategic collaboration that gets you in front of warm aligned already trusting you audience. A curated bundle with experts who serve the same client as you without competing. A co hosted workshop with someone whose audience needs what you do. A podcast swap where both of you send it to your lists and highlighted on socials. Stop trying to grow on your own.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:45]:
Get borrowed trust on purpose. The third thing that I want you to do is tap into smaller, more targeted visibility actions. This is not about going viral. This is about being in the right rooms, even if they’re small as fuck. Right? So I want you to pitch three niche podcasts where your dream client already listens with intent. Maybe you do two inbox swaps, freebie swaps with biz friends whose people need what you have to offer. Maybe you share your lead magnet with a warm dm. No sleaze, just, hey, I thought this might support you.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:12]:
This kind of micro visibility, it compounds over time. It brings in qualified people, the ones who are already looking for somebody like you. Number four, I want you to audit the hell out of your call to action. So let’s play a game. I want you right now. Press pause on this episode. Go and look at your podcast outro, your email signature, your blog sidebar, the link in your bio, literally anywhere that you show up online. And then I want you to answer honestly.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
Is there one clear action that you’re asking people to take or are you throwing seven fucking links at them and hoping for the best? Let me be clear. Clarity converts. Simplify your funnel. Point to one thing at a time and make sure it’s something that gets them closer to working with you. Confused people don’t click, they scroll away. Right? We have enough in our world that confuses us, that overwhelms us, that makes us feel like it’s all too much. Don’t be that person online for them. Clarity converts.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:07]:
And then number five, lastly, do some market research. Here is your reminder. If your messaging feels off, it probably is. You’re likely too close to your brilliance. You’re using expert language, too much AI, not your ideal client’s late night Google search language, right? So fix it at the source. Go out there and fucking ask your people. Literally run a survey, open a few DMs, start a conversation in your stories. Jump on zoom and talk to a human.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:32]:
Ask your past clients why they said yes. What tipped the scale? What words would they use to describe the problem before you solved it? The amount of gold you will get from these conversations is going to change absolutely everything for you. So let’s recap these five strategies that I recommend if your audience isn’t growing. 1. Refresh your lead magnet positioning. Don’t create a new one. Refresh the positioning. Number two, do one high quality collaboration.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:57]:
Not five bundles, not a summit and a giveaway. One strategic collaboration that gets you in front of warm aligned leads. Number three, tap into smaller, more targeted visibility. This is not about going viral. This is about being in the right rooms, even if they feel small as hell. Right? Number four, audit the hell out of your call to action. Make sure you have one clear action that you’re asking people to take wherever you’re showing up online. And then number five, do some market research.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:23]:
Go and talk to people, your ideal clients, so that you can tweak that messaging. The bottom line Here, audience growth isn’t about doing more, but it is about doing the right things for the right people in the right way. And sometime the strategy isn’t add more leads, it’s get sharper with the ones that are already circling. Also, can I say this? Sometimes your audience isn’t growing because you’re in a nurture season, not a growth one. That’s okay too. Make sure you’re going inward and see what kind of season you are in at the moment. Don’t try and force visibility if you yourself are craving rest. Instead, focus on deepening relationships with the people already in your world.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:00]:
When the season shifts, that’s when you can go out there and be more public and do another visibility push that it’s going to land so much stronger. So let me leave you with this. If your audience isn’t growing right now, it doesn’t mean you’re failing. It might just mean that you’re being invited to pause, pivot or simplify. Because your audience isn’t built by hustling harder, it’s built by getting clearer, bolder and more strategic with how you show up and what you say. And of course, if you need support figuring this out, come and join me inside the Email Growth Club where we build strategies that actually feel good. Or jump into one of my business breakthrough audits 44 and I’ll help you get clear on your best next step and audit the shit out of everything you’ve got going online. Links to both are in the show notes.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:44]:
Thank you so much for being here. I hope you got some value out of this episode and I can’t wait to share the guest expert that we have coming to your earbuds next week, Nadine. She is sharing all about how to write your best copy and finally build genuine connections with your audience. Trust me, it’s going to be one that you don’t want to miss. I will see you then. Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others.

Kylie Kelly [00:13:22]:
Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 205

Hey hey – welcome back to The Email Growth Show! I’m Kylie Kelly, your visibility coach, email marketing strategist, and biz bestie who’s here to help you grow an aligned, sustainable business… without burning the f*ck out.

And today?

We’re going behind the scenes of my Q3 plan.

I’m walking you through exactly:

  • What I’m prioritising
  • What I’m saying no to
  • And how I’m building this next 90 days to support both my growth and my energy

Because here’s the thing:

Just because something is a good idea… doesn’t mean it belongs in this quarter.
Just because you’re capable of more… doesn’t mean you have to do more.

If you’ve ever looked at a blank calendar and thought “WTF do I focus on next?” – you’re going to want to hit play on this one!

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why 90-day planning actually works (even for multi-passionate biz owners)
– What I’m prioritising this quarter: list growth, soft selling, repurposed content, and mastermind prep
– What I’m saying no to: live launches, IG hustle, and shiny new offers
– How to map your own Q3 based on your goals, energy, and season of life

Want help planning your quarter?

Book a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit: I’ll review your visibility, list growth, and offer flow, and send back a personalised action plan to help you move forward with confidence. Click here to grab your audit!

💌 Or come join us inside The Email Growth Club, where strategic planning, visibility, and list growth aren’t just buzzwords… they’re the damn plan. Check it out here!

Why I plan my business in 90-day cycles

Meet my AI biz bestie: Strategic Planner Sally!
She’s part COO, part coach, part “Kylie, don’t overcommit again” energy.

She helps me zoom out and plan every quarter with clarity, based on my visibility, offers, content rhythm, and energy.

Here’s why 90-day planning works so well:

→ It’s long enough to build momentum: to grow your list, test a funnel, or run a campaign… but short enough to stay agile.
→ It fits my Manifesting Generator energy: I move fast, I get excited, and I change my mind. So locking in a whole year? Nope.
→ Q3 is a recalibration season: After a big season with Inside The Inbox and my 40th birthday, I’m slowing things down and stacking what already works.

This quarter is all about conversion, consolidation, and clarity, not hustle, not chaos.

What I’m prioritising in Q3

Here’s what’s getting my full energy over the next 90 days:

1. List growth with integrity

No paid ads, no reels, no hamster wheel.

I’m keeping it simple and strategic:

  • Guest podcast interviews (5 booked!)
  • Freebie swap series with aligned partners
  • SEO refresh on 3 high-performing blog posts
  • Launching my new quiz in July

2. Selling The Email Growth Club (softly but consistently)

No launch needed.

Just a steady drip of value + intentional invites:

  • Highlighting member wins
  • Hosting two live workshops (list growth + nurture)

3. Prepping for Headliner Mastermind launch (October)

  • Locking in the messaging & positioning
  • Creating 3 new case studies to share online and on the podcast

4. Content with purpose

One podcast episode per week (on Fridays), then repurposed to:

  • A weekly email
  • SEO-optimised blog post
  • Strategic blog swap collabs with past partners

5. Space for real life

I’ve got school holidays, a silent retreat, and October travel on the horizon – so I’m building in the white space now, not scrambling later.

I’m not taking my foot off the gas.
I’m just learning to drive smarter.

What I’m not doing in Q3… and why that matters!

I planned this quarter to feel spacious, strategic, and seasonal, which means clearing out the clutter.

Here’s what I’m saying no to:

🚫 NO LIVE LAUNCHES

This quarter is about warming people up, not burning myself out.
Everything I’m doing, from the Lead Magnet Lovefest to the quiz funnel, is slow, strategic, and backend-driven.

🚫 NO POSTING JUST TO POST

Instagram? Still retired. 🙌
I’m showing up where it matters:

  • My podcast
  • My email list
  • Guest interviews
  • Strategic bundles + workshops

🚫 NO NEW OFFERS

Not even that tempting low-ticket idea I almost launched (don’t worry, I wrote it down for Q4 😂).

This quarter is about depth, not novelty.
I’m focused on the two core containers that actually move the needle:

The Email Growth Club: A monthly membership for business owners ready to grow their list, build connection, and sell with ease, without relying on social media or paid ads.

The Headliner Mastermind: A high-touch mastermind for bold women ready to become the go-to name in their niche through aligned visibility, strategic offers, and thought leadership.

What you can steal for your own Q3 plan

If we were planning your quarter together (which – if you’re in my world, we probably are 😏), here’s where I’d have you start:

1. Pick ONE list-growth strategy

Guest interviews? A curated bundle? Freebie swaps?
Pick one. Do it well. That’s it.

2. Choose a nurture rhythm that works for you

  • Weekly email?
  • Short-form private podcast?
  • Monthly roundup?

Whatever it is – make it sustainable and consistent.

3. Map your revenue path

What’s already working?
What feels heavy?
What are you selling and where’s the ease?

Simplify your offer suite now so Q4 isn’t chaos.

4. Schedule your damn rest

Block off a 3-day weekend.
Take a Friday for CEO time.
Rest is strategy. Don’t forget that.

5. Anchor everything to your Q3 goal

Visibility?
Cash flow?
Ease?

Write it down.
Revisit it.
Align your plan to it.

Wanna plan Q3 together?

If this episode gave you ideas, clarity, or just the permission slip you needed to slow down and do things smarter – I’d love to support you.

🎯 Book a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit: I’ll review your visibility, list growth, and offer flow, and send back a personalised action plan to help you move forward with confidence. Click here to grab your audit!
💌 Or come join us inside The Email Growth Club, where strategic planning, visibility, and list growth aren’t just buzzwords… they’re the damn plan. Check it out here!

Let’s make Q3 your most intentional, aligned, and wildly sustainable quarter yet.
You’ve got this and I’ve got you. 💪

Full Transcript:

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
So if you’re watching others spin up new things and feeling like maybe you should be doing more too, I really want to offer you this. Sometimes the most strategic move isn’t creating something new. It’s making what you already have even more powerful. For me, that’s what this quarter is all about.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:20]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Strategy Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:40]:
And the same is possible for you, too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:43]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:51]:
Hey. Hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show.
