And today, we’re going full behind the scenes. I’m walking you through exactly how I’m planning Q3 inside my business, what I’m prioritizing, what I’m saying no to, and how I’m making sure that the next 90 days support both my growth and my energy. Just because something is a good idea doesn’t mean it belongs in this quarter. And just because I’m capable of more doesn’t mean that I have to do more.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
So if you’ve ever looked at a blank calendar and thought, why the fuck do I focus on next? Or you’ve wondered how to get it all done and don’t kill yourself in the process, this episode is for you. Now, you’ve probably heard me talk about my AI biz bestie strategic planner Sally, the custom GPT that I created to help me zoom out and actually see my quarters before I try to fill it. She’s part coo, part coach, part Kylie don’t over commit again energy. And she helps me map out every 90 days with my visibility offers and content rhythm and most importantly, my energy levels in mind. Planning in 90 days is the perfect stretch. It’s long enough to build real momentum to run a campaign, test a new funnel, grow my list, make sales, but it’s also short enough to stay agile, to pivot if I need to breathe. Now, as a manifesting generator, this rhythm feels really good for me. I move fast, I get excited, I change my mind a lot.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:25]:
So instead of trying to lock in a whole year which never felt aligned anyway. I focus on this quarter and I build it in a way that reflects what I’ve already created, what’s light me up now, and what I want to lean into next. And this quarter Q3, it’s coming off the back of a big season I did Inside the Inbox Season 2 in May. My quiz funnel has just gone live and I’m intentionally slowing things down a little bit with a couple workshops, a quiet retention campaign for the Mastermind, and a fresh perspective after turning 40 last month. So here is how I’m treating Q3. It’s not a scale everything quarter. It’s not a launch heavy season, but I’m looking at it as a conversion and consolidation quarter. A quarter to support my people, to solidify what’s working and warm up for the next big move without burning myself out in the process.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:15]:
In short, I’m not creating anything from scratch. I’m stacking, I’m leveraging and I’m refining. So if you’re listening to this and thinking, ugh, I don’t even know what I’m doing next week, Kylie, let alone for the quarter, take this as your loving nudge to try it. Sit down, look at the next 90 days and ask yourself what? What am I already working towards? Where do I want to focus my visibility? What feels light and fun and what feels heavy? And what season of life am I in? How can I plan around that? Remember, you don’t have to plan the perfect quarter. You just need a plan that reflects the business and life you actually want. And if that feels hard to map out alone, you know where to find me. I’ve also included the link in the show notes to my custom GPT strategic planner Sally, so you can go and grab her for free and she will help you as well. Now let’s talk about what I’m prioritizing in Q3.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:06]:
So here are the big rocks for my Q3 that are going on in my world. So I’m focusing on list growth with integrity. Still no dancing, still no hamster wheel content, but I’m leaning into guest podcast interviews. I’ve got about five lined up. I’m leaning into a freebie swap series with some highly curated partners in Crime that I cannot wait to swap with. I’ve got an SEO refresh with a couple of the high performing blog posts and show notes that I want to give a little George and my new quiz has just gone live. So they are my list growth strategies that sounded like a lot but really, it’s just guest podcasting, a freebie swap, a little bit of SEO, and my new quiz lead magnet. My second focus is selling the email growth club softly but consistently.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:50]:
No big launch there, just a consistent drip of value and invitations. I want to start highlighting member wins better than I already do because they are having so many wins and making so much progress in that membership and I often forget to share about it. So I’m going to start highlighting member wins. I’m also creating two live workshops I want to do, one that is based around list growth and one that it’s based around nurture. When I put them out to my list, it will be what I call an option funnel. They’ll be able to either purchase the workshop by itself or join the membership to get the workshop for free. So they’re the two main ways that I’m mindfully going to be inviting people to come and join the membership. And then lastly, I’ll be preparing for my Headliner Mastermind launch in October.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:32]:
Now, I say launch lightly because the Mastermind is actually evergreen. It’s always open, it’s rolling, you can sign up at any time. But even with an evergreen offer, it’s really important to have periods where we have a focus on it, right? Where we’re actually intentionally selling it and inviting people inside. So that’s what’s going to happen in October. For Headliner, this means I need to finalize the positioning and the messaging and all of that beautiful copy that’s on the sales page and around that container. I’m also creating some case studies from the incredible women inside that again, have had some incredible wins. From securing TEDx stages and keynote speaking opportunities, to resigning from the their corporate job to go all in on their business, to scaling their team and hiring their first assistant. Some really, really exciting, exciting wins.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:17]:
So I’ll be creating some case studies with the ladies that are happy to do so. And I’m also obviously republishing those case studies here on the podcast as well. And then, as you guys probably know, I’ve gone back to just one podcast episode a week, which drops on Fridays. More intentional, more strategic. And then I repurpose that content to my email list and my blog post show notes that are optimized for SEO. So that will be continuing. I do every month of the year, rain, hail or shine. Right? So that’s really important to have something that is consistently going out.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:48]:
I’m also pitching a few women that I’ve collaborated with in the past for guest blog post swaps. Now this is something new that I’m trying and I’ve done it a couple of times now. And the whole goal with this is to have more and more reputable sites linking to mine so I can show Google that I am the real deal. Kind of a really fun, easy way to collaborate with somebody. So if you have a website, if you have a blog and it’s just your own content, think about maybe this strategy could work for you too. It’s very simple to get started. And other than that, I’ve got school holidays. I’m going to a silent retreat at the end of this month.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:22]:
So there’s a lot of travel coming up in October. So I’m intentionally building in space for rest and family time now in Q3 before things get full again, I’m not taking my foot off the gas, but I’m learning how to drive smarter. So let’s talk about what’s not on the calendar this quarter and why, what I’m choosing not to do. Because when I sat down with strategic planner Sally to map out Q3, I knew I wanted it to feel spacious, strategic and seasonal. This is a recalibration quarter for me. It’s not a sprint, not a try all the things season. It might be different for you, but for me it is not that. It’s all about staying rooted in what’s working and clearing the noise so that I can start Q4 feeling resourced, energized, focused and ready to fucking go.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:03]:
So here’s what I am intentionally not doing in Q3. I am not doing any live launches. So this is probably the biggest shift for me from the other quarters in the year. There’s no big public push. There’s no long email launch sequences, no open cart. Instead, everything that I’m doing from the lead magnet Love Fest in July that I’m hosting for members of the club to these workshops that I mentioned to the quiz, it’s all designed to warm up my audience, not hard pitch them. And why is that? Because I want to set the Runway for Q4 where I’m going to do that strategic headliner mastermind push and host the webinar to launch that right? So right now it’s all about visibility, nurture and backend conversions only. Slow burn, not flashy fireworks.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:47]:
I’ll still be making money. My business now runs pretty well on my reoccurring monthly revenue. So without doing any big pushes or any big launches, I have a pretty consistent income, which I am very, very grateful for. So this just means that any invitations that I make will be made personally, right? Be made through email, through one on one conversations. This still will be sales, but it’s just no big public push. And then obviously nothing else has changed in terms of how I show up. So I don’t post anywhere for the sake of it. My Instagram is still retired, my 9 grid is still up.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:22]:
And that’s plenty for me. I’m not creating anything just to be seen. I’m showing up where it matters, which for me is this podcast, my email list, those guest interviews. I think I’ve said yes to one or two bundles and obviously strategic visibility plays like my quiz and the workshops that I’m going to host. So the purpose of me sharing this with you is for you to think about how can you create depth over volume, which I think is something more of us need permission to do. You don’t need to be everywhere, you don’t need to say yes to everything. Instead pick one or two things and create depth, right? Show up really well there and really develop those relationships and you’ll be surprised at what can come from that. Another thing that I am not doing is no new offers.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
None. Not even a little low ticket thing I’ve been tempted to create. I have written it down for Q4, but for Q3 I’m holding my offers steady. Why? Because everything I’m doing is building towards two core containers. The email growth club where I support list growth, email strategy and visibility foundations. And of course the headliner mastermind where I help women become the go to name in their niche through aligned visibility offers and thought leadership. That’s it. Like I said, I’m choosing refinement over reinvention.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:33]:
So if you’re watching others spin up new things and feeling like maybe you should be doing more too, I really want to offer you this. Sometimes the most strategic move isn’t creating something new, it’s making what you already have even more powerful. For me, that’s what this quarter is all about. So for those that made it this far, I wanted to share what you can steal for your own Q3 plan. So if we were mapping out your quarter three together, which if you’re in the club or mastermind, I probably am here is exactly what I’d have you focus on. I want you to pick one list growth strategy, not 10, just one, I want to ask you, are you over committing to four summits, three bundles and launching a podcast all at once? I want you to take a deep breath. Don’t do that. Instead, pick one strategy that feels light, that feels aligned, that feels doable with the energy you actually have.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:20]:
Maybe like me, it’s guest podcasting four interviews in the next 90 days, right? Maybe it’s saying yes to one curated bundle with the right audience. Maybe it’s doing two to three freebie swaps or inbox collabs to start slow, right? The key is focus. When you pick one and do it with intention, you’re going to grow a more qualified list, not just a bigger1. The second thing I want you to do is decide how you’ll nurture. Most people think nurture means 52 pre written emails or a three part automation. It’s none of that. Your job is to build trust consistently and in your own voice. So choose a rhythm that feels doable and matches your strengths.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:58]:
Perhaps it is one thoughtful weekly email. Maybe it’s a short form private podcast. Maybe it’s a blog post or a podcast roundup once a month, or even just showing up on your existing podcast, but doing it with intention. Make sure going into quarter three that there is a clear way people can hear from you regularly and this is especially important if you’re planning to launch or sell strongly in quarter four. Make sure think nurture, nurture, nurture. How are you going to be intentionally building trust with the audience that you already have? And then number three, I want you to map your revenue streams. Where is your money actually coming from and what are you holding onto out of fear, guilt? Or maybe one day I want you to ask yourself what’s already working, what’s feeling heavy and where is the conversion happening with ease? Maybe this is the quarter you lean into low ticket workshops to build momentum. Or maybe you pause an old offer that hasn’t converted in six months and finally go all in on your membership or signature program.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:55]:
I want you to make it a focus to clean up your offer suite now so that you’re not scrambling mid launch in October. And then number four, I want you to plan your rest. Yes, actually block it out. Q3 tends to feel productive, but burnout can creep up if you don’t pause. So I want to make sure that you block off a three day weekend now, even if it’s to nap and read, put it in the calendar. I would encourage you to take one Friday a month off for CEO catch up days. And if you’re running events, schedule recovery time after them. That’s one of the hardest lessons that I learned after hosting my first summits was that they almost killed me.

Kylie Kelly [00:13:31]:
Schedule recovery time after them and I would even schedule in a massage. More white space equals more clarity every single time. Your business is going to thank you for it. And then lastly, I want you to anchor everything to your big goal. What is your intention in quarter three? Is it visibility? Then focus on list growth and nurture? Is it cash flow? Then get clear on your offer pathway and your pricing. Is it ease and simplicity? Then remove anything that feels like a should and learn to say no. Write down your big goal, put it on your wall, come back to it every week because your plan should serve that goal, not distract you from it. Now, if you’re still here with me, thank you so much for being here.

content:
Let’s talk email – and bust a few myths while we’re at it.

Because if I had a dollar for every time someone told me “email is dead,” I’d be sipping cocktails on a balcony somewhere bougie right now.

Truth is?

Email marketing is very much alive and still one of the highest-converting, most connection-building tools you can use.

But there’s a lot of bad advice out there.

So if you’re a creator or online biz owner trying to grow your list without burning out, this post is for you.

We’re cutting through the noise and clearing the air on what actually works (and what to ditch, like, yesterday).

In this post, you’ll learn:

  • What outdated email strategies to stop doing now
  • What modern email marketing really looks like
  • How to build trust and engagement through email, without burning out

Myth #1: You need a massive list to make email work

The truth: You don’t need 10k subscribers.

You need 300 right-fit humans who are obsessed with what you do.

A small, warm list of people who trust you will always outperform a cold list of randos who forgot why they signed up in the first place.

→ What works: Quality over quantity every single time. Focus on building genuine connections, showing up consistently, and delivering value that makes your people go, “omg I needed this.”

Myth #2: You have to email every day to stay top of mind

The truth: Unless you love writing daily emails (and your audience loves getting them), this is a one-way ticket to Burnoutville.

Sustainable > aggressive. Always.

→ What works: Find a rhythm that you can actually stick to. Weekly, fortnightly, whatever, just make it consistent. Your people don’t need you in their inbox every day… they just need you to be real when you do show up.

Myth #3: No one reads emails anymore

The truth: People still read emails. Especially when they’re thoughtful, value-packed, and sound like a real human wrote them.

ROI stats don’t lie – email marketing is still crushing it with an average return of $36 for every $1 spent. (Yeah, wild.)

→ What works: Skip the corporate vibes and speak from the heart.
Tell stories.
Share something useful.
Be a real f*cking human. That’s what people connect with.

Myth #4: Email funnels are gross & manipulative

The truth: A funnel is just a series of emails.

It’s not inherently sleazy – it’s how you use it that counts.

→ What works: Build trust. I treat my welcome sequences like a first coffee date. Real talk. Real value. Real connection.

No pressure. Just me being me and showing them how I can help.

Myth #5: One lead magnet is enough

The truth: One-size-fits-all freebies are not the vibe.

Your audience is multi-faceted. Their needs change. Your offers evolve. So yeah, your lead magnets should too.

→ What works: Create a few freebies that align with your core offers or content pillars. Test them. Update them. Make them work for you.

Let’s rewrite the rules…

You don’t need a massive list.
You don’t need to email daily.
You don’t need to feel icky about funnels or settle for freebies that don’t convert.

You just need a real strategy that feels good to you and a list full of humans who want to hear from you.

💬 So tell me: what email myth has been holding you back?

Slide into the comments, spill your tea, or reply to this post if you’re nodding along and ready to do email your way.

Not sure how to show up in a way that actually works for you?

Take my Visibility Personality Quiz and get your custom strategy in 2 minutes.
You’ll walk away knowing exactly how to grow your audience without burning out!

content:
Feat. Jillian Leslie

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 204

Ever created a freebie that felt a little… meh?

You poured time into it.
Designed the Canva PDF.
Maybe even followed a template from someone you admire.
But when you put it out there… crickets.

If you’ve been wondering why your lead magnet isn’t converting, this is the episode you need to hear.

In this candid conversation with the brilliant Jillian Leslie (OG blogger, tech founder, and queen of making business simple), we break down what actually makes a freebie irresistible – and the real reason most of them flop.

This isn’t just about slapping together another PDF.

It’s about triggering desire, solving real problems, and meeting your audience exactly where they are.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why most freebies don’t convert (and what to do instead)
– The 6 psychological purchasing triggers your offers must tap into
– How to make your lead magnet feel like a must-have, not a nice-to-have
– What to do if your current freebie isn’t working (without scrapping the whole thing!)
– Why simplicity beats polish every single time

Why Most Freebies Don’t Convert

According to Jillian, the freebies that convert aren’t the prettiest.

They’re the ones that solve a pokey problem – something your ideal client actually feels in their day-to-day life. We’re not talking vague “top 10 tips” here.

We’re talking:
“10 protein-packed foods to stock your fridge with so you stop stress-snacking at 3pm.”

The best freebies:

  • Trigger emotion
  • Solve one specific pain point
  • Are simple to consume
  • Lead directly into your paid offer

6 Must-Have Triggers for Any Freebie or Offer

If your freebie taps into at least one of these six purchasing triggers, you’re on the right track:

  1. Make money
  2. Save money
  3. Save time
  4. Move toward happiness
  5. Move away from pain
  6. Increase social status

Bookmark these.

Use them everywhere – in your freebie, your sales page, your emails.

They work.

Want the cheat sheet? Jillian shares it here: 👉 milotree.com/triggers

The Secret to a High-Converting Freebie?

We often think our freebie needs to prove our value. So we over-deliver.

We write 10-page ebooks. Record multi-module mini-courses. Add extra bonuses. Create complex designs.

But Jillian says what your audience actually wants?

A cheat sheet. A checklist. A quick win.

✨ Something they can use today.
✨ Something that makes them feel a shift – fast.

What if your current freebie isn’t working?

Here’s Jillian’s advice (and I couldn’t agree more):

🛑 Don’t burn it all down.
✅ Get curious.
✅ Ask yourself if it’s hitting one of those six triggers.
✅ Rewrite the way you talk about it.

And if in doubt? Ask ChatGPT.

Seriously. Dump your messy ideas in there. Ask it to simplify. To help you uncover the problem you actually solve. And to rework your copy through a new lens.

Another powerful takeaway from this episode?

Your freebie isn’t a stand-alone product.
It’s the first step in a journey.

If you don’t know where you want to lead people, your freebie is going to fall flat.

Jillian and I both teach this:
✨ Reverse engineer your lead magnet from your main offer.
✨ Make sure it solves the first problem your ideal client faces on their path to buying.

Your next step:

Ready to create a freebie that actually grows your list and leads to sales?

Here’s where to start:

1. Grab the Free Trigger Cheat Sheet
👉 Download Jillian’s 6 Purchasing Triggers and use them to assess your current lead magnet (or brainstorm a new one).

2. Audit your current freebie
Ask yourself:

  • Does this solve a pokey, specific problem?
  • Does it tap into at least one of the 6 triggers?
  • Is it fast + simple to consume?
    If not, it might be time for a refresh.

3. Reverse-engineer your lead magnet
Think about your core offer.
Then ask: What’s the very first step someone needs to take to be ready to buy it?
That’s your freebie.

4. Use ChatGPT as your co-creator
Got messy ideas? Voice dump them into ChatGPT and ask it to help you simplify, clarify, and connect the dots between your audience’s pain and your solution.

5. Keep it simple and hit publish
One page. One win. One problem solved.
Don’t wait for perfect – your people need help now.

Want to create a lead magnet that actually builds trust and makes sales?
Join The Email Growth Club and get my signature Freebie Flow training inside.

Jillian Leslie is the founder of MiloTree, a user-friendly software platform that helps online entrepreneurs sell digital products and grow their audiences with ease. She’s also the creator of Catch My Party, the largest party ideas site on the web.

As the host of The Blogger Genius Podcast, Jillian has spent the past six years interviewing hundreds of successful content creators, bloggers, and online business experts, always digging into what’s actually working behind the scenes.

content:
You don’t need more noise.
You need a visibility strategy that actually works – for you.

Because let’s be real: most of what’s out there about “getting seen” is just a fast-track to burnout.

Do more.
Post more.
Be everywhere.
Hustle harder.
And somehow… still feel invisible?

Nah. We’re not doing that anymore.

That’s exactly why I created the RISE Framework™ – a four-part approach to visibility that’s built on alignment, not anxiety. This is your roadmap to being seen, known, and trusted without selling your soul or sacrificing your sanity.

If you’re building a business that’s meant to support your life, not run it into the ground, keep reading.

Here’s what we’re going to cover in this blog post:

  • What the RISE Framework is and why it’s a total game-changer
  • How each pillar supports sustainable growth and visibility
  • How to figure out where you are (and what to focus on next)

What the heck is the RISE Framework?

It’s not just a method – it’s a movement.
The RISE Framework is a holistic, aligned approach to visibility and audience growth that doesn’t force you into strategies that feel off-brand or off-balance.

It’s built around one truth I know from working with clients across the board:

→ Real, sustainable success happens when your visibility strategy, your business model, and your mindset are working together, not competing for your energy.

The RISE Framework isn’t a checklist.

It’s a flow.

Let’s break it down (first this is what it looks like you so can visualise how this works!)

REACH: Get in Front of the Right People

This pillar is all about being seen, but not just by anyone.

REACH is about getting in front of aligned audiences. The people who are already looking for what you do and are ready to hear it.

Think: bundles, summits, podcast guesting, creative collabs that light you up.

This isn’t about chasing clout or empty recognition.

It’s about putting yourself in spaces where your dream clients are already paying attention.

⚡️ Hot tip: You don’t need 10k followers. You need 10 right-fit humans who give a shit.

INFLUENCE: Keep ‘Em Close AF

REACH brings people in.
INFLUENCE keeps them close.

This is where we build trust, nurture connection, and make your content actually convert.

No more yelling into the void. We’re talking consistency, storytelling that sticks, and a nurturing strategy that feels like you.

Email. Socials. DMs. Whatever your jam – INFLUENCE is about showing up like the damn expert you are and making sure your people know it.

Because visibility without influence? Is just background noise.

SCALE: Grow With Systems, Not Stress

Let’s ditch the one-hit wonders and build something that lasts.

SCALE is about creating repeatable, rinse-and-repeat systems that work while you rest. Visibility rhythms that don’t drain you. Funnels that flow. Offers that support your big-picture goals (and your real-life schedule – we love AND need that!)

You don’t need to be “on” 24/7.
You need systems that do the heavy lifting so you can breathe.

EMPOWER: Step Into Your CEO Era

This is the mindset piece and it matters big time.

EMPOWER is about owning your expertise, raising your standards, and making decisions like the leader you are. It’s about alignment, boundaries, bravery, and finally letting go of the shit that’s keeping you small.

You’re not here to play cute.

You’re here to lead.

And this pillar?

Is where your visibility starts to feel f*cking powerful.

The RISE Framework in Action

Each pillar builds on the next and when they work together, that’s when the magic happens. Whether you’re stuck at the starting line or scaling up fast, the RISE Framework gives you a clear AF way to grow your audience and your impact without sacrificing your peace.

This is the foundation I use with every client.
It’s how I went from “who the hell is she?” to booked out with dream humans who found me through smart, aligned visibility.

Wanna Know Where You Are in the RISE Flow?

Let’s figure it out – together.

Grab one of my Business Breakthrough audits for just $44 and let me review everything you have going on (or perhaps not going on) and give it to you straight. I’ll tell you exactly what I would do if I were in your exact shoes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFO: Business Breakthrough
Spots are limited, ‘cause my calendar is real human-sized.

Final thoughts…

You’re not “Too Late” – You’re just not aligned (yet!)

If visibility has felt overwhelming, exhausting, or straight-up not worth it, I see you.
You’re not doing it wrong.
You’ve just been sold a strategy that doesn’t fit you.

The RISE Framework is your permission slip to grow differently.
To grow better.
With strategy, alignment, and actual joy.

And if you’re ready to build a visibility plan that feels like freedom?

Well, you know where to find me.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 203

You know that buzz you feel after your list has grown from a summit, a bundle, a podcast guest appearance, or a powerful freebie?

That yes, people are here! kind of buzz?

But then comes the question:

Now what?

If you’ve ever stared at your email dashboard and thought, “What do I send them now?” – this blog post is for you.

Because here’s the truth:

List growth isn’t the problem.

It’s what you do next that actually matters.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The biggest mistake most business owners make after growing their list
– How I personally onboard and nurture new subscribers after a bundle or summit
– 3 things you must do within 7 days of someone joining your list
– Why trust (not automation) is your most powerful conversion tool
– How to shift from “list-building mode” to sustainable connection and conversion

Your next step:

If you’ve recently grown your email list – from a summit, a bundle, a podcast feature – and you’re wondering what to do next, this is your invitation to stop overthinking and start building real relationships.

✨ Ready for support that goes beyond the algorithm?
Come join me inside The Email Growth Club, where we map out your nurture strategy together, with templates, tools, and real-time coaching to help you turn subscribers into super fans.

Or if you’d rather talk it out 1:1 –
→ Apply for a free 30-minute Visibility Audit Call and I’ll help you create a post-growth plan that’s simple, strategic, and totally aligned with you.

→ Click here to apply for a free visibility audit
→ Or join The Email Growth Club here

Because subscribers don’t convert from funnels alone –
They convert from connection.

1. The Most Common Mistake After Growing Your List

We work hard to grow our lists.

We show up.
We collaborate.
We pitch ourselves for summits, bundles, and podcasts. We swap freebies with biz besties.

And then the subscribers roll in…and we freeze.

We ghost.
We overthink.
We let the connection go cold.

Or worse – we wait until launch time and pop into inboxes with a pitch and a prayer.

Sound familiar?

Trust me, I’ve done it too. But I’ve learned (the hard way):

Trust has a shelf life.
And if you’re not showing up soon after someone joins, that trust expires fast.

2. My Go-To Post-Event Nurture Strategy

After Inside The Inbox Season 2, over 700+ new subscribers joined my world. Here’s exactly what I did to nurture them and what you can try too:

1. I skipped the welcome sequence (kind of)

Instead of a 5-email funnel, I sent one curated “Start Here” email.

It included:

  • A warm intro and what I’m about
  • A “Start Here” list of my best resources
  • A behind-the-scenes personal note
  • A direct invitation to hit reply
  • A soft invite to my membership or mastermind

Why?

Because I send a lot of real-time emails. I don’t want new subscribers stuck in automation while all the juicy, relevant stuff is happening live.

Want to try this?
Create one juicy, helpful, human email that gives new subscribers what they need right now.

2. I personalised their journey

If someone joined from a speaker like Cat Griffin during the bundle, I followed up with list-growth resources.

This makes the experience feel tailored and intentional.

It shows I’m paying attention – not just throwing content at them.

3. I gave them something bingeable

Think: podcast episode, case study, or even a juicy behind-the-scenes voice note.

Let them feel your voice and value.

It helps build that relationship from the jump.

4. I invited a conversation

Seriously.
I just asked them to hit reply.
It doesn’t have to be a big thing.

A simple, “Tell me where you’re at” or “I’d love to hear what you’re working on” goes a long way.

3. Why Your List Might Not Be Converting (Even If It’s Growing)

Here’s the thing:

  • It’s not your open rate
  • It’s not your lead magnet
  • It’s not even your offer

It’s likely that you just haven’t been nurturing.

It’s not a launch issue.
It’s a relationship issue.

People forget fast.

And if they haven’t heard from you in weeks or months, they don’t trust you enough to buy. Yet.

Want to hear more on this?
Check out [Episode 144 with Sophia Parra] – we talk all about how to build intimacy and spark real conversations with your list.

4. Reframe: Your List Is Not a Number

You don’t have “327 subscribers.”

You have 327 humans with inboxes full of noise.

Busy lives.
Big dreams.
And they want to trust you – but only if you show up like a real person.

Write to her.

The one who’s still here.

The one who’s opening your emails.

She matters.

Ready to Make That List Growth Actually Convert?

If you’ve just grown your list, amazing.

Now let’s make it mean something.

Join me inside The Email Growth Club to get:

  • My plug-and-play Start Here email template
  • My nurture email framework
  • Real-time coaching and support

OR apply for a free Visibility Audit Call and let me help you map out what to send, what to skip, and what will actually convert.

Either way?

Let’s stop wasting list growth and start turning subscribers into super fans.

The main thing I want you to get is that you’re welcoming them, you’re making them feel seen, you’re referencing where they’ve come from, you’re Giving them more value and you’re inviting them to start a conversation. This is how we make a fantastic first impression. So if you’re like, oh my God, Kylie, that feels really overwhelming.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:57]:
I wanted to break down what you do next. So the next time that you are going to be in a summit a bundle, you have a podcast guest spot coming up, you’re doing a freebie. So whatever it looks like for you, I want you to make sure that every new subscriber gets a personal welcome email. Make sure that your email service provider is set up to use their first name if possible, share something behind the scenes. Invite them to tell you where they’re at. Start the conversation. If you can, send them to one high value resource, something that shows your personality and helps them think. A fun quiz, a mini training, a case study, a podcast episode, don’t overthink it.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:34]:
But one high value resource is, is what you should be linking them to. And then I want you to also introduce your paid work gently. Not a hard sell, but a soft like if this resonated, you might also love. We’re not hiding the fact that we sell things right. We are a business, we are not a hobby. We are here to make money. If we can get money into the hands of more great women, I know great things will happen. So we want to make sure that we are making it very clear that we are here to sell as well.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:59]:
So make sure you are introducing your paid work gently and let them know this is how I can help you. Here’s what that looks like and here is what to do next. Don’t overthink it. Keep it simple, human and strategic. And if you need to follow this step by step, if you need to look at the notes, please go over to the show notes for this episode on my website because I have listed this out step by step in a blog post for you. Now, I see a lot of people focusing on email list growth, on audience growth, which is fantastic as what I teach. Highly recommend that you were growing your audience, especially in between your launches or in between your selling periods. Right? But not all email lists convert, even when they’re growing.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:40]:
And I wanted to call that out with love, but also with honesty. It is not your open rate, it is not your lead magnet, and no, it’s not the size of your list either. The real problem I see far too often is that you haven’t nurtured the relationship. I see it all the time. And babe, let me say this with zero judgment because I’ve absolutely been there. But you do the thing. Maybe you speak at a summit, you join a bundle, you run a free challenge or launch that shiny new quiz. Your list grows, you’re riding that fucking dopamine wave high.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:08]:
And then crickets. You don’t email them for a week and then it’s two. Or maybe it’s been three months and suddenly you’re asking people to buy from you and you’re shocked when they don’t. It’s not a launch issue, it’s a relationship issue. You wouldn’t meet someone once, ghost them for months, and then ask them to invest in your signature offer. And yet, that’s exactly what most business owners do with their email list. So what does real relationship first nurture actually look like? Let me give you some ideas that you can literally swipe and use this week. It’s a behind the scenes build with me email, right? Tell your email list what you’re working on, what’s messy, what’s coming up.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:43]:
This is going to build anticipation and trust. Maybe it’s a quick win tip that’s hyper specific. Not three ways to grow your email list, but something like the exact subject line I use that got a 51.2% open rate last week. Obviously that’s my own example. But think about how you can get hyper specific and include a quick win tip in your next email. Maybe it’s a podcast episode that deepens the conversation. For example, episode 144 is all about how to nurture your email list and start conversations with Sophia Parra. If you haven’t listened to that one, please do now.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:16]:
This is an example, but this is actually true. In that episode, Sophia shares some brilliant ways to invite replies, create intimacy, and use your emails to spark real conversations. Not just clicks, but actually connection. So again, I think you should go and listen to episode 144 after this. Maybe you choose to nurture them with a voice note style email. Something raw and real that starts with I wasn’t going to send this or Can I be honest with you? Or maybe it’s a story led email with a soft call to action. Tell a short true story and gently point to how your offer solves that deeper pain behind it. Subtle, not sleazy.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:50]:
The bottom line is nurture doesn’t have to mean 52 weeks of mapped content, but it does mean showing up. It means being in their inbox when you’re not selling. It means building a relationship where people want to hear from you, not just tolerate your next p. Because as I said before, trust has a shelf life. And without nurture, it expires fucking fast. So if your list, if your audience isn’t converting right now, don’t overhaul your funnel, don’t scrap your offer, don’t assume you need more people, start nurturing the ones you already have. And of course, if you want support doing that, this is exactly what we do inside the email growth club. There’s a whole module in there about relationship based nurture, including how to write re engagement emails, how to repurpose content from your podcast or blog, and how to use simple frameworks that save you time.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:36]:
Your people are waiting to hear from you. Please, for the love of Taylor Swift, do not keep them waiting. And lastly, I just wanted to talk quickly, before we wrap this up, about how your list is not a number. We need to talk about this because it is so easy, especially when we’re in a growth season, to reduce our list to a dashboard stat. 327 subscribers. 3,000 subscribers. 10,452 subscribers. Like whatever it is, right? But here’s what I need you to remember.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Your list is not a number. It’s not a vanity metric. It’s not just a launch audience. It’s not just email real estate. It’s living, breathing humans with inboxes full of noise, with families and full calendars. With hopes, fears and decisions they haven’t even made yet. With goals that they’re scared to say out loud, but that your work could actually help them reach. And every time that you show up in their inbox, you have a choice.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:27]:
You can either be more noise or you can be the one email they actually want to open. You can either ask for the sale without context, or you can build that kind of relationship that makes the self feel like it’s the next right step. Your words are powerful. Your stories are sticky. Your voice is fucking magnetic. And when you treat your email list like the community that it is instead of a cold marketing channel, everything will change, babe. Everything. Because trust doesn’t happen from one launch.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:55]:
It doesn’t come from a perfectly polished funnel. It doesn’t happen when you write like a marketing robot trying to get one more sale. Trust is built one email at a time, one story at a time, one perspective at a time, one real moment that makes someone and go like, ha, she gets me. So no matter what your list size is today, I want you to zoom in. Don’t write to your audience. Write to her. That one woman who’s thinking about giving up, that one woman who’s craving some clarity, that one woman who needs to feel seen and not sold to. That is the magic of email.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:27]:
That is what we’re here to do. And if you’ve been stuck in the trap of my list is too small to matter, please hear me when I say it matters more than ever. Show up, serve, speak like you, speak like a human. And trust that those 327 people, they’re listening and they’re the exact right foundation for everything that you want to build Next. So if you’ve just grown your email list, congrats. Now let’s make that growth mean something. If you need support crafting your nurture sequence, planning your email content, or just figuring out what the heck to say next next, come and join me inside the Email Growth club. Or if you want one on one eyes on your strategy.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:05]:
I would love to invite you to apply for a free visibility audit where I can help you map out what to send, what to skip and what will actually move the needle. Both of the links are in the show notes. More than anything, I want you to stop wasting list growth and start turning those subscribers into super fans. Thank you again for being here, my love. I have so much love for you. I am cheering you on always and I see you next week. Bye for now.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:28]:
Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 202

There’s a season no one warns you about in business.

You’re not failing…
But things aren’t really working either.

You’re showing up.
You’re launching.
You’re tweaking the funnel [again].
You’re sending the emails.

And somehow, it all still feels… flat.

This episode was born from a client call where she didn’t want another strategy, another idea, or another “just push through it” pep talk.

She wanted permission.

So today, I’m giving it to you too.

Because pausing isn’t quitting – and honestly?
It might be the most strategic move you make this year.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

[00:00:00] I don’t think most women in business need another strategy. I think they need to loosen their grip on timelines, on expectations, on proving that the last investment that they made wasn’t a mistake. Today I’m gonna be talking to every woman that has been burnt by a mastermind and kept going. Anyway, I’m also gonna share a really personal story of my own mastermind drama that I’ve never brought to the podcast.

[00:00:22] So buckle in. Let’s get started.

[00:00:25] Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the email growth show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for YouTube.

[00:00:49] Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

[00:00:56] Hey. Hey, welcome back to the email growth show. I am so [00:01:00] excited that you’re here. So this episode is for the woman who’s invested before she’s shown up before, she has trusted a room, a mentor, a promise, and walked away tighter and not lighter. It’s also for the woman who isn’t burnt out, but is definitely overworking.

[00:01:16] Let’s talk about both here is what I’m noticing. A lot of smart, capable business owners are working really hard. Really hard, not falling apart. They’re not chaotic. They’re just constantly gripping. Gripping the plan, gripping the data, gripping the strategy, gripping the outcome, and when things don’t move fast enough.

[00:01:40] The instinct is to grip tighter, right? To invest again, to push harder, to stay longer, to prove something, especially if you’ve been burnt before. That’s why this idea of a clenched fist hit me so deeply because a clenched fist can work, but it can’t receive. And I realized [00:02:00] honestly, that I do this too. I hold tightly to my timelines, my expectations, my definition of success, the numbers, the metrics, the proof when sometimes what the business actually needs is just for me to breathe, to slow down, to open that clenched fist and actually receive, not to stop caring, but to stop forcing. A lot of us have been disappointed. A lot of us have been burnt by masterminds or group coaching or coaches or investments before. If you’ve learned the hard way that not every shiny room is safe, your nervous system learns to protect you.

[00:02:37] So gripping harder feels responsible. It feels smart, it feels like you’re in control, but over time, it also makes growth heavier than it needs to be. Now I wanna share a little context here because this didn’t come from nowhere for me. My very first mastermind experience was back in 2021. It was with someone who was very Instagram famous in the online space at the [00:03:00] time.

[00:03:00] I listened to her podcast and I joined full of trust, full of belief, full of excitement. I stayed for over a year, and I even renewed after that and became alumni, and over that time. Oh, fuck. I got burnt bad, not in a like dramatic public way, but in a really quiet, painful way. Ideas that I’d shared were taken and passed off as her own.

[00:03:24] The boundary between friend and client became blurred, and when my personal life went through a genuinely hard financial season, there was no softness. There was no compassion, no empathy. There was just the contract, and look, I signed it. I wasn’t asking for special treatment, but what broke something in me was that realization that I wasn’t actually valued as a person in her space.

[00:03:45] I was a number, I was a transaction, I was a seat. And for somebody that feels things deeply, which I am, I’m a total empath, that really hurt me, especially because I’d been led to believe that we were friends. So the deeper lesson here is [00:04:00] that that experience changed how I show up in business.

[00:04:03] It taught me that proximity doesn’t equal care. It taught me that access doesn’t equal safety. And also that success doesn’t mean somebody has integrity. When you have been burned like that, when you’ve been hurt deeply by somebody like that, you do grip harder.

[00:04:18] Next time you watch more closely, you protect yourself. You stay longer than you should. You tell yourself, I just need to make this work. And that’s not weakness, like that’s self protection.

[00:04:29] And that’s what our nervous system is wired to do. That is a good thing. so this week I just wrapped up my third empire expansion event. It was amazing. The women inside that room were incredible. We had some great connection, some great conversation, and it honestly filled me up.

[00:04:46] At the end of day two, I said to my husband like, oh my gosh, this is what I was made to do. Like I loved it so much, but it was interesting ’cause there was a theme that came out of day one especially, and. Not that anybody that came to the event was burnt [00:05:00] out. They were definitely functioning. They’re capable, they’re ambitious, but they were overworking so incredibly much.

[00:05:08] and a lot of it in invisible ways. There was a lot of overthinking. There was over efforting, there was overhold, and that clenched fist energy slowly teaches our body that growth needs strain, right? That growth requires that overworking when actually. It doesn’t, and when we are used to that, when we’re wired for that,

[00:05:28] , when our past experience, whether that’s the past six months, two years, or whatever, when our past experience has told us that that is what we need to do when opportunities show up, when support is available, receiving feels unsafe. So I wanted to speak to any of the women listening that have been burnt by a mentor, a mastermind, a coach, anyone in the online space specifically before, I just want you to hear this.

[00:05:54] Just because you were burnt doesn’t mean you were bad at choosing, right? It just means that you were more discerning now, which is a [00:06:00] fantastic thing. At a certain level of business, you don’t need louder height, more content, or bigger rooms. You need safety. You need clarity. You need collaboration and relationships, and you need leadership that doesn’t disappear when things get human or when life starts to life because it is bound to happen, right?

[00:06:20] That is not being difficult, that is just being experienced. So I wanna wrap this conversation up with this thought, and this is a thought that I keep coming back to. Growth, actually doesn’t respond to pressure. It responds to clarity. And clarity often comes when you loosen your grip.

[00:06:40] When you open your hand, right, when you stop forcing timelines, when you stop proving, when you stop staying out of obligation. An open hand doesn’t mean giving up. It means that you’re trusting that you don’t have to strangle your business to make it grow. So this is also why I’ve built my work the way I have.

[00:06:59] I have [00:07:00] smaller rooms now. I have clearer expectations. I have real conversations. Human support, not keep up or fall behind, not performance, not pretending we’re friends when the money is the only thing holding us together. And that’s an episode all for its own, I think. But I never want someone in my world to feel like a number.

[00:07:20] I actually had one of our celebration calls, which is like the wrap up calls I do with every attendee after the empire expansion events. I actually had one of them yesterday. It was the first one out of the group that I’d had and. The attendee said something so beautiful to me. Towards the end of the call, she said, you were the first coach.

[00:07:37] You were the first mentor that I’ve actually felt safe with, that my nervous system has actually felt safe with, and I got emotional. Like I could have started crying on the call because that is exactly the type of feeling. That I want people to know they can have with me. I want the women that I’m working with to feel safe with me, to know that they’re safe with me, to be able [00:08:00] to breathe and relax and loosen their grip and open their hand, and then we work together and they get to receive.

[00:08:06] Like that is the experience that I’m going for. And to hear that mirrored back from somebody that was at the event Was everything that little testimonial or mention in that conversation meant more to me than. the flashy income claims, right? Like I’ve got those two. Like, yes, my clients have three times their revenue, have hit milestone months have grown their email list by 300%. Like whatever. Like, I’ve got all of those, but to me it’s more about how do they feel?

[00:08:33] And if somebody can feel safe, then fuck yeah, we can go after all of those business goals and we can get them, But how they feel is everything. I never want somebody in my world to feel like a number. So in closing, if you’ve ever been burnt before, if you’re listening to this, please don’t harden.

[00:08:47] Please don’t close. Please don’t grip so tightly that nothing you can reach you. And if you are working really hard right now, if you know that you are exhausted in your bones and you are pushing whatever you can uphill, you’re not falling apart, but you’re [00:09:00] holding everything And your knuckles are turning white.

[00:09:03] This is your permission to soften the grip this year. This is your permission to open your palm to breathe, to let support land instead of forcing it progress. Trust me my love. You do not need to push harder. You might just need to receive a little bit differently. Alright, that is all for me this week.

[00:09:20] Thank you so much for trusting me with this conversation and thank you for being the kind of woman who’s willing to lead with both wisdom and heart. I love you so much. I’m so grateful that you are here, and I will see you next week. Alright, bye for now.

[00:09:34] Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others.

[00:09:51] Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you, who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their [00:10:00] business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening, and I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why we don’t talk enough about the in-between seasons of business (& how they impact your mindset)
– What I learned from a client who swapped urgency for a Pause Plan – and finally started breathing again
– What a Pause Plan could look like (real examples + low-pressure ideas)
– How to know if you’re truly in burnout – or just disconnected from your own voice
– Why pausing isn’t quitting (and how to reconnect with your business without pushing harder)

Your next step [when you’re ready]

If you want clarity without burning yourself out, this is exactly what my Business Breakthrough Audit is for.

I’ll personally review your visibility, offers, and email strategy — and send you a clear, grounded 3-step plan for what actually makes sense next.

👉 Book your Business Breakthrough Audit here

And no – it’s not about doing more.
It’s about doing the right things, in the right season.

P.S. If this post felt like it was written for you, it was.
Pause. Reset. Then, when you’re ready – book your Business Breakthrough Audit here.

The sneaky season no one talks about

This isn’t full-blown burnout.

It’s worse.

It’s that quiet, in-between season that whispers things like:
“You should be further along by now.”
“Why does this feel so hard?”
“Why does it look easier for everyone else?”

Your revenue is okay-ish.
Your list is growing slowly.
Your offers technically exist.

But inside?
You’re exhausted. Second-guessing everything. Wondering if you’re the problem.

I’ve been there. More than once.

And here’s the truth no one tells you – just because you can push through, doesn’t mean you should.

The client call that cracked this wide open…

This client had done everything right.

Offers built.
Membership launched.
Bundles. Summits. Visibility. Consistency.

And her first words on our call?

“I’m tired… and I don’t know what else to try.”

She wasn’t asking for ideas.

She was asking for permission to stop forcing things.

So instead of fixing her funnel, we built something else entirely – a pause plan.

No KPIs.
No relaunch.
No 20-email sales sequence.

Just space.

What a strategic pause actually looks like

This wasn’t “burn it all down” energy.

It was intentional AF.

Here’s what she kept:
– Her podcast [because it still felt good]
– One email a week [no pressure to sell]
– Pinterest running quietly in the background

Here’s what she let go of:
– Live membership calls no one was attending
– Being “on” every day in Slack
– Forcing offers that felt heavy

And just like that?

Her body softened.
Her energy shifted.
She could feel again.

That’s the part no one tells you – clarity doesn’t come from pushing harder. It comes from creating space.

Your business isn’t a machine – it’s a garden

We love pretending business is math.

Audience + funnel + nurture = sales.

But it’s not that clean.

Your business has seasons.

And if everything feels heavy right now, it doesn’t mean you’re broken.
It might just mean you’re in winter.

Things are meant to rest.
Some things are meant to die off.
So new things can actually bloom.

Pausing isn’t quitting.
Pausing is strategic.

A gentle pause plan you can steal

If you’re scared of losing momentum, try this instead:

– Pick one platform you still enjoy [podcast, newsletter, YouTube]
– Send one email a week… no selling, just connection
– Scrub your email list [smaller + stronger beats big + disengaged]
– Stop creating new offers for now
– Ask yourself daily: what actually feels good?

Start there.

When the energy returns – and it will – you’ll know exactly what to build next.

You’re not behind. You’re human.

If you’ve been forcing, tweaking, showing up, and trying…
And it still isn’t working?

It’s not because you suck at business.
It’s not because your audience hates you.

It’s because you’re tired.

And you’re allowed to rest without losing your dream.

A Grounded Next Step

If this resonated and you’re craving clarity on what to keep, what to pause, and what actually matters next, this is exactly what my Business Breakthrough Audit is designed for.

It’s a calm, personalised review of your business – without pressure to push or overhaul everything.

Just clear perspective.
Supportive direction.
And permission to choose what fits now.

You’re not quitting.
You’re recalibrating.

And that might be the most powerful move you make this year.

Feat. Email marketing and funnel strategist, Allison Hardy

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 201

Let’s be real: If you’re exhausted by the algorithm and wondering if bundles are worth the hype… this case study is going to blow your mind.

Alison Hardy – email marketing strategist, mom of two, and all-around badass – used my Bundle Like a Boss system inside The Email Growth Club to grow her list from 4,000 to over 10,000 engaged subscribers.

No paid ads.
No dancing on Reels.
No burning out.

Just a repeatable system that works.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, Alison breaks down exactly how she did it and why she now runs multiple bundles every year with ease (and epic ROI).

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Allison used a bundle strategy to drive thousands of targeted email signups.
– She repurposed existing freebies instead of creating new ones, keeping it simple and sustainable.
– Her success came from choosing the right bundles: aligned audience, high-quality curation, and visibility beyond just opt-ins.
– She nurtured new subscribers with intention, showing up, sharing stories, and building connection from day one.
– No ads. No dancing reels. Just relationship-first growth that feels aligned and gets results.

Allison Hardy’s strategy for email list growth without ads

Alison had been using Facebook ads and dabbling in summits, but she craved faster, more sustainable list growth.

“I was spending either a ton of money or a ton of time. Bundles gave me a way to grow without sacrificing both.”

After participating in a couple of my bundles and seeing opt-ins jump from 150… to 300… she had a lightbulb moment: “If I’m getting this much growth as a contributor, what would happen if I hosted my own?”

Spoiler alert: She hosted her first bundle in December 2020 and hit 1,200 subscribers in five days.

Implementing bundles for email list growth

In 2024, Alison ran eight bundles, some broad, some niche, and every one taught her something new.

  • Which topics convert best
  • How list quality matters more than quantity
  • Why niching down leads to better leads and higher revenue

By the end of the year, she’d grown her list to over 10,000 subscribers and was generating consistent sales from her email funnel.

“I finally had a program I knew worked. I just needed more people to see it.”

Bundles helped her do just that and now she’s hosting 3 more in the next two months.

The real secret? The bundle marketing system.

Allison didn’t reinvent the wheel. She used the Bundle Like a Boss dashboard inside The Email Growth Club and followed it step by step.

“Once I figured out the process, it was easy to not only use your system but also make it my own.”

The structure gave her freedom to play with topics (like her new AI bundle!), test different contributor sizes, and create a rinse-and-repeat growth engine.

And the ROI? “For the amount of work I put in, it was like tenfold. More signups. More sales. Way less stress.”

More bundle tips from Allison:

Here’s Allison’s advice (and I couldn’t agree more):

💡 Start small – 10 contributors is enough for your first try.
💡 Get super niche – broad topics = more unsubscribes.
💡 Ask for referrals – contributors love recommending others (and it expands your reach!).
💡 Track what works – test and tweak as you go.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 200

Two hundred episodes.

That’s 200 times I’ve hit record – in between school pickups, late at night, or pacing the floor with a million doubts in my head.

200 times I’ve spoken directly to you – the female founder building something bold in a world full of noise.

And today, I’m sharing what I know for sure after 200 episodes, hundreds of hours behind the mic, and years of building a business that’s designed to last.

Because if you’ve ever found yourself wondering…

“Is this worth it?”
“Am I doing it right?”
“Why is this taking so long?”

…this post is for you.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The 10 biggest lessons I’ve learned after 200 podcast episodes (yep, all the juicy ones)
– Why audience growth without alignment will burn you out – fast
– What I’d focus on first if I were starting my business from scratch in 2025
– The visibility strategies I wish I’d tried sooner (and the ones I’d leave behind)
– How podcasting has shaped my voice, my business, and my confidence as a thought leader

Your next step:

If you’re building a business that feels different – slower, more personal, less about perfection – this episode is your permission slip to keep going.

✨ Ready for support that actually meets you where you are?
Come join me inside The Email Growth Club or book a free 30-minute Visibility Audit Call and let’s build a strategy that fits YOU.

→ Click here to apply for a free visibility audit
→ Or join The Email Growth Club here

Because if there’s one thing I’ve learned in 200 episodes… it’s this:
You’re not behind. You’re just building something that actually lasts.

1. You Don’t Have to Be Loud – Just Consistent

I didn’t start this podcast with a fancy launch plan or a content calendar.

I started it with a message – and a mic.

Some episodes were recorded in the car. Others after bedtime. Many with no idea if anyone would actually care.

But I kept going.

And here’s what I’ve learned:

You don’t need to be the loudest. You just need to show up.

This podcast has brought in coaching clients, mastermind members, summits, collaborations, friendships – but more than that? It’s built trust.

Because when you show up consistently with real value, honesty, and a little fire in your belly… people remember. This is visibility that lasts.

2. Email Is Still My Ride-Or-Die

Let’s talk inbox.

After working with hundreds of women and writing thousands of emails, I can tell you this with total certainty:

  • Your list doesn’t need to be big. It needs to be alive.
  • Email is where connection turns into conversion.
  • Templates won’t build trust – your voice will.

Some of my best-performing emails?

Wrote them in five minutes. No fluff. Just truth.

Email lets you say the things that actually matter. No algorithm. No pressure to perform. Just connection.

Still, after all this time?

It’s the most powerful tool in my business.

3. Visibility Is About Alignment – Not Algorithms

I used to think visibility meant MORE.

More content. More platforms. More pressure.

Now I know it’s about being memorable.

That has nothing to do with dancing on Reels.

It looks like:

  • Hosting an audio-only summit that brought in 1,100+ new subscribers and raised thousands for charity
  • Saying yes to one podcast interview that led to 100+ new leads
  • Building intentional, sustainable relationships through email collabs and freebie swaps

Visibility that works won’t burn you out.

It fuels you.

4. What I Believe About YOU, 200 Episodes In

Here’s the part that always gets me.

If you’re here – reading this – I already know something about you:

You are not average.

You’re here because you care.
You want to do this differently.
You want to build something with a heartbeat – not just a highlight reel.

So let me say it clearly:

You are not behind.
You are not lazy.
You are not failing because you haven’t hit 10k in 10 minutes.

You’re building a real business – one rooted in integrity. One that lasts.

And that?

That is brave.

What’s Next? The Mission’s Just Getting Started

200 episodes in and I’ve never been clearer:

I’m here to help 1 million women grow wildly engaged email lists and become go-to names in their niche – without burnout, without bro marketing, and without relying on social media.

I’m here to shift the narrative from “do more” to “do what matters.”

And I’d love to help you do the same.

→ Apply for a Visibility Audit
→ Join The Email Growth Club

Final Words: You Get to Do It Your Way

Whether you’re reading this from the car, while walking the dog, or mid-cleaning sprint – I want you to hear this:

You’re doing amazing.
You are needed.
And your voice? Your message? Your magic?

It matters.

Thank you for being here.
Thank you for trusting me in your earbuds and inbox.
Here’s to the next 200.

With so much love,
Kylie x

Feat. SEO Strategist Britt Reber

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 199

What if growing your email list didn’t require dancing on reels or throwing cash at paid ads… but simply optimising your website to talk to Google?

In this tactical episode of The Email Growth Show, I’m joined by SEO strategist and agency owner Britt Reber to break down the three SEO traffic secrets that can help you get seen, get clicks, and grow your list – all with just two hours a month.

This isn’t your typical SEO advice. Britt skips the jargon, ditches the overwhelm, and shows you exactly how to start using SEO to bring in high-quality leads and email subscribers – without needing to become a full-time SEO nerd.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why keyword research is optional (and what to do instead!)
– The simple setup that tells Google exactly what to rank your page for
– How to publish fresh content fast, without writing 3,000 word blog posts
– The truth about backlinks and why they matter more than ever
– A monthly SEO routine you can actually stick to!

Let’s dive straight into Britt’s 3 proven strategies that you can implement with just 2 hours a month to start ranking on Google! We’re talking simplified SEO, visibility that compounds, and the one tech tweak you can make today to tell Google exactly what you want to rank for.

Strategy 1: Communicate Clearly with Google

Skip the keyword rabbit holes. Instead, type your offer into Google, see what comes up, and use those real-world search terms across your site.

Then, use Britt’s golden rule: one keyword per page.

Make sure your chosen keyword appears in your:

  • H1 header (that’s your page title)
  • Meta title
  • Meta description

That’s how you create a crystal-clear communication channel with Google – so your site ranks for what you want it to rank for.

Strategy 2: Post fresh content (even if it’s short)

Google loves active, relevant websites.

That doesn’t mean publishing essays every week.

Start small:

  • Repurpose a podcast or reel into a blog post
  • Embed a video with a quick blurb
  • Share a story you posted on social media

Britt recommends publishing at least once a week – even if it’s short and AI-assisted.

Consistency builds credibility.

Strategy 3: Build trust with backlinks

Google trusts sites that others trust.

That’s why backlinks are so powerful.

Every time another website links to yours, it passes a little credibility along. The more high-quality backlinks you collect (think podcasts, PR, guest posts, collaborations), the more Google sees you as an authority.

Not sure where to start? Britt’s advice: aim for one good backlink a month.

That could be:

  • A podcast you’re featured on
  • A roundup blog you contribute to
  • A press feature or local article

Already been featured somewhere?

Go back and ask for a link!

Real SEO results without the hustle…

Britt’s agency often ranks client websites in under 30 days – but even if you’re DIY-ing with just two hours a month, you’ll start seeing traffic in a few months.

And that traffic? It converts.

SEO leads tend to be more engaged and more likely to buy because they were already searching for what you offer.

Your next step:

  • Choose one keyword per page and update your H1/meta tags
  • Post one new piece of content this week (keep it simple!)
  • Ask for one backlink from a past feature or collaboration
  • Set up Google Analytics and Search Console to track what’s working

Come join us inside The Headliner Mastermind – where we blend PR, visibility strategy, mindset coaching, and real community to help you grow your authority, get seen in all the right places, and become the go-to name in your niche (plus getting featured in PR is certainly going to help your SEO and Google rankings too!)

Guest Spotlight: Britt Reber

Britt is the founder of Growing Your Traffic, an SEO agency helping online business owners rank on Google and grow their traffic with smart, strategic SEO (no keyword overwhelm required).
