So, yeah, % worth it to go back and make sure you always have a link from all of those collaborations you’ve done in the past.

Kylie Kelly [00:16:19]:
Yes. I love this. So when somebody goes and does all of these traffic secrets, these three things that are actually really easy to do, simple, easy to do. When they do that, what do you see with your clients? Like, how long does it take to rank? And I know that’s probably a hard question because it depends on the industry. But is there, like, a bit of an average? Is it is it six months? Is it twelve months? Like, what what can we expect from doing this work?

Britt Reber [00:16:41]:
Yeah. Good question. It definitely depends on the industry. It also depends on how fast you’re going. So my agency, we have done for you SEO Go services where you pay us and our team goes and does all of this for you. So we optimize your site. We add the fresh content to your site. We get those backlinks for you on a monthly basis.

Britt Reber [00:16:57]:
And when you have our whole team doing that for you full time, you can rank really quickly. Most of our clients, we have them ranked in less than thirty days for sometimes some really major keywords even on a national level. But if you’re doing it yourself and you’re doing it with just a minimum, like, I’m talking about spending about two hours a month just doing, you know, just adding some fresh content maybe once a week, doing a blog post, and then getting one backlink a month, it does depend on the industry, but usually, it’ll take a few months before you actually start seeing some traffic coming in from Google. So again, that’s if you go bare minimum and you’re just taking it slow, going easy, and just making it kind of a side project, it probably will take a few months. But the thing about SEO is it works like a snowball. So it’s very much an investment. If you think of paid ads like a paycheck where you put it the money into the ad funnel and then the money comes out immediately, SEO is a lot more like a long term investment. So it’s kind of like putting in that time a little bit here, a little bit there.

Britt Reber [00:17:52]:
And as you go, it’ll stack and snowball. And as Google starts to rank you for some less competitive keywords, it’ll start ranking you for more and more, eventually, competitive keywords, and then the traffic just keeps growing and growing over time that way. So even though it might seem like, oh my gosh, a few months out before I start getting traffic. First of all, it’s free traffic. It’s organic traffic. So it’s usually really highly engaged. We usually see in our clients back ends that the what the traffic coming in from Google, they’re usually clicking the most, they’re buying the most, so they’re converting the most. It’s just the best traffic.

Britt Reber [00:18:24]:
And it’s free traffic. So even though it might be a few months out if you take it slow, it’s a % worth it to go after that traffic.

Kylie Kelly [00:18:31]:
Absolutely. And I think the way that you’ve described it as well, like, it does it doesn’t take that much. But two hours a month, we can be doing that. And while we’re waiting for that to build and waiting to see the results, we can be doing other things to grow our audience. So we still have that audience growth there. But then what I can imagine when the SEO catches up and we’re starting to see results from both, it could just do amazing things for our businesses.

Britt Reber [00:18:52]:
Oh, yeah. %. And, again, it’s that snowball thing. So as you start getting more and more clients coming in and you start getting reviews on your website, testimonials, you know, just as things build, your rankings just continue to go up, up, up, which makes your traffic go up, up, up. So it definitely builds over time like that.

Kylie Kelly [00:19:09]:
Yes. I love that. And on, I guess, a bit of a last note, but I think it’s really important to mention, like, have Google Analytics set up. Like, we need to know where this traffic is coming from. Right? So, if anyone’s listening that hasn’t got Google Analytics, I think this is a good little reminder to set that up as well.

Britt Reber [00:19:25]:
Yes. %. Google Analytics and Google Search Console because those are both free tools from Google, and there’s tutorials online that can teach you how to set it up. So if you’re not techie, you know, you can pay someone on Fiverr really cheap to set it up for you, or you can just watch some tutorials and get it done and, you know, knock it out in one afternoon. But it’s totally worth it because you get to see all those insights as to what are people searching for when they find you, what search results are you already showing up in that you can maybe lean a little harder into to get higher up in those searches. So, yeah, it just gives you really good data. And like you said, the traffic data too. Who’s coming to your website? Where are they coming from? What are they doing on your site? All of that stuff can really help guide your strategy.

Britt Reber [00:20:02]:
So totally worth setting up those two free tools.

Kylie Kelly [00:20:05]:
I love that. Amazing. Amazing. So, Brit, anyone that wants to dive in deeper to SEO or perhaps look into your agency, say, like, oh, I just I’m just gonna get somebody else to do it for me. Where can we send

Britt Reber [00:20:14]:
them to find out more about you? Great question. We actually just started growing our Instagram account, so you can find us there. It’s just at growing your traffic, gr0wingy0urtraffic. Super easy, growing your traffic. And you can actually download everything I talked about today, those three secrets. I have it in a PDF form, so it’s really easy to go back and look through that. And there’s a little bit little bit more ex explanation for some of this stuff too. So if you wanna download that cheat sheet, just go to growingyourtraffic.com/unlimitedtraffic.

Britt Reber [00:20:46]:
So this is my guide for basically getting unlimited traffic from Google searches just by setting up your website to rank in the search results.

Kylie Kelly [00:20:53]:
So good. Well, we’ll put the links in the show notes. I’m gonna go and download it now. Thank you so much for

Britt Reber [00:20:58]:
being here. Yeah. Of course. I I just am such a power to the people kind of person. And so I think that we need more small businesses showing up in Google searches. Because for a long time, they’ve been dominated by all the big players that have a lot of money. And so the more people that we can get, the more small business owners that we can get who actually know SEO and know how to optimize their sites so that they can show up in search results, the better. It just is better for everybody on the planet.

Kylie Kelly [00:21:25]:
Mhmm. Yes. Okay. I’m on board with that mission. I love it. Thank you so much.

Britt Reber [00:21:29]:
Yeah. Of course. Thanks for having me, Kylie.

Kylie Kelly [00:21:31]:
Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of The Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you, who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode.

title: How I’d Build My Email List From Scratch in 2025 Without Social Media or Ads
excerpt: THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 198 Let’s pretend it’s day one. No email list.No audience.No ad budget. Just a big vision and a deep desire to grow a business that actually feels good to run. If I were starting again in 2026, I can tell you exactly what I wouldn’t do – and what I’d […]
content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 198

Let’s pretend it’s day one.

No email list.
No audience.
No ad budget.

Just a big vision and a deep desire to grow a business that actually feels good to run.

If I were starting again in 2026, I can tell you exactly what I wouldn’t do – and what I’d focus on instead.

Because growth does not need to feel chaotic to work.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. I hope you feel inspired to create your own start here email and ditch the welcome sequence if it is no longer serving you and your ideal clients. Reach out if you have any questions.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:19]:
I love you loads and I will talk to you really soon, like really soon. I’ve got some really good stuff coming your way and next week’s episode is our guest episode with an incredible, incredible PR expert. You’re going to want to tune in. All right, I will see you then. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:51]:
Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:55]:
Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why most “visibility hacks” are just busywork (and what I’d stop doing today)
– The 3 strategic moves I’d focus on if I were starting from scratch
– How to position a lead magnet that actually leads to paid offers
– Why bundles, podcast guesting, and freebie swaps still work in 2025
– The email approach I’d use to build connection from Day 1
– How to build momentum without burning out

A Simple Way to Get Support

If you’re reading this thinking this is exactly what I want, you don’t have to figure it out alone.

Inside The Email Growth Club, I help you plan visibility, grow your list, and build email strategies that actually convert — without social media pressure.

And inside The Empress Mastermind, we zoom out and design a full ecosystem around your energy, offers, and long-term vision.

What I Would Ignore Completely

Let’s start with what I would not waste my time on.

I would not post daily on Instagram hoping the algorithm finally decides to like me.

I’ve tried it.
You’ve probably tried it.

It’s visibility for the sake of being seen – not connection or conversion.

I would also stop creating generic freebies that attract freebie collectors instead of buyers.

If it’s another “10 tips to…” situation, I’m out.

And I would absolutely not run paid ads before anything is validated.

Ads amplify what’s already working. They don’t create magic.

Step One: Create One Killer Lead Magnet

Not five.
Not a library.
One.

One irresistible lead magnet that does two things:

  • Delivers a real transformation
  • Naturally leads into your paid work

Think:

  • A quiz that positions your expertise
  • A case study that tells the truth
  • A private audio training that feels intimate

Your free resource should not just teach.

It should position.

Step Two: Choose 2–3 Aligned Visibility Plays

If you want to grow without social media, this is where the magic happens.

I would say yes to 2–3 high-quality visibility opportunities and ignore the rest.

Bundles.
Podcasts.
Freebie swaps.
Inbox collaborations.

Not everything.
Just what’s aligned.

Visibility only works when the right people are paying attention.

And every time I show up, I’d have one clear call to action that leads directly to my email list.

Your list is your home base.

Everything points there.

Step Three: Prioritise Consistency Over Complexity

If I had 23 people on my list, I’d write to them like they were 2,300.

You don’t need funnels stacked on funnels.

You need connection.

One email a week.
Written like a human.
Not a marketer.

My highest-performing emails are never the polished ones. They’re the honest ones.

People don’t want perfection.

They want presence.

Step Four: Build Relationships Like It’s Your Job

Because it is.

Growing without social media turns visibility into a relationship game.

That means:

  • Personal podcast pitches
  • Thoughtful inbox collaborations
  • Following up with gratitude
  • Being someone people actually want to support

You don’t need to go viral.
You need to be visible to the right people.

Let’s Recap

If I were building from scratch in 2025, I’d keep it simple:

  1. One irresistible lead magnet
  2. Two to three aligned visibility strategies
  3. One consistent, relationship-led email
  4. A mindset rooted in connection, not numbers

No dancing.
No ads.
No burnout.

You Don’t Have to Start From Scratch Alone…

If you want to grow your list without ads, algorithms, or burnout, this is the support I offer.

The Email Growth Club is where we build consistent, relationship-led email growth.
The Empress Mastermind is for designing the bigger picture – visibility, offers, and strategy that fit how you actually work.

You don’t need to do everything my love.
You just need to do the right things consistently.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 197

I need to say this clearly, lovingly, and without any fluff.

You are not lazy.

If your motivation feels patchy, if consistency feels hard, if your business makes you want to disappear instead of show up – that is not a character flaw.

That is information.

And most of the time, it’s pointing to one thing.

You’re building a business that doesn’t fit you.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
I need to tell you something that genuinely surprised the shit out of me. A few days ago, I started a school community, fully expecting it to be fine, helpful, quiet, and instead it has lit me up in a matter of days. I’ve had deeper conversations with people on my email list than I’ve had in years and it’s made something really clear to me. Today I want to tell you about my school experiment. Why I’ve decided to jump on in what I am seeing and and the lessons that I’m already learning so that you can take all of these learnings and apply it to your own business in your own way. Let’s talk about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:39]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years. And the same is possible for you too. Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:11]:
Hey. Hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. Now today’s episode is very much a thinking out loud one and if you’ve been here a while, you know that these episodes are actually my favorite. So today I want to talk about my school experiment. And before you tune out thinking this is about a platform, it really isn’t. This is more about connection, depth, fun and remembering why we started business in the first place. Now let me be very clear.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:40]:
I was very skeptical. I did not jump into school excited. I resisted it for a long time because honestly, I’m not a huge Hermozy fan. I didn’t understand the tape on the nose. I thought that this space being school from the outside, I thought it would be very much bro marketer kind of hustle culture. Like I just didn’t think it would be very aligned. I have since googled her Moses tape situation and found out that it actually helped him breathe. So now I feel a bit shitty judging him on that.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:11]:
But regardless, he also made that part of his personal brand which I do think is weird. That aside, if you are listening to this thinking, hang on, you started a school community. Same. I am surprised too. This wasn’t a grand strategy. There was no funnel, there was no monetization plan. I created this school group purely out of curiosity. That was it.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:32]:
I honestly thought people would lurk, engagement would be really slow it would take weeks for anyone to open up and it might feel a bit flat. You know that feeling when something is fine but it’s not alive? A lot of Facebook groups have that feeling, right? That’s kind of what I expected. But instead, within days, I have over 130 people that have joined from my email list. People are posting, they’re being thoughtful, open, honest. We’re having really deep conversations. And this has caught me so much off guard. I’ve already had one on one conversations with people inside that group who until now were just a name and an email address on my list. Some of them have been on my list for years.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:14]:
Years. And yet we’d never actually spoken. There was no tone, no nuance, no back and forth, just email receive, repeat, right? But suddenly in a smaller room, they’re telling me what’s really going on. Not the polished version, not the this sounds smart version, the actual real version. And it reminded me of something I think we’ve all forgotten a little bit. Going deep beats going wide. Every single time. Small rooms change how people speak.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:44]:
They soften, they stop performing, they stop trying to impress. They just talk. And trust forms fast when people feel safe. We know this now. This actually connects to something I shared back in episode 222, which was called the number one email strategy that no one’s talking about. In that episode, I talked about the Empire Mixer. So back in October last year, I started hosting networking events for my email list. Invite only superintentional connection led.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:14]:
And on paper they were great. We’d have maybe 50, sometimes 55 women register and then around 30 to 35 would actually attend. And then I noticed something interesting. Each time I hosted one, which was monthly, the attendance dropped slightly. Not because people didn’t care, not because the conversations weren’t valuable, everyone loved them. But because of life time zones, kids, energy, capacity, it started to feel like, oh, another zoom meeting, right? And what this school experiment has shown me is that accessibility wins every time. A space people can drop into when it suits them, when they have the energy, when it feels fun for them. Like that creates far more connection than a calendar dependent event ever can.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:59]:
Because inside this community, no one is missing out if they can’t make a call. The conversation is already happening, the connection is already there. And then, yes, we can host networking calls inside the group, right? Amazing. But they’re layered on top of connection already, not replacing it. So if you can’t make the call, you’re still a part of the room, you’re still a part of the group, you’re still being seen, you still feel connected. This feels so much more human and so much more sustainable. Now I want to be really clear and make sure I say that this isn’t about email failing. I want to be super clear with this.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:33]:
This is not an email doesn’t work conversation. Email is still my home. It is still powerful. It’s still where long term relationships get built. But community adds a different dimension because email is me talking to you, community is us talking with each other. And that changes everything. I’ve had more meaningful conversations in a few days than I sometimes do in months of sending emails. Not because the emails are bad, but because intimacy is built in these smaller spaces.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:02]:
The other thing that I am loving about this school experiment is, is that I am getting a voice of customer without feeling gross about it, right? So from like a voice of customer perspective, holy shit, it’s gold. People are telling me in their own words what they’re stuck on, what they’re tired of, what they don’t want anymore, what they’re craving instead. And then here’s the part that matters most to me. There’s nothing for sale in this group. It’s free. There’s no pitch. So people aren’t guarded, they’re not wondering, is this leading somewhere? They’re just being themselves. And that kind of insight, you can’t fake it, you can’t survey it, you can’t reverse engineer it.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:38]:
You just have to listen and it’s there. Which I think is so incredible. Now I want to share something personal as well. I have a post it note on my desk that says what feels fun right now? Voice notes.
Mastermind conversations.

Because I’ve been there too.

I’ve built businesses that looked perfect on the outside – clean strategies, impressive plans, all the “right” moves – and felt deadening on the inside.

The issue wasn’t my work ethic.
It was the structure.

Doing Too Much of the Wrong Shit Is Exhausting

Let’s be honest.

You’re probably not doing too little.

You’re doing too much of what doesn’t suit you.

A content calendar that makes you want to fake your own disappearance.
Visibility strategies that drain you by mid-morning.
Client structures that leave you resentful instead of fulfilled.

If your business makes you want to hide, that’s not laziness.

That’s self-protection.

The “Should” Strategy Is the Real Problem

Just be more consistent.
Post every day.
Reels are the future.
If you’re not launching, you’re losing.

None of these statements take you into account.

Your energy.
Your season of life.
Your nervous system.
Your values.

I’m a Manifesting Generator. I need momentum, variety, and freedom. Put me in a rigid, pre-planned funnel that takes six months to build and I will combust.

That doesn’t mean I’m broken.

It means the system wasn’t built for me.

Aligned doesn’t mean easy.

You still work hard.

But it feels different.

You don’t dread your calendar.
You don’t second-guess yourself every time an algorithm changes.
You don’t feel like you’re performing someone else’s version of success.

Aligned means:

  • Choosing visibility that works for you
  • Building offers that light you up
  • Knowing why you’re doing what you’re doing

Your strategy fits your life, not just your income goals.

What You Actually Need Right Now

Not another funnel template.
Not another free challenge.
Not another planner you abandon by Thursday.

You need clarity.

Clarity on:

  • What kind of business fits you now
  • What visibility matches your energy
  • How to grow with joy, not just grit

Because here’s the truth most people avoid.

Everything works.
But not everything works for you.

You’re Not Broken. You’re Evolving.

If something inside you keeps whispering surely it doesn’t have to feel like this — that’s not weakness.

That’s your inner CEO waking up.

You’re not lazy.
You’re not failing.
You’re not behind.

You’re craving a better way.

And that is more than allowed.

If You’re Ready for a Better Way

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 196

I didn’t expect hosting 60+ expert conversations to change my identity.

I thought it would grow my list.
Build authority.
Maybe sell a few more offers.

What it actually did?

It completely shifted how I see myself as a leader.

And if you’ve ever considered hosting a summit, podcast series, interview event, or collaborative project – this might be the permission slip you didn’t know you needed.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE TO READ THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Your audience doesn’t need another 30-slide presentation. They’re fucking overwhelmed with all the information. They want your real voice, your perspective, your presence, and little snippets of what they could do tomorrow to take action and see results. Implementation. That is what 2025 is all about.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:21]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online?

Kylie Kelly [00:00:29]:
Or throwing cash at paid ads?

Kylie Kelly [00:00:31]:
Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from 0 to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:41]:
2 years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:44]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:53]:
Hey, hey, welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility coach, audience growth strategist, founder of Inside the Inbox, and the biz bestie who’s always up for a little behind-the-scenes truth talk. And today, I want to take you inside the making of something that’s honestly changed everything for me— Inside the Inbox. I’ve now hosted over 60 expert conversations through this event, and what started as a simple idea, literally recorded through Voxer while in active mum mode, has turned into a lead generation machine, a trust-building visibility tool, and, well, one of the most fulfilling things I’ve ever created in my business. But more than that, it’s also changed how I think, how I sell, how I lead. And today I want to break down what I’ve learned from hosting 60+ short, punchy, wisdom-packed interviews, how it’s impacted my offers, my content, my confidence, and my community, and why I believe that this kind of visibility, the real relationship-first conversations, might be exactly what you need too. So let’s get into it. Firstly, everyone is doing it differently and it’s working.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:59]:
Before hosting Inside the Inbox, I thought maybe I’d start seeing the secret formula, the thing that everyone successful must be doing, right? But after 60+ interviews, I realized there is no formula. There’s only alignment. I’ve interviewed women with tiny lists making full-time income from micro offers. I’ve interviewed creators who only sell through email, no sales pages, no launches. I’ve interviewed coaches who batch weekly emails 6 months in advance and others who write daily from the school pickup line. I’ve chatted with people who grow with Pinterest, with SEO and blogging, in-person events and comments, quiz funnels, collaborations, DMs, pop-up podcasts. You fucking name it, they’ve done it. And the best part? It’s all working.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:41]:
They’re all growing on their own terms. So the takeaway that I want you to realize is that the strategies that succeed are the ones built around you, your strengths, your bandwidth, your vibe, your voice. There is no right way. It all fucking works. There is just your way. What is right for you and for your audience. Now, the second thing that Inside the Inbox made me realize is that intimate conversations convert way better than expert presentations. And let’s be real, most summits feel like they were created in Canva and forgotten in Google Drive.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:12]:
I wanted Inside the Inbox to feel different, so I stripped the slides, I ditched the Zoom links, I recorded every single interview as an audio-only Voxer chat, which meant no pressure for guests to get camera ready, no scheduling nightmares across time zones because Australia is a nightmare, and best of all, no bloated 45-minute lectures. Instead, we got casual, real-talk conversations, tangible takeaways, ideas you could implement in 15 minutes or and that shift changed the game. People binge the event like a podcast. They shared it, they remembered it, and my inbox blew up with “this is the best summit I’ve ever attended” messages. Why? Because your audience doesn’t need another 30-slide presentation. They’re fucking overwhelmed with all the information. They want your real voice, your perspective, your presence, and little snippets of what they could do tomorrow to take action and see results. Implementation.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:04]:
That is what 2025 is all about. Now, the next thing I wanted to share with you is that thought leadership doesn’t mean talking louder. It means hosting the room. I used to think to be seen as a leader, I have to say more, but Inside the Inbox showed me something different. By simply creating the stage, curating the speakers, asking the right questions, and holding space for honest stories, I’ve become a trusted voice by association. When people see you in proximity to others they admire, they start to trust you too. And that trust, it spills onto your audience, your sales, your visibility, your confidence. For me, Inside the Inbox has led to hundreds of new subscribers every single season, mastermind and membership applications within days of the event launch, DMs from aligned humans saying, I’ve been watching and listening and I’m ready to work with you now.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:51]:
I didn’t shout louder, I just hosted the room, I built the stage and let my reputation be built through relationships. So in my opinion, hosting a space where people feel seen, that is real leadership, even if you say less, you’re making space for more. Now, this event— hosting your own event, building the stage— it’s not just visibility. It can actually be an entire visibility ecosystem. It’s not just a one-and-done launch. It can create months’ worth of content and the kind that works hard behind the scenes. Here’s some ways that it can do that. So each interview can become a blog post.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:25]:
Hello, SEO and backlinks, right? Every session can be a podcast replay on my main show. More evergreen content. I could pull quotes for Instagram carousels and email openers, and those interviews, I can reference them in coaching calls, masterminds, and trainings all the time. Now, I don’t do all of those things. You guys know I’m not on social. I don’t have the bandwidth right now to create the blog post. Like, I don’t do all of that, but you could, right? When you have a clear strategy of how you want to repurpose the content, it can become an entire ecosystem that then brings even more people into your world. So not only can you attract leads, you can stay top of mind for months after.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:01]:
This is the power of intentional content, not content for the sake of content like fucking Instagram Reels, but visibility that keeps working while I’m on the floor building Lego towers with Sam and Spencer, right? So if you’re putting effort into showing up, I want to really say this firmly, make it count. One summit can equal 100 repurposing opportunities. So make sure if you go ahead, if you build the stage, if you do the summit, if you do the event, you actually do this, make sure you use them. Think about 1 or 2 things and 1 or 2 ways that you can repurpose this content long after the doors have closed on the summit. Now, something else I wanted to share with you, but hosting these events has changed my identity as a thought leader. Leader. This part is a little tender to share, but the biggest thing that Inside the Inbox gave me, it was the permission to stop hiding behind the label of email marketing girl. It gave me proof that I could lead bold conversations, that I could be in the same room as these brilliant women, that I was a voice, not just a strategist.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:56]:
After season 1, I changed how I introduced myself. I wasn’t just an email marketing strategist anymore. Now I’m a visibility coach. I’m an audience growth expert. I’m a thought leader, and I feel that in my fucking bones. You can hear it when I say it, right? Like, it is powerful. And hosting events like helps you step into that identity more fully with every time you do it, every conversation, every story that’s shared. And I think that’s the biggest ROI of all, right? Hosting events, building your own stages will stretch you.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:25]:
It will call you into leadership and it will show you who you already are, even if you haven’t claimed it yet. So if you’ve ever had an idea for a summit, a series, a podcast, a bundle, but you’ve talked yourself out of it because who am I to host that, let this episode be your permission slip because I promise you, you do not need 100,000 followers. You do not need the perfect tech stack. You do not need to be the loudest voice in the room. You just need to start the conversation. That’s what I’ve done with Inside the Inbox and it has changed everything. So if you’re trying to do it all alone, posting, creating, launching into the void, this might be why it’s not landing. You don’t need more content.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:00]:
You need more connection, more shared platforms, more real voices, more yes-worthy conversations that turn strangers into superfans. And if you want help building that kind of visibility, join me inside the Email Growth Club, my low-ticket membership that’s stacked with tools, coaching, and strategy for growing your email list. Or you can apply for the Headliner Mastermind, where we map out your entire visibility plan and I walk alongside you as you become the go-to name in your industry. Both doors are open this week during Inside the Inbox Season 2, and you’ll find all the links in the show notes below. Until next time, my loves, be bold, be visible, and keep building that beautiful business your way. And from heart to yours, I really want to encourage you to build your own stage. Do not wait for the invitation. I have so much love for you, and I will see you next week.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:47]:
Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:50]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:52]:
I hope you found valuable insights into.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:54]:
The next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads.

If you enjoyed this episode, please take.

A moment to rate and review the.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:04]:
Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:08]:
Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:10]:
To say goodbye to social media and.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:12]:
Leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:16]:
Thank you so much for listening, and.

I’ll see you in the next episode.

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why there is no universal formula for business growth
– Why intimate conversations convert better than expert presentations
– How hosting expert interviews builds authority without shouting louder
– How one event can become a long-term visibility ecosystem
– The identity shift that happens when you build your own stage

Let’s build your visibility strategy together…

If you’re done guessing…
Done posting into the void…
Done hoping your next launch “just works”…

It’s time to stop winging your visibility and start engineering it.

👉 Book your Business Breakthrough Audit.

I’ll personally review your visibility, email list, and offer positioning – and send you a tailored 3-step action plan showing exactly where to focus next.
Just clarity, strategy, and momentum.

Secure your audit here → https://kyliekelly.com/breakthrough

P.S. If building your own platform has been sitting in your Notes app for months… this is your sign.

There is no secret growth formula – only alignment

Before hosting Inside the Inbox, I secretly believed something.

If I interviewed enough successful women…
If I asked the right questions…
Eventually I’d uncover the formula.

The blueprint.
The “this is what they all do” strategy.

But after 60+ expert interviews?

There isn’t one.

I’ve spoken to:

  • Women with tiny email lists making full-time income from micro-offers
  • Creators who sell only through email – no launches, no sales pages
  • Coaches batching six months of content in advance
  • Others writing emails from the school pickup line

And they’re all growing.
Why?

Because their strategy is aligned.

Hosting expert interviews for business growth taught me that success isn’t about copying someone else’s method – it’s about building something that fits your bandwidth, strengths, voice, and audience.

Everything works – when it’s aligned.

Conversations convert better than presentations

Let’s talk about something most people won’t say out loud.

Most online summits are rubbish.

Slides.
Over-produced training.
Forty-five minutes of theory with zero implementation.

When I built Inside the Inbox, I stripped it back completely.

No slides.
No Zoom fatigue.
No pressure.

Every session was an audio-only Voxer conversation.

Casual. Real. Implementable.
And that decision changed everything.

People binged it like a podcast.
They implemented what they learned.
My inbox filled with “this is the best event I’ve attended” messages.

Your audience doesn’t need more information.

They’re already overwhelmed.

They want perspective.
Presence.
Real conversation.
Tangible next steps.

Thought leadership is about hosting the room…

Here’s the lesson I didn’t expect:
Hosting expert interviews positions you as a leader – even if you’re not the one teaching the entire time.

I used to think visibility meant:

  • Saying more
  • Teaching more
  • Posting more
  • Proving more

But leadership can look like:

  • Curating powerful voices
  • Asking strategic questions
  • Holding space for honest stories
  • Building the stage

When people see you in proximity to others they admire, trust transfers.

And that trust spills into your:

  • Audience growth
  • Applications
  • Sales
  • Reputation

You don’t need to shout louder.

You need to host better.

One event = An entire visibility ecosystem

Here’s where this gets strategic.

Hosting expert interviews isn’t just a one-time launch.

It can become a long-term visibility ecosystem.

Each interview can become:

  • A podcast replay
  • A blog post [SEO gold]
  • Email content
  • Social proof
  • Coaching references
  • Quote graphics
  • Evergreen nurture sequences

That means one intentional project can replace 100 pieces of scattered content.

Instead of posting daily just to “stay visible,” you create a strategic asset that compounds.

That’s sustainable visibility.

Not hustle visibility.

The identity shift is the real ROI

This part feels tender to admit.

Before hosting these conversations, I hid behind “email marketing strategist.”

After Season 1?

Something shifted.
I wasn’t just a service provider.
I was a visibility leader.
An audience growth expert.
A curator of powerful conversations.

Hosting expert interviews for business growth doesn’t just grow your audience.

It expands who you believe you are.

And that identity shift changes how you sell, show up, and lead.

That’s the real ROI.

Should you build your own stage?

If you’ve ever thought about hosting:

  • A summit
  • A collaborative series
  • A private audio event
  • A bundle
  • A podcast interview series

But stopped yourself with:

“Who am I to do that?”

Here’s the truth.

You don’t need:

  • 100k followers
  • Perfect branding
  • Fancy tech
  • To be the loudest voice

You need connection.
You need conversation.
You need courage to start.

Visibility isn’t about being everywhere.
It’s about being remembered.

  • How many emails I sent
  • Which ones performed best
  • What the open and click rates looked like
  • And how I added 346 new subscribers without paid ads, without being everywhere, and without burning out

Let’s get into it.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE TO READ THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Before we get into today’s episode, I have to tell you that if you’re ready to take your email marketing to the next level and you want real strategies, expert coaching, and a supportive community to help you grow, then you need to be inside the Email Growth Club. Now, this isn’t just another membership. It’s a space where I share what’s working now in email marketing, and you get my personal guidance on how to grow, nurture, and monetize your list in the smartest way possible. If you’re tired of guessing what to send or you’re struggling to make sales from your emails, this is where you need to be. I would love for you to join us now. The link is in the show notes below. Now let’s jump on into the episode. Hey, hey, welcome back to another mini episode on the Email Growth Show.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:43]:
These Tuesday episodes are like cheeky little voice notes from your biz bestie. And today is a juicy one because I’m pulling back the curtain and showing you exactly what happened inside my inbox in April, how many emails I sent, which one performed best and why, and how I added 346 new subscribers without paid ads, without being everywhere and without burning out. I was running a live workshop, working with clients, and yep, raising two wild little humans while doing it. So if you’ve ever been wondering, can I really send more emails and grow my list right now? The answer is a big yes. Okay, so how many emails I sent in April. Here is the breakdown. I sent 13 emails to my full entire list. They were a mix of value, affiliate emails, reminders, and behind-the-scenes emails.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:32]:
And I also sent 17 client member-only emails for members of the Email Growth Club or the Headliner Mastermind. These included exclusive trainings, call reminders, and personalized coaching. So that’s a total of 30 emails in April. Yes, 30. And guess what? No one emailed me to say you’re annoying. No one unsubscribed with a hate note. No one died. So today’s takeaway: you can send more than you think.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:57]:
When your emails are helpful, human, and full of heart, your subscribers won’t resent you, they’ll actually look forward to hearing from you. So which emails were the best performing emails of the month? This part makes my little marketing heart pretty happy. The best performing email I sent in April was titled Real Numbers, Real Results, Real Visibility. It was sent to 5,735 subscribers, had an open rate of 51.2% and a 1.8% click rate. But honestly, the real magic wasn’t the metrics of this email, it was the message. Because this email wasn’t perfect,. It wasn’t pre-written or copy-edited within an inch of its life. It was raw.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:38]:
It was honest. It was me saying, hey, I had this idea. I skipped the funnel and it changed my business. Inside that email, I shared the story behind Inside the Inbox, how I created the audio-only event. This is back in season 1. The fact that it had no slides, no stress, and it ended up bringing in some incredible results. All of that from trusting my gut and trying something new and sharing it honestly. So when I sent this email, I linked to the case study that I created, which is one of my new free resources that leads to my mastermind, right? So I created the case study and then I sent it out to my list.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:09]:
So I want you to remember that people, they don’t want polished, they want personal. They want energy, truth, stories. So if you’re about to hit send on something that makes you nervous, I want to encourage you to do it. You’re probably onto something great. And I also want to remind you that you need to remember to send out any new free resources, anything that you make in your business that gets you excited, that you are going to use as a part of your customer journey, send it to your existing subscribers as well. We often forget this step, but it’s a really easy one to take so that you can nurture your existing list and just love all over the people that are already in your world. Now I do have a runner-up email for this category today, and I sent an affiliate email for a friend of mine, Brenna McGowan, when she was promoting her Pre-Launch Plan program. So there are a couple programs that I affiliate for during the year that I absolutely love, and Brenna is incredible at what she does at the pre-launch system of an offer, right? TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– How many emails I sent (and why nobody freaked out about it)
– The email that hit a 51.2% open rate and 1.8% click rate – and what made it stand out
– Why storytelling and authenticity are STILL outperforming polished funnels
– How I grew my list by 346 new subscribers with one bundle, one summit, and one workshop
– Why list growth isn’t just a numbers game – and how to make subscribers stay

How many emails I sent in April

Brace yourself.

I sent 30 emails in April.

Yep. Thirty.

Here’s the breakdown:

  • 13 emails to my full list
    These were a mix of value emails, affiliate promotions, reminders, and behind-the-scenes stories.
  • 17 member-only emails
    For the Email Growth Club and Headliner Mastermind. Trainings, reminders, coaching support.

And do you know what happened?

No hate mail.
No dramatic unsubscribes.
No one telling me I was “too much.”

Because when your emails are helpful, human, and rooted in relationship, people do not resent hearing from you.

They look forward to it.

You can send more than you think.

My best performing email of the month

The top email in April was titled:

“Real Numbers, Real Results, Real Visibility.”

Here were the stats:

  • Sent to 5,735 subscribers
  • 51.2% open rate
  • 1.8% click rate

Solid.
But the numbers are not the most important part.
The magic was in the message.

It was not polished.
It was not perfectly pre-written.
It was not overly strategised.

It was honest.

I shared the story behind creating Inside the Inbox as an audio-only event. No slides. No stress. Just trust in my gut and trying something different.

And inside that email, I linked to a brand new case study I had created, which now leads into my mastermind.

Here is the lesson:

People do not want polished. They want personal.

They want energy.
They want stories.
They want to see what is actually working.

And here is another reminder most people forget.

When you create a new free resource, send it to your existing list.

Do not only promote it to new leads.
Love on the humans already in your world.

The runner-up that surprised me

The second highest performer was an affiliate email for Brenna McGowan’s Pre-Launch Plan program.

Subject line:

“Want a sold-out launch? Open this.”

Stats:

  • 53.1% open rate
  • 1.9% click rate
  • 103 clicks to her sales page

That tells me something important.

People want real results.

They are tired of noise.
They are tired of theories.
They want proof.

And here is another key piece.

I did not copy and paste Brenna’s swipe copy, even though she is an incredible copywriter.

I rewrote it in my voice – because affiliate emails are not just sales emails.
They are nurture opportunities.
They are connection moments.

If it does not sound like you, your audience will feel it.

Let’s talk list growth

Now for the part that makes me very happy.

In April, I added 346 new subscribers.

I had 15 unsubscribes.

That left me with 331 net new humans in my world.

Here is what I actually did to make that happen:

  • Participated in one strategic bundle collaboration
  • Spoke in one summit
  • Hosted my own Visibility Map Workshop
  • Continued publishing my podcast
  • Continued sending emails

That is it.

No 10 new freebies.
No posting 12 Reels a week.
No frantic visibility sprint.

Just aligned moves.

The workshop alone sold 18 paid spots and also created visibility because attendees shared it with their networks.

When you create something genuinely useful, people talk about it.

And when your email strategy is solid, they stay.

The two problems you actually need to solve

If your list is growing but no one is clicking?
It is a nurture problem.

If you are sending emails but your list is not growing?
It is a visibility problem.

It really can be that simple.
Visibility brings people in.
Nurture makes them stay.
Strategy turns that into sales.

Why I share the numbers

Not to flex.

Not to say “look at me.”

But to model what is possible when you treat email like a relationship instead of a megaphone.

Every subscriber is a human.
Every click is curiosity.
Every reply is trust.

And when you keep showing up, even when life is messy, even when you are tired, even when things feel uncertain, that is when momentum builds.

Your homework

Go check your numbers.

  • What were your open rates?
  • What actually got clicks?
  • What flopped?
  • What surprised you?

Look for patterns.

Then send something.

Even if it is messy.
Even if it is short.
Even if it is not perfect.

Just start.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 194

Ever feel like traditional summits just don’t hit the mark anymore? This one’s for you.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I take you behind the scenes of Inside The Inbox Season 2 – the audio only summit that flips the script on what it means to grow, nurture, and sell through your email list in 2025.

We talk about what inspired the event, how Season 2 goes even deeper than before, the charity component I’m beyond proud of, and what’s waiting for you inside the feed.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why I created Inside The Inbox (spoiler: I was done with the BS)
– What’s new in Season 2 (30+ speakers, 3 themed days, and Voxer-style episodes)
– How this event gives you actionable strategies to grow, nurture, and sell
– Why it’s rooted in real relationships – not slides or sales pitches
– How we’re raising money for Small Steps 4 Hannah with every VIP pass

Your next step:

Ready to grow your email list, build real trust, and learn what’s actually working in 2025?
Join Inside The Inbox Season 2 – the audio only event designed to help you grow, nurture, and sell with confidence.

🎧 It’s free, fluff-free, and made for women who want visibility that converts.

Why I Created Inside The Inbox (and Why Season 2 Is Next-Level)

This whole event?
It was born from sheer frustration – straight up.
Frustration with the cookie-cutter summits. The performative panels. The “visibility” advice that looked shiny on the outside but left you with nothing to actually do afterward.

I’m talking about those summits where everyone sounds like they’re reading off the same damn teleprompter.
30-minute Zoom recordings with zero depth, zero personality, and absolutely zero actionable takeaways.
And the ones that dangle “free access” – but it expires before your morning coffee’s even cooled.

And don’t even get me started on the email marketing tips…
“Write good subject lines!”
“Add value!”
“Be consistent!”

Cool. But how?
What does that actually look like today in 2025, when inboxes are crowded, AI summaries are replacing your preview text, and your audience is completely over the bro marketing nonsense?

So I sat with that frustration and thought – what if we did this differently?

What if we took out the pressure and the posturing, and instead created an event that was:
✅ Easy to consume
✅ Grounded in real strategy
✅ Rooted in relationships first
✅ And actually… dare I say… fun AF?

That’s how Inside The Inbox was born.

An audio-only, private podcast event you can binge in your leggings while packing lunchboxes or folding washing.
No slides. No fluff. No Zoom fatigue.
Just honest, tactical, generous conversations with people who actually know what they’re talking about.

Season 1 was our little experiment – and honestly? It blew me away.
Over 1,100 signups.
$1,458 raised for charity.
And the feedback was so positive, I knew we had something special.
You can watch the case study all about how that went down here!

Season 2?
We’re going even bigger – and better.

This time, I’ve even created a quiz to help you figure out exactly what strategies, speakers, and sessions are going to move the needle for your unique business. Because this isn’t about bingeing 20 interviews and walking away with another giant to-do list.
No thanks.

This is about clarity. Intention. Strategy that serves.

So I made it even simpler:

At the end of every single episode in Season 2, I outline one action step you can take that day – yes, that day – to grow your audience or improve your email strategy. No guesswork. No pressure. Just one clear move forward.

Because if I know anything, it’s this:
We don’t need more information.
We need direction.
We need to know what’s working – and then feel confident enough to actually try it.

That’s the whole energy behind Inside The Inbox.

It’s not about more noise.
It’s about better results – built on real strategy, real people, and real relationships.

What’s Coming in Season 2

Season 2 of Inside The Inbox is designed to cut the fluff and bring you smart, soulful, bingeable strategies that actually work in 2025.

We’ve got 4 powerful days, 30+ incredible voices, and every episode is under 15 minutes – so you can learn while you’re making lunch, on school pick-up, or squeezing in a walk.

Let’s break it down:

Step One: List Growth That Feels Like You

No cookie-cutter lead magnet advice here – we’re getting real about how to grow a list that’s aligned, intentional, and full of dream clients who want to hear from you.

Some of the speakers I’m highlighting include:

→ Dallas Travers shares how she donates $1 per subscriber – and how that value-driven approach changed her list growth and her business.
→ Nadalie Bardo breaks down how she uses Pinterest to drive evergreen traffic and signups, without the pressure of constantly creating content.
→ Tiffany Crenshaw shows how to turn real-life conversations into subscribers – reminding us that offline connection still works wonders
… and more!

You’ll walk away with fresh, creative strategies to attract the right people – without the burnout.

Step Two: Nurture Without the Noise

Want your emails to actually mean something? This is about building trust, connection, and a nurture strategy that keeps people coming back for more.

→ Emjae reframes email with her soulful “write to one, speak to many” mindset – it’s a game-changer.
→ Tara Reid walks through her 6-month nurture sequence that keeps her list warm, loved, and ready to buy.
→ Susan Lovett makes a bold case for ditching the templates and finally using your own voice in the inbox.

These are the conversations that will help you turn subscribers into superfans – setting you up beautifully for step 3…

Step Three: Selling That Feels Good

No sleazy tactics. No manufactured urgency. This is all about selling with integrity – and building a business that actually gets paid.

→ Jessica Andersen shares how a “post-launch” email – the one she almost didn’t send – ended up making the sale.
→ Lise Cartwright teaches her system for weekly flash sales that bring in consistent revenue, no stress required.
→ Sreedevi V reveals what happened when she emailed every day for a month – and why she’s doing it again.

You’ll leave with at least 3 new ways to sell that feel simple, strategic, and so you.

What Makes This Format So Damn Effective

Look, I’m a mum. I’m running two programs. I’m managing my team.
I don’t have time for another summit that requires 27 logins and 14 Zoom links.

So I made this for people like us.

• You sign up here: kyliekelly.com/inbox
• You get access to a private podcast feed.
• You listen when and how you want – no fluff, no pressure, no replays that expire in 6 seconds.

And the best part? You feel like you’re in the room.
These conversations are raw, real, and totally voxer-style – because I want you to hear the “ums,” the laughter, the human-ness. That’s where the magic is.

Let’s Talk About the Charity (Because This Matters)

Just like last season, Inside The Inbox isn’t just about growing your email list or learning smarter strategies – it’s also about giving back.

Just like last time, I’ve chosen to support Small Steps 4 Hannah – an incredible Australian charity doing life-saving work to end domestic and family violence. They’re leading the charge in creating change through education, community programs, and public advocacy – all in honour of Hannah Clarke and her three beautiful children.

This cause hits me hard.

Because while we’re out here building businesses and chasing big, bold dreams, there are women who are simply fighting to feel safe in their own homes. And if Inside The Inbox can help change even one life through this event… then that’s the kind of impact I want this business to have.

So here’s how we’re doing it:

Every time someone upgrades to the VIP Pass, a portion of the profits goes straight to Small Steps 4 Hannah.

No gatekeeping.
No extra donation buttons.
No “portion of proceeds will maybe go to charity.”

Just real impact. Built into the business. No questions asked.

Last time, we raised $1,458 – and honestly? That blew me away.
This time, I want to double that.

So when you upgrade to VIP – yes, you get lifetime access to the episodes, co-working sessions with me and exclusive bonuses…
But more importantly?

You help take a small, powerful step toward making the world safer for women and children.

And I don’t know about you but that’s the kind of business I want to run.
One that creates ripple effects beyond just revenue.
One that stands for something.

Final Thought From Kylie

Inside The Inbox Season 2 is here. And it’s built for women like you – busy, brilliant, ready for more.
If you’ve been craving a smarter way to grow – without selling your soul – this is it.

Sign up: kyliekelly.com/inbox
Share it with a biz bestie.
Grab your VIP Pass if you can.
And let’s raise some money for a cause that actually matters.

I’ll see you inside the inbox.

title: Let’s Stop Calling It “Value” If It Doesn’t Actually Help Anyone
excerpt: THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 192 Can we talk about “value” for a second? content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 192

Can we talk about “value” for a second?

Because if I see one more vanilla-ass carousel claiming to “add value” with five productivity tips and a beige Canva template, I might actually scream.

Somewhere along the way, “just give value” became the holy grail of online marketing.

Lead with value.
Post value.
Create valuable content and the sales will follow.

But here’s the uncomfortable truth.

Not everything we label as value is actually helpful.

And if your content isn’t helping, it’s just noise.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE TO READ THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Hey, hey, welcome back to a mini solo episode of the Email Growth Show. These Tuesday episodes are short, spicy, and sound a whole lot like a voice note I’d send you after seeing one too many vanilla-ass Instagram carousels pretending to be valuable. Today, you guessed it, we’re talking about value. That word is everywhere. Just give value, lead with value, create valuable content and sales will follow. But you know what? If I see one more carousel with 3 tips to stay productive on a Monday, I might actually fucking scream. Because here’s the truth. Not everything we think is value actually is.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:36]:
We have to stop calling it value when it’s just noise. Just because you posted something educational, just because you shared a how-to or a tip or a motivational quote doesn’t mean your audience actually felt anything. And that’s the whole point, right? Real value creates momentum. It makes someone stop scrolling. It makes them feel understood. It gives them a next step or a new lens to look through. Now, I’m gonna say something bold, but I know you are here for that, right? Your audience does not need another Canva graphic of the buyer’s journey. They don’t need more content.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:07]:
They need more clarity. They need more connection. They need to feel like you’re the real fucking deal, not just the next pretty voice in the void. Let me paint you a little picture. You write a post, 5 ways to improve your lead magnet, but then what? There’s no call to action, no story, no invitation into your world, just a little hope this helps at the end, and then crickets. But imagine instead, and I’m going to use myself as the example, if I told them why lead magnets usually don’t work, if I explained how I used mine to grow my list by 10,000 subscribers, if I shared a client example, and then I said, do you want help fixing yours? Come and join the Email Growth Club. I’ve got a whole workshop waiting for you. That is value.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:49]:
It’s not just helpful, it actually leads somewhere and it moves the relationship forward. So let me be really clear here. Real value equals clarity, connection, and conversion. If it’s not building trust, if it’s not making your audience feel something, and if it’s not rooted in who you are and how you serve, then it’s just content for content’s sake. And I say this with so much love because I’ve been there too. I’ve written posts because I felt like I had to. I’ve shared tips that sounded good on paper but didn’t do shit for my business. I’ve pushed value out into the world because I thought I was supposed to.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:25]:
But I wasn’t really saying anything at all. And do you know when it changed? When I started asking myself, does this move someone? Does this help them take action or see things differently? Does this sound like me? And honestly, that shift changed everything because now when I share content, normally on the podcast, it’s with purpose. I write with rhythm in my emails and I sell with so much less pressure because the value is already doing half the work for me. So if you’re wondering, why isn’t my content converting? Why is no one opening my emails? Why does everything feel like I’m shouting into the fucking void? Let me gently, or not so gently, ask you this. Is your content actually helping anyone? Or are you just checking the be consistent box? Because consistency without connection is just busy work. And something that I learned the hard way, busy work does not pay the bills. So here’s your spicy little assignment for today. I want you to stop overthinking what to post.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:22]:
Stop trying to sound like your favorite online online coach. Stop posting value just because it looks good on your grid. I want you to start creating content that’s true. True to your voice, true to your offers, and true to your audience. Tell the stories you’re scared to tell. Share the opinion that makes you stand out. Write the fucking email that sounds like you, not another email template. Because that, that is what people remember.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:45]:
That’s what builds trust. That’s what’s going to make someone want to work with you. So look, if this hit home today, come and find me on Instagram. You can find me over at @KylieKelley. Send me a DM. Tell me what kind of fake value you’re leaving behind and what kind of content you’re ready to start sharing instead. And of course, if you want support creating messaging that actually connects and sells, that’s what I help my members do inside of the Email Growth Club. You’ll find the link in the show notes below.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:09]:
Now, I’ll see you Friday for a full episode on my Signature Rise Framework, the exact structure I use with my clients to help them build visibility with purpose. Until then, go and make some real fucking magic. You’ve got this. I love you, and I will see you on Friday. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning in.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:26]:
To this episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:37]:
If you enjoyed this episode, please take.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:39]:
A moment to rate and review the show and share it with others.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:42]:
Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening, and I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The difference between surface-level “value” and content that actually converts
– Why connection > content (especially during a trust recession)
– How to shift from performative posting to purposeful visibility
– Why intentional strategy always trumps volume

Ready to create messaging that actually connects?

If you are done creating content that looks good but does nothing for your business, this is your next move.

Inside the Empire Expansion Event, I teach you how to build visibility with purpose and create messaging that connects and converts.

We go beyond generic “value” and build a strategy rooted in clarity, connection, and conversion.

👉 Save your spot at the Empire Expansion Event here!

P.S. If you want your content to stop feeling like noise and start driving real momentum, the Empire Expansion Event will show you exactly how to make that shift.

Educational does not equal valuable…

Just because you posted something educational does not mean it created impact.

A how-to.
A checklist.
A motivational quote.

That alone is not value.

Real value does three things:

It creates clarity.
It builds connection.
It leads somewhere.

If your audience reads your post and feels absolutely nothing, that is not value. That is content for content’s sake.

And content for content’s sake does not pay the bills.

Your audience does not need more content

They need more clarity.
They need to feel understood.
They need to believe you are the real fucking deal, not just another pretty voice floating around the internet.

Let me give you an example.

You post: “5 ways to improve your lead magnet.”

Cool.

Now what?

There is no story.
No opinion.
No call to action.
No invitation into your world.

It ends with “Hope this helps” and then… crickets.

But imagine instead you told them:

Why most lead magnets fail.
How you used yours to grow your list by 10,000 subscribers.
What a client changed that doubled their opt-ins.
And then you said, “If you want help fixing yours, come join my Email Growth Club. There’s a full workshop waiting for you.”

That is value.

Because it moves the relationship forward.

Real value has direction

Here is the framework I want you to burn into your brain:

Real value = Clarity + Connection + Conversion.

Clarity means your audience understands something better than they did five minutes ago.
Connection means they feel seen, understood, or challenged in a way that resonates.
Conversion means there is a next step. It does not have to be a hard sell. But it leads somewhere.

If your content is missing one of those pieces, it is probably not working as hard as you think it is.

Consistency without connection is busy work

This one might sting a little.

If you are posting three times a week, sending weekly emails, showing up everywhere, and still hearing crickets, it might not be a consistency problem.

It might be a connection problem.
I say this with love because I have been there.

I have written posts because I felt like I had to.
I have shared tips that sounded smart but did nothing for my business.
I have created “value” because I thought that was what good marketers did.

But I was not really saying anything.

The shift happened when I started asking myself:

Does this move someone?
Does this help them see something differently?
Does this actually sound like me?

When the answer was yes, everything changed.

My emails felt lighter.
My selling felt easier.
The pressure dropped because the value was already doing half the work.

If it is not moving someone, it is just noise

Let me gently ask you something.

When you look at your last five pieces of content, did they actually help someone take action?

Or were they ticking the “be consistent” box?

Because consistency without purpose is just busy work.

And busy work does not create sales. It creates burnout.

Your audience does not need more generic tips.

They need your opinion.
Your stories.
Your lived experience.
Your perspective.

They need content that feels like it came from a human, not a template.

Here is your spicy assignment

Stop trying to sound like your favourite online coach.

Stop posting “value” because it looks good on your grid.

Stop watering down your message so it feels safe.

Start creating content that is true.

True to your voice.
True to your offers.
True to the transformation you actually deliver.

Tell the story you have been holding back.

Share the opinion that makes you stand out.

Write the fucking email that sounds like you, not something you copied from a swipe file.
Because that is what builds trust.
That is what people remember.

That is what converts.
