content:
Feat. Business Consultant Angela Henderson

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 191

What if the next big growth moment in your business had nothing to do with funnels or fancy sales pages… and everything to do with genuine connection?

In this powerful episode of The Email Growth Show, I’m joined by business consultant and event queen Angela Henderson to unpack how one in-person event (that wasn’t even designed to sell!) turned into $300,000+ in sales.

Angela doesn’t hold back – she shares the real numbers, the intentional backend strategy, and how different buyer types respond to different follow-up approaches. This one’s a masterclass in connection, courage, and not leaving money on the table.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– How Angela ran a live 100-person event without selling from stage (and still made over $300K!)
– The real role follow-up plays in your revenue (and why you’re probably skipping it)
– The 4 types of buyers Angela sells to – and how each one needs a different experience
– What it really means to self-sabotage (and how childhood patterns show up in business)
– Why simplicity and inner work are the keys to sustainable growth

From hug meditations to mastermind sales

Angela’s 2024 Australian Women in Business conference wasn’t your typical high-pressure business event.

No one sold from stage. Every speaker agreed: no hard pitches. There was a hugging meditation. There were real moments. And the entire thing was designed as a top-of-funnel brand experience – a place to build connection, trust, and authority.

The result?

  • 100 attendees
  • $25K in revenue from the event itself (without selling anything)
  • Over $300K in mastermind sales afterward

Angela focused on creating an experience that built deep, embodied trust. And when she followed up with warmth, intention, and options?

The sales came in – and keep coming.

The fortune is in the follow-up

You don’t need a fancy system. You don’t need a new funnel. You probably don’t even need more leads.

You need to follow-up.

Angela shared how a single follow-up effort after the holidays turned into a $36,000 week – simply by revisiting conversations she had months earlier.

“Not one of those people followed up with me… but when I reached out again, they were still interested. I would have left $36,000 on the table if I hadn’t initiated.”

Her reminder?

You are responsible for your results. Don’t wait to be chosen. Follow up.

The 4 types of buyers (& why you need to market to all of them)

Angela breaks down her framework of four buyer types based on levels of consciousness:

  1. Intuitive Buyers – Gut instinct. Quick to take action. (Hi, it me 🙋‍♀️)
  2. Wilful Buyers – Want basic details + light validation.
  3. Intellectual Buyers – Need all the info, testimonials, calls, case studies.
  4. Reactive Buyers – Urgency-driven. Countdown timers. Scarcity.

You need to speak to all four in your launch content, your emails, and your visibility strategy.

Missing one could mean missing a sale.

Inner work & visibility go hand in hand

This episode went way deeper than conversion strategy. Angela opened up about the inner work required to stop hiding behind your business and start showing up.

Whether it’s an old classroom trauma or subtle childhood rejection, many of us are still carrying patterns that lead to procrastination, perfectionism, and people-pleasing.

Angela’s advice?

  • Get curious about what’s really driving your fear
  • Heal where you need to
  • Don’t let inner work become another form of hiding

Your next step: Do the simplest thing

Want to stop spinning and start selling?

Start with these:

  1. Follow-up with someone you’ve already talked to
  2. Look at your content through the lens of your buyer types
  3. Prioritize real connection (hello, audio summits and bundles!)

And if you’re ready to grow your business in a bold, relationship-first way?

Come join us inside The Headliner Mastermind – where we combine powerful visibility strategy, mindset coaching, and real community to help you become a household name.

Guest Spotlight: Angela Henderson

Angela is a business consultant, podcaster, speaker, and event host who helps women create personalized strategies and master their mindset. She’s the founder of the Australian Women in Business Conference and a powerhouse when it comes to sustainable growth and embodied leadership.

Website: angelahenderson.com.au

So you are more that intuitive. This feels right. It’s a full body yes. Do you know what I mean? And I’m in. You know? You’re like, I don’t need the sales page. I don’t like, I’m like, you were in.

Angela Henderson [00:08:33]:

It’s the inner work. And I would say you’re self sabotaging. And I would say that self sabotage is ultimately just self protecting. But in your brain, because you’re only four and your brain’s only developed so much, you cognitively have told yourself a story, but your mind and body and soul have also felt this. Angela Henderson [00:13:04]:

One of the other sayings that I love that you have drilled into me since we’ve been working together is the fortune is in the follow-up. Oh, gosh. It was a a mistake that I made. Even sometimes, I’ve gotta remind myself, you know, the list goes on. But the fortune is in the follow-up. So often, we continue to keep making new things, new connections, new follow-up, new podcasts, new outreach, new whatever. But you actually have so much low hanging fruit just right in front of you. So a lot of people are like, I need 20 more discovery calls. Okay.

Angela Henderson [00:17:49]:
But have you followed up with the past 20 discovery call people? Oh, well, I sent them an email after our discovery call. Did you follow-up after that? No. Well, okay. I’ll give you an example. So Christmas came. I had 10 people who had said to me in November and December that they wanted to work with me for 2025. But Christmas, someone died. There was a bunch of things.

Angela Henderson [00:18:09]:
So I said, cool. No worries. None of those 10 people reached back out to me, but I’d written on a piece of paper what they had said, why they couldn’t do it, what they were looking forward to. It doesn’t mean they don’t need you.

Angela Henderson [00:18:42]:
And some of those other people I didn’t hear back from. I have to be okay that just because it’s a no now doesn’t mean it’s a no forever. But I literally could have thrown away $36,000 if I wouldn’t have been the one to initiate the follow-up. So follow-up is so important, and I encourage you to do so every day I try. But then I will literally write out who are the three people I need to follow-up with today.

Angela Henderson [00:19:09]:
And I’ll, like, write it out. Just three. Sometimes it’s more than three, but it should be a minimum of three. Who could you be outreaching to to follow-up on that podcast that you thought? Who could you be reaching out to to, do you know what I mean? Spark new conversations. Every day we would have people to follow-up on. And what I love

about you, Ange, I can imagine it’s simple follow-up. Right?

Angela Henderson [00:19:27]:
No. It’s literally like, hey, Kylie. I know you talked about getting me on your podcast. Just wanted to see if we can get that date in. And sometimes people will let their ego start to come in the way because they’ll be like, well, Kylie should’ve it’s her podcast. She should’ve emailed me. No. That didn’t happen, by the way, for the listener, but I’m using it as an example.

Angela Henderson [00:19:43]:
But it’s like, yeah. But Kylie might just again, maybe her grandma died. Maybe her the cat died. Maybe someone got unwell and had COVID, and the whole house was sick, and she was the only one that could go and manage it. I don’t know. But quite frankly, it doesn’t matter because we had that conversation. I’m responsible for my life. I wanna go on Kylie’s podcast, so I will reach out to her.

Angela Henderson [00:20:02]:
Drop the ego. Follow-up. And then it’d be like, sure, Ange. No worries. Yes. Here’s my booking link. Okay. Don’t over complicate things.

Kylie Kelly [00:20:09]:
I love it when people follow-up because my inbox can often look like a dumpster fire. Right? So it, like, pops it to back to the top. I’m like, oh, yes. I wanted that.

Angela Henderson [00:20:17]:
A %. Yep. And that’s the reality is everyone’s just living busy lives. You’ve got kids. You’ve got extracurricular activities. You know, that’s a whole job within itself. I believe it’s a yes until someone tells me a no. So then why aren’t we not following up? There’s opportunities every single day, but then people are like, oh, I’ll just start a new lead magnet.

Angela Henderson [00:20:36]:
Oh, I’ll just go start a new course. Oh, I’ll just this isn’t working. But a lot of times, things are actually working in your favor if you just go back to basics.

Kylie Kelly [00:20:45]:
Mhmm. Do you have a system for this?

Angela Henderson [00:20:46]:
I’ve got my calendar that I use, but I also a lot of times, like, especially when I’m working with clients and things like that, I just I’m still old school notes. And so it’s like, even today, for example what else do I have on here? Follow-up about speaking event. Follow-up about podcast. Follow-up about quiz. Do you know what I mean? Like, these that’s three things. And so I’ll just write it down so that I know that I need to follow it up. I do that. But when it’s, like, following up with other partners, for example, that I may have worked with in the past, we just have all the partners’ names down, put it in a spreadsheet, follow it up on this day, and reach out to people.

Angela Henderson [00:21:17]:
So it it does come down to having a good system, but it doesn’t have to be overcomplicated. Use your calendar. Set a reminder. Use your notebook and paper. Create a spreadsheet. Do whatever that works for your brain.

Kylie Kelly [00:21:28]:
Yeah. I love that. And I guess, like you said before, I think our the conversation we just had about triggers and things works here too. Because what stories are you telling yourself that’s stopping you following up. Right?

Angela Henderson [00:21:37]:
100%. If I follow-up, I actually might get more money. And if I get more money, I might actually have to quit my day job. There’s three primary reasons around, like, our subconscious that make up 97% of the decisions that we do, which is I don’t feel safe, I don’t belong, and I’m not enough. Even before our decision comes out of our mouth, we’ve already it’s one of those three things typically that has made those decisions for us. Again, it goes back to the inner work. Thank you for sharing so much with us. You’ve left me with a lot to think about as always after our conversations, which I just adore. If anyone wants to know more, work with you, dive into your world, where should we send them?

Yeah. I just say I always go go to my primary ecosystem, which is angelahenderson.com.au. And then from there, you can listen to my podcast. You can book a discovery call, look at the event. Amazing. Thank you. Thank you so much for being here, and I’ll put the link in the show notes for everybody as well.

No worries. Have a beautiful day, my friend.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 189

This idea that you have to pick one business model?

Fuckin’ toss it.
Burn it.
Pour a spicy mug on it and dance on the ashes.

You are allowed to build a business that’s smart.
That’s layered and rooted in your values.

Let’s talk about it.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why the “one model only” advice is so outdated (and limiting)

The “Pick One” pressure is real

You’ve heard it.

“Only sell high ticket – you don’t need a big audience.”

“No babe, low ticket is how you scale. Passive income forever.”

“Never sell anything under $1,000.”

Honestly?

It’s exhausting – and for most women building real businesses with real humans on the other side – it’s completely unrealistic.

You’re not a robot.
You’re a multidimensional business owner.

And your audience? They’re not all in the same place either.

Some are ready to invest deeply right now.
Some need nurturing.
Some want to test the waters.

If you only build for one type of buyer, you’re missing:

  • Revenue
  • Impact

  • Momentum

Here’s what I actually believe

You don’t have to choose.

You need a layered offer suite.

One that:

  • Brings in cash flow
  • Builds recurring revenue
  • Warms up future premium clients
  • Supports people at every stage

Let me show you what that looks like in real life.

How my business is structured

Inside my world, I have:

High-Ticket: My Mastermind

Deep, high-touch, transformational work.

Weekly hot seats.
1:1 strategy.
Mindset coaching.
Visibility mapping through my R.I.S.E. framework.

This is intimate, powerful, and results-driven.
It’s where massive breakthroughs happen.

Low-Ticket: Skool Community with a $49 p/m paid tier

Accessible.
Scalable.
Community-based.

Templates, tools, coaching calls, accountability.

It builds trust.
It nurtures buyers.
It creates recurring revenue.

It’s also where I test ideas and nurture future mastermind clients – without pressure.

Free Content: Podcast, Emails, Events

This is the handshake.
The shop window.
The “I see you.”

This is where trust starts long before someone clicks buy.

And here’s the magic:
Most of my mastermind clients didn’t start there.

They started with free content.
Then joined the community.
Then upgraded.

That’s a human funnel.

Why this model works

Let’s break it down simply.

High Ticket Gives You:

  • Immediate cash injections
  • Deep transformation
  • Fewer clients, higher impact
  • Intimate, premium support

Low Ticket Gives You:

  • Scalability
  • Recurring revenue
  • Audience growth
  • Buyer segmentation
  • A pathway to upgrade

Free Content Gives You:

  • Trust
  • Authority
  • Demand

When these three work together?
You stop trying to force one model to do everything.

You build depth.
You build sustainability.
You build options.

The real problem with “Pick a Lane” advice

It boxes you in.

It makes you think: “I can only be this kind of business.”
But you’re allowed to evolve.

You’re allowed to serve beginners and CEOs.
You’re allowed to have recurring income and big cash months.
You’re allowed to design your offers around your life.

Not the other way around.

A business with layers = A business with power

When you give people a clear next step, they take it.
When you design your offers intentionally, upgrades feel natural.
When your ecosystem makes sense, revenue becomes predictable.

And most importantly?

You stop feeling like you’re rebuilding your business every time someone new on Instagram declares “THIS is the only way to scale.” No.
There are multiple ways – and you get to choose what aligns.

If your offer suite feels messy or confusing…

If you’re not sure:

  • What your high-ticket should be

This is exactly what I help you map out inside a Business Breakthrough Audit.

No more choosing between high-ticket or low-ticket.

Design both.
Layer it intentionally.
And build something that actually supports the life you’re creating.

You’re allowed to want depth and scale.

Let’s build it. 💛

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 188

Here’s what I’m anti.

Copy-and-paste marketing that makes you sound like a robot.
Strategy shortcuts that ignore who you are and who your audience is.
Funnels that look good on paper but fall flat because there’s zero connection.

If your entire visibility and email strategy is built on swipe files you bought in someone’s $97 tripwire funnel…

Babe.
We need to talk.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. I hope you feel inspired to create your own start here email and ditch the welcome sequence if it is no longer serving you and your ideal clients. Reach out if you have any questions.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:19]:
I love you loads and I will talk to you really soon, like really soon. I’ve got some really good stuff coming your way and next week’s episode is our guest episode with an incredible, incredible PR expert. You’re going to want to tune in. All right, I will see you then. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the.

Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The #1 problem with overused templates and swipe files
– Why cookie-cutter funnels fail (even if they “worked for her”)
– How to build connection and trust without burning out
– How I use GPT bots + custom templates inside The Email Growth Club (and why they work)

Ready to build your business alongside other women ditching social media?

If you’re done hiding behind swipe files and ready to build funnels rooted in trust, come join us inside my free Skool community!

This isn’t plug-and-play marketing.

It’s relationship-first strategy that converts.

👉 Join the community here: kyliekelly.com/group

Less copy-paste.
More connection.

That’s where the magic is.

I’m not anti-template (but…)

Let’s clear something up.
I am not anti-template.

I create templates.
I give templates to my clients.
I use frameworks in my own business.

Templates can be powerful – but only when they’re used as a starting point – not a personality replacement.

The problem isn’t the template.
The problem is when you:

  • Copy.
  • Paste.
  • Hit send.
  • And hope it magically converts.

Because what worked for someone else worked for a reason. It was build on their unique voice, their offer, their audience and most importantly, the trust that they have built with their email list.

You cannot shortcut that.

“But it’s easier…”

I get it.

You’re busy and tired and you’ve probably got 1001 things on your to do list.
You’ve got clients, kids, laundry, content deadlines, and 37 open tabs in your brain at any given time… me too.

So when someone says:
“Here’s my exact 10-email nurture sequence that made $250K.”

Of course it sounds like the dream.

But here’s what they don’t tell you:
That sequence converted because their audience already trusted them.

It reflected their personality.
Their positioning.
Their lived experience.

When you drop it into your business without adapting it?

It sounds polished but it feels hollow.
And your audience can feel that.

We’re in a trust recession

This is the part most marketers aren’t talking about.

We are in a trust recession.

People have:

  • Seen the fake Stripe dashboards
  • Watched the AI-generated launch videos
  • Clicked on glossy sales pages with zero substance
  • Been overpromised and underdelivered

Your audience is more skeptical than ever.
When they open your email, they’re not just asking:

“What’s in it for me?”

They’re subconsciously asking:

  • Do I trust this person?
  • Does this feel real?
  • Is this safe?

If the answer is no?

It doesn’t matter how optimized your funnel is – they will be out.

What actually works

Here’s what I see working – in my business and in my clients’ businesses:

Emails that sound like they were written on your phone, coffee in hand, waiting at daycare pickup.
Funnels that are simple, soulful, and built to nurture – not manipulate.
Messaging that feels aligned as fuck because it’s yours.

Not Jenna’s.
Not Amy’s.
Not the latest guru’s.

Yours.

Because people don’t buy because your funnel is technically perfect.

They buy because they feel:

Seen.
Safe.
Understood.

They buy because they feel like you actually give a shit.

So should you ditch templates completely?

No – but you should customize the shit out of them.

You should:

  • Inject your voice
  • Add context
  • Rewrite examples
  • Change stories
  • Break the rules when they don’t feel aligned

Whenever I give my clients templates, I don’t just give them over and say see you later.

We unpack why they work.
We tweak them.
We humanize them.
We layer in strategy and nuance.

Because the swipe file alone is never the strategy.

Relationship-first marketing is.

If your funnel isn’t converting…

Let me lovingly say this:

If your list is growing but no one is buying…
If your emails are “technically right” but falling flat…
If your funnel looks impressive but feels disconnected…

It might not be a tech problem.
It might be a voice problem.
It might be a trust problem.

It might be that you’ve been squeezing your magic into someone else’s formula.

And your audience can feel that misalignment.

Here’s your permission slip

You do not need:

  • A 92-email launch sequence
  • Fake urgency timers
  • Scarcity triggers that make you cringe
  • To sound like the “next big name” online

You need to sound like you.

That’s the real secret.

Not louder.
Not more complicated.
Not more automated.

More honest.
More human.
More connected.

Stop sounding like everyone else

If you’ve been relying on swipe files, plug-and-play funnels, or “proven” email sequences that don’t quite feel like you… this is your sign to do it differently.

Come and join my free Skool community and start to learn how to build your email list with relationships at the centre.

This isn’t about hacking the algorithm.
It’s about building authority.
It’s about building trust.
It’s about building something that lasts.

👉 Join my community here: http://kyliekelly.com/group

No more copy-paste confidence.
No more hiding behind “what works.”

It’s time to send emails that actually sounds like you – and converts because of it. 💛

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 187

We’re in a trust recession – and it’s changing how people buy, engage, and say yes online. In this episode, I’m walking you through what’s really going on in the online business space, and 5 real ways to build trust that actually converts.

Let’s be real – the online space feels noisy as hell right now.
Sales feel slower.
Launches aren’t landing.
Engagement is… meh.
And it’s not just you – we’re in what people are calling a Trust Recession.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– What the ‘trust recession’ actually means
– How visibility without trust leads to silence (and how to fix it)
– 5 ways to build trust in 2025 without burning out
– Why saying the thing others won’t = instant credibility
– What works right now in Kylie’s own business

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Ready to build an aligned audience – that actually engages & buys?
Join The Email Growth Club – and let’s do this together.

Click here to join today!

The online space feels… noisier than ever

Everywhere you scroll, someone is selling something. AI is generating copy. Launches are popping up left, right, and centre. Someone shared a million-dollar Stripe dashboard recently that was completely fake – and it looked so legit it could fool anyone.

It’s no wonder audiences are more cautious.

People are skeptical. Jaded. Distrusting.

And that means your job as a business owner is not just to stand out.
It’s to rebuild trust.
Because visibility on its own? It isn’t enough anymore.

We’ve all seen it. Someone goes viral, gains thousands of followers overnight, and then? Crickets. No buyers. No real traction.

Why?

Because visibility without trust doesn’t convert.

That perfectly curated feed? Doesn’t matter if no one believes you can help them. That 10k email list? Doesn’t matter if no one opens your emails. That 5-day challenge? Doesn’t matter if no one trusts you enough to buy at the end of it.

So… what do we do about it?

We shift.
We get intentional.
And we rebuild trust at the core of our businesses.

👀 Pssst – This is exactly what we’re working on inside The Email Growth Club and Headliner Mastermind. Ready to rebuild trust and grow without burning out? Book a free 30 minute visibility audit with me today!

Here are 5 powerful ways to do that:

1. Show your face. Use your voice.

People trust people – not logos, not taglines. Show up. Be seen. Use your podcast, emails, or video to let people get to know you. Let them hear your laugh, your accent, your stumbles.

Because connection? It starts with showing up as YOU.

2. Say the thing that others won’t.

If you’re always playing it safe, never rocking the boat, never saying what you really think… you’re not building trust.

You’re being vanilla.

Have a point of view. Let it be clear. Thought leadership doesn’t mean controversy for the sake of it – it means honesty. It means depth. It means being known for something real.

3. Deliver what you promise – and then some.

This one’s simple.

If your freebie says it’ll teach something? Teach it.
If your email says it has a gift? Deliver it.

Trust grows in the micro-moments where you keep your word.

When people walk away thinking, “Wow, she actually delivered.”

4. Show the journey, not just the highlight reel.

Share the behind-the-scenes.

Talk about the failed launches. The lessons. The messy middle.

Let people see that you’re in it with them – not just standing on the mountaintop yelling, “Look how great I am!”

5. Prioritise connection over conversion.

Reply to DMs. Answer emails. Show up in rooms your dream clients are already in.

Relationship-first visibility always outperforms the surface-level stuff.

Every single time.

Final Thought: This is the kind of work I help my clients with!

Whether it’s inside The Email Growth Club or my Headliner Mastermind, this is what we focus on:

Not just audience growth, but aligned audience growth.

Not just email marketing, but email marketing that connects.

Not just visibility, but visibility that leads somewhere.

Because when you lead with trust?

The sales still come. Actually – they come easier.

So if you’re feeling like launches are quiet, content isn’t landing, or you’re starting to second-guess everything, come back to trust… and start there.

Things are uncertain economically, socially, globally. There’s been this collective pulling back, this caution in the air. People are more intentional about where they spend their time, their energy, and especially their money. Plus, AI is everywhere, and more and more of what we’re seeing is fake as fuck.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:59]:
Last night, I legit saw someone post a photo of a Stripe dashboard showing a million dollar year and it turns out it was all fucking AI generated, but it looked so real. And this is exactly the problem. So as business owners and marketers, we can’t pretend like it’s business as usual because it’s not. We can’t rely on the flashy tricks or the one size fits all templates. We can’t out hype a trust recession. The only thing that cuts through the noise right now is real trust. And that means it’s time to double down on what actually works. Building relationships, showing up consistently, creating content that connects instead of just converts, and treating your audience like fucking humans, not just leads.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:42]:
Let me say this clearly. Trust is the strategy. Inside my own business, I’ve felt this shift really deeply. The best results that I’ve seen lately, they’re not from some magic funnel. They’re from things like inside the inbox where people told me that they felt seen and supported. This podcast, yep, this one that you’re listening to right here, which has become a consistent trust building engine for me. And simply being in people’s inboxes with value, transparency and realness. Because here’s the thing: when someone trusts you, they’ll listen.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:12]:
When someone trusts you, they’ll refer you. And when someone trusts you, they’ll buy from you again and again. So how do we actually build trust when this online world feels a little bit shaky? Let me walk you through five ways to build unshakable trust with your audience even during a so called trust recession. Number one. Show your face. Use your voice. People trust people. Not logos, not brands.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:40]:
You. Show up in your emails. Use your podcast to speak from the heart. Record a voice memo. Post a photo without a filter or makeup. Let them see the real you because people buy from humans, not from Canva graphics. And if this makes you hesitate, if this makes you cringe, I need to tell you with love to get out of your own fucking way. People do not care what you look like.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:02]:
They do not care about if you’re carrying a little bit of extra weight right now. They don’t care about how beautiful your kitchen is. They want to connect with you, the person behind the business, the person that could help them solve a really painful problem if they got out of their own way and showed up. Right? If they could start to show their audience that they trusted them. And you have to show your face. You have to use your voice to be able to do that. Number two. Say the things that others won’t.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:30]:
Now you don’t need to be edgy or spicy for the sake of it, but you do need to have a fucking point of view. Stop playing it safe. Stop being vanilla. Vanilla does not build trust. It builds forgetability. Is that even a word? But it’s fucking forgetful. Right? Speak the truth. Say the quiet part out loud.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:47]:
Say what your dream clients wish somebody would finally have the guts to say. Some of my spicy takes are definitely coming onto the podcast every Tuesday, hence the new little mini solo episodes. And they revolve around some of these opinions that I have. They revolve around the fact that you don’t need a fucking email template, you just need to be using your own voice. That saying yes to everyone isn’t a strategy, right? Like there are so many little truths that I am not afraid to say anymore. And I must admit, like, this was part of my journey. This was something that I’ve grown into. But right now, even if this makes you a little bit uncomfortable, you need to get better at speaking up.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:24]:
You need to get better at using your voice to have an opinion so that you can stand out, so that you can attract your perfect people that agree with your opinion, that want to be in your world, that then can start to trust you, so that you can serve them, so that you can grow an audience of people that know, like, and trust you, that want to work with you, that that actually support you in everything that you do. Because that, right there, when you start using your voice, when you start saying the things that others won’t, that is a thing that is going to change everything for you. Right? That’s going to change your business. If you’re sitting here and you are feeling vanilla and stagnant and you’re not making progress and you don’t know what to do next, fucking start using your voice. Start saying the things that others won’t. Have a point of view. Have an opinion and start speaking out about the things that you feel really passionate about in your industry, in your niche, in your corner. Because I can guarantee that there are gonna be other people that are thinking the exact same thing.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:15]:
Number three. Deliver what you promise and then some. This one is simple but so overlooked. If your freebie promises a three step system, make sure it actually teaches them something. If you’re hosting a bundle, make sure it’s fucking high quality and well organised and clear. If you are going to go live, fucking show up. Don’t pull the pin last minute. Like truth grows in micro moments.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:36]:
It grows when people feel like you do what you say you’re going to do. Become a woman of your word. Make sure that you deliver what you promise and then some. Be the person that over delivers every damn time. People will notice. Number four. Show the journey, not just the highlight real. We do not trust perfection.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:53]:
We trust real. We trust messy. We trust behind the scenes. So don’t just share the striped screenshot, whether it’s AI generated or not. Share what you tested to get that result. Share the freebie that failed. Share the ghost town webinar that you did last year that only your mum attended. Hell, if it was me, no one was there.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:08]:
Not even my mum. Let your people in and not because it’s vulnerable for vulnerability’s sake, but because that’s how trust is built. They need to see the journey. They need to see the progress. Then they can picture themselves in your shoes, trying the things to get to the result. And they’re going to trust that you’re not full of shit, that you actually have done the work to get to where you are. There is no such thing as an overnight success. We know that.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:30]:
Right? All the income claims that we see on fucking social media are bullshit. We know the truth. So when you’re not showing us the journey, when you’re not showing us anything but the highlight reel, we don’t trust you. Right? Because we know it’s not that easy. Start to show the journey so that we can start to trust what’s actually going on in your business and who you say you are and what you say you do. And then number five, prioritize connection over conversion. Every single time. Visibility isn’t about going viral.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:58]:
You guys all know that I’m not on social media. I don’t try to go viral. I was never good at dancing reels, pointing and all that fuckery. Right? I was never good at that. And lucky for me, it’s not about going viral. It’s about being remembered. It’s about being known and it’s about being trusted. This is why I spend time in my DMs.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:14]:
I don’t show up on Instagram. I never post to my feed on Instagram, but I do show up in my DMs. Right? I’ll reply back with voice notes. I reply to emails. This is why I collaborate with humans I adore and I show up when my dream clients are already hanging out. This is why I create it inside the inbox. This is why I host private bundles. This is why I’m obsessed with aligned strategic collaborations, not just for growth, but for connection.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
It’s how I make friends as an adult, for goodness sake. So we need to remember: connection builds trust and trust builds conversions. Right? So the more connections you have And we’re going to come into this with the right intention. Right? We want to actually do it to build trust. We’re not doing it just to make the dollar, but it is a known fact that the more connections that we have, the more conversions we will see. So prioritise connections every single time. Deepen the relationships. Spend time with people.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
Make sure you are taking time to reply to any of the emails that land into your inbox, the DMs, the messages. You don’t need to be perfect, men. I’m a mom of two little boys and I definitely am a little delayed on the responding aspect of things, but still make it a priority to connect. Right? Let people in. Think of ways you can grow your business intentionally with connection. And here’s the beautiful part of all of this. When you lead with trust, right, the sales will come. Actually, they’ll come easier.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:35]:
Right? There’ll be more joy, more spaciousness, more alignment because you’re not convincing anymore. You’re simply inviting. You’re not forcing. You’re magnetising. If you’ve been feeling this shift lately, if your content’s not landing like it used to, if you’re questioning your strategy, it might not be your offer. It might not be the algorithm. It might be time to rebuild trust. Now, again, those five things you’re going to focus on, you’re going to show your face and use your voice, say the things that others won’t and have an opinion, share your point of view, deliver what you promise and then some, show the journey, not just the highlight reel in your content, and prioritize connection every single time.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:13]:
And finally, babe, you don’t have to do it alone. This is the exact work that I do with my clients inside the Email Growth Club and inside Headline and my Mastermind. We build trust, we grow audiences, and we create content that connects and converts without out the burnout or the bullshit. Right? So if you’re ready for that next level, for growth rooted in real connection, that’s going to build trust, come and find me. Let’s rebuild trust together. You’ve got this. Thank you again for being here. I hope you found this episode really helpful.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:43]:
All the links that you need are in the show notes and I will see you again next week. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of The Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 186

This is a little mini, voice-note-from-your-biz-bestie kind of episode.

And if you’ve been in my world for a while, this one might surprise you a little.

Because yes… I love email marketing.
Yes… I teach email marketing.
Yes… I will probably always talk about email marketing.

But here’s the truth I’ve been sitting with lately:

I’m not just in email marketing anymore.

And honestly? I haven’t been for a while.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. I hope you feel inspired to create your own start here email and ditch the welcome sequence if it is no longer serving you and your ideal clients. Reach out if you have any questions.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:19]:
I love you loads and I will talk to you really soon, like really soon. I’ve got some really good stuff coming your way and next week’s episode is our guest episode with an incredible, incredible PR expert. You’re going to want to tune in. All right, I will see you then. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:51]:
Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:55]:
Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The retreat moment that made me rethink how I describe my work
– Why email is just one part of the visibility puzzle
– A behind-the-scenes look at my RISE Framework™
– How I’m evolving (and how you might be too)

Need someone else to look over your business?

If you’re done playing small and ready to grow your visibility, influence, and audience in a way that actually converts – I’d love to support you inside the Business Breakthrough Audit.

This is where I personally review your visibility, offers, and email strategy and send you a private Loom with the three biggest shifts I’d make if I were you.

Clear.
Strategic.
No fluff.

👉 Book your Business Breakthrough Audit here: https://kyliekelly.com/breakthrough

Let’s make sure your positioning matches your expansion – because you’re not here to fit into a box.

You’re here to build an empire.

The identity shift I couldn’t ignore

At a recent business retreat, I kept introducing myself the same way:

“I’m an email marketing strategist.”

Over.
And over.
And over again.

And every time I said it, something felt… off.

Like I was shrinking myself to fit inside a box I’d already outgrown. It wasn’t wrong but it wasn’t fully true either – not anymore.

What I do now actually do goes so much deeper than email.

Email was never the whole story

Do I help women grow email lists that convert? Absolutely.

But the reason those lists convert isn’t just because we wrote better subject lines.

It’s because:

  • They built visibility in the right places
  • They attracted aligned people
  • They nurtured trust
  • They positioned themselves as leaders

Email is part of the ecosystem.
But it’s not the entire ecosystem.

I’m in the business of visibility.
Of audience growth.
Of helping female business owners be seen, heard, and trusted by the right people.

That’s the real work.

The framework that changed everything: R.I.S.E.

This clarity led me to fully own something I’d already been teaching behind the scenes.

My R.I.S.E. Framework.

Because when I zoomed out, I realized this is the full journey I walk my clients through:

R – Reach

Getting seen by the right people with strategic visibility.

Not shouting into the void.
Not dancing on TikTok if you hate TikTok.
Not chasing trends.

Strategic visibility.

I – Influence

Building trust and authority so your audience actually wants to hear from you.

Because visibility without trust?
Doesn’t convert.

S – Scale

Putting systems in place so your visibility becomes sustainable.

Email.
Automation.
Evergreen funnels.
Repurposing.

This is where momentum compounds.

E – Empower

Stepping into your CEO mindset so you stop hiding and start leading.

This is the part no one talks about enough.

The identity shift.
The confidence.
The expansion.

The moment you stop playing small.

The language finally feels right…

For years, I said: “I’m an email marketing strategist.”

Now?

I say: “I’m a visibility coach and audience growth expert.”

And let me tell you…

That language feels expansive.
It feels aligned.
It feels true in my gut.

It honours the depth of the work I do.

Helping women grow businesses that are:

  • Seen
  • Trusted
  • Profitable
  • Sustainable

Without burnout.
Without forcing themselves onto platforms that don’t align.
Without awkward dancing for the algorithm.

What this means for you

You’re going to see more conversations around:

  • Visibility strategy
  • Audience growth beyond just email
  • Sustainable 90-day planning
  • Thought leadership
  • Systems that support your expansion

Yes, email is still here. Always.
But we’re zooming out.

We’re talking about the full ecosystem that actually grows a business.

And we’re doing it in a way that feels aligned, strategic, and sustainable.

If you’re outgrowing your own box…

Maybe this episode isn’t just about me.
Maybe you’re feeling it too – that subtle tug that something doesn’t quite fit anymore.

Growth isn’t always clean.
Evolution isn’t always convenient.
But shrinking yourself to stay comfortable?

That’s the real risk.

If you’re stepping into something bigger this season – even if it feels wobbly – I’m right here beside you.

We’re allowed to evolve.
We’re allowed to expand.
We’re allowed to own the full scope of what we do.

This is bigger than email

If you can feel that you’ve outgrown your current strategy… your messaging… maybe even your niche – don’t ignore that.

Expansion requires recalibration.

Inside my Business Breakthrough Audit, I look at your visibility, your offers, and your email ecosystem as a whole – and show you exactly where you’re leaking momentum and where your biggest opportunity sits.

You’ll get a private Loom from me breaking down the three strategic shifts that would unlock your next level.

No generic advice.
No “post more” nonsense.
No overwhelm.

Just clarity you can act on immediately.

👉 Book your Business Breakthrough Audit here: https://kyliekelly.com/breakthrough

Because when your positioning evolves, your strategy has to evolve with it.
And you’re not here to stay comfortable.

You’re here to lead.

content:
Feat. Pinterest Strategist Heather Farris

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 183

Pinterest is back – but not in the way you think.

It’s not about trends or Reels or adding “pinning” to your already overflowing content calendar.

It’s about building long-term visibility that works in the background while you focus on building a business you love.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I chat with Pinterest strategist Heather Farris, who breaks down how to use Pinterest SEO to drive traffic to your offers, freebies, podcast, blog, and more – even if you haven’t touched your Pinterest account in years.

We’re talking sustainable growth without burnout – aka the kind of marketing I’m all about.

Want support building a visibility strategy that actually grows your list (without reels or paid ads)?
Join The Email Growth Club here.

Listen to this episode here:

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why Pinterest is not social media – and what that means for your strategy
– How Pinterest traffic works (with real client numbers)
– What to do if your account is a mess (it’s fixable!)
– Heather’s exact steps for building a Pinterest SEO plan
– How to save time with AI and batching tools like PinBot

The truth about Pinterest (& why it’s different from social media)

If the algorithm on Instagram is draining you (🙋‍♀️), you’re not alone.

Pinterest is different. It’s not social media – it’s a visual search engine. People go there with intention. They’re looking for solutions, ideas, and answers. That means they’re more likely to take action, click through, and join your list.

And the best part?

Unlike Instagram where your content disappears in 24 hours, a pin you post today could drive traffic for years.

How to get started with a Pinterest strategy…

One of my favourite parts of this episode is how Heather breaks everything down into simple, doable steps – even if you haven’t touched your Pinterest account in five years.

Here’s what she recommends:

  • Batch your content ahead of time. Heather recommends creating and scheduling pins monthly, which keeps everything running on autopilot.
  • Start with your evergreen content. Look at your top-performing blog posts, podcast episodes, lead magnets or offers – those are the pieces you want to prioritise.
  • Do keyword research on Pinterest. Use the search bar to find what your audience is actually searching for.
  • Create keyword-rich boards. Each of your content pillars can become its own board. This helps with visibility and organisation.
  • Design multiple pins per post. Pinterest wants fresh content. That doesn’t mean new blog posts – it just means new pins.

Let’s talk about traffic & results

I asked Heather what kind of traffic Pinterest is actually sending her – and her clients.

Here’s what she shared:

  • Her own account brought in 788 outbound clicks in 30 days (in a smaller niche like marketing)
