THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 180

Apple Mail just made a big move – and if you send emails, you need to know about it.

They’re rolling out AI-generated summaries that replace the preview text you thought you had control over. Which means… the inbox is changing. Again.

So what does that mean for your open rates? Your subject lines? Your content strategy?

In this solo episode, I’m breaking it all down in plain English – no panic required – and walking you through how to adapt right now so your emails still land, get opened, and convert.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– What Apple Mail’s AI summaries are (and who they impact)
– Why preview text might be dead 💀
– How to adapt your subject lines and intro copy
– Why your sender name and relationship with your list just became 10x more important
– 5 steps to make your emails stand out in the new inbox era

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Want help staying ahead of email marketing changes like this one?
Inside The Email Growth Club, I share real-time updates, templates, and coaching to help you grow a list that converts – no burnout, no guesswork.

Join The Email Growth Club now!

What are Apple Mail’s AI summaries?

First things first – what exactly is happening?

  • Apple Mail is introducing AI-generated summaries. Instead of showing the preview text that you carefully craft, Apple Mail will automatically generate a summary of your email.
  • Subject lines are still important. Your subject line will remain unchanged, meaning it’s still your #1 opportunity to grab attention.
  • The first lines of your email now matter more than ever. Since Apple Mail’s AI pulls from your actual content, the first few sentences of your email might influence what people see in the inbox.
  • You lose control over your preview text. If you’ve been optimising your preview text to boost open rates, that strategy may no longer work for Apple Mail users.

And let’s not forget – Apple Mail has a massive market share.

So even if this doesn’t impact Gmail or Outlook (yet), it’s still a huge deal for email marketers.

What this means for your email strategy?

So, what’s the impact? Will this destroy your open rates? Not necessarily.

Here’s what matters more than ever:

Your sender name is CRUCIAL.

Let’s be honest – your best subscribers aren’t just opening because of the preview text or even the subject line. They’re opening because they know, like, and trust YOU. If you’ve built a strong relationship with your list, people will actively look for your name in the inbox.

This is why engagement matters more than ever. Your goal isn’t just to get subscribers – it’s to build a community that wants to hear from you.

Subject lines still carry the weight. Since AI summaries are replacing preview text, your subject line is now the only element you fully control. You need to make it count!

Your first few sentences must be STRONG.

AI summaries might pull from the first few lines of your email – so instead of wasting space with fluff, get straight to the point. Use a hook, ask a question, or share a bold statement to capture attention fast. social.

Clear, engaging content matters more than clever tricks. If you’ve been relying on “preview text hacks” to increase opens, it’s time to shift focus to the overall quality of your emails.

A strong relationship with your list will outperform any algorithm or technological change.

5 things you can do to adapt right now!

1. Strengthen your sender name. If your subscribers trust you, they’ll open your emails no matter what Apple Mail does. Build that relationship.

2. Refocus on subject lines. Treat your subject line like a headline – it’s the first (and sometimes only) chance to capture attention.

3. Start your emails with impact. The first sentence needs to hook the reader – because Apple Mail might turn it into your preview text.

4. Keep an eye on your email analytics. Track open rates to see if Apple Mail users respond differently. Test different approaches and refine over time.

5. Engage your list regularly. Your subscribers should expect to hear from you – so email consistently, provide value, and make your audience WANT to open your emails.

Final Thoughts: Apple Mail’s AI Summaries aren’t bad.

Change happens all the time in digital marketing, and this is just another shift to navigate. If you’re building genuine relationships with your subscribers, you have nothing to worry about.

Yes, you’ll need to tweak your approach. Yes, you should test and optimise. But at the end of the day? The best email marketers will always win – because they focus on value, not hacks.

If you want to dive deeper into email marketing strategies, make sure you’re inside The Email Growth Club – where I share up to date insights, templates, and coaching to help you make email marketing work for YOU.

Feat. Evergreen Course Strategist Caitlin Bacher

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 178

Tired of launch burnout? You’re not alone – and there’s a better way.

If you’ve been stuck on the launch hamster wheel (plan, hype, launch, crash, repeat)… this episode is for you. I sat down with Caitlin Bacher, founder of Scale With Success, to chat about making consistent course sales without launching — and how she built a $1M+ business using evergreen funnels.

Whether you’re new to courses or totally over live launches, this convo is packed with real talk and actionable strategy.

Want help building visibility that fuels evergreen sales like Caitlin’s?
Join The Email Growth Club here and start growing your audience with aligned strategy.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The difference between live launching vs evergreen sales (and which is right for you)
– The most common mistake creators make when trying to “go evergreen”
– How Caitlin made $1M in 9 months without launching
– The key mindset + strategy shifts you need to sell courses consistently
– How to get started with evergreen — even if you’re just beginning

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Want to build an audience that’s ready to buy year-round – not just during launches?
Inside The Email Growth Club, you’ll learn how to grow your list, build real trust, and create a visibility strategy that supports consistent, scalable sales (just like Caitlin teaches!)

Click here to join us and start building your evergreen growth engine today..

What is an evergreen course funnel?

An evergreen funnel allows you to sell your course year-round, without needing to open and close your cart. Instead of forcing all your potential customers into a one-week launch window, an evergreen funnel lets them join when they’re actually ready to buy.

Caitlin shares how switching to evergreen completely changed her business, giving her consistent revenue and allowing her to scale without the high-stress spikes of live launches.

Why evergreen course sales work…

One of the biggest myths Caitlin debunks in this episode is that you need to have a successful launch before switching to evergreen.

False!

The truth is that evergreen selling is an entirely different strategy from launching – and you should learn to sell the way you actually want to sell. If your goal is to build a business that doesn’t rely on exhausting launch cycles, you need to master evergreen from the start.

She also shares the biggest mistakes course creators make when trying to go evergreen, including why repurposing a live webinar as an evergreen webinar almost never works (and what to do instead!).

Caitlin’s journey to a million-dollar evergreen course sales

Before Caitlin mastered evergreen selling, she was deep in the launch cycle. But everything changed when she met a course creator who was making hundreds of thousands of dollars per month – without launching at all.

After seeing the numbers, she knew there had to be another way, so she committed to figuring out how to sell consistently through evergreen funnels. Within nine months, her business hit its first $1 million in revenue!

And the best part? She did it without constantly being in launch mode.et goals and reflecting on the past year with compassion, can offer profound insights and relief.

The differences between launching & evergreen

Many course creators think that selling evergreen is as simple as repurposing a live webinar into an automated one – but Caitlin reveals why that approach fails almost every time.

  • Live launching: Creates urgency, but requires high energy and constant promotion.
  • Evergreen sales: Require a clear, automated system that converts visitors into buyers without you being involved.

The mistake most course creators make? Thinking their live launch strategy will work for evergreen sales. Evergreen funnels require clearer messaging, more refined positioning, and a different approach to objections since buyers can enter at any time.

How to start selling evergreen

If you’re thinking, Okay, this sounds amazing – but where do I even start?

Caitlin breaks it down in simple steps:

1. Pick ONE course to sell. Don’t try to create a whole suite of offers – focus on one course that solves a clear problem.
2. Set up an evergreen course sales funnel. Instead of a live launch, create an automated system that nurtures leads and converts them into buyers.
3. Test with organic traffic FIRST. Before running ads, make sure your funnel is working with warm traffic from your email list or collaborations.
4. Optimize based on real data. Instead of tweaking your offer based on a “flop” launch, gather real feedback and refine your messaging to make it stronger.

Kylie’s biggest takeaway?

If you’re tired of launch stress, want more consistent revenue, and crave a more scalable business model, then evergreen sales could be your answer.

As Caitlin shares, there’s no single “right” way to sell your course – but if you’re feeling burnt out by live launches, it might be time to explore a better way.

Caitlin is the founder of Scale With Success and an industry leader in evergreen course sales. She teaches course creators how to scale their income and impact without the pressure of launching.

excerpt: THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 177 Here’s the truth no one wants to say out loud: You’re not stuck because you’re lazy.You’re not stuck because you’re bad at business.You’re stuck because your visibility strategy is leaking energy. content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 177

Here’s the truth no one wants to say out loud:

You’re not stuck because you’re lazy.
You’re not stuck because you’re bad at business.
You’re stuck because your visibility strategy is leaking energy.

I see it every single week – brilliant, capable women showing up, posting, tweaking their bio, redesigning their Canva graphics… and still feeling invisible AF.

If you’re doing “all the things” and it still feels like you’re shouting into the void?

One [or more] of these visibility mistakes is likely at play.

Let’s fix it.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. I hope you feel inspired to create your own start here email and ditch the welcome sequence if it is no longer serving you and your ideal clients. Reach out if you have any questions.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:19]:
I love you loads and I will talk to you really soon, like really soon. I’ve got some really good stuff coming your way and next week’s episode is our guest episode with an incredible, incredible PR expert. You’re going to want to tune in. All right, I will see you then. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:51]:
Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:55]:
Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why relying too much on social media is keeping you stuck (and how to fix it)
– How collaborations, bundles, and summits help you tap into aligned audiences (without waiting for people to find you)
– How to normalize selling in your emails so it never feels pushy or awkward
– The real reason trying to do everything alone is slowing you down – and what to do instead

It’s Time to Own Your Visibility

You don’t need more posts.
You need better rooms. Better strategy. Better support.

That’s why I created Headliner – my 6-month mastermind for women ready to become the go-to name in their industry.

We focus on strategic visibility, collaborations, authority, and list growth that actually converts.

No hustle. No algorithm obsession. Just momentum.

If you’re done playing small, this is your move.

Apply for Headliner now.

P.S. The right room changes everything. This could be yours.

Mistake #1: Relying Too Much on Social Media

I’m just going to say it.

If Instagram is your entire visibility strategy… we have a problem.

Social media is rented land.
The algorithm is moody.
And organic reach? Let’s not even start.

If your growth depends on whether Mark Zuckerberg feels generous that day, your business will always feel unstable.

And the bigger issue? You’re competing with hundreds of posts a day. Even if someone sees you – will they remember you?

Probably not.

The Fix

Use social media as a traffic driver, not your whole damn marketing plan.

Your real focus should be:

  • Building your email list
  • Creating SEO-driven content
  • Leveraging collaborations
  • Owning your audience

Because when someone joins your email list?

You’re no longer fighting the algorithm.
You’re building a relationship.

And relationships convert.

Mistake #2: Avoiding Collaborations and PR Opportunities

This one drives me wild.

So many women tell me:
“I’ll pitch myself when I’m bigger.”
“I need more followers first.”
“I’m not ready yet.”

Nope. Hard no.

Collaborations are how you get bigger.

When you speak on a podcast, join a summit, participate in a bundle, or run a freebie swap — you’re stepping into a room where trust already exists.

That audience already trusts the host.
So when you’re introduced?

Instant credibility boost.

Over the past year alone, I’ve added thousands of aligned subscribers purely through collaborations.

Not viral reels.
Not dancing.
Not paid ads.

Strategic rooms.

The Fix

Start pitching. Start applying. Start reaching out.

Try:

  • Guesting on podcasts in your niche
  • Joining digital bundles or summits
  • Running freebie swaps with complementary biz besties

Stop waiting to be discovered.

Go where your dream clients already are.

Mistake #3: Not Leveraging Your Email List Properly

You’ve built a list… but you barely email it.

Or worse – you only show up when you’re launching.

And then you wonder why sales feel awkward.

Your email list is your most powerful asset.

But only if you actually use it.

Your subscribers signed up to hear from you. Not to sit in your Gmail graveyard while you overthink the “perfect” email.

The Fix

Start showing up consistently.

Tell stories.
Share lessons.
Be honest.
Be bold.
Be you.

The more your audience hears from you outside of launch week, the easier selling becomes.

Because trust is built in the in-between.

Mistake #4: Being Afraid to Sell

Let’s normalize something.

Selling is not gross.
Selling is service.

If you only talk about your offers when you’re desperate for cash, of course it’s going to feel icky.

You’ve attached pressure to it.

Instead – weave selling into your weekly rhythm.

Talk about:

  • Client wins
  • Behind-the-scenes insights
  • Why you created your offer
  • Who it’s perfect for

Selling shouldn’t feel like a sudden jump scare in your marketing.

It should feel like a natural invitation.

You’re not forcing anyone.
You’re offering transformation.

And your dream clients are literally waiting for that invitation.

Mistake #5: Trying to Do It All Alone

This is the big one.

If you’re white-knuckling your visibility strategy solo, you’re probably wasting time second-guessing yourself.

Business is easier in the right rooms.

When you’re surrounded by women playing at the level you want to reach, your standards rise. Your decisions sharpen. Your excuses shrink.

And let’s be honest – how many freebies are sitting in your inbox right now?

Bought with good intentions.
Never opened again.

Information isn’t the issue.

Implementation is.

And implementation thrives in accountability.

The Bigger Picture

Visibility isn’t about being louder.

It’s about being strategic.

It’s about:

  • Owning your audience
  • Building trust consistently
  • Getting into the right rooms
  • Selling with confidence
  • Having support behind you

If you’re nodding along thinking, “Yep… I’m doing at least two of these,” then good.

Awareness is the first shift.

The next one is action.

Ready to Fix Your Visibility Strategy?

If you’re done playing small and ready to become the go-to name in your industry, my Headliner Mastermind is open.

This is a 6-month mastermind for ambitious women who are ready to:

  • Get visible in the right rooms
  • Build authority strategically
  • Grow their email list sustainably
  • Stop relying on social media for every sale

We focus on strategic, sustainable visibility that actually moves the needle.

Not hustle.
Not burnout.
Not throwing spaghetti at Instagram.

If you want support, strategy, and the right room to step into your next level?

Apply for Headliner now.

And if you’re unsure whether it’s the right fit? Book a clarity call. I’ll tell you honestly.

No pressure. Just alignment.

Let’s stop waiting to be found.
Let’s start owning our visibility in 2025.

No secrets.

Just strategy.

– My exact list growth numbers and why her email engagement is higher than industry standard

First – Why I Don’t Use Social Media for List Growth

Yes, I have Instagram.

If Instagram disappeared tomorrow, I’d shrug and send an email.

Because I built my business on relationship-based marketing – not algorithm dependency.

As a former wedding photographer (hello perfectionism 🙃), I found the pressure to:

– Post daily
– Create aesthetic content
– Keep up with algorithm changes
– Perform constantly

Exhausting.

And I’m a mum of two little boys. Daily content wasn’t just draining – it was unrealistic.

So when I pivoted online, I doubled down on strategies that:

✔ Grow my email list
✔ Build real relationships
✔ Feel sustainable
✔ Actually convert

And that decision changed everything.

The V2 Visibility Framework That Fueled My Growth

Everything I’ve done sits inside my V2 Visibility Framework.

Imagine a capital “V.”

One side is Search & SEO:
– Pinterest
– YouTube
– Blogging
– PR
– Anything searchable

The other side is Collaborations & Relationships:
– Bundles
– Summits
– Podcast guesting
– Freebie swaps
– Email collaborations

– Networking

  • Bundles & summits
  • Podcast guesting
  • Freebie swaps & email collaborations

The Real Growth Drivers (With Numbers)

Let’s talk receipts.

🎉 Bundles & Summits

I participated in over 15 collaborations in 12 months.

The biggest growth came from the ones I hosted.

Birthday Bash Bundle
→ 2,700 subscribers joined
→ 1,300 remain (lesson: generic = leaky)

Ultimate Email Marketing Bundle
→ ~1,500 subscribers joined
→ Majority still engaged

The difference?

Specificity.

When your bundle directly solves your dream client’s problem, the retention is dramatically higher.

Alignment matters.

🎙 Podcast Guesting & Speaking

Smaller numbers.

Huge authority.

People listening while driving or folding laundry don’t always opt-in immediately – but credibility compounds.

And credibility sells.

🤝 Freebie Swaps & Email Collabs

Highly aligned audience swaps.

Example: collaborating with Alison Hardy.

Her audience = automation.
Mine = list growth.

Complementary, not competitive.

High-quality subscribers who were already primed.

That’s strategic visibility.

The Biggest Email Mistakes I See

1️⃣ Not Tracking What’s Working

If you don’t know what grew your list, how can you repeat it?

Track. Everything.

2️⃣ Only Focusing on Social

Likes don’t pay the bills.

Email does.

Build what you own.

3️⃣ Taking Email Too Seriously

Your inbox isn’t a corporate boardroom.

It’s a conversation.

Write like you talk.

Talk like you would over wine or coffee.

One of my favourite hacks?

Open a private Zoom room.
Hit record.
Talk it out.
Download the transcript.
Drop it into ChatGPT.
Turn it into an email.

Done.

Stop staring at a blinking cursor for 12 hours.

The Bigger Truth

Your audience might hang out on social.

But they buy in the inbox.

If Instagram disappears…

What if I told you that every single email you send could be working harder for you – quietly, consistently, and without you needing to create more content, post more on Instagram, or do another awkward Reel?

No dancing.

What the hell is a super signature?

A super signature is the section at the bottom of your emails.
Sometimes in the PS, sometimes as a footer – that gives your reader clear, low-pressure next steps.

Not a pushy sales pitch.
Not a “BUY NOW OR ELSE” moment.

Think of it like the end of a helpful conversation.

You’re saying:

“Hey, if you want more of this… here’s where to go next.”

That’s it.

And the magic?
It works whether you’re sending:

  • A weekly nurture email
  • A broadcast from your ESP
  • Or a casual one-to-one email from Gmail

Yep. Even your personal inbox can be doing some heavy lifting for your business.

Why this works [without being annoying AF]

Most people want to know how to work with you.

They just don’t want to be yelled at.

A super signature keeps your offers visible without hijacking the email itself. It meets your reader where they’re at – whether they’re ready to binge, buy, or just snoop around your world.

It’s subtle.
It’s strategic.
And it compounds over time.

I’ve had people join my email list, grab freebies, and even join my membership from emails that weren’t selling anything at all.

Just… replying to a message.
With a smart super signature in place.

What a super signature actually looks like

Here’s a real example of mine:

P.S. Whenever you’re ready, here are 3 ways I can help you grow your email list:

1️⃣ Grab my free guide: Your Next 1,000 Subscribers
2️⃣ Join my membership: The Email Growth Club
3️⃣ Listen to a related episode of The Email Growth Show

That’s it.

Four sentences.
Three links.
Clear paths forward.

I’m not forcing a decision – I’m opening doors.

Should you use this in every email?

Short answer: no.
Long answer: use it intentionally.

Use a super signature when:

  • You’re sending regular nurture emails
  • You’re replying to people in Gmail
  • You’re networking, collaborating, or following up
  • You want your offers visible without making the email “about” selling

Skip it when:

  • The email is transactional [receipts, confirmations, support replies]
  • The message is deeply personal
  • You’re in a heavy launch window and want one CTA front and centre

Clarity always wins.

The formula for a high-converting super signature

Steal this.

1. Start with a clear call to action

Something simple like:

  • “Whenever you’re ready, here’s how I can help…”
  • “Ready to take the next step? Start here…”

2. Link to your most strategic resources

This could be:

  • A free lead magnet
  • Your core paid offer or membership
  • High-value content [podcast, blog, YouTube]

3. Keep it tight

Two to three links max.

More options = more confusion.
And confusion kills clicks.

Don’t forget your Gmail [this is where most people drop the ball]

If you only take one thing from this post, let it be this:

Your personal inbox is prime real estate.

Every reply.
Every follow-up.
Every “great to meet you!” email.

Instead of signing off with just your name…

Imagine ending with:

P.S. I’d love to stay connected – here’s how:

→ Free email growth guide
→ Podcast for visibility tips
→ Membership for hands-on support

That one tweak has brought me so many new subscribers and clients – without trying to sell a damn thing.

Your action steps [do this today]

Don’t overthink it.

1️⃣ Add a simple super signature to your next email in your ESP
2️⃣ Update your Gmail signature with a subtle version
3️⃣ If you want inspo, email me at hello@kyliekelly.com and check out mine when I reply

That’s it.

No funnel rebuild.
No content calendar.
No algorithm stress.

Just smarter emails.

The bigger picture

A well-placed super signature is one of the most underrated email growth strategies out there.

It’s non-salesy.
It’s easy to implement.
And it works quietly in the background – every single day.

Your emails are already being opened.
You may as well let them do more for you.

Feat. PR Coach Gloria Chou

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 174

Think PR is only for celebrities and influencers? Think again.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I chat with PR coach Gloria Chou about how you can become your own publicist – without spending thousands on an agency or having a massive audience.

Gloria breaks down her signature CPR pitching method, explains how to find the right media contacts, and shows you how to pitch yourself in just 15 minutes a day – even if you’re brand new to PR.

Whether you’re looking for more credibility, better SEO, or just want to get your name into the right rooms – this episode is a must-listen.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– What PR actually is (and why it’s NOT just marketing)
– How to use Gloria’s CPR Pitch Method to land media coverage
– Tools + tactics to find the right journalists and opportunities
– Why having a small audience doesn’t hold you back from getting featured
– Real examples of successful PR pitches from business owners like you

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Want to land guest features, grow your audience, and build credibility like this?
Join The Email Growth Club – it’s where visibility strategies like these turn into growth that actually sticks.

What does PR do for your small online business?

Unlike social media, PR gives you long-term credibility and SEO benefits. As Gloria explains, marketing is you talking about yourself, but PR is your industry talking about you – and that third-party validation is priceless.

Getting featured in high-authority sites like Forbes, Business Insider, and top podcasts not only boosts your brand awareness but also gives you powerful backlinks that improve your website’s SEO, making it easier for ideal clients to find you.

And the best part? You don’t need a PR agency to do it!

How to start getting featured in the media

Gloria breaks down exactly how any business owner – even without experience – can start getting media coverage by following her simple PR system:

1. Find the right journalists to pitch to—using free tools like Google Alerts, HARO, LinkedIn, and Twitter hashtags like #journorequest.
2. Craft a compelling pitch using the CPR Method:

  • Credibility: Why are YOU the right person to speak on this topic?
  • Point of View: What makes your insight unique?
  • Relevance: Why is this timely and worth covering NOW?

3. Send your pitch with a strong subject line – it should read like a potential headline, not a generic introduction.

4. Follow up the right way – without being spammy (Gloria shares exactly how to do this inside the episode!)

How to pitch journalists the right way

If you’re wondering what to actually say in your pitch, Gloria provides a proven email template that follows her CPR framework:

Subject Line: 3 Surprising Productivity Hacks That Are Changing the Way Entrepreneurs Work

Email Body:

  • Relevance: “With more entrepreneurs struggling with burnout in 2025, productivity strategies are more important than ever.”
  • Point of View: “As a business coach, I’ve found that these 3 unconventional hacks have helped my clients get more done in less time…”
  • Credibility: “I’ve worked with over 500 entrepreneurs and have been featured in Forbes, Inc., and Fast Company.”
  • Call-to-Action: “I’d love to provide insights or a guest article. Let me know if this fits with your upcoming editorial calendar!”

Pro Tip: Journalists are BUSY. Keep your pitch short, relevant, and to the point.

The #1 PR myth: “you need a huge following”

One of the biggest misconceptions about PR? That you need a huge audience to get featured.

NOT TRUE!

Journalists aren’t looking for influencers – they’re looking for expert insights. If you have experience, a unique perspective, or data to share, you have everything you need to land PR opportunities. Gloria shares how business owners at all stages – even with small followings – have landed features in top-tier publications just by knowing how to craft a great pitch.

Kylie’s biggest takeaway?

If you’re tired of chasing social media algorithms and want to build long-term visibility and credibility, PR is one of the most effective and sustainable strategies you can invest in.

And the best part? You don’t need to spend hours every day doing it. Just 15 minutes a day – finding journalists, writing a pitch, or following up – can lead to incredible opportunities.

Guest Spotlight: Gloria Chou

Gloria is a small business PR coach and the creator of the CPR pitching method. She helps entrepreneurs get featured in top-tier media without needing expensive agencies or a huge following.

Writing sales emails can feel fucking awkward.

You sit there staring at a blank screen thinking:

– “What do I even say?”

And then you overthink it…
…and overthink it some more…
…and suddenly you’re three hours deep and still haven’t sent the damn email.

Here’s the good news:
You don’t need to reinvent the wheel every time you sell.

There are proven sales email formulas that work – not because they’re manipulative or hypey, but because they tap into how humans actually make decisions.

Today I’m breaking down five high-converting sales email formulas you can start using immediately – whether you’re launching, nurturing, or handling objections mid-sale.

No fluff.
No sleaze.
Just strategy.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:23]:

The call to action, of course, is to invite readers to achieve a similar result by taking action. So as an example, as I said, the subject line, how Sarah got 500 new subscribers in 30 days. TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– The Problem-Solution Formula and why it’s perfect for addressing your audience’s pain points
– How to use the Storytelling Formula to create emotional connections that inspire action
– The Objection-Handling Formula and how it helps you overcome buyer hesitation with confidence
– The Social Proof Formula to showcase results and build credibility
– The Scarcity/Urgency Formula and how to motivate your audience to act quickly

Ready to grow without social media?

Come join my free Skool community where I teach visibility and email growth strategies that don’t depend on social media.

We focus on:

  • Relationship-based growth
  • Search-based visibility
  • Email-first sales systems

No dancing.
No chasing trends.
No burnout.

Just steady, profitable growth.

Join here: https://www.skool.com/online-biz-growth/about

Formula #1: The Problem – Solution Formula

This one is a classic for a reason.

It works because it meets your reader exactly where they are.

You start with the problem they’re already thinking about – then position your offer as the solution.

How it works:
– Subject line calls out the problem
– Opening validates their experience
– Body introduces your solution
– CTA makes the next step obvious

Why it converts?
Because people feel seen.

When someone thinks, “Holy shit, she’s talking about me,” you’ve already won half the battle.

This formula is perfect for:
– Cold or lukewarm audiences
– Evergreen offers
– Straightforward solutions

Simple doesn’t mean ineffective.
It means clear.

Formula #2: The Storytelling Formula

Humans are wired for stories.

We tell them to our kids.
To our friends over wine.
To our coaches when we’re processing something messy.

Stories create emotional buy-in… and emotional buy-in leads to action.

Instead of leading with the offer, you lead with experience.

How it works:
– Subject line teases the story
– Opening shares a real challenge
– Body reveals the turning point
– CTA invites them into the same transformation

The key here?
Tell real stories. Not made-up internet bullshit.

Your audience doesn’t need perfection…
they need honesty.

This formula works incredibly well when:
– You’re selling something you’ve personally used
– You want to deepen trust
– You’re nurturing before a bigger sell

Stories stick.
And what sticks, sells.

Formula #3: The Objection – Handling Formula

If someone hasn’t bought yet, it’s rarely because they “don’t want it.”

It’s usually because something in their head sounds like:
– “I don’t have time.”
– “I’m not ready.”
– “What if this doesn’t work for me?”

This email meets those thoughts head-on.

How it works:
– Subject line speaks to hesitation
– Body names common objections
– You calmly address each one
– CTA reassures and invites action

This formula builds massive trust.

It shows your audience:
– You understand their concerns
– You’ve thought things through
– You’re not here to pressure them

And in an online space where people have been burnt before, that level of care matters.

Formula #4: The Social Proof Formula

People trust people.

Not sales pages.
Not claims.
Not vibes.

Results.

Social proof removes risk by showing what’s possible.

How it works:
– Subject line highlights a result
– Body shares a real client story
– You connect the dots to your offer
– CTA invites them to get similar results

If you don’t have testimonials yet… use your own experience.

Every offer starts somewhere.
Your results count too.

This formula works best when:
– You want to boost confidence
– You’re mid-launch
– You’re selling a proven offer

Evidence converts faster than explanation.

Formula #5: The Scarcity – Urgency Formula [Use Responsibly]

Scarcity works – when it’s real.

Not fake timers.
Not pretend deadlines.
Not “last chance” emails that magically reset every week.

Real urgency respects your audience.

How it works:
– Subject line signals limited availability
– Body explains why timing matters
– You highlight what they’ll miss
– CTA is clear and time-sensitive

Used with integrity, this formula helps people decide instead of procrastinate.

Used poorly, it destroys trust.

Choose wisely.

How to actually use these formulas

You don’t need to use all five at once.

Pick one formula.
Test it.
Refine it.
Repeat.

Sales emails aren’t about being clever – they’re about being clear.

And clarity builds confidence.
Confidence builds trust.
Trust builds sales.

And most people guard their inbox.

Think about it.
We’ve all signed up for a million things… then spent years unsubscribing from the chaos.

So when someone says, “Yep, I want you in my inbox,” that’s not casual.

That’s trust.

Compare that to social media:

No commitment.
No effort.
No loyalty.

Social media is rented land.

They were real conversations.

When you consistently show up in someone’s inbox – thoughtfully, intentionally, and as yourself = they stop seeing you as just another account.

– Following is effortless

It’s just you and your subscriber… one-on-one.

No shouting required.

Show up to help – not just pitch.

Speak to what people actually care about.

Consistency builds trust – and trust is everything.

Encourage replies.

That’s how relationships are built.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 171

Social media’s getting louder.

Algorithms are getting tougher.

But email? Email is your secret weapon.

In this solo episode of The Email Growth Show, I’m breaking down exactly why email marketing should be your #1 focus in 2025 – and how to make sure your strategy keeps up.

We’ll talk trends, predictions, and the one mistake I don’t want you making this year (hint: ignoring your list). Let’s make 2025 the year your inbox becomes your business’s most valuable asset.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why email marketing is still the smartest growth strategy in 2025
– What’s shifting in the online space – and how email keeps you grounded
– The biggest mistake business owners are making with their list right now
– Why relying on social media is riskier than ever
– What to focus on this year to grow, nurture, and monetise your audience sustainably

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Ready to build a list that converts in 2025?
Join The Email Growth Club – the membership where smart strategies meet sustainable growth. Click here to join today!

Why Email Marketing is the Queen of ROI

Let’s break it down: Why is email marketing so damn powerful?

First off, it gives you something social media can’t – direct access to your audience.
When you send an email, it lands right in someone’s inbox. No algorithms deciding if you’re “worthy” of visibility, no guesswork about whether your message gets seen.

Now, compare that to social media. Even your absolute best content? It might only reach a teeny-tiny percentage of your followers. The difference is staggering.

And then there’s the ROI – return on investment.
For every $1 spent on email marketing, you can expect to make an average of $36. Let’s just take a moment to let that sink in… $36 for every $1?! Now stack that against paid ads, which are becoming pricier and less effective by the minute. It’s clear why email marketing doesn’t just stand out – it completely steals the show.

But here’s the real mic drop moment: you OWN your email list.

You don’t own your social media followers. Platforms change. Algorithms shift. And yes, we’ve seen platforms straight-up disappear. Your email list? That’s an asset you control. It’s the foundation of a sustainable, reliable, and scalable business. No matter what trends come and go, your list is yours – and it’s priceless!

This is why email marketing isn’t just “a strategy.” It’s THE strategy for growth, connection, and long-term success. Let’s make it your priority in 2025.

Email Marketing vs. Social Media

First off, let me just say – I’m not here to talk shit about social media. When used intentionally, it’s an incredible tool. But if we’re comparing apples to apples, let’s talk about the key differences between email marketing and social media.

  • Visibility:
    The average open rate for emails? 20–30%. And for some of us, it’s even higher (my current 90-day average is sitting pretty at 50.35% 👀). Compare that to organic social media posts, where reach is often less than 5%.
  • Longevity:
    Emails live in someone’s inbox until they’re opened, read, or deleted. Social media posts? They’re here today, gone in hours – swallowed whole by the algorithm.
  • Trust:
    Email is personal. It’s like sitting down for a one-on-one conversation with your audience, creating connection and trust in a way that’s hard to replicate on social.

Here’s what I see coming in 2025 – more business owners will shift away from relying solely on social media and start focusing on sustainable platforms like email. Algorithms are exhausting you guys. If you want your content to convert into actual sales, email is where you need to plant your flag

BUT… inboxes are going to get noisier.

This means one big thing: you’ll need to email more often – and do it in a way that feels good for both you and your audience. Now’s the time to take a hard look at what your email marketing strategy looks like, find opportunities to dial it up, and build a plan that’s both impactful and sustainable.

Because in a world of fleeting posts and changing algorithms, email marketing isn’t just your safety net – it’s your secret weapon for growth in 2025.

The power of strategic messaging

Let’s talk about messaging, because if there’s one thing that can make or break your email strategy, it’s this: Personalization matters more than ever.

  • Segment your audience.
    Stop sending blanket emails to everyone and start creating targeted messages that speak directly to the person on the other end.
  • Get real.
    With AI tools like ChatGPT everywhere, people can sniff out a generic, one-size-fits-all script from a mile away. Your audience craves authenticity. They want to feel like your email was written just for them.

Here’s how to make your messaging magnetic:

→ Speak to their pain points. Show them you get it – and then show them how you can solve it.
→ Be YOU. Write how you speak. Bring your personality into every word.
→ Stay clear and strategic. Don’t overcomplicate. Make it easy for them to say, “Yes, this is exactly what I need.”

Data is your secret weapon

One of the best things about email marketing? The data doesn’t lie.

You can’t hide from:
Your open rates, your click rates or which topics and CTAs are resonating with your audience!

This data? It’s pure gold. It tells you what’s working, what’s not, and where you need to tweak and pivot.

Pro tip: Different audiences perform differently, so knowing your numbers is essential. Use that insight to fine-tune your strategy and give your audience exactly what they need.

Prediction for 2025: Make It Personal or Miss Out

Here’s the truth: audiences are getting more discerning. Generic emails just won’t cut it anymore, and you might see conversion rates start to drop if you’re not connecting on a personal level. But don’t let that scare you. Let it motivate you to step up…

  • Focus on emails that feel personal, real, and human.
  • Lean on your data to guide your strategy.
  • Build deeper connections.

In 2025, data will continue to be the driving force behind what works and what doesn’t. The brands that pay attention – and use it to create connection-driven content – are the ones that will win.

Speaking to different types of buyers

Here’s the tea: your audience isn’t one-size-fits-all. You’ve got buyers in all different stages of their journey – some are ready to hit “buy now,” others need a little more nurturing, and some? They’re just browsing the shelves, curious about what you offer.

Your job? Craft emails that speak to ALL of them.

When you tailor your messaging to meet buyers where they are, you’re showing them something powerful:
You see them.
You hear them.
You understand what they need.

And guess what? When people feel like you’re talking directly to them, they’re way more likely to take action.

Prediction for 2025: Personalisation is the new standard

This year, personalized, audience-specific messaging is going to be everything.

Gone are the days of tossing all your subscribers into the same sales sequence or funnel and hoping for the best. That approach doesn’t feel good now – and it’s going to feel even worse as buyer expectations evolve.

Here’s where the magic happens: Start thinking about the customer journey. Your subscribers don’t all need the same thing, so stop treating them like they do.

Instead:
Segment your audience into groups based on their stage in the journey.
Craft emails that resonate with each type of buyer—whether they’re ready to buy now, need nurturing, or just want to learn more.
Focus on connection. Make every email feel personal, intentional, and aligned with their needs.

The goal? To make your subscribers feel seen, heard, and loved every step of the way. When you do that, the conversions will follow.

This year is all about stepping up your email game, thinking deeper about your customer journey, and showing up in a way that makes your audience excited to hear from you.

So, how do you make email marketing your top priority in 2025? Here are three simple steps to get started:

  1. Create a lead magnet that speaks directly to your ideal audience and start growing your list.
  2. Map out a simple welcome sequence to make a strong first impression with new subscribers.
  3. Commit to sending one valuable email each week to nurture your audience and build trust.

Email marketing is your ticket to stability, scalability, and deeper connections with your audience. It’s not just another strategy – it’s THE foundation of a sustainable business.

Ready to make 2025 your email year?

Check out The Email Growth Club – the ultimate toolkit to help you grow your list, nurture your audience, and make email marketing work for you.

Here’s to making 2025 your most impactful year yet.

So that is the prediction for 2025, the big shift. We know that email gives us more visibility. It’s seen by more people, lives longer in the inbox, and builds more trust. It’s kind of a no brainer to make sure that we’re growing and email full of our ideal clients whether we’re on social or not. Now, let’s talk about messaging.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:48]:
Because if there’s one thing that can make or break your email strategy it’s this, personalization matters more than ever. So because people will be sending more emails, we wanna make sure that we’re sending the right emails to the right people. Right? We’re looking after and respecting our subscribers. How do we do that? We segment our audience. Stop sending blanket emails to everyone and start creating targeted messages that speak directly to the person on the other end. And we also need to get real. Of course, I love productivity tools like Chativity. Saves me so much time every week as a solo business owner.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:24]:
But with the prevalence of AI tools, people can sniff out generic one size fits all scripts from a mile away. Your audience craves you, craves authenticity. They want to feel like your email was written just for them. So, this is how we make our messaging magnetic. We speak to their pain points. We show them that we fucking get it. And then we show them how we can solve it. We be ourselves.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:47]:
We write how we speak. And we bring our personality into every word. I’m going to link a past episode with Marisa Corcoran in the show notes below. She talked a lot about our accessories closet and the words that we use and how we can actually bring our personality out in really easy ways. I think it’s going to be worth listening to if this is something that you want to focus on in 2025. And then lastly, we need to stay clear and strategic to make sure our messaging is magnetic. Don’t over complicate it. Make it really easy for your subscribers to say, yes, this is exactly what I need.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:23]:
Now, one of the best things about email marketing is that the data doesn’t lie. Right? We can’t hide from our open rates, our click rates, and which topics and calls to actions are resonating with our email list. This data is pure gold. It tells you what’s working, what’s not, and where you need to tweak and pivot. So a little pro tip, different audiences perform differently. So knowing your numbers is essential. Use that insight to fine tune your strategy and give your audience exactly what they need. So my prediction for 2025 when it comes to data and messaging is that you need to make it personal or you’re going to miss out.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:56]:
Because here’s the truth, audiences are getting more discerning. They’re smart. Right? Generic emails won’t cut it anymore, and you might see conversion rates start to drop if you’re not connecting on a personal level. Level. But don’t let it scare you. Let it motivate you to step up and focus on emails that feel personal, real and human. Lean on your data to guide your strategy and build deeper connections. In 2025, this year, data will continue to be the driving force behind what works and what doesn’t.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:23]:
The brands that pay attention and use it to create connection driven content are the ones that are going to win out. The next thing I want to talk about was speaking to different types of buyers. So here’s the tip, your audience isn’t a one size fits all. You’ve heard me talk about that already multiple times. You’ve got buyers in all different stages of their journey. Some are ready right now to hit buy. Others need a little more nurturing. And some of them, they’re just browsing the fucking shelves, curious about what you offer.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:50]:
That’s okay. It’s our job to craft emails that speak to every single kind of buyer, to speak to all of them. When you can tailor your messaging to meet buyers where they are, you’re showing them something powerful. You see them, you hear them, and you understand what they need. And guess what? When people feel like you’re talking directly to them, they’re way more likely to take action. So my prediction for this year is personalization is going to become the new standard. This year audience specific messaging is going to be everything. Gone are the days of tossing all your subscribers into the same sales sequence or funnel and hoping for the best.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:26]:
That approach, it actually doesn’t feel good now as a subscriber on the other end. And it’s going to feel even worse as the buyer expectations evolve. So here’s where the magic happens. Start thinking about the customer journey right now. Your subscribers don’t need all the same thing. So stop treating them like they do. Instead, I want you to segment your audience into groups based on the stage in their journey. How do you do that? Ask them some questions, poll your audience, get them to vote, tag and segment them based on what they click on, on what they vote on.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:58]:
Start to do that now even in smaller sections so that going into this year you’re going to be able to really craft emails that resonate with each type of buyer. Whether they’re ready to buy now, whether they need nurturing, or whether they just want to learn more. And then I also want you to focus on connection. Make every email feel personal, intentional, and aligned with their needs. Yes. You can still use email templates. That’s okay. They still have a place here.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:23]:
But I want you to make sure that you’re doing everything that you can to personalize that template so that it feels you’ve written it just for that person that’s reading it. So that they feel connected. So that they feel seen. So that they feel heard. So that they feel that you know exactly what they need. The goal here is to make your subscribers feel seen, heard, and loved every step of the fucking way. And when you can do that, then the conversions will follow. This year is all about stepping up your email game, thinking deeper about your customer journey, and showing up in a way that makes your audience really excited to hear from you.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:58]:
So I know that was a lot. How do you make email marketing your top priority in 2025? Here are 3 simple steps to get started. Number 1, I want you to create a lead magnet, a free resource that speaks directly to your ideal audience and starts growing your list. If you haven’t started growing your list or you have a small list and you need more eyes, more people, more ideal clients on there, please don’t sleep on this. Let’s get that thing rocking and rolling. And if you need support the email growth club is where you need to be. I’ll put the link in the show notes. Come and join the membership and let me help you grow your email list full of the right people.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:38]:
Then secondly, if you have an email list that is humming, that is doing really well, I want you to make sure that you’ve mapped out a simple welcome sequence to make a strong first impression with new subscribers. I want you to make sure in that first email, that delivery email where they’re signing up and they’re hearing from you, that very first email that they get, I want you to ask them a question and get them to click on a anchor link or vote on a poll so that you can start to segment them from that very first interaction that you have. Data is power. Information is power. The more we can have when it comes to who’s on our list and what kind of buyer they are, the better content you’re going to be able to send them. So map out that simple welcome sequence. Or if you already have one, go to that first delivery email and make sure that you are asking them a question or getting them to click on a link or vote in a poll and tagging and segmenting them and getting that data about where they are in their customer journey. And then lastly, I want you to commit to sending at least one valuable email each week to nurture your audience and build trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:13:41]:
Like I said, this year there’s going to be more people sending emails than ever. So yes, ideally I want you to be sending more than 1 email a week. However, if you were not doing that now. If you are not comfortable doing that now, if you are feeling afraid to send more than 1 email a week, if you’re not consistent, get consistent first. Email marketing, my loves, is your ticket to stability, scalability, and deeper connections with your audience. Hence why I’m so fucking passionate about it. It’s not just another strategy. It’s the foundation of a sustainable business.

Kylie Kelly [00:14:12]:
I hope that you found this episode helpful. I know that there was a lot in it. If you need to listen to it again and take notes, please do. And if you’re ready to make 2025 your email year, please check out the Email Growth Club. It’s the ultimate membership to help you grow your list, nurture your audience, and then make email marketing work for you. The link is in the show notes, as I mentioned. And don’t forget, please hit reply on any of my emails. Here’s to making 2025 your most impactful year yet.

Kylie Kelly [00:14:39]:
Thank you again for tuning in to The Email Growth Show. I have so much love for all of you. I’m cheering you on, and let’s make this year one to remember. Alright, my loves. I will see you next week. Thank you so much for tuning into this episode of The Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoy this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others.

Kylie Kelly [00:15:08]:
Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you, who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 170

Can you believe it? We are already diving headfirst into 2025. I’ve got my coffee steaming beside me, a notepad filled with dreams, and a heart that’s ready for all the possibilities this new year holds.

Today, I want to share something deeply personal yet incredibly powerful with you – my journey of choosing a ‘Word of the Year’.

This simple practice has been a game-changer for me, guiding my life and business in the most profound ways.

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why Kylie chose “Bold” as her word of the year for 2025
– A look back at the words that shaped her past 5 years
– How your word can become an anchor for decision-making
– Tips for choosing your own word of the year
– Why this simple practice can change the way you lead

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

If bold is part of your 2025 vision too – whether that’s launching your first bundle, building your list from scratch, or finally owning your voice online – I’d love to support you inside The Headliner Mastermind or The Email Growth Club.

Let’s make this the year you stop playing small.

The Power Of Choosing One Word

Since 2020, I’ve embraced the practice of choosing a single word to serve as my guiding light throughout the year. This word becomes more than just a theme; it functions as a touchstone for decisions, a filter for my mindset, and an anchor amidst the chaos. It’s not about finding the perfect word, but rather discovering one that resonates deeply within you – a word that lights you up and keeps you focused.

As we look forward, it’s crucial to reflect on the past and recognize how previous words have shaped our journey.

In 2020, amidst the upheaval and uncertainty of a global pandemic, my word was “BREATHE“. It reminded me to slow down, stay grounded, and take life one day at a time.

Moving into 2021, my word “ADAPT” encouraged flexibility and growth as I faced new beginnings and challenges.

2022 brought about “PLAY“, a permission slip to experiment and embrace the fun of life and business, leading to the creation of my membership.

In 2023, the word “BUILD” focused on laying solid foundations for my dreams. It was a year of quietly strengthening my business and confidence without the immediate demand for results.

Then, 2024’s word “BALANCE” shifted my attention to creating harmony between my roles as a mother, wife, and business owner.

Each word acted as a guide, allowing me to prioritise what truly matters and adjust as needed.

Bold: My Word Of The Year for 2025

And now, standing on the threshold of 2025, my word of the year is “BOLD“. This isn’t just about taking risks; it’s about stepping into my fullest self with courage and intention. Boldness for me means making decisions and taking actions that resonate with authenticity and purpose. It’s about not holding back, even when it feels uncomfortable or uncertain.

Being bold involves launching new offers and stepping outside my comfort zone.

For example, in February I’ll be opening the doors to my Headliner Mastermind, a six-month program designed to elevate women to household names, amplifying their impact, influence, and income. Hosting such a space has been a dream, and now, with boldness by my side, I’m ready to bring it to life.

This year, I’m not just inviting boldness into my business moves but also into my daily interactions. It means speaking my truth clearly and unapologetically, whether on this podcast, in emails, or during any interaction. Over time, I’ve learned that playing small benefits no one, and this year is about showing up with big energy, vision, and action.

I’ve also prioritised having support to navigate this bold journey. Joining a mastermind with my coach Angela Henderson has equipped me with the support needed to keep my nervous system steady as I tackle new challenges and expansions.

Choosing Your Word Of The Year

If you’ve never chosen a word of the year before, let me assure you that it’s a transformative practice. Whether it’s “Focus”, “Freedom”, “Growth”, or another word that speaks to you, this word will become the guiding star for your decisions and actions over the next year.

Write it down, place it somewhere visible, and let it lead you towards the life and business you envision.

As we sail into 2025, I invite you to embrace the bold with me – make this the year of big moves and growth. Whether you join the Headliner Mastermind, the Email Growth Club, or work with me one-on-one, let’s embark on this incredible journey together.

Email Growth Club: Click here for more info!
Headliner Mastermind: Join the waitlist here
Interested in 1:1? Send me an email for a chat.

Here’s to a year of being bold!

content:
Feat. EFT Practitioner Jacqui Acree

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 169

Feeling stuck, burnt out, or like you’re falling short of your goals? Let’s tap through that.

In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I sat down with one of my closest biz besties and brilliant EFT practitioner Jacqui Acree to talk about the power of Emotional Freedom Techniques (aka tapping) – and how it can support entrepreneurs who are juggling big dreams, self-doubt, and the pressure to “keep it together.”

From unmet goals to self-sabotage, we cover it all – and how tapping can help you feel more calm, clear, and grounded as you grow your business (and your self-trust).

TL:DR:

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– What EFT tapping is – and how it works on your nervous system
– How tapping helps entrepreneurs reframe unmet goals and emotional pressure
– Why your “self-sabotage” is actually a form of protection
– How to use tapping to rebuild self-trust and emotional regulation
– Why emotional safety is the foundation for sustainable business growth

Listen to this episode here:

Your next step:

Want to keep growing with more connection, calm, and community?
That’s exactly what we focus on inside The Email Growth Club.
Let’s grow sustainably and strategically together. Click here to join today!

Why EFT tapping is a great tool for business owners

Sometimes affirmation – or white knuckling it – don’t always work. It’s all too common for affirmations to feel awkward when there’s a disconnect between our logical mind and what we truly feel. Jacqui shared her initial struggle with affirmations, realising they failed to resonate due to the misalignment between her internal emotions and external proclamations. Through EFT tapping for entrepreneurs, she discovered a method that doesn’t just superficially plaster over doubts but welcomes them, allowing emotions to be truly addressed rather than resisted.

How Jacqui discovered eft tapping

It was fascinating to hear Jacqui’s tale of encountering tapping for the first time – in a public bathroom stall, no less. Imagine walking in filled with anger and emerging with clarity after just a few moments of tapping! While Jacqui admits such rapid transformation isn’t typical, it was nonetheless compelling. It serves as a reminder of how accessible and immediate the effects of tapping can be, making us curious about its potential in our own lives. Jacqui and I touched on a critical issue: the fast pace of life that often leaves us out of touch with our own thoughts and feelings.

In our businesses and day-to-day activities, we are prone to looking externally for validation or guidance. Society conditions us to doubt our instincts, often from a young age, reinforcing the belief that others know better. EFT tapping for entrepreneurs is a gentle yet profound way, to encourage us to pause and listen to ourselves, fostering self-trust that is crucial in the ever-evolving landscape of our businesses.

Embracing change through personalised tapping

Change can threaten our sense of safety, pushing us to feel stuck or inadequate. Jacqui discussed these feelings candidly, emphasizing the importance of self-trust to navigate transitions.

Whether it’s a shift in our business strategy or an unexpected personal challenge, tapping reminds us that we have the wisdom within to find solutions. It’s about being flexible and resilient, adjusting our sails when the winds change direction.

Throughout our conversation, Jacqui highlighted the nuances of personalised EFT tapping sessions.
