content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 158

Today we’re diving into something I feel extremely passionate about: why social media is not the only way to grow your business. I know that might come as a surprise, especially since we’re constantly bombarded with messages telling us that platforms like Instagram, TikTok & Facebook are essential.

But the reality is, social media is 100% optional.

Now, I want to start with a quick story. Yesterday I attended a business conference virtually where the questions from attendees seemed to revolve entirely around social media.

People were asking things like:
– ‘What am I doing wrong on social?’
– ‘How can I make time in my already busy day to make Instagram reels without burning out?’

And the advice they were getting was good, but there was something important missing from the conversation: You don’t need it. You DO NOT have to rely on social media to build a successful business. In fact, there are other ways that might feel more aligned with your values and your goals.

I was literally yelling at my zoom screen in frustration as these 7 figure business owners that were answering their questions, hoping someone could hear me. They couldn’t. So the conversation didn’t change.

So… today I want to unpack this together. I’ll share with you why social media isn’t the only path to business growth and show you alternative strategies that can help you grow your business -without spending all day glued to your phone. If that sounds like a relief, then stick with me because we’re about to break down why social media is optional and how you can build a thriving business without it.

Click play to listen to the episode in full below:

Why Social Media Isn’t the Only Answer

Ok, let’s start by diving into why social media isn’t the secret or the only answer for growing your business. Now, don’t get me wrong – social media can definitely work. There are countless success stories of people who’ve built thriving businesses using Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and other platforms.

But here’s the thing: just because it works for some doesn’t mean it’s the only way to build a business.

The problem is that social media is exhausting for a lot of us. You’re constantly trying to stay relevant, figure out the algorithms, and come up with new content ideas. It feels like this never-ending cycle, and if you’re not seeing immediate results, it can be incredibly discouraging. I’ve been there myself, and I know the frustration of putting in all that effort and still feeling like you’re not gaining any traction.

But here’s the truth: You don’t need to rely on social media to grow your business. Think about it – social media is just one tool in your toolbox, but it’s not the only tool. In fact, there are other strategies that can be just as, if not more, effective in helping you build your audience, grow your email list, and increase your revenue.

So as we dive into this conversation, I want you to take a moment to reflect on your own relationship with social media. Are you using it because you genuinely enjoy it and it aligns with your business goals, or are you using it because you feel like you have to? This coming week, I challenge you to step back and evaluate whether social media is really serving you OR are you just going through the motions because you feel like you have to and it’s draining you of all your fucking energy – like it use to me.

What’s the Alternative? How You Can Grow Your Business Without Social Media?

So, if social media isn’t required, how do you actually grow your business without it?

The good news is, there are multiple alternative strategies that don’t involve algorithms or the constant pressure to post. These are the methods I’ve used to grow my email list from zero to nearly 10,000 subscribers, and I can’t wait to share them with you!

1. Email Marketing

Let’s start with my favourite – email marketing. Your email list is your most valuable business asset. It’s a direct line to your audience, and unlike social media, you fucking own it. There’s no algorithm to fight against, and when you send an email, it goes straight to your subscriber’s inbox. The best part? Your subscribers are already warm leads because they’ve chosen to hear from you. It’s consent based marketing – they’ve put their hand up and said – YES. PLEASE email me. I want to hear from you. This makes email marketing one of the most powerful tools for building trust, delivering value, and making sales

If you’ve been focusing all your efforts on social, it’s time to shift some of that energy toward growing your email list. Start by creating a free resource – something that your ideal clients would find valuable – and use it as a lead magnet to attract subscribers. Once they’re on your list, you can nurture that relationship over time and, eventually, sell to them directly through email. If you are in my membership, The Email Growth Club, I have a training all about how to level up your lead magnet and actually create a resource that brings LEADS into your business. If you’re not in the membership, what are you waiting for? Click here to join today: The Email Growth Club.

2. Collaborations

Next, let’s talk about collaborations. This is another method I’ve used extensively to grow my email list. Collaborations could look like participating in summits, joining digital bundles, doing freebie swaps with other aligned business owners, or podcast guesting. The key is to find partners that serve the same ideal clients in a complimentary way. You’re essentially borrowing their audience and introducing yourself in a way that feels authentic and mutually beneficial.

With collaborations, you’re not depending on a social media algorithm to be seen. Instead, you’re partnering with other business owners who have already earned the trust of their audience, and they’re essentially endorsing you in the process. Plus, as an adult with an online business, this is how I make most of my friends these days. Total perk.

3. SEO & Evergreen Content

Let’s not forget about search engine optimisation (SEO). SEO might not be the sexiest strategy, but it’s powerful, and it still works. Whether it’s blogging, YouTube, or even podcasting – creating content that’s optimised for search engines means you’ll attract people who are already looking for what you offer. Once you’ve created that content, it works for you long after it’s been published.

Again, unlike social media, where your post disappears within hours, if it gets seen at all – discoverable content optimised for SEO can bring you traffic for months, even years, down the line.

If you want to listen to more detail about How You Can Grow Your Email List with Collaborations & SEO specifically, tune into episode 149 of my podcast The Email Growth Show, where I dived into exactly that. I shared my simple V2 Visibility Framework that outlines the options you can choose from when you’re thinking of what you want to try when it comes to collaborations or search & SEO based list growth strategies. Here’s the link: My V2 Visibility Framework: How You Can Grow Your Email List with Collaborations & SEO

Now in case you’re thinking – that’s great for you Kylie but maybe you’re the exception and not the rule. Let me tell you about a few of my members, now friends, that have seen this work for them too.

  • Amy went from 45 email subscribers to just under 800 in one month using aligned collaborations. She shared a screenshot in the email growth club because she couldn’t quite believe that it was real.
  • Andria that added 300 subscribers to her list with one bundle and also sold some of her tripwire offers as well – that had never happened to her before.
  • Destiny just shared last week that she’s grown her email list from 200 to just shy of 1800 with the things I’m talking in this episode.

All of this happened WITHOUT fucking social media.

Why Social Media Can Feel Like a Trap (And How to Escape It)

It’s not hard to understand why so many business owners feel stuck in the social media hamster wheel. We’re told over and over again that social media is essential for growth. It’s marketed as this must-have tool, and seeing others seemingly thriving on Instagram or TikTok can create a lot of pressure to stay active.

But the truth is, social media can also create a lot of stress. You feel like you constantly have to keep up with posting schedules, engaging with comments, and figuring out the ever-changing algorithms. And what happens when you don’t see results? You start to wonder, ‘What am I doing wrong?’ You compare yourself to others and feel like you’re behind.

Here’s what I want you to take away:

Social media is a tool, not a strategy. And it’s definitely not the only way to grow your business. If social media isn’t working for you, it’s okay to step back and look for other, more sustainable methods.

Personally, I’m hardly ever on social. I have a 9 grid that is permanently posted on my Instagram profile – think of it like a shopfront – so if anyone comes across my profile or searches me out to see if I’m legit – I can’t be the only one that does that – it’s there. I show up on stories when I want to. I’m in a couple Facebook groups that I like engaging in. That’s it. It’s what feels good for me – and it’s all completely 100% fucking optional.

So… if social media is causing you stress – but you’re not ready to leave or it feels scary to really pull back – I’d encourage you to take a social media break for a few days or a week. During that time, focus on another strategy – like email or collaborations – and see how it feels to pour your energy into something different. It might surprise you!

Building Your Business in a Way That Feels Good

One of the best things about running your own business is that you get to choose how to build it. You get to decide what feels good, what aligns with your values, and what brings you joy. If social media doesn’t fit into that vision for you, then guess what? You don’t have to use it.

I know many business owners who have stepped away from social media entirely, and they’re thriving. They’ve built businesses through email marketing, SEO, collaborations, and word-of-mouth referrals – and they’re happier for it.

The beauty of this approach is that it gives you more control. You’re no longer at the mercy of algorithms or the pressure to create viral content. Instead, you’re building a business that feels sustainable, intentional, and aligned with your goals. Take a moment today to think about what your dream business looks like. Your dream life as a CEO. Does it include social media? If not, what are the strategies you want to focus on instead? Write them down and start planning how you’ll implement them in your business.

So, to wrap this up: social media is optional.

You don’t need it to grow your business.

There are countless other ways to connect with your audience, grow your email list, and make sales – all without the algorithm dictating your every move or the pressure to see that social media following number increase.

Here’s my challenge for you: if you’ve been relying on social media and feeling stuck, try stepping back for a bit. Experiment with one of the alternative strategies I’ve mentioned today – whether that’s email, collaborations, or SEO.

See how it feels. See what results you get.

And if you’re ready to really dive into these strategies and grow your email list faster, grab my free Your Next 1000 Subscribers – Ultimate Collaborations Guide. It’s packed with actionable steps to get started with collaborations right away – click here to grab it today!

I can’t wait to hear about your progress and the steps you’re taking to build your business without relying on social media. Remember, you’re in control of how you want to run your business, and it can be in total alignment with your values. Until next time, keep growing, keep connecting, and keep doing business your way!

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 157

Today, we’re diving into something that can seriously move the needle for your email list growth: collaborations! Specifically, we’re talking about how to find aligned partners to collaborate with – AND – what mistakes to avoid when using collaborations to grow your email list!

Now, collaborations are one of the most powerful list building strategies but here’s the thing – it’s not about sitting back and waiting for the perfect person to come to you. Spoiler alert: that’s not going to happen!

In this post, I’ll walk you through a proactive approach to finding the right partners – people who align with your values, goals, and audience. I’ll share how you can build genuine relationships that lead to incredible collaborations that will help grow your email list fast. So, grab your pen and paper, because you’ll want to take notes on this one!

Click play to listen to the episode in full below:

Why Collaborations Can Grow Your Email List Fast

Let’s kick things off by talking about why collaborations are such a game-changer for growing your email list.

I often say that collaborations are the shortcut to building your email list quickly, and here’s why.

When you collaborate with someone who already has an engaged audience that aligns with yours, you’re essentially getting access to a group of warm leads. These people already trust the person you’re collaborating with, and when that person recommends you, that trust transfers to you.

Think of it this way: You’ve probably tried social media and maybe even paid ads to grow your list. But here’s the truth: social media can be inconsistent, and ads can be expensive – especially if you’re not getting the results you want.

Collaborations, on the other hand, are based on relationships, which means they have the potential to build trust faster and provide higher engagement.

The magic happens when you find a partner whose audience has the same pain points, struggles, and desires as yours. This is what makes the partnership aligned. You’re not just reaching random people—you’re getting in front of an audience that’s ready to hear from you.

Mistakes To Avoid When Using Collaborations To Grow Your Email List

Before we dive into how to find aligned partners, let’s talk about what NOT to do when you’re looking for collaborators. This is important because I’ve made these mistakes before, and I don’t want you to waste time like I did!

Here are the mistakes to avoid when using collaborations to grow your email list:

The first thing to avoid is being passive.

You can’t just drop a post in a Facebook group saying, ‘I’m looking for collaboration partners,’ and expect people to come running to you. This approach is too broad, too vague, and it usually attracts people who aren’t the right fit.

Secondly, you don’t want to skip the relationship-building process.

One of the biggest mistakes people make is reaching out to someone cold with an immediate pitch for collaboration. Imagine if you received a message from someone you’ve never heard of, asking for something – how would that feel? It’s likely you’d be put off, and that’s exactly how others feel when you do the same.

Building a relationship should come first. Follow their work, support them, engage with their content, and let them know you care about what they’re doing. Only after you’ve built that connection should you approach them about collaborating.

Finally, don’t make the collaboration feel one-sided.

You need to ensure that both parties benefit from the partnership. When pitching a collaboration, be clear about how you can help them just as much as they can help you.

Now, Let’s Dive Into How To Actually Find Aligned Collab Partners

This isn’t about sitting back and waiting for someone to come to you – it’s about going out and making those connections.

1. Start with RESEARCH

You want to find people who share similar audiences or values. Start by following podcasts or blogs in your niche. Listen to their content and see if they’re speaking to the same challenges and goals that you are. Look at summits or bundles that people in your industry have participated in – these are often great places to find potential partners. Don’t limit yourself to social media – check newsletters, LinkedIn, podcasts and guest blog posts.

2. Leverage your network:

One of the best ways to find great collaboration partners is through your existing network. Reach out to people you’ve already worked with, or people you know in your industry, and ask if they know anyone who might be a good fit. Word-of-mouth recommendations are incredibly powerful, and it’s much easier to approach someone when you have a mutual connection.

3. Engage before you pitch:

This is key: engage with potential partners before making an ask. Comment on their posts, share their work, respond to their stories – show up as a real human being who genuinely appreciates what they’re doing. This will make your eventual pitch feel much more natural, because you’ve already established rapport.

4. Go deep instead of wide:

Don’t feel like you have to collaborate with dozens of people at once. Focus on finding a few high-quality partners who share your values and goals. Deep, meaningful collaborations will always produce better results than spreading yourself thin.

Pitching Collaborations the Right Way

Okay, you’ve done the research, and you’ve built up a relationship – now it’s time to pitch. But how do you approach this without feeling salesy or pushy – so it’s a win-win for both of you.

Here are a few ways:

  • Personalize your pitch:
    This is so important! Don’t send out a generic ‘Hey, I’d love to collaborate’ message. You need to show them that you’ve done your research. Mention specific things you’ve seen them post about or talk about that resonate with you. Show them that you’re not just looking for any collaboration—you’re looking for an aligned one.
  • Focus on what you can offer.
    When you’re pitching, don’t make it all about what YOU will get out of the collaboration. Focus on what you can bring to the table. Be clear about how your partnership will benefit them and their audience. A great example is: ‘I see that your audience loves learning about [specific topic], and I think they’d really benefit from my [resource/service]. I’d love to share it with them, and I’d be happy to promote [something they have] to my audience as well.

How Do We Turn These Collaborations Into More…

Collaborations aren’t just a ‘one and done’ situation.

Ideally, you want to turn these collaborations into long-term relationships.

Here’s how:

  1. Follow up.
    After a collaboration, don’t just disappear. Send a thank-you email or message. Let them know how much you appreciated working with them, and be specific about what went well in the collaboration.

  2. Stay engaged.
    Even after the collaboration is over, keep engaging with their content. Continue to support them, and keep the lines of communication open.

  3. Look for future opportunities.
    Keep the door open for future collaborations. If the first collaboration went well, there might be opportunities down the road for more projects. Don’t be afraid to suggest future partnerships if the timing feels right.”

To recap, finding aligned partners for collaborations is all about being proactive, building genuine relationships, and offering value.

It takes time and intention, but the results are absolutely worth it.

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 156

Feeling overwhelmed by the thought of your next launch? You’re not alone.

In this episode, I chatted with pre-launch strategist Brenna McGowan, who is revolutionising the way entrepreneurs approach launching. Brenna believes that the traditional launch model is backwards and often leads to unnecessary stress and burnout.

In this episode she shares her insights on crafting an effective pre-launch strategy that not only reduces stress but also aligns with your personality and business style. If you’ve ever felt like you wanted to “burn everything to the ground” during a launch, this episode is packed with practical tips and fresh perspectives to help you rethink your approach.

Click play to listen to this episode in full:

Today we covered:

  • Rethinking Traditional Launch Strategies:
    Brenna shared her insights on why the conventional way of launching is often backwards and can lead to unnecessary stress and overwhelm. She emphasised the importance of aligning your launch approach with your personality, business size, and resources, rather than trying to replicate the strategies of industry giants.

  • The Power of Pre-Launch Planning:
    We dove deep into what a pre-launch is and why it’s a critical component of a successful launch. Brenna explained that the pre-launch phase, typically 4-6 weeks before your official launch, is about preparing your audience by selling the process, not just the product. This approach can lead to increased sales, better client fit, and a more enjoyable launch experience.

    We also discussed strategies for creating content that resonates, such as sharing personal stories, using audio or video to connect, and being mindful of your audience’s current feelings and objections. Brenna stressed the importance of not over-educating during the pre-launch phase to avoid overwhelming your audience.

  • Structuring Your Pre-Launch Content:
    We explored Brenna’s method for organising pre-launch content using weekly themes:
  1. Week 1 – Why: Share your reasons for doing what you do to connect with your audience on a deeper level.
  2. Week 2 – Pain Points: Address the specific challenges and struggles your audience is facing without immediately offering solutions.
  3. Week 3 – Myths and Objections: Tackle common misconceptions and barriers that prevent your audience from taking action.
  4. Week 4 – Transformation: Paint a vivid picture of the results and transformation your audience can achieve.
  • Building Relationships and Growing Your Email List:
    Brenna talked about how to leverage collaborations and relationship-based strategies to grow your email list during the pre-launch. She suggested practical tactics like email swaps, voxer chats for market research, and being intentional about planning collaborations that align with your launch timeline.

Want a practical next step if you’re planning to launch an offer soon?

Start by mapping out your pre-launch strategy.

Outline the next 4-6 weeks leading up to your launch, assigning each week a specific theme as Brenna suggested. By planning your pre-launch intentionally, you’ll set the stage for a more successful and less stressful launch.

title: When & How To Start Selling To Your Email List… Without Feeling Salesy.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 155

If you’ve ever wondered when the right time is to start selling to your email list, or if you’ve felt a little icky or guilty about making an offer, you’re not alone… But here’s the thing: selling is a natural part of running a business, and your email list is actually the perfect place to do it – when done right.

Growing your email list is just the first step, but knowing how and when to start selling to your email list – without feeling pushy – is where the magic really happens. Imagine sending an email that not only nurtures your relationship with your audience but also gently introduces your offers in a way that feels natural and aligned.

Today, I’m going to share practical tips on how to subtly sell through email, how to avoid that salesy feeling, and finally get your offers in front of the people who need them most. So, if you’re ready to turn your email list into a powerful business tool and start making consistent sales without feeling gross about it, grab your coffee, get comfy, and let’s dive in!

Click play to listen to the episode in full below:

When To Start Selling To Your Email List

The question I probably get the most once someone has started to grow their email list. When should you start selling to your email list? Here’s the good news: you don’t need to wait until you have thousands of subscribers to start making sales. You can – and should – begin introducing your offers from the start, even if you have just a handful of people on your list.

But here’s where it’s important to set realistic expectations: with a smaller list, you may not see huge sales numbers right away, and that’s okay. It’s not about the size of your list; it’s about the quality of the connection you have with your subscribers.

Even a small, engaged list can be incredibly powerful.

Remember, each person on your list is a real person who has shown interest in what you offer. Focus on serving them well, and those sales will come – they may be small to start but they still count.

Now, it’s not about just jumping in with a sales pitch right away. The key is to build trust first. Your subscribers joined your list because they’re interested in what you have to say, so your first job is to provide value. Focus on nurturing your relationship with them, get to know them, and let them get to know you.

Think of it like a new friendship. You wouldn’t ask a new friend for a favour the first time you meet, right? You’d build that relationship first, before you felt comfortable coming in with an ask. It’s the same with your email list. Your goal is to create that trust and familiarity before anything else. If you’re wondering how do you know though – how do you know that you’ve done enough relationship building before you start to sell?

I love the rule of three for this: for every sales email, send three value-packed emails that educate, entertain, or inspire your audience. This balance helps you stay top of mind without overwhelming them with pitches.

How Do You Introduce Sales Into Your Emails?

So, how do you start selling to your email list, without feeling like you’re selling? Here are some of my favourite subtle ways to introduce your offers…

Casual Mentions:

One of my favourite ways to introduce an offer is through casual mentions within your content. Let’s say you’re sharing a tip or telling a story – mention how your product, service, or membership played a role. For example, ‘The other day, while working with a client inside The Email Growth Club, we discovered…’ This approach doesn’t feel like a sales pitch; it feels like part of the story (and of course, I hyperlink the offer to the sales or waitlist page for those that are interested in checking it out!)

Use The P.S or Email Footer Section:

The P.S. section of your email is gold and in my opinion, totally under utilised! It’s often one of the most read parts of your email, and it’s the perfect spot for a soft sell. You can add something like, ‘P.S. If you’re ready to take the next step, check out [your offer].’ It’s gentle, it’s not in-your-face, and it gives your audience a little nudge without too much pressure.

I also love those stylised 4 x 4 footers you’ve most likely seen around – originally created by Dama Jue – I am a big of fan of selling in the email footer like this as well. In case you haven’t seen it, imagine a grid of four at the bottom of an email, with a simple roundup of things – Dama teaches:

  • What I’m working on
  • Tech I’m testing
  • Events I’m eyeing &
  • Exciting biz ideas


You can create this with any four things you’d like your readers to know about though and this is a great way to subtly sell both offers you’re selling, but also earn affiliate income from tech or other creators that you promote and support. My one piece of advice with this, don’t use it in every single email. If you send a weekly newsletter, include it there – but if you’re sending more than that (promoting collaborations or doing market research etc) don’t include it every time.

Here’s a screenshot of a recent footer so you can envisage what this strategy looks like – and you can find my affiliate link to the training Dama sells on this strategy in the show notes of this episode too.

Share Success Stories:

There’s nothing more powerful than sharing stories of transformation. Highlight your clients’ successes or testimonials in a way that feels like helpful advice rather than a sales pitch. For example, ‘One of our members, Sarah, struggled with growing her email list for months until she joined The Email Growth Club, and now she’s seen incredible growth.’ You’re showing your audience what’s possible without overtly pushing them to buy (and once again, whenever you mention your offer, make sure you link to the sales page!)

Promote Free Content That Leads to Paid Offers:

Another great way to introduce sales is by leading with free content that naturally connects to your paid offer. This could be a free webinar, guide, or challenge that ends with a pitch. You’re providing tons of value upfront, and the offer feels like the next logical step for your audience – a no brainer for them to say yes to. I talk about this a lot when I teach how to create a lead magnet – a freebie – that actually brings leads into your business – it’s all about reverse engineering this.

How do you do that?

You work backwards, start with the end in mind and create a resource that helps them with the very first step they need to take. Then you lead them to the main paid offer that you know will help them with the remainder of the transformation – or solve the rest of the problem that they have. For example, my lead magnet is a guide called Your Next 1000 Subscribers – which you can get in the show notes of course – this guide shares with the reader 11 different collaborations or ways that they can grow their email list without social media or paid ads. It helps them see the options that they have – that they don’t need to be dancing and pointing at the camera to build an audience… and then the next logical, no brainer next step, is to invite them into The Email Growth Club – my membership that dives in deeper to each of these strategies. I lead them there through the email sequence on the backend of the guide that goes out automatically.

Now, Let’s Dive Into Some Tangible Tips To Help You Sell – Without Feeling Salesy:

1. Focus on Benefits, Not Features:

Your audience wants to know, ‘What’s in it for me?’ So instead of just listing features, highlight the specific benefits of your offer. How will it change their life? For instance, instead of saying, ‘The Email Growth Club has over 20 trainings,’ try, ‘Inside The Email Growth Club, you’ll learn how to create a free resource that actually brings in leads, build a visibility plan that works, and access the ultimate collaboration database updated weekly to keep your list growing.’ See the difference – focus on the transformation and always ask yourself, what does this mean for them?

2. Ask Questions to Spark Curiosity:

Curiosity is a powerful tool. Use questions in your subject lines or email body that lead naturally into your offer. ‘Ever wondered how successful entrepreneurs grow their email lists so quickly? Here’s what they do differently.’ You’re opening a loop that makes them want to click and learn more. This goes for all of your content – blog posts, social, podcast episodes – but of course, includes your emails!

3. Provide Consistent Value:

Always lead with value. Share actionable advice, quick wins, or behind-the-scenes insights that build goodwill and trust with your audience. Remember, on the other end of an email address is a human that comes with their own baggage – good or bad. Perhaps they’ve been burnt before, perhaps they’re naturally risk adverse, perhaps they are excited and can’t wait to work with you (that’s the good baggage!) Regardless, when they see you consistently showing up for them, your sales emails will feel like a natural extension of the value you’re already providing – and they’ll feel the energy behind your intentions.

4. Use Soft Language:

And lastly, instead of aggressive sales language, use softer, more inviting phrases like ‘If you’re ready,’ ‘consider this,’ or ‘you might like.’ It feels less like a command and more like a friendly suggestion, which makes you and your audience feel more comfortable – especially when you’re just starting to sell to your email list! Of course, if you’re in a traditional launch period for a specific offer – let’s say you’re sending 8 emails over 5 days with an open and closed cart period, you’re going to want to be more direct, especially towards the end of the launch – but if it’s not that, and you’re just getting used to subtly selling to your email list, the soft language will certainly help you both.

What About Transitioning From Value To Sales?

So how do you transition from providing value to asking for the sale without it feeling abrupt?

Here are a few ways:

  • Call to Action with Care:
    When it’s time to ask your audience to take action, keep it clear but gentle. Instead of ‘Buy now!’ try something like, ‘If this resonates with you, I’d love for you to check out The Email Growth Club.’ It’s inviting and puts the decision in their hands.
  • Overcoming Objections Naturally:
    Address objections in a way that feels conversational. For example, if you know a common objection is price, you could say, ‘I get it, investing can feel scary, but think of how this could pay off when you have an email list of 500, 1000, 5000 of your ideal clients that could be waiting on the other side.’
  • Show the Journey:
    Take your subscribers behind the scenes. Share your why, your process, and the value behind your offer. Let them see what goes into it – this transparency builds trust and makes them more receptive to your sales pitches. Especially when this is so different to everything else they see online!

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 154

Today, I want to introduce you to something that is close to my heart and that is transforming the businesses of so many amazing business owners inside – my membership, The Email Growth Club.

If you’ve ever felt stuck, staring at the same subscriber number month after month, or overwhelmed because you can’t seem to be consistent on social media no matter how hard you try, this is for you. Maybe you’ve been pouring your heart into creating content, showing up on social media, and still, the results just aren’t there. You’re feeling frustrated, overwhelmed, and quite honestly, just over it. I get it because I’ve been right where you are – and that’s exactly why I created The Email Growth Club. So today, I’m pulling back the curtain to show you exactly what’s inside and how it could be the community & the solution you’ve been looking for.

Click play below to listen to this episode in full:

Why did I start The Email Growth Club?

I started The Email Growth Club because I saw a gap – a real need for a space where women entrepreneurs could get real, actionable help with growing their email lists. I’m talking about those of you who feel stuck, frustrated, overwhelmed and you aren’t sure what to do next. Maybe you’ve tried posting on social media, showing up consistently, and even trying to create lead magnets – freebies that seem to sit on your website for 5 years and do nothing but collect virtual dust, nothing seems to actually work. You’re spinning your wheels, but the results just aren’t there.

I’ve heard from so many women in this exact spot. They’re trying so hard to be consistent, posting all the things and ways that they’re told to, trying to be on all the platforms, prioritising it over everything else, and then when they miss a day or week because #life, the guilt sets in – and through it all, they’re still not seeing any growth – or making any money. They’re stuck at the same subscriber number, or worse, they haven’t even started their email list because the whole thing just feels so intimidating. And let’s not even get started on the fear of sending that first email – what if no one reads it? What if they unsubscribe? What if they don’t care? It’s a lot.

The Email Growth Club was created to change all of that. I wanted to provide a space where you could get the support, the resources, and the accountability to not just grow your email list, but to actually enjoy the process. I wanted you to feel confident that the time and effort you’re putting in will pay off. And the transformation I want for every single member is clear: I want you to see your email list as a powerful, profitable asset that works for you, day in and day out.

This membership isn’t about grinding harder; it’s about working smarter with strategies that are proven to work and don’t require you to burn out. We focus on relationship-based growth – things like collaborations, bundles, guest speaking, freebie swaps and more! These are strategies that build your email list organically, that connect you with other like-minded entrepreneurs that also serve the same idea clients as you, and that allow you to grow in a way that feels authentic, fun and actually works!

So what’s exactly inside The Email Growth Club?

So let’s talk about how we get you from feeling stuck and frustrated to seeing real growth in your email list. The Email Growth Club is packed with resources & trainings, but what makes it truly powerful is the combination of strategy, community, and accountability.

Inside the club, we have an Email Marketing 101 training for those of you who are just starting out or need a refresher on the basics. This training breaks down everything from how to set up your list to understanding your email data and analytics. If you’ve ever looked at your open rates and thought, ‘What does this even mean?’- this training is for you.

Next, we have a step-by-step guide on how to create a free resource that actually brings in leads. This isn’t about throwing together another PDF that sits on your website and collects dust. We teach you how to create something that acts as the first step in your sales funnel, making sure that every subscriber is not just a number but a potential client.

And then there’s the 30-day visibility plan training, where we map out a clear strategy for showing up and getting seen, using methods that work for your specific business. You’ll learn all about different growth strategies through my visibility framework, like freebie swaps, bundles, guest speaking and summits – and how to choose the ones that align best with your goals.

On top of the short, value packed trainings – one of the other standout features of The Email Growth Club is our Ultimate Collaboration Database. I personally update this 2-3 times a week with fresh opportunities, whether it’s a summit, a bundle, a podcast looking for guests, or a freebie swap. Imagine having a list of curated collaboration invitations at your fingertips – all you have to do is apply. Talk about a game changer!

And if that wasn’t enough, I also host quarterly bundles exclusively just for members. I host these bundles solely to help you grow your email list even faster, with the bundle being promoted to my own email list as well. These bundles can help you add 50 – 100 of subscribers to your email list in a matter of days.

The Transformation You Can Expect When You Join The Email Growth Club

The real magic of The Email Growth Club isn’t just in the resources or the strategies; it’s in the transformation that happens when you’re no longer trying to do it all on your own. When you join, you’re not just getting trainings and templates – you’re gaining access to a community of female business owners who get it. Female business owners who know what it feels like to struggle, to feel stuck, and who are committed to lifting each other up.

Imagine having a go-to place where you can get feedback on your strategies, share your wins and struggles, and get real-time advice when you’re feeling lost. Imagine not having to Google every question you have about email marketing because the answers—and the support—are right there.

One of our members, Amanda, shared that before joining the club, she felt completely overwhelmed and guilty because she could never keep up with the latest strategies. She was stuck in a cycle of inconsistency and felt like her business was just treading water. But after diving into the training on creating a visibility plan, she finally felt like she had control. She knew exactly what to focus on each week, and for the first time, she actually enjoyed growing her list. And the best part? Her open rates and engagement have never been higher. She is just one example from over 250 current members of the club.

So if you’re ready to stop feeling stuck and start seeing real growth, just like Amanda, I’d love to invite you to join us inside The Email Growth Club. This is your chance to finally take control of your email marketing, connect with other incredible women, and build an email list that works for you (so you can finally step away from social media, if that’s what you want!)

Head to the link in the show notes, check out all the details, and sign up today. I can’t wait to welcome you into our community and watch you thrive. Until next time, keep growing, keep connecting, and remember, your email list isn’t just a number—it’s the foundation of your business success.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 153

Today, we’re tackling a super important part of email marketing – one that can literally make or break your email campaigns: writing email subject lines that actually get your email opened. Because let’s face it, you can have the best content inside your email, but if no one opens it, it’s all for nothing, right?

Today I’m sharing 5 proven strategies for writing winning email subject lines that grab attention and entice your audience to open. These tips have not only helped me achieve consistently high open rates (45% or higher) but have also worked wonders for my 1:1 clients and membership members.

Click play to listen to the episode in full:

Why Do Email Subject Lines Matter?

First things first, why do email subject lines matter so much? Your email subject line is essentially the gatekeeper of your email. It’s the first impression, the ‘thing’ that convinces someone to open and read. Think of it like the headline of a news article – if it’s not compelling, no one’s going to bother reading what’s inside.

Here’s a crazy stat from an Optin Monster article I found: 47% of people open an email based on the email subject line alone! That means almost half of your audience makes a split-second decision based on those few words. And what’s even more surprising? About 69% of email recipients report an email as spam based solely on the subject line… and we want to avoid being marked as spam as much as we can help it!

So, mastering the art of email subject line writing is crucial if you want your emails to get opened and read.

And remember, it’s not just about getting the open – it’s also about setting the tone for the entire email. If your subject line creates intrigue, urgency, or promises value, it primes your reader to engage with the content inside.

But if it falls flat, your amazing email content goes to waste.

5 Proven Strategies for Writing Winning Email Subject Lines

Alright, let’s dive into the good stuff – my top five strategies for writing winning email subject lines that will help you boost your open rates.

1. Use Curiosity to Spark Interest

People are naturally curious, and tapping into that can work wonders for your subject lines. Think about headlines that make you go, ‘Wait, what?’ that’s the power of curiosity. For example, try using something like ‘You Won’t Believe What Happened Last Week’ or ‘The Secret to Growing Your Email List…’

Action Step: Go through your existing content and pull out a surprising fact or result. Turn it into a curiosity-driven subject line that makes people think, ‘I need to know more.’ The key is to give just enough information to make them want more, without giving everything away. Avoid being misleading, though – your email should deliver on the promise of your subject line.

2. Create a Sense of Urgency or Scarcity

Urgency works because it plays on FOMO – fear of missing out. Subject lines like ‘Last Chance to Grab This’ or ‘Only 3 Spots Left!’ can drive your audience to take immediate action.

Action Step: Look at your upcoming promotions, sales, or time-sensitive offers. Use phrases like ‘Ends Tonight’ or ‘Only Until Midnight’ to create that urgent nudge. Just remember, don’t overuse urgency – reserve it for genuine scenarios to maintain credibility and continue to build that trust with your email list.

3. Personalise Your Subject Lines

Personalisation goes beyond just adding someone’s first name. Think about including details that make your reader feel seen, like referencing past purchases or interests. For example, ‘Hey Sarah, This Is Just for You’ or ‘Your Perfect Community Is Waiting For You.’

Action Step: Use your email platform’s data to personalise your subject lines with details that matter to your audience. Try experimenting with personalisation beyond names – consider mentioning location, past interactions, or any unique details you have about your subscribers. This is where segmenting your list can come in handy – if you want to dive more into what that can look like, check out: How To Level Up Your Email Marketing for an 1000+ Email List where I dive more into some simple segmentation practices you can try!

4. Make It Benefit-Driven

Your audience wants to know, ‘What’s in it for me?’ A benefit-driven subject line answers that question right away. Focus on the outcome your email provides. For example, ‘How to Double Your Sales in 30 Days’ or ‘Get More Done with This Simple Trick.’

Action Step: Next time you write a subject line, ask yourself: What’s the key benefit the reader will get? Rewrite it to highlight that. Make it clear and specific, so they instantly see the value in opening your email.

5. Keep It Short and Sweet

And lastly, but I argue most importantly – remember, to keep them short & sweet. Email subject lines often get cut off, especially on mobile devices. Keeping them short – ideally under 50 characters – ensures your full message is seen. For example, ‘New Offer Inside’ or ‘Quick Tip for Better Results.’

Action Step: Use a character count tool when drafting subject lines and try writing three versions – short, medium, and long. Test them on your phone to see what gets cut off. Stick with the short version that packs the most punch.

Some Common Mistakes to Avoid With Your Email Subject Lines

Now that we’ve covered the best practices, let’s talk about some common mistakes to avoid with your email subject lines that can harm your open rates.

Mistake #1: Being vague or misleading. If your subject line promises something, make sure the email delivers on that promise. Misleading subject lines might get clicks initially, but they’ll damage trust and hurt your long-term engagement…

Mistake #2: Using all caps or too many exclamation points or emoji’s. It looks spammy and can often lead to your emails landing in the dreaded spam folder. Keep your subject lines professional and clean, and let your words do the talking.

Mistake #3: Relying solely on clickbait. Clickbait can work once or twice, but it’s not sustainable. You want to build trust, not trick people into opening your emails. Plus, this will lead to a higher rate of subscribers leaving, when all you wanted them to do was open your email.

Action Step: Go through your recent subject lines and audit them for these mistakes. Replace anything that could seem misleading, overly salesy, or too pushy.

The Importance Of Testing & Tweaking Your Email Subject Lines

One of the best ways to improve your subject lines is through testing. Try A/B testing different subject lines to see which ones perform best for your audience. Maybe test a curiosity-driven subject line against a benefit-driven one, or compare personalisation against a standard format. Remember, this is a relationship we’re building so it’s important that we get to know what our perfect person likes to open, so we can tailor our email subject lines to them – and the only way we can find this out, is by testing and tweaking those subject lines!

Now, if you have no idea how to do this – simply google ‘how to A/B test with – and the name of your email service provider. I personally use and rave about ConvertKit – and they make it super easy right on the broadcast page where you write your email – here’s my affiliate link in case you want to try them out!

Action Step: Set up A/B tests in your email platform. For your next email, draft two versions of the subject line using different strategies and let the data guide you. Look at your open rates at least 24 hours after you’ve sent it, but also track other metrics like click rates and responses to see which style resonates most with your audience.

So there you have it – five proven strategies to write email subject lines that get opened – and some mistakes to avoid as well. Remember, your email subject line is your first impression, so make it count. Use curiosity, urgency, personalisation, and benefits, and keep it short and to the point.

Avoid common mistakes, and don’t forget to test and tweak along the way.

I hope you found these tips helpful, and I can’t wait to hear about the subject lines you create! If you want more support when it comes to growing, nurturing or selling to your email list, check out my membership, The Email Growth Club! I’d love to support you with this!

Until next time, keep growing, keep connecting, and keep nailing those subject lines!

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 152

Are you struggling to write authentic email copy that truly feels like you? In this episode of The Email Growth Show, I sit down with Marisa Corcoran, copy expert and creator of The Copy Confidence Society, to dive into the secrets of crafting authentic, personality-filled copy that magnetically attracts your dream clients.

Click play to listen to the episode in full:

Today we covered:

  1. Why Copy is Essential for Your Business: Marisa explains that copy is everywhere – from emails to social media posts and even the words you speak. It’s not just about writing; it’s about connecting and communicating your unique message. Whether you’re tweaking your website or sending a sales email, knowing what to say and how to say it is a crucial skill for any business owner.

  2. Personalising Your Copy: Marisa shares her tips for creating a “word closet” and an “accessories closet” – two techniques to infuse your personality into your writing. These help you identify your go-to words, phrases, and personal touches that make your copy unmistakably yours – and will help you write authentic email copy. From your favourite cookies to the little phrases you use daily, these elements help your audience connect with you on a personal level, increasing the trust they have in you & your business!

  3. Overcoming Imposter Syndrome and Getting Specific: One of the biggest barriers to great copy is a lack of clarity. Marisa emphasises the importance of specificity in your messaging.
    Instead of being a generalist, be the specialist your audience is seeking.
    She shares examples of how narrowing your focus can help you stand out, connect deeply, and build trust with your audience.

  4. Lastly, How To Using Copy to Build Relationships: Great copy isn’t just about selling; it’s about building a relationship with your readers. Marisa and I discuss how authentic email copy can be a game-changer for your business, creating connections that go beyond just numbers on your email list.

Feeling inspired to revamp your copy & write more authentic email copy?

Start by creating your word and accessories closet, and don’t be afraid to let your true personality shine through.

excerpt: THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 151 Today, I’m going to share with you my absolute favourite strategy for growing my email list in 2024 – hosting free digital bundles. content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 151

Today, I’m going to share with you my absolute favourite strategy for growing my email list in 2024 – hosting free digital bundles. Now, if you’ve been following me for a while, you know I’m all about finding effective, relationship-based ways to grow your email list without the constant grind of social media or paid ads… and let me tell you, digital bundles are an absolute game changer!

Over the past year, I’ve hosted multiple bundles – some within my membership, The Email Growth Club, and others publicly, like The Goal Getter Biz Bundle, The Empowered Mompreneur Bundle, The Visible AF Bundle, and of course, Kylie’s Birthday Bash Bundle. These bundles have collectively added thousands of engaged subscribers to my email list, and today, I’m going to share exactly why they work so well and how you can start using this strategy too.

Click play to listen to the episode in full:

What Are Digital Bundles and How Do They Work?

First things first, let’s talk about what digital bundles actually are.

A digital bundle is essentially a collection of high quality, normally paid resources or digital products, all packaged together and offered to a targeted audience, to solve a specific problem. The magic happens when you bring together multiple contributors – each offering something valuable – and in exchange for access to these resources, participants sign up with their name & email addresses. It’s a win-win: contributors grow their email lists AND participants get amazing resources, and as the host, you get to expand your reach in a big way.

The process of organising a bundle might sound a bit daunting at first, but it’s really straightforward once you break it down. You start by choosing a theme or topic that resonates with your ideal client – something that addresses a specific problem or need they have. Then, you recruit contributors who align with that theme, set up a landing page for sign-ups, create a gift page linking to all the resources that they can get for free inside the bundle and promote the bundle like crazy while it’s live – which is generally 5 – 7 days. The bundle attendees normally then have a little bit of extra time after the bundle live period is over, where they can go through the gift page and sign up for any of the resources that they want access to.

Now, I want to share a bit about my own experience with digital bundles. I host these bundles quarterly for the members of The Email Growth Club, and I’ve also publicly hosted four big bundles:

  • The Goal Getter Biz Bundle,
  • The Empowered Mompreneur Bundle,
  • The Visible AF Bundle, and
  • my most recent as recording this, Kylie’s Birthday Bash Bundle.


AND I actually have a new one going live next week called The Ultimate Email Marketing Bundle! Each of these bundles has been an incredible opportunity to connect with new people, provide immense value, and most importantly, grow my email list. I’m talking hundreds – and sometimes even thousands of new subscribers from each bundle! It’s been a game changer not just for me, but for the members of The Email Growth Club as well. We’ve seen significant growth, more engagement, and an influx of new opportunities because of these free digital bundles.

Now of course, because I like to keep things real around here: there is a significant amount of work that goes into hosting your own digital bundle. There’s a lot of coordinating with multiple contributors, testing and uploading, and emails back and forward to make sure everything runs smoothly – but in my opinion, the benefits far outweigh the time spent. I’ve learned so much from hosting these bundles, and I can honestly say they’ve been one of the most effective strategies I’ve ever used for list growth to date.

So, Why Are Free Digital Bundles The #1 Way To Grow Your Email List In 2024?

Let me break it down for you.

First, they offer massive exposure. When you collaborate with multiple contributors, you’re not just tapping into your own audience – you’re accessing the combined reach of every contributor involved. That means your bundle has the potential to reach thousands, even tens of thousands, of people who might not have heard of you otherwise.

Second, the quality of subscribers you get from a bundle is often higher than other methods. Because these participants are opting in for specific, targeted resources that align with their interests, they’re more likely to be engaged and interested in what you have to offer. These are people who genuinely want what you’re providing, which means they’re more likely to open your emails, click your links, and eventually, become paying customers.

Third, bundles are a fantastic way to build relationships and network. By working closely with other entrepreneurs, you’re not only expanding your reach, but you’re also creating valuable connections that can lead to future collaborations, joint ventures, or even just friendships that support you on your entrepreneurial journey. That is worth every minute spent in my opinion – some of my closest business friends have come from collaborating with them in a bundle – whether I was the host or just the contributor. If you think about it, it makes sense as we already have something in common, we serve the same ideal clients!

And finally, free digital bundles are scalable. Whether you’re just starting out or you’re an experienced entrepreneur, you can tailor your bundle to fit your needs. You can start small with just a few contributors and grow as you gain confidence and experience. It really is up to you what kind of bundle you want to host or how big you want it to be!

Ok, So What Is Involved In Hosting a Free Digital Bundle?

If you’re ready to give digital bundles a try, here’s a quick step-by-step guide to get you started.

  1. First, start with planning. Choose a theme that resonates with your ideal client and addresses a specific need or problem they have. That is key – we don’t want some fluffy, vague, shitty type bundle – there are enough of them out there and that won’t attract your perfect person. Remember that is the goal… so be specific. Then, start reaching out to potential contributors who align with that theme & topic. The key here is to ensure that every resource in the bundle provides REAL value and is something your audience will be super excited about!

  2. Next, move on to execution. Set up a landing page for sign-ups, manage the contributions from your collaborators, and plan out your promotional strategy. Make sure everyone involved knows what’s expected of them and when to promote the bundle to their audience.

  3. Finally, don’t forget about the follow-up. Once the bundle is over, it’s crucial to nurture your new subscribers. Set up a welcome sequence to introduce them to your world, provide additional value, and let them know what to expect from you moving forward. This is where you start building that relationship that will turn new subscribers into loyal followers and customers!

Remember, you are allowed to start small with this. If this is your first time hosting a bundle, don’t feel like you need to go big right out of the gate. Start with a smaller bundle, maybe with just a few contributors, and see how it goes, how it feels. You’ll learn a lot from that first experience, and you can always scale up from there…

Remember that consistency pays off. I’ve seen incredible growth in my email list from hosting bundles consistently. It’s not just about the immediate boost in subscribers; it’s about the long-term relationships and opportunities that come from those collaborations.

And if you’re looking for more support or guidance, I’d love to have you join The Email Growth Club. It’s a space where we dive deep into strategies like these, with step by step action plans and a lot of support – so if you want to host your own bundle in the next couple of months or even next year, come and join us and get the process started – with a whole community of entrepreneurs to connect, collaborate and cheer each other on! Simply visit: kyliekelly.com/emailgrowthclub for more details!

To quickly recap, digital bundles are an incredible way to grow your email list – offering massive exposure, high-quality subscribers, valuable networking opportunities, and scalability.

If you haven’t tried hosting a digital bundle yet, I encourage you to give it a go. It could be the game changer you’ve been looking for – and if you’re not quite ready to host your own bundle event, find one to participate in. When it comes to where to find bundles – there are certain FB groups that you can search to find bundle opportunities to be in – but, that’s actually one of things that I help my members do in The Email Growth Club! I get a lot of opportunities come to me through personal invites (which I love because as you all know, I’m not a huge fan of social media and don’t spend a great deal of time on there!) so I make all of those opportunities available for my members in the Collaborations Database. At the time of recording this, there are over 30 different opportunities open for them to apply to immediately. Well worth the $27 a month on it’s own!

I’m so glad you were here with me today – until next time, keep growing, keep connecting, and remember – your email list is your most valuable asset.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 150

Today, we’re going to tackle some of the biggest myths around email marketing. These are the kind of myths that might have you second-guessing your strategies or even holding back from going all-in with email marketing. But trust me, by the end of this episode, you’ll see that these myths are just that – myths. And I’m here to clear them up and make sure you know the truth behind it all!

If you want to listen to this episode in full, press play below:

Myth #1: You Need Social Media to Grow Your Email List & Be Successful Online

Now, I get it. Social media is everywhere, and it feels like everyone’s saying you need to be on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok – whatever’s trending – to build your email list, or even more broadly than that, your business. But here’s the thing: while social media can be a helpful tool, it’s not the end-all, be-all.

In fact, it’s not even close.

Let’s talk about some of the benefits of not relying on social media to grow your email list or your business.

  • First, there’s the freedom from algorithms. When you build your email list without social media, you’re not at the mercy of constantly changing algorithms that decide whether or not your content gets seen. One day you might reach thousands of people, and the next, just a handful. It’s unpredictable and can be incredibly frustrating & stressful. But with email, you’re in control. When you hit send, you know your message is going straight to your subscribers’ inboxes. There’s no middleman deciding who gets to see your content and when.
  • Second, it reduces the pressure & overwhelm. Let’s be honest, social media can be overwhelming. The need to constantly post, engage, and keep up with trends can be exhausting, especially if you’re a busy entrepreneur, or like many of us, mothers in business. By focusing on email list growth strategies that don’t rely on social media, you can reclaim your time and energy. You can spend more time creating meaningful content, building relationships, and actually enjoying your business- and life, rather than feeling chained to your phone or computer.
  • Third, it fosters deeper, more meaningful connections. When someone joins your email list, they’re inviting you into their personal space, their inbox. This creates an opportunity for a deeper connection than what’s often possible on social media. Your emails aren’t competing with a feed full of distractions; they’re a direct line to your ideal client, your perfect person, allowing for more personalised and impactful communication and relationship.
  • And finally, it’s about sustainability. Social media platforms come and go, but your email list is something you own. It’s a sustainable asset that grows over time, giving you a solid foundation for your business. You’re not building your business on rented land; you’re creating a valuable resource that belongs entirely to you.

So, if you’ve been stressing about needing to be everywhere on social media, take a deep breath and remember: there are plenty of other ways to grow your email list and business. If you haven’t tuned in yet to the last episode on this very podcast, Episode 149, I shared my visibility framework and all the options we have to grow our email lists, without paid ads or social media – and there is a lot!

So… let’s consider this Myth. Busted.

Myth #2: You Must Offer a Free Resource To Get New Subscribers

Moving on to Myth #2: ‘You must offer a free resource – or a freebie – to get subscribers.

This one’s pretty common, and I’ve even fallen into this trap myself. The idea is that you have to give something away for free, a guide, a checklist, a mini-course, to get people to sign up for your email list. I remember thinking that this was the only way when I first started my photography business – I created an amazing wedding photography guide for couples, posted it on my website – and waited a long time, I’m talking years, and never really got much interest. Maybe you can relate?

Then you think, perhaps it’s the ‘wrong’ resource, so you create something else… and soon, you’ve spent an embarrassing amount of time creating resources that you aren’t even sure about anymore – and feeling more confused and overwhelmed than ever. If you were to take one look at my Canva graveyard of unfinished designs & haphazard resources, you’d realise I’m speaking from experience.

Now most of the time – and what most coaches won’t tell you – is the reason that these freebie’s aren’t effective is actually because you just don’t have the traffic on your website to get the signups to your email list. You don’t need to create anymore of them.

So back to the myth, free resources – when you have traffic coming to your website can be super effective, but they aren’t the only way to build your email list. I actually have a training all about no freebie list building inside my membership, The Email Growth Club, because sometimes, when someone joins that doesn’t have a free resource created yet… I don’t want them to spend the next month building something. I want them to start growing their list straight away. We’re all about taking action and seeing fast results in there.

When it comes to growing your email list, what really matters is providing value – and opportunities for your ideal clients to join your list. You can do this through exclusive content, like behind-the-scenes insights or first access to new products. Maybe it’s a weekly email that delivers so much value that people can’t wait to get in on it. Or perhaps it’s the promise of being part of a community or getting insider tips that aren’t available anywhere else.

The key is to make sure that whatever you’re offering aligns with what your audience wants and needs. For example, if I decided to go all in on digital bundles to grow my email list, I would need a digital product, but it would be one that I usually sell, but I am happy to provide to the bundle for free as my contribution. New subscribers could then come into my world through the collaboration. Or let’s say you were wanting to go all in on Pinterest – perhaps you have a blog and have a multitude of pins created for each blog post that you pin on Pinterest and strategically on the blog post, you have an opt in to join your email list to get first access to blog posts just like the one they’re reading before anyone else – or maybe it’s a bonus call with you when they first join. No freebie required.

So… you don’t always need a traditional free resource. Sometimes, just being you, sharing your expertise and connecting on a personal level, with an intentional no freebie list building strategy is enough to get your ideal client to join your email family.

Another myth. Busted.

Myth #3: Email Marketing is Outdated & Ineffective

This one always makes me smile because it’s just so far from the truth. Email marketing is anything but outdated. In fact, it’s one of the most powerful tools you have at your disposal.

Why? Because email is direct. It’s personal. And it’s yours.

Unlike social media, where you’re at the mercy of algorithms and constantly changing rules, your email list is something you own. When someone joins your list, they’re giving you permission to show up in their inbox, and that’s a big deal. They’re not scrolling past your content; they’re opening your emails because they want to hear from you. I honestly imagine my subscribers sometimes sitting in a room, with their hands raised, saying “Kylie, please send me that email. I want to hear from you!” Weird to imagine. Perhaps. But it helped me big time when I used to worry about annoying them or hitting that send button.

Look you know I’m a fan but the numbers back it up. Email marketing consistently delivers higher conversion rates than social media. When people are ready to buy, they turn to their inboxes, not their Instagram feeds – unless it’s midnight and they can’t sleep – we’re all guilty of those purchases aren’t we! Email is where the real connections happen, where trust is built, and where sales are made.

So, if you’ve heard that email marketing is a thing of the past, think again. It’s more relevant now than ever, especially as people crave real, meaningful connections in an increasingly noisy online world – full of highlight reels and fake positivity and income claims. Honestly, if I see another Instagram post sharing that this is the secret to making 10k months and you can do it too, I think I’ll throw my phone at the wall. I’m not even being dramatic. Well, maybe a little but you get my point.

So again – myth busted.

Okay, let’s recap the myths we’ve busted today:

  • Myth #1: You need social media to grow your email list. Not true. There are so many other effective strategies like collaborations and SEO-driven content that will do this for you.
  • Myth #2: You must offer a freebie to get subscribers. Once again, nope! Value-driven content and authentic connections can be just as powerful.
  • Myth #3: Email marketing is outdated and ineffective. Far from it—email is where the magic happens, with higher engagement and conversion rates than social media.

I want you to take a moment to think about how these myths might have been holding you back. What could you do differently now that you know the truth? Maybe it’s time to rethink your strategy, focus on what truly works for you, and let go of the pressure to follow outdated advice.

With over 250 incredible women just like you, it’s the most supportive community you’ll find on the internet – all focused on community, collaboration and growing that email list without paid ads or social. We’d love to have you!
