content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 149

Today, we’ll be diving into two powerful approaches: collaboration-based strategies and search/SEO-driven tactics. These are the exact methods I’ve used to grow my own email list and help my clients & members of The Email Growth Club use to achieve incredible results. Whether you’re just starting out with your email list or looking to take your email marketing to the next level, this framework is going to give you the clarity and direction you need to start seeing real progress.

Click play on the episode below to listen to it in full:

The Power of Email Marketing For Your Online Business

Before we dive into the details of my visibility framework, let’s talk about why email list growth is so important. You’ve probably heard a lot of buzz about social media, and while it has its place, there’s something uniquely powerful about email marketing that often gets overlooked.

  • First, let’s consider the difference between social media followers and email subscribers. When someone follows you on social media, you’re relying on algorithms to get your content in front of them. And let’s be honest, those algorithms can be tricky, unpredictable, and ever-changing. You could have thousands of followers, but if your posts aren’t showing up in their feed, it’s like they don’t exist at all.

    Plus, social media platforms can change their rules, or worse, they could disappear altogether – taking all your hard-earned followers with them. But with email, it’s different. When someone joins your email list, they’re giving you direct access to their inbox. You don’t have to worry about competing with algorithms. Instead, you have the ability to connect with your audience in a more personal, direct way.

  • On top of that, email has consistently been shown to have higher conversion rates than social media. When people open your email, they’re already in a mindset to engage, whether it’s reading your content, clicking a link, or making a purchase. It’s proven to be a much more reliable way to drive sales.
  • And the best part in my opinion? Your email list is something you own. It’s a business asset that belongs to you – no one can take it away. Unlike social media, where your account could be suspended or deleted at any time, your email list is yours to keep and grow. It becomes a valuable part of your business, and over time, it can even be a significant factor in the valuation of your business if you ever decide to sell.

So… how does my visibility framework fits into all of this?

The framework I’m sharing with you today is specifically designed to help entrepreneurs grow their email lists quickly and sustainably. The strategies I’ve included aren’t just about adding numbers – they’re about building lasting relationships with the right people. People who are genuinely interested in what you have to offer and who are more likely to become loyal customers of yours in the future!

One of the biggest challenges I see small business owners face is overwhelm – and I get it, there is always so much to do and so little time to do it. When we then add social media and all the platforms we’re told to be consistent on… it’s exhausting. That’s why this framework is so powerful – it gives you a clear and direct path to follow, leveraging collaborations and SEO-driven strategies instead of social media, so you can grow your email list in a way that feels manageable, effective, and aligned with your business and your life.

So, as we move forward in this episode, keep in mind that the strategies I’m sharing aren’t just about quick wins. They’re about creating a sustainable, long-term approach to building your email list and ultimately, growing your business.

Introducing My Simple V2 Visibility Framework

Ok, let’s dive into my simple V2 Visibility Framework. Now this is something I’ve used myself to grow my own email list fast, without social media or paid ads, and it’s also something I teach over 250 members in The Email Growth Club as well.

So, what does this framework look like? Picture a big ‘V’ with two sides. On one side, we have collaboration-based strategies, and on the other, we have search and SEO-driven strategies. These are two powerful approaches that work together to give you the best of both worlds when it comes to visibility and email list growth.

Collaboration-Based Email List Growth Strategies:

Collaborations are all about leveraging other people’s audiences to grow your own. This isn’t about competition; it’s about working together to create something bigger than what we could achieve on our own. And there are a few key ways to do this effectively.

First up, we have summits, bundles, and freebie swaps. These are fantastic ways to get in front of a large audience quickly. Imagine participating in a virtual summit or contributing to a digital bundle where your ideal clients are already hanging out. By offering something valuable – like a free guide or a mini-course – you can attract a ton of new subscribers to your list.

The main thing to remember with this is to make sure that the resource that you provide is something that is going to speak to your perfect person, your ideal client, and lead them eventually to your main paid offer. More on how you do that in a future episode!

Next, let’s talk about podcast guesting and guest speaking. By guesting on other people’s podcasts or guest speaking in existing groups or masterminds, you get to showcase your expertise to a whole new audience. It’s an incredible opportunity to build trust and connection, and when you provide a clear call to action – like a free download that adds subscribers to your email list – you’re not just sharing your knowledge; you’re growing your list at the same time.

My biggest piece of advice with this is to make sure you have ONE clear call to action at the end of an interview or presentation – don’t send them to your website, your instagram profile, your podcast, your free resource. You want ONE link for them to go next – and that link should always be adding them to your email list.

Now, here’s the thing with collaborations: you don’t need to do all of them at once. In fact, I wouldn’t recommend it! Pick one of these strategies that resonate with you and focus on it for the next 90 days. The key is consistency and building genuine relationships with your collaborators – and make sure you check in at the end of each month and check the data.

  • What kind of results have you gotten?
  • Have you enjoyed this strategy?
  • How does it make you feel?

This is all important to take note of and use in deciding to continue with that strategy for the next 30 days or to tweak and change it up.

Search and SEO-Driven Email List Growth Strategies:

Now, let’s move over to the other side of the ‘V’- the search and SEO-driven strategies. These options are all about making sure that when your ideal clients are searching for solutions online, they find YOU.

The first piece of this puzzle is long-form content and SEO. This could be blog posts or podcast episodes that are optimised for Google. When you create content that’s rich in keywords and answers the questions your ideal clients are asking, you start to show up in their search results. This kind of content continues to work for you long after it’s published, driving organic traffic to your site and growing your email list passively. Remember to again always have a clear call to action that leads the reader or listener to your email list – that is always our goal.

Then, there’s the social media as SEO angle. Platforms like Pinterest, YouTube, and even TikTok are more than just social networks, they’re search engines in their own right. By optimizing your content for these platforms, you’re not just posting into the void and praying someone sees it; you’re creating content that can be found by people who are actively looking for what you offer. Remember to consider keywords in the content you create for these platforms and try repurposing long-form content to save yourself some time.

And finally, traditional PR plays a role here too. Getting featured in articles, being interviewed by media outlets, or writing guest posts can significantly boost your visibility and credibility. These opportunities often come with backlinks and mentions that enhance your SEO, making it easier for people to find you.

So, whether you’re focusing on collaborations, search, or a combination of both, the goal is the same: to grow your email list with strategies that feel good, are sustainable, and don’t rely on the unpredictability of social media.

Remember, you don’t have to do it all at once. I’d recommend choosing one strategy from the Collaboration side of the V and one from the Search & SEO side of the V – focus on them for the next 90 days, and track your progress each month.

You’ll be amazed at the growth you can achieve.

How Do You Choose Which Email List Growth Strategy To Try?

First, let’s recap the two main strategies within my visibility framework: collaborations and search/SEO. These are the pillars of your email list growth strategy, and they’re designed to work together to maximise your reach, impact & fast track your growth.

First, we have collaboration-based strategies – these are all about leveraging the audiences of others to grow your list quickly. Think about summits, bundles, freebie swaps, networking and podcast guesting or guest speaking. These strategies allow you to tap into already established communities and bring in highly engaged subscribers who are likely to resonate with your message.

On the other side, we have search and SEO-driven strategies – these focus on creating content that’s discoverable and searchable over time. This includes long-form content like blog posts, podcast episodes – much like this one, and optimising your presence on platforms like Pinterest, YouTube and even TikTok. These strategies are more about playing the long game, ensuring that your content continues to bring in new subscribers well after it’s been published.

Now, here’s what I want you to do: Choose one strategy from each category – one collaboration and one search/SEO strategy to focus on for the next 90 days. The key here is to stay consistent and give each strategy enough time to show results.

By narrowing your focus, you’ll avoid overwhelm and be able to execute these strategies more effectively.

How Do You Know If These Email List Growth Strategies Are Working?

As you dive into these strategies, it’s crucial to track your progress. Keep an eye on your email list growth, engagement & conversion rates, and any other metrics that matter to you. If you find that one approach isn’t giving the results you expected – and you’ve given it enough time – don’t be afraid to adjust.

This is all about finding what works best for you and your business. Little spoiler here – but all of these strategies actually work. It’s not about choosing ‘the right one’ – it’s about picking the strategy that’s right for you! It has to feel good for you AND give you results – when you can land on something that does that, that’s when you know you’re onto a growth strategy that is sustainable and will work for the long-term.

As we wrap up I want to remind you, by focusing on collaborations and SEO-driven tactics, you’re not only building your email list, you’re building relationships with people who genuinely care about what you have to offer. This is about creating a sustainable, long-term strategy that helps you grow your business in a way that feels good and aligned with your values.

Before you go, don’t forget to check out the free resource I have for you – Your Next 1000 Subscribers Guide. You can sign up for it through the sidebar on the right or visit this link: https://kyliekelly.com/guide

… and if you’re looking for even more support, consider joining The Email Growth Club, my membership where we dive deep into all things email marketing and visibility. You’ll get access to a community of like-minded entrepreneurs, exclusive resources, and so much more. Click here to find out more: https://kyliekelly.com/emailgrowthclub

Remember, I am cheering you on every step of the way. If you have questions, need advice, or just want to share your progress, please reach out to me. I love connecting with my listeners and helping you navigate your email marketing journey. The best place to find me is on Instagram – just shoot me a DM, and let’s chat. Or if you prefer, you can always send me an email – hello@kyliekelly.com.

Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to The Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from 0 to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than 2 years and the same is possible for you too. Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode. Hello. Welcome to episode 149. I am so excited to have you here today. If you’re tired of feeling overwhelmed by social media and frustrated by slow email list growth, you’re in the right place.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:49]:
In this episode, I’m going to walk you through my simple visibility framework, a proven strategy to grow your email list fast without the need for paid ads or constant social media hustle. Doesn’t that sound good? Today we’ll be diving into 2 powerful approaches: collaboration based strategies and search and SEO driven tactics. These are the exact methods I’ve used to grow my own email list and the strategies I use to help my clients and members of the Email Growth Club to achieve incredible results. Whether you’re just starting out with your email list or looking to take your email marketing to the next level, this framework is going to give you the clarity and direction you need to start seeing real progress. So grab a cup of coffee, probably a notepad, and let’s dive in. Now first, I want to briefly talk about why email list growth is so important for your online business. Mainly because we don’t want to dive into these strategies about growing your email list if you don’t really understand why we need to focus on it. Right? Now, I know you’ve probably heard a lot of, shall I say, gurus say how important social media is.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:53]:
And while it has its place, there’s definitely something uniquely powerful about email marketing that often gets overlooked. Firstly, let’s consider the difference between social media followers and email subscribers. When someone follows you on social media, you’re relying on algorithms to get your content in front of them and let’s be honest, those algorithms can be pretty fickle, unpredictable and ever changing. You could have thousands of followers like I do on my Instagram but if your posts aren’t showing up in their feed, it’s like they don’t exist at all. And like I’ve said before, if you spend a lot of time creating that content and then no one sees it, it’s just not a smart way to use our time. When we pile on top of that the fact that social media platforms can change their rules or worse disappear altogether, taking all of your hard end followers and a way that you might even be making revenue with them, it’s just not a smart decision to build our business on that kind of foundation. But with email, it’s so different. When someone joins your email list, they’re giving you direct access to their inbox.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:52]:
You don’t have to worry about competing with algorithms. As long as the content is good and you are smart about your subject line, you have the ability to connect with your audience in a more personal, more direct way. You’re more in control. And here’s what I love the most. Email has consistently been shown to have high conversion rates in social media. When people open your email, they’re already in a mindset to engage whether it’s reading your content, clicking a link, or making a purchase. It’s actually proven to be a much more reliable way to drive sales than anything else. So why wouldn’t we use it? Why wouldn’t we build our email list so that we could connect with our perfect people, our ideal clients? We could show them what we do.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:30]:
We could serve them. We could help them. We could build a relationship with them and then we can invite them into our office and actually create more revenue in our business. And the best part, your email list is something that you own. It’s actually a business asset that belongs to you. No one can take it away. Unlike social media where your account could be suspended or deleted at any time, your email list is yours to keep and to grow. Again, this just breeds a sense of safety.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:54]:
Right? And I don’t know about you, but my nervous system cannot handle the fact that my business could just disappear overnight. Like, no. We do not want that. We are here for the long term and we’re here to make smart decisions. And building your email list is one of those smart decisions that you are making. How does my visibility framework fit into all of this? The framework that I’m sharing with you today is specifically designed to help entrepreneurs grow their email list quickly and sustainably. The strategies that I’ve included aren’t just about adding numbers, they’re about building lasting relationships with the right people, with your ideal client, with the perfect person that you want to serve. People that are genuinely interested in what you have to offer and who are more likely to become loyal customers of yours.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:34]:
One of the biggest challenges that I see entrepreneurs and small business owners face is overwhelm. Right? And I get it. There is always so much to do and so little time to do it. My husband, Nick, and I have 2 little boys, and we are only ever working school hours. So very rarely do we have extra time, so we need to be smart with the time that we do have. Have. When we then add social media and all the platforms that we’re told to be consistent on, on top of everything else, it’s so fucking exhausting. That’s why this framework is so powerful.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:03]:
It gives you a clear and direct path to follow, leveraging collaborations and SEO driven strategies instead of social media so you can grow your email list in a way that feels manageable, effective, and aligned with your business and your life. So as we move forward in this episode, keep in mind that the strategies I’m sharing aren’t just about quick wins. They’re about creating a sustainable long term approach to building your email list and ultimately growing your business. So let’s dive into the framework. Grab your pen and paper. You might want to take some notes And let’s cover all of the options that you have to grow your email list fast. Okay. So what does this framework look like? I want you to picture a capital letter v with two sides.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
On one side of that v, we have collaboration based strategies. And on the other side, we have search and SEO driven strategies. These are 2 powerful approaches that work together to give you the best of both worlds when it comes to visibility and email list growth. Let’s talk about the collaboration side of things first. Collaborations are all about leveraging other people’s audiences to grow your own. This isn’t about competition. It’s about working together to create something bigger than what we could achieve on our own. And there are a few key ways to do this effectively.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:16]:
First up, we have summits, bundles, and freebie swaps. These are all fantastic ways to get in front of a large audience quickly. Imagine participating in a virtual summit or contributing to a digital bundle where your ideal clients are already hanging out, already signing up to, already being a part of it. Right? By offering something valuable like a presentation in a summit or a free guide or a mini course in a bundle, you can attract a ton of new subscribers to your email list. The main thing to remember with this is to make sure that the resource you provide is something that’s going to speak to your perfect person, your ideal client, and lead them eventually to your main paid offer. I personally like to reverse engineer this and think about where I want to lead them first and work backwards. What is that first step that they need to take in order for them to be ready for my main paid offer? There’ll be more on how you do this in a future episode. Next, let’s talk about podcast guesting and guest speaking.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:08]:
By guesting on other people’s podcasts or guest speaking in existing groups or masterminds, you get to showcase your experience to a whole new audience. It’s an incredible opportunity to build trust and connection. And when you provide a clear call to action at the end, like a free download that adds subscribers to your email list, you’re not just sharing your knowledge, you’re growing your list at the same time. My biggest piece of advice with this is to make sure you have one clear call to action at the end of an interview or presentation. Don’t send them to your website, your Instagram profile, your podcast, your free resource. A confused mind won’t make any decisions. You want one link for them to go to next and that link should always then lead them to your email list. Now here’s the thing with collaborations.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:48]:
You don’t need to do all of them at once. In fact, I would not recommend it. I want you to pick one of these strategies that resonates with you and focus on it for the next 90 days. The key is consistency and building genuine relationships with your collaborators and to make sure you check-in at the end of each month and check the data. What kind of results have you gotten? Have you enjoyed the strategy? How does it make you feel? This is all important to take note of and you can use this when you’re deciding whether to continue with the strategy for the next 30 days or to tweak and change it up. Now let’s move over to the other side of the v, the search and SEO driven strategies. These options are all about making sure that when your ideal clients are searching for solutions online, they find you. The first piece of this puzzle is long form content and SEO.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:34]:
Now this could be blog posts or podcast episodes that are optimized for Google. When you create content that’s rich in keywords and answers the questions your ideal clients are asking, you start to show up in their search results. This kind of content continues to work for you long after it’s published, driving organic traffic to your site and growing your email list passively. Remember to again always have a clear call to action that leads the reader or listener to your email list. That is always our goal. Then there’s social media as SEO angle. Platforms like Pinterest, YouTube or even TikTok are more than just social networks. They’re search engines in their own right.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:09]:
By optimising your content for these platforms, you’re not just posting into the void and praying someone sees it. You’re creating content that can be found by people who are actively looking for what you have to offer. Remember to consider keywords in the content you create for these platforms and what I love to do is repurpose that long form content to save you some time. And finally, traditional PR plays a role here too. So getting featured in articles, being interviewed by media outlets, or writing guest posts can significantly boost your visibility and also your credibility. These opportunities often come with backlinks and mentions and enhance your SEO, making it easier for people to find you online. So whether you’re focused on collaborations, search, or a combination of both, the goal is the same: to grow your email list with strategies that feel good, are sustainable, and don’t rely on the unpredictability of social media. Now remember, I know that’s a lot.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:02]:
You don’t have to do it all at once. I’d recommend choosing one strategy from the collaboration side of the V and one from the search and SEO side. Focus on them for the next 90 days and track your progress each month. You’ll be amazed at the growth that you can achieve. Now, how do you choose which email list growth strategy to try? 1st, let’s recap the 2 main strategies within the framework. Right? Collaborations and search and SEO. So these are the pillars of your email list growth strategy and they’re designed to work together to maximize your reach, impact, and fast track your growth. So remember, we had the collaboration based strategies? So they were about leveraging the audiences of others to grow your list quickly.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:41]:
Think summits, bundles, freebie swaps, networking and podcast guesting or guest speaking. So these strategies allow you to tap into already established communities and bring in highly engaged subscribers who are likely to resonate with your message and what you do. On the other side, we have the search and SEO driven strategies. So these focus on creating content that’s discoverable and searchable over time. So this includes long form content like blog posts, podcast episodes, much much like this one, and optimizing your presence on platforms like Pinterest, YouTube, and even TikTok. These strategies are more about playing the long game, ensuring that your content continues to bring in new subscribers well after it’s been published. Now here’s what I want you to do. Choose one strategy from each category.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:24]:
1 collaboration and one search and SEO strategy to focus on for the next 90 days. The key here is to stay consistent and give each strategy enough time to show results. By narrowing your focus, you’ll avoid overwhelm and be able to execute these strategies more effectively. So how do you know if it’s even working? As you dive into these strategies, it’s crucial to track your progress. I want you to keep an eye on your email list growth, your engagement and conversion rates, and any other metrics that might matter to you. If you find that one approach isn’t giving you the results you expected and you’ve given it enough time, don’t be afraid to adjust it to switch it up. This is all about finding what works best for you and your business. And little spoiler here, but all of these strategies actually work.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:08]:
It’s not about choosing the right one. It’s about picking the strategy that’s right for you. It has to feel good and give you results. And when you land on something that does that, that’s when you know you’re onto a growth strategy that is sustainable and will work for the long term. Now as we wrap up today’s episode, I want to remind you, by focusing on collaborations and SEO driven strategies, you’re not only building your email list, You’re building relationships with people who genuinely care about what you have to offer. You’re building relationships with people that also serve your ideal clients so you’ll get more opportunities to collaborate with them again in the future. It gets easier and easier and easier. This is about creating a sustainable long term strategy that helps you grow your business in a way that feels good and is aligned with your values.

Kylie Kelly [00:12:51]:
It’s not about putting a freebie on your website and waiting 5 years for it to work. It’s not about dancing and pointing on social and hoping somebody sees you. It’s about building relationships. And by doing it this way means that you’re going to see results faster than you even thought possible. Now before you go, don’t forget to check out the free resource I have for you. I have a guide that is going to lay all of this out beautifully called your next 1,000 subscribers. You can grab the link in the show notes or head over to kyliekelly.com/guide and sign up for it there. And remember, if you’re looking for even more support, consider joining the Email Growth Club, my membership where we dive deep into all things email marketing and visibility.

Kylie Kelly [00:13:30]:
You’ll get access to a community of like minded entrepreneurs, exclusive resources, and so much more. Keep in mind, I’m cheering you on every step of the way. If you have questions, need advice or just want to share your progress, please reach out to me. I love connecting with my listeners and helping you navigate your email marketing journey. You can always send me an email hello at kyliekelly.com or if you do prefer social, jump on over to Instagram. I’m not on there often, but I do check my DM. So shoot me a DM and let’s chat. Thank you so much for tuning in today.

Kylie Kelly [00:14:00]:
I’m so grateful to have you here, and I can’t wait to see how these strategies work for you. If you haven’t already, make sure you subscribe to the podcast so you don’t miss any future episodes filled with actionable tips just like these to help you grow your email list and your business. Until next time, take care and keep on growing that email list. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning in to this episode of The Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact. Thank you so much for listening and I’ll see you in the next episode!

THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 148

In this special episode, I’m thrilled to reintroduce myself and officially welcome you to The Email Growth Show! After a lot of reflection and planning, I’ve decided to rebrand the podcast to better serve you and align with my passion for helping female entrepreneurs grow their email lists, without the stress of social media or paid ads.

Click play to listen below:

What we covered in this episode:

  • I shared my transition from a wedding photographer to an email marketing strategist and the decision to rebrand the podcast to “The Email Growth Show” to better serve female entrepreneurs seeking email list growth.
  • What you can expect and the details about the weekly episodes, monthly guest interviews, and the focus on actionable tips, strategies, and insights for email list growth – so you can take action in your own business straight away!
  • The exciting giveaway that I’m hosting to celebrate the rebrand & relaunch of the podcast!

Giveaway Details:

All you need to do is listen to the new episodes and leave me a review.
Email me at: hello@kyliekelly.com with a screenshot of the review and you’ll be in the draw to win: 

  • Prize 1: 7 Day Voxer Support with Kylie – receive personalised feedback on how you can grow your email list fast. Valued at $497. 
  • Prize 2: 30 Minute Strategy Call with Kylie – Valued at $197 
  • Prize 3: One Free Month in The Email Growth Club – valued at $27 

Prizes will be drawn on August 30th & winners notified by email.
 
* If you want a bonus entry, share your biggest takeaway on Instagram and tag me (​@_kylie_kelly_​) and you’ll get a second giveaway entry!

Full Transcript:

Kylie Kelly [00:00:04]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or throwing cash at paid ads? Welcome to The Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from 0 to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than 2 years and the same is possible for you too. Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode. Hello. Oh my gosh. Welcome to The Email Growth Show. In this special episode, I’m so excited to reintroduce myself and officially welcome you to The Email Growth Show.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:49]:
After a lot of reflection and planning, I’ve decided to rebrand the podcast to better serve you and align with my passion for helping female entrepreneurs grow their email list without the stress of social media or paid ads. In this episode, I wanna share a little bit about my journey, the story behind the rebrand, and what you can expect from this podcast going forward. So let’s dive on in. Now, firstly, if you are new to this podcast, if you are just finding us today, welcome. Hi. I’m so glad you’re here. I wanted to introduce myself. So my name is Kylie Kelly, and I call myself now an email marketing strategist, which can I say sounds a little bit boring because what I do is actually super exciting, and I help female business owners grow their email list fast in a way that feels good for them? I’ve actually been self employed for close to 14 or 15 years now, but I started out on this journey as a wedding photographer.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:39]:
And then 2020 happened. And even though my calendar was fully booked for 2 years, I had to refund all of these canceled weddings, which honestly almost sent me bankrupt. And although it was a very stressful time in my personal and business journey, it was this moment where I actually got to stop and reflect on what the next step was for me. At that point, I was pregnant with my younger, Sam, and we already had Spencer. He was a toddler. And being a wedding photographer didn’t give me the flexibility that I yearned for that I wanted. It meant that I was working weekends and I was traveling a lot. And it was a lifestyle business, which isn’t a bad thing.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:14]:
It was paying the bills and it was paying my salary, but it wasn’t enabling us to buy a home or upgrade a car or any of those more luxurious expenses. Right? So when the pandemic happened and I had this moment where I got to decide, do I push forward and start again or do I pivot to something else? I chose an online business. Now I didn’t know what I wanted to do. I knew I wanted to help other women just like me, but I didn’t know how. However, what I had learned from the previous decade of being self employed as a photographer was that I needed to grow an audience first because there is no point coming up with the most amazing offer, the most amazing service, the most amazing client experience if I didn’t have clients. If nobody knew I existed, if I had nobody to sell to, then it wasn’t gonna work very quickly, was it? So I set about building an email list. Now why an email list? Mainly because I hate social media. Perhaps it’s because I was a photographer, but I was a perfectionist in curating my feed, into creating the graphics, writing the copy.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:13]:
I wanted it to be perfect. And because of that, I put a lot of pressure on myself. And when I actually sat back and looked at the results, looked at the data, looked at what I was getting from that social media presence, it wasn’t giving me anything. I wasn’t getting clients. It wasn’t paying my bills. I wasn’t growing an email list. Nothing was happening. Right? I would get 50 views on an Instagram story or on a post.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:36]:
It was frustrating. So I decided to do things differently, which is why I focused on my email list since then. So I hosted my first virtual event in 2022, and the whole reason for that was to grow my email list. And in one event, it went from 0 to 600 ideal clients that were then a part of my world. It was a lot of work. I won’t sugar coat it. Of course, it was a lot of work, but it enabled me to actually grow my list without social media, without spending a cent on paid ads really quite quickly, and I enjoyed it. I was hooked.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:06]:
In the last 2 years, I’ve grown my email list from 0 to almost 10,000 ideal clients, 10,000 subscribers through relationship based strategies, which is what we’re gonna be talking about on this podcast going forward. So we’re talking bundles, summits, podcast guesting, freebie swaps, and so much more. Since then, I’ve created a membership called the Email Growth Club where I teach other women to do just that. So I had decided to niche this podcast down for ambitious female business owners who want to build an online business, who want to build an email list in integrity and alignment with their life. They wanna see results fast. You might be listening and you might be frustrated with the endless grind of marketing your online business on social media like I was, seeing minimal results for your efforts. You might wish that you could grow your email list in a way that feels good to you that actually works so you can start to make reliable revenue. Isn’t that the dream? Imagine having a business that’s not only easy and fun but also aligns with your life, allowing you to be the mother or the woman or the wife, the person that you wanna be.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:06]:
You don’t have to put a freebie on your website and wait 5 years to build a large engaged email list anymore. I mean, who wants to wait that long anyway? I certainly didn’t and that’s why around here we do things a little bit differently. On this podcast, we’re going to uncover the secrets to building an email list full of your ideal clients that will drive your growth and success faster than you thought was possible. So if you are a coach, course creator, or online business owner looking to grow your email list and elevate your email marketing, this podcast is for you. I’m so excited about this. For those of you that don’t know, before this rebrand, my podcast was called This Mama Means Business, and I created that in 2020 when I was lonely. I didn’t have any friends. We just moved interstate after the pandemic hit.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:46]:
I just wanted to speak to women who got it, who were doing the same thing as me, that were trying to figure out this whole online business thing, that were trying to be the best mom they could be, that were trying to do it all. And I felt like I was failing at everything. Right? I just closed down my business, as you heard, and I was pregnant with Sam, and I didn’t feel like I had anyone to connect to. Have you ever felt like that? It is horrible. That feeling of, like, not belonging in any space. And I remember even though we’d moved interstate, there weren’t any local groups I could go to. There were a few mothers groups meeting online, and I remember tuning into 1 and just feeling like such an outsider. I didn’t wanna speak about my kids all the time.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:21]:
Like, I love them to death, but I don’t wanna speak about them all the time. There is so much more to my personality, to who I am that I’m passionate about than just my children. So that’s why I created this mama means business, and it enabled me to have these really deep conversations because I hate surface level shit. Really deep conversations with women that were trying to build something bigger than themselves, were trying to grow their business, trying to teach their kids how to be good humans. Right? They were doing everything, and it enabled me to really connect and grow some really deep friendships out of it. So I am so grateful. And if you were from those days, thank you so much for listening and being a part of that community. It honestly means the world to me.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:59]:
And although I feel like it is time to shift focus, I still have such a special place in my heart for what that podcast brought into my life. So what can you expect from this new show? So I’m going to be dropping episodes every single week. So every Friday, there will be a new episode dropping starting with a couple right now that you can binge. Of course, I had to try and get a couple ahead of you so that you had a few to choose from as you listen to this new aligned email growth show. But going forward, you can expect episodes to drop on a Friday. I will have one guest interview a month that I am handpicking to make sure that that guest brings you very tangible action steps. Just like Sofia Parra’s episode, episode a 144, that has been so popular. She spoke to us about how to nurture your email list and start conversations, and it really made us think about nurturing our email list a little bit differently.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:49]:
And that nurture piece is so important when it comes to selling to our list and building really genuine relationships. So that episode is a must listen. If you haven’t listened to that, just go back a couple, episode a 144. A great episode to tune into. That is the standard of my monthly guest episodes. That’s what you can expect. So I can tell you the next guest episode that will be dropping on the 30th August is with the incredible Marisa Cochrane. She’ll be sharing with us how to craft compelling email copy to send to our list, so it’s gonna be one that you’re going to definitely want to tune into.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:22]:
So weekly episodes are dropping on a Friday, one incredible guest episode every month. And once again, every single episode, whether it’s a solo episode with me or a guest episode with a special guest, it will include actionable tips, strategies, and insights because I’m all about you receiving things that will actually help you on your journey, things that will actually help you achieve tangible results when it comes to growing, nurturing, and selling to your email list. That is what we are all about. Now, of course, what is a relaunch? What is a rebrand without a really exciting giveaway that I wanna share with you quickly now? So to celebrate, I have 3 different prizes that are up for grabs. Prize number 1 is a 7 day Voxer support week with me. So you can have me in your pocket to receive personalised feedback on how you can grow your email list fast through a handy mobile app Voxer, which is kind of like a walkie talkie app if you haven’t used that before. That prize itself is valued at $497. Prize number 2 is a 30 minute strategy call with me.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:20]:
So we can dive into anything that you want on this call. It can be anything to do with your business, with your growth strategy, with how you’re growing your list, how you’re selling to your list. Anything at all that I can help with, we can dive into it. So that is valued at $197 and that is prize number 2. And then prize number 3 is 1 free month in the Email Growth Club. So the Email Growth Club is my membership that is all about growing your email list without social media or paid ads. With over 250 members, it is such an incredible supportive community. So I’d love to gift the 3rd winner a free month in the email growth club valued at 27 dollars.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:53]:
So if you want to enter this giveaway, if you want to be a part of celebrating with me, all you need to do is listen to the other 2 new episodes that dropped today and leave me a review. Now because Apple Podcasts sometimes don’t upload reviews straight away, especially when it’s an international audience, I’d encourage you to take a screenshot of the review before you post it. Email me at hello@kyliekelly.com with that screenshot and you will be entered into the draw. The prizes are going to be drawn on the 30th August and I will notify all the winners by email. And just a secret little tip for all of my incredible listeners. If you want a bonus entry, if you can share your biggest takeaway on Instagram from one of these first three episodes and tag me, which is just at_kyleigh_kelly_. Gotta love the underscores. And you’ll get a second giveaway entry.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:37]:
I’ve included all the notes for this giveaway in the show notes below. So if you need to have a little look to follow the instructions, please do that there. Know that they are there for you. But I would love for you to celebrate this rebrand alongside me and go into the draw to win some pretty incredible prizes to make sure that you start to grow your email list even faster. Now as I mentioned, there are 2 other episodes that just dropped today as well. There’s one on my visibility framework where I share all the different ways, all the different options you have to grow your email list, both through a variety of different collaborations and also strategies that rely more on search and SEO. So, again, through that visibility framework, you will notice that social media is mentioned very, very minimally and paid ads is definitely not a part of that discussion whatsoever. So if you’re looking to understand some different ways that you can go about growing your email list but you don’t know where to start, that’s gonna be a great episode to listen to.

Kylie Kelly [00:11:28]:
Again, nice and short 20 minute episode, but I think that that’ll be really helpful for you to just pause and think about what strategy do you wanna try next to leverage relationships and grow your email list fast. So that is episode a 149. And then episode a 150 is all about challenging email marketing myths and beliefs. content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 185

If you’ve ever felt like you need to be everywhere to grow your business – Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, TikTok, blogging five times a week and somehow also being a thought leader on f*cking LinkedIn – this is your permission slip to stop.

Because here’s the truth:

Visibility without relationships doesn’t convert.

And if your visibility strategy isn’t helping you build actual trust with real humans? It’s not a strategy.

It’s a burnout plan.

In this episode, I’m sharing the three visibility platforms I’m focusing on in Q2 – and more importantly, what visibility that actually converts really looks like.

Listen to this episode here:

CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL TRANSCRIPT

Kylie Kelly [00:00:00]:
Let me ask you something. When was the last time you actually enjoyed going through a welcome sequence? Not skimmed, not tolerated? Actually enjoyed it because that question is the reason I stopped sending them. And what I do instead has changed how people engage with my emails completely. Let’s chat about it.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:22]:
Are you a female business owner frustrated with battling the algorithm and looking for growth strategies that don’t involve awkwardly pointing or dancing online or for growing cash at paid ads? Welcome to the Email Growth Show. I’m your host, Kylie Kelly, visibility and email marketing strategist. I grew my email list from zero to almost 10,000 subscribers in less than two years, and the same is possible for you too.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:45]:
Are you ready to build your email list and start making more money in your online business? Let’s head into today’s episode.

Kylie Kelly [00:00:54]:
Hey hey. Welcome back to the Email Growth Show. I am so, so excited that you are here today. We are talking about welcome sequences because I don’t send them anymore. And before anyone panics or thinks I’m saying that they’re dead or useless, that’s not what this is. This is me sharing why they no longer fit, how I want to show up, or how my audience wants to be treated in 2026. And honestly, funnels and sequences just annoy the fuck out of me now. Not because they don’t work in theory, but because my audience is smart.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:28]:
They know when they’ve entered a funnel. They know when they’re being walked through something step by step. And yes, while I could name it and wink at it and say, yes, welcome to my funnel, I just don’t want to. I don’t want my emails to feel like machinery. I want them to feel like a room that you just walked into. So instead of a traditional welcome sequence, I send one email. Want to know about it? It’s called a Start Here email. Now let’s talk about why I stopped sending them.

Kylie Kelly [00:01:56]:
Most welcome sequences are built on an old assumption that attention equals readiness. That if someone downloads a freebie, they’re ready to be introduced to your story, educated, nurtured and gently pushed towards an offer within a handful of days. But inbox behavior has changed across email platforms. We’re seeing that open rates are highest on Delivery emails, often 20 to 40% higher than follow up emails in that same sequence. Click rates tend to peak there too. Not email three. Not email five. Not the just checking in email.

Kylie Kelly [00:02:31]:
The first one, the delivery email. That’s the moment of peak attention. So instead of dragging someone through five or seven emails, hoping they stay engaged long enough to Warm up. I decided to respect that moment. If this is the email they’re most likely to open and actually read, then I want it to do the work. That’s why my start here email replaces the welcome sequence, the orientation emails, the here’s who I am and what I do content. It’s all in one place now. Not sneakily, not manipulatively, just super fucking clearly.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:04]:
I do want to say funnels aren’t broken, but people are more aware. And I don’t think that coaches or educators, people in the online space are talking about this enough. Funnels used to work really well because people didn’t recognize them. Now they do. Most business owners on your list have either bought multiple courses, joined multiple lists, been through dozens of sequences or funnels. They know the rhythm, they know the pacing, they know when they’re being nurtured. And while awareness doesn’t automatically mean resistance, it does change how people feel. When somebody realizes they’re in a sequence, their nervous system shifts, they skim a bit more, they delay clicking, they wait it out.

Kylie Kelly [00:03:46]:
Not because they don’t like you, but because they want to regain control. They want to feel safe. Now that’s the part that I care about. I never want my emails to trigger someone’s internal just wait and see response or what she up to response, right. I want them to feel like they’re in control, like they’re choosing to stay so important. Now, if you want to hear a really quick episode about how one of my clients turned off all of her beautiful funnels and actually made three times her monthly revenue within 60 days of working together, go back to episode 230. I’ll link it in the show notes and have a listen. I think if you weren’t sure right now about funnels, that this is really going to bring it home.

Kylie Kelly [00:04:28]:
The fact that we can turn them off, that you do have options and you can still make the revenue that you are aiming to make, or even more like in Julie’s example now. Now let’s talk about the start here email. What does a start here email actually do? So this is the email that it still delivers, the thing they signed up for. That part matters. So you’re still going to have at the top of that email the link to that free resource or whatever it is that they’ve opted into. But it also answers the questions that every new subscriber has, whether they’re consciously thinking them or not. Who are you really? What kind of emails do you send? How often am I going to hear from you? What do you actually help with? And where should I go if I want more? I don’t drip feed that fcking information over a week. Like no, I give it to them upfront and I let them decide what happens next.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:17]:
And yes, this email has way more than just one link. And I know that breaks the old rules, but I’m all about breaking rules over here. Those rules come from a time when we assumed people couldn’t make decisions without being guided carefully. From point A to point B. That time is over. My list is full of intelligent women. They’re capable of choosing what’s relevant to them. They don’t need to be funneled down a narrow path like they’ll get overwhelmed by options.

Kylie Kelly [00:05:43]:
They don’t need to be spoon fed. Giving them choice builds trust. And trust is what converts when they’re ready. Not welcome sequence length. Now listen, here’s what I’m noticing across email lists. Last year and heading into 2026, people aren’t short on information so fucking everywhere, right? They’re short on orientation. They don’t need more emails explaining why email marketing matters. They need to know am I in the right place? Is this person for me? And does this feel safe, calm and relevant? A start here.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:13]:
Email can answer all of that without pressure. And because it lives in a single reference point, it then can become an anchor. People can save it, bookmark it, come back to it. They can click it when they’re ready. That behavior lines up with what we’re seeing across inboxes. Fewer impulsive clicks, more considered engag. Longer decision cycles, but stronger trust when people do move. So what do I include in my start here email? I will include my full template in the show notes so you can see exactly how I write this.

Kylie Kelly [00:06:44]:
But conceptually, here’s what it does. I introduce myself like a human. Not a brand bio, not a resume. I set expectations clearly. How often I email, what kind of content I send, what they won’t get from me. That part matters more than people realize. Again, predictability builds safety. Safety builds trust.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:04]:
Then I give them a few clear places to explore. A free resource that people genuinely love. The podcast. One way to work with me. And I invite conversation. I ask them to reply. I remind them that it’s actually me. I ask them how they found me.

Kylie Kelly [00:07:19]:
Because email still works best as a two way channel, even if most people never reply. That invitation alone can change how the inbox feels and what they feel when they see my sender name pop up in their inbox next time. So the deeper reason that I do that this way is that it’s more about tone, right? A welcome sequence often says, sit down, I’ll take you through this. A start here. Email says, oh my gosh, welcome, you’ve arrived, you’re here, let me show you around, take what you need. Can you feel the difference there? That matters. It tells your subscriber that they’re not a number, that they’re not a lead, that they’re not something to be warmed up before they’re allowed to choose. They get agency from the very first email and in my experience that creates better long term engagement than any perfectly timed sequence ever could.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:09]:
Now, if you’re thinking of trying this, if you’ve been feeling resistance around welcome sequences, or maybe you don’t even have one set up yet, no shade if your emails feel heavier than they used to, if you want your inbox to feel more human, this is a simple experiment worth running. You don’t need to burn everything down, you don’t need to overthink it. You just need to write one email that does the job. All you need to do, turn off your welcome sequences, put up this one email, track it for 30 days. Obviously get people onto your list to receive the thing, track it for 30 days and see. See how it feels. See what the data tells you, see what the responses are like. I don’t think you’ll be disappointed.

Kylie Kelly [00:08:49]:
Now, like I said, I’ll put my full start here template in the show notes. You can adapt it for your own voice, your own offers, your own people. I’m so excited for you to try this and I want to know if this episode sparks something or if you want help simplifying how your emails actually work together. You know exactly where to find me, my loves. That is it for today. I hope you enjoy this. I hope you feel inspired to create your own start here email and ditch the welcome sequence if it is no longer serving you and your ideal clients. Reach out if you have any questions.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:19]:
I love you loads and I will talk to you really soon, like really soon. I’ve got some really good stuff coming your way and next week’s episode is our guest episode with an incredible, incredible PR expert. You’re going to want to tune in. All right, I will see you then. Bye for now. Thank you so much for tuning into.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:37]:
This episode of the Email Growth Show. I hope you found valuable insights into the next steps you can take to grow your email list and boost your business without relying on social media or paid ads. If you enjoyed this episode, please take a moment to rate and review the.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:51]:
Show and share it with others. Your feedback helps me reach more female.

Kylie Kelly [00:09:55]:
Entrepreneurs just like you who are ready to say goodbye to social media and leverage email marketing to grow their business and make a bigger impact.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:03]:
Thank you so much for listening and.

Kylie Kelly [00:10:04]:
I’ll see you in the next episode.

TL:DR

What you’ll learn in this episode:

– Why visibility without relationships won’t convert (and what to do instead)
– The 3 visibility channels I’m using right now to grow intentionally
– How I use Strategic Planner Sally (my AI biz bestie!) to map it all out
– Why you don’t need to be everywhere – just in the right places
– What sustainable, relationship-first audience growth really looks like!

Ready to Simplify Your Visibility?

If you’re tired of trying to keep up with every platform and craving a strategy that actually works, I’d love to support you.

Inside my Empire Expansion Event, we build a visibility plan rooted in relationship-first marketing – the kind that grows your audience, strengthens trust, and converts without burning you out.

No more throwing content at the wall.
No more guessing what to focus on.
No more chasing trends that don’t align.

Instead, we map out a clear 90-day plan built around your strengths, your season, and your dream clients.

👉 Join the Empire Expansion Event here: https://kyliekelly.com/empire-expansion

Stop scattering your energy.
Start building real momentum.
Grow in a way that actually feels good.

I’ll see you inside. 💛

Visibility Isn’t About Being Loud. It’s About Being Known.

There’s a lot of noise online right now.

Post more.
Be consistent.
Show up daily.
Start a YouTube.
Go viral.

But here’s what I believe (and what I’ve seen over and over again in my own business):

Visibility on its own isn’t enough. It has to lead somewhere.

It has to create connection.
It has to build trust.
It has to open the door to a relationship.

Relationship-first marketing is about showing up as yourself in the places your ideal clients are already paying attention – and creating consistent opportunities for connection so that when the time is right, they say yes.

Visibility isn’t about being loud.
It’s about being known, trusted, and remembered.

When someone says, “I need help launching,” or “I need to grow my email list,” do you come to mind?

That doesn’t happen because you’re on 12 platforms.
It happens because you went deep instead of wide.

My 3 Visibility Platforms for Q2

Every 90 days, I reassess where I’m focusing my energy. Seasons shift. Goals shift. Capacity shifts.

And right now, these are the three platforms I’m doubling down on.

1. Hosting My Own Podcast

This one is non-negotiable.

My podcast lets me show up consistently, speak directly to you, and position myself as a trusted voice in the visibility and email marketing space.

It’s long-form.
It’s nuanced.
It builds depth.

And because my show notes are SEO-optimised, it also supports search-based discoverability. That means my content doesn’t just work today – it compounds over time.

This is the sweet spot:

  • Relationship-based trust through your voice
  • Search-based visibility through SEO

It’s not about going viral.
It’s about building a body of work that builds credibility.

2. Guest Speaking in Memberships, Masterminds & Summits

This is where the relationship side of visibility really shines.

When I guest speak inside memberships, masterminds, and summits, I’m stepping into warm rooms. These audiences already trust the host. That trust transfers.

And when I show up live – answering questions, interacting, having real conversations – that connection deepens fast.

These opportunities often convert far better than cold visibility ever could.

Why?

Because trust is already in the room.

For this season of life (mum mode included), this strategy works beautifully. I get to:

  • Show up powerfully
  • Deliver value live
  • Build relationships
  • Then log off and be present at home

That’s sustainable visibility.

3. Freebie Swaps & Email List Collaborations

This one is all about intentional list growth.

Freebie swaps.
Inbox takeovers.
Bundles.
Collaborative campaigns.

But here’s the key:

I’m not chasing vanity metrics. I’m not trying to grow the biggest list in the room.

I want aligned subscribers.
People who are genuinely interested.
People who will open, click, reply, and engage.

Because an engaged list of 3,000 beats a dead list of 30,000 every single time.

When you combine collaborative visibility with consistent nurturing, you create visibility that actually converts.

The Balance: Search + Relationships

You’ve built a list… but you barely email it.

You need both.

Long-term discoverability (SEO, evergreen content, searchable platforms).

And
Relationship-based visibility (collabs, guesting, live rooms, shared audiences).

One builds reach.
The other builds trust.

Together? That’s momentum.

How to Choose Your Visibility Strategy

If you’re sitting there thinking, “Okay Kylie, but what should I focus on?” – start here.

Journal on these questions:

  • What visibility action makes me feel most like myself?
  • Where do I feel most confident showing up?
  • Where is my ideal client already paying attention?
  • What feels sustainable for the long haul?

If your current strategy feels draining, forced, chaotic, or like you’re constantly behind…

It’s probably not the right one.

You do not have to dance on Instagram.
You do not have to be on every platform.
You do not have to force yourself into spaces that don’t feel aligned.

Because if it’s not sustainable, it won’t scale.

You Don’t Need to Be Everywhere

I used to think I had to do it all.

Post daily.
Be available 24/7.
Create new content for every platform.

Now?

I repurpose strategically.
I speak where people are already listening.
And I double down on relationships over reach.

That’s how I’ve grown a business I love.
That’s how I’ve filled it with dream clients.
That’s how I’ve built an email list without relying on social media or paid ads.

Visibility doesn’t have to be exhausting.

You don’t have to be everywhere to grow.

You just need to be seen by the right people, in the right places, in the right way – consistently.

And when you do that?

The growth takes care of itself.

Your Next Move

If you’re done trying to be visible everywhere and ready to focus on what actually moves the needle, this is your moment.

Inside my Empire Expansion Event, we build a visibility plan that’s strategic, sustainable, and rooted in relationship-first marketing. No dancing for the algorithm. No “post more” nonsense. Just clear direction, smart systems, and momentum that compounds.

This is where you choose your platforms.
This is where you simplify your strategy.
This is where your next 90 days get mapped out properly.

Less noise.
More alignment.
Real growth.

Let’s build this the smart way. 💛

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 144

Today, I’ve got the incredible Sophia Parra joining me to talk all about how to nurture your email list! Sophia is a marketing coach that is an expert at all things online business – from nurturing, to building key relationships and driving sales. She’s all about genuine connections & relationships, which is totally something we can get behind right?!

Before we get started, here are the links mentioned in this interview with Sophia:

  • Join Sophia’s Marketing Mail here: https://www.gotocoach.club/marketingmail
  • 12 Strategies To Find & Convert Your Next Client On Social: https://www.gotocoach.club/clients

Click play to listen to the interview here:

The 3 Pillars of Engaging Your Audience

In our conversation, Sophia emphasised the importance of focusing on 3 main pillars in your marketing strategy: Growing Your Audience, Nurturing Your Audience, and Making Sales. Understanding and implementing these three pillars can significantly enhance your ability to connect with your audience and achieve your business goals.

Let’s break down each one:

  1. Growing Your Audience: The foundation of a successful business is continuously expanding your audience – I know you understand this! Luckily, this doesn’t mean increasing social media followers; it’s about growing a community actively interested in what you offer. Strategies like collaborations, podcast guesting and leveraging your email list are the key to reaching new potential customers in meaningful, intentional ways.

  2. Nurturing Your Audience: I think this is where Sophia shines! She explained that nurturing isn’t just about posting content; it’s about fostering genuine conversations and relationships. Whether through social media, email marketing, or direct interactions, the goal is to engage in meaningful dialogues that make your audience feel valued & understood. Sophia pointed out that if your business isn’t regularly sparking conversations, it’s time to reevaluate your nurturing strategies. She also shared some examples on how you can nurture your email list that I just loved!

  3. Making Sales: The ultimate goal of growing and nurturing your audience is to guide them towards making a purchase. However, Sophia highlighted that sales should feel like a natural step in the customer journey, not a pushy pitch – which I couldn’t agree with more if I wanted to! By building trust and demonstrating value through your nurturing efforts, sales become a byproduct of the relationships you’ve cultivated.

How To Nurture Your Email List for Real Results

Sophia explained that when you’re thinking about how to nurture your email list, you need to keep in mind that it’s all about creating meaningful connections. By focusing on starting real conversations and measuring success based on engagement, rather than superficial numbers on social media, you can cultivate a loyal and invested email list that’s truly connected to your brand.

She shared practical examples of her nurturing events and the importance of personal touches, like exclusive email content or interactive Q&A sessions. These strategies not only elevate your audience’s experience but also solidify their connection to your brand or business, making them more likely to support you when it comes time to make a purchase.

Creating Genuine Connections with Your Audience

We also chatted about creating events that nurture your email list and will genuinely resonate with your audience. Exclusive invitations for email subscribers and personalised interactions through videos can elevate the level of engagement and connection with your audience. This kind of personalisation fosters a deeper, more meaningful relationship with your audience and email list, taking your business to the next level!

So, what I learned from Sophia is that when you’re thinking about how to nurture your email list, it’s more than just business strategy; it’s about transforming the way we connect with others and creating meaningful, long-term success through conversation. I’m excited to put these insights into action myself, and I can’t wait for you to do the same.

content:
THE EMAIL GROWTH SHOW EPISODE 143

Today I wanted to dive in to all things email deliverability and how you can actually do everything in your power to make sure that your emails actually reach your audience. I’m chatting through some of the more technical aspects of email deliverability – email authentication and the crucial role that it plays. Plus, I cover the importance of regularly cleaning your email list, personalising email content, and what you can do to try and avoid spam triggers.

On top of all that, there are some practical tips and resources to help you create a healthy, engaged email list for your business!

Click play to listen below:

Email Authentication & The Authentication Process

The first step in ensuring that your emails reach your audience’s inboxes is email authentication. This involves verifying your domain to prevent your emails from being lost in spam folders or, even worse, being blocked.

Now this feels heavy and super technical – and it is a little bit – but we need to put our CEO hats on and get this done, because without it, email marketing isn’t going to work for us.

When we’re looking at the process to authenticate our domain emails (the email that is coming from your domain – @yourdomain.com not gmail, hotmail or anything free) we need to understand three elements that allow us to do this (please know that these are general guidelines but depending on what email service provider you use and where your domain is hosted, they might differ!)

  • SPF: you’ll need one SPF record per domain. This record will include a little bit of code for every single piece of software that sends emails to your clients on behalf of your domain. For example, it might Convertkit, Google Workspace, Shopify – all added together in one line of code that you add to your DNS server.

  • DKIM: For everyone software that sends emails on your behalf, you’ll need individual DKIM records to be added. So from the example above, you’d have a seperate DKIM you’d add for Convertkit, another one for Google Workspace and then another for Shopify. You’ll end up with multiple DKIM records on your DNS.

  • DMARC: You’ll have one DMARC record for your domain – and if you use a free took like PostMark it is super easy to set up and you’ll receive weekly reports to let you know if any issues arise. PostMark: https://dmarc.postmarkapp.com


These are the three elements that we need to set up in order to tell the Internet gods that we’re legit and make sure we’re authorised to send emails to our subscribers.

Without this, our emails won’t go through.

If you need help, I’d highly recommend these two resources from Cheryl Rerick (where I learnt everything I know about email deliverability from!)

Cheryl Rerick’s Google Updates: Deliverability Webinar Free (affiliate link)
Cheryl Rerick’s Email Deliverability Unboxed Series (affiliate link)

… and here is the link to MX Toolbox that I referenced to check that you’ve done your authentication right: https://mxtoolbox.com/emailhealth

Why It’s Important To Regularly Clean Your Email List…

Regularly cleaning your email list is essential for maintaining high engagement and demonstrating to email service providers that your content is valued by your audience – and therefore should be landing in the inbox!

When it comes to cleaning our list – I’m talking about removing cold subscribers, which those who aren’t opening or engaging with your emails. They shouldn’t be there and they need to be routinely removed from your email list.

While some marketers opt for re-engagement campaigns to win back these inactive subscribers, I believe that’s not the best way to spend your time. Data tells us that there is a very minimal chance that they’ll re-engage, especially if they haven’t opened or clicked an email in 30 days or more – so there isn’t much point in sending re-engagement emails in my opinion.

Instead, on the first of every month I log into my email service provider – Kit – and select all the cold subscribers and just delete them. I don’t look at them, I don’t think twice. Just delete. This practice has helped keep my open and click rates high – whilst also helping me have the best chance to actually land in my ideal clients inboxes in the future.

How To Personalise Emails That You Send & Why You Should!

When you think of personalisation, you probably think of just starting the email with the subscribers first name right? While that’s a good start, it goes way beyond that! It extends to tailoring the content to their interests, previous interactions, and preferences, as well as using their first name in the subject line occasionally too!

By personalising your email content, you create a stronger connection with your audience, leading to higher engagement and improved deliverability – which is what we’re aiming for after all!

My favourite way to do this is to make sure I’m using the subscribers name, throughout the body of the email where it makes sense and also segmenting my list according to their previous purchases (for example all the members of The Spotlight Club are segmented as such in my ESP, so that I don’t send them sales emails for the membership – because they’re already in it!)

Spam Filters & Best Practices To Avoid Them…

Several factors can trigger spam filters and land us right in the dreaded spam folder.

Here’s some things to take it into consideration when you’re emailing:

  1. Your language (don’t use words like “buy now”, “free”, “guarantee” in the subject line!)
  2. Don’t use too many images or images that are too big (resize them in Canva if you’re unsure!)
  3. Make your subject lines relevant to the topic of the email – no click bait here
  4. Don’t use URL shorteners – just hyperlink the original URL to a sentence or button in the email
  5. Try to refrain from excessive caps or too many exclamation points!!!
  6. Do your best to foster engagement by sending out valuable emails, instead of just sending an email to send an email.

By steering clear of these spam triggers and prioritising genuine & engaging content, you increase the likelihood of your emails reaching your audience’s inboxes.

Ok, So Action Steps From Today:

  • Do the work to make sure your domain email is authenticated. The hard deadline for this is April 1, 2024 but honestly, the sooner the better!

  • Create a routine around cleaning your list, in a way that feels good for you. If once a month is too much, make it every second month but put it on your calendar and make sure it happens!

  • Focus on sending out valuable, personalised content to your email list once a week, checking that you’re doing all you can to avoid those spam triggers and keep an eye on your email analytics to make sure they’re going in the right direction.

That little test is gonna do you really well when it comes to evaluating whether or not the language you’re using in your emails and your subject line is that of a human. Try to use it as much as you can and just be really careful if you are shortening them. In an email campaign, I think the best practice is just to hyperlink a sentence and link it to the long link.
